stickseum/getting-started.b:
:: Characters = 28
:: Modes = 14 (plus 10 daily modes)
:: Players = 2–32
:: Platform = Browser (no install)
:: HP = 300

Stickseum is a real-time stickman brawler. It opens right in your browser with nothing to install, and one link is all it takes to fight in the same room as your friends. There are 28 characters, 14 modes and 10 daily modes, and 2 to 32 players can play together.

## How to open the game
- Hit **Play Now** on the site and the latest version opens right away.
- If you'd rather have a file, download it and double-click it. You still need an internet connection, though.
- When playing with friends, everyone should join through **Play Now**. If versions differ, chat, skins or new characters may not show up for some people. If someone joins on a different version from the host, a notice pops up in the room.
- Change the language in Settings. You can pick Auto, the 13 real languages and the 5 fictional languages (Newspeak, Translator Korean, Aurebesh, Standard Galactic, Emoji).

## Your first steps
1. Pick a nickname (up to 15 characters).
2. Choose a mode in **Online Play** and start matchmaking, or create a room in **Private Play** and send the 6-character code to your friends. Codes use uppercase letters and numbers.
3. When the match starts, pick a character. Duels, team battles and ranked have a 20-second ban stage first, and character select only begins once both sides have chosen their bans. In duels there is another ban stage before every round. In team battles, every teammate picks one character to ban. On the character select screen you can search for characters by name. You have 15 seconds to pick, and once everyone has picked, the choices are revealed for 3 seconds. No confirmation window appears after you pick.
4. Want to get a feel for things first? Practice solo in **Practice Mode**.
5. New accounts can play a 7-step tutorial. Finish it and you get 100 sC (the currency was called gold before).

## Matchmaking and bots
- Online matchmaking puts people looking for the same mode into the same room. You don't pick the map; it follows a rotation that changes every 10 minutes.
- When looking for a room, 6 rooms are checked at the same time, which makes it faster. All rooms are still checked.
- If the room still isn't full 15 seconds after the last person joins, bots fill the empty slots and the match starts. Rooms of 16 slots or fewer get filled completely; larger rooms are filled up to 10 players.
- If only one person is in an online room, bots fill in right away with no notice. Bots also join quickly. If you are in a party or there are 2 or more people, the usual 15-second wait applies.
- Hide and Seek is not part of online matchmaking. It can only be played in private rooms (v360), and bots can't play it either. Ranked matches don't allow bots.
- In private rooms, the host adds bots directly. Bot difficulty can be Easy, Normal or Hard.
- Bots pick and lock in a weapon within 5 seconds.
- Bots also use teleport. When their health is low and an enemy is close, they move to a distant platform. If a capture point is far away, they move to it. Melee-character bots move next to a distant opponent. They don't teleport into lava pools.

## Basic rules
- All characters have 300 HP (except in modes where HP is set separately).
- When you die you usually respawn after 5 seconds. Depending on the mode, the respawn time changes or there is no respawn.
- There is no natural regeneration. Instead, if you stay in the same spot for 3 seconds without moving, you recover 5 HP every 0.5 seconds. Standing still to shoot is fine. In survival and one-hit modes there is no recovery.
- On the same team you can't pick the same character (except on large maps where teams are so big that overlaps are unavoidable).
- In duels, you can't pick a character you used in an earlier round again in the next round.
- In duels, before each round both players ban one of the other's characters. The ban only applies to character select for that round.
- When a match ends, the results screen shows your team's characters (left) and the opposing team's characters (right). The winning side does a victory pose and the losing side a defeat motion. In a draw, both sides do the defeat motion (build 395). A draw plays an oddly short tune.

## Controls at a glance (defaults)
- A / D to move, W or Space to jump, aim with the mouse and click to attack.
- Q dash, E teleport, R ultimate, F skill. For detailed controls, see the Controls & Settings page.

## Base cooldowns
- Skill 5 seconds, ultimate 20 seconds, teleport 10 seconds.
- Dash is 1.5 seconds by default (assassins 0.5 seconds).
- Teleport doesn't go off instantly. It charges for 1 second and then moves you.

## Saving your progress
- If you're not logged in, gold, skins and levels are saved only in the browser you're using. If the site address changes or you open the game as a file, it starts fresh.
- Logging in with a Frenchfries777 account also saves your progress to the account, including gold, cosmetics, levels, mastery, achievements, missions and season pass. When you log in on another device, it loads or merges your progress. When merging, the side with more progress is kept.
- When two different accounts log in on the same browser, progress (gold, skins, levels), highlights and recent players don't mix. Each account is kept separately in this browser, and a new account doesn't inherit the previous account's progress. Existing progress belongs to the first account that logs in.
- Friends, clans, ranked, parties and gifts require logging in.

## Good to know
- If the game tab goes to the background, the browser may slow it down so it looks frozen. It's best to keep the tab open while you play.
- Practice mode and private rooms don't earn rewards such as gold, XP, achievements or missions.
- During a private-room match, there is an Exit button at the top right. If the host leaves, the match ends for everyone, so a confirmation window appears first (build 598).
- The site help notes that this is a keyboard-and-mouse game and recommends a computer. On touch devices, touch controls turn on automatically.
- The intro at startup can't be skipped.
- On the intro, instead of the STICKSEUM wordmark, a picture representing that update appears as the background, and the update's gold English name and version appear at the top center. Right now it's IN SEARCH OF GOLD and v0.8. The background and name change with each update.
- As the intro starts, a 5-second intro tune plays, and a loud sound bursts when the title appears. It doesn't play if you turn off background music in Settings. The lobby music doesn't start until the intro is over.
- At the top center of the lobby, 🟢 N online is shown. That is the number of people who are logged in with a Frenchfries777 account and have the game open.

stickseum/controls-settings.b:
:: Move = A / D
:: Jump = W or Space
:: Dash / Teleport = Q / E
:: Ultimate / Skill = R / F
:: Emote wheel = V (up to 8)
:: Frame Limit = Unlimited / 60 / 30 FPS

Here's everything about keyboard/mouse and touch controls, plus what you can change in the Settings screen.

## Keyboard & mouse (defaults)
- A / D: Move left/right (the tutorial says you can use the arrow keys too)
- W or Space: Jump
- Mouse: Aim, Click: Attack
- Q: Dash, E: Teleport, R: Ultimate, F: Skill
- Enter: Chat, V: Emote wheel, Tab: Scoreboard (shown while held)
- S or Down arrow: Used to fly down as Dracula in bat form, and to move into the darkness below as Kurus while in darkness.
- The bat (Baseball Player) doesn't hit with just a click. You have to swing: hold the click, pull the mouse down, then bring it back up.
- Teleport (E) moves you to where your mouse is pointing. It charges for 1 second after you use it, then moves you.

## How ability keys work
Skill, Ultimate, Dash and Teleport keys behave according to the **Ability Activation** setting. The default is the first option.
- **Hold and release to use**: An aim indicator appears while you hold the key, and the ability fires when you release. Click while holding to use it at that spot.
- **Press to use instantly**: The ability fires the moment you press the key.
- **Press once to aim → press again to use**: The first press aims, the second press fires.
- In any mode, Esc or right-click cancels aiming. Clicking while an ability key is held doesn't count as an attack.
- Hold Shift and press the Skill or Ultimate key to use it right away on the nearest enemy. A mint-colored circle briefly appears over that enemy.

## Rebinding keys
- In Settings under **Key Bindings**, you can change Move Left, Move Right, Jump, Dash, Teleport, Ultimate, Skill, Open Chat and Emote — 9 actions in total.
- Click the slot you want to change, then press the new key. Press Esc to cancel.
- Each key does only one thing. If you pick a key that's already in use, the action that had it gets your old key instead.
- Esc, Tab, Space, the arrow keys and S can't be used as the chat key.
- **Reset to Defaults** puts everything back. On-screen help text updates to match your new keys too.

## Quality-of-life settings
- **Sound Effects**: On or Off. Buttons in the game make a shorter, softer "tok" sound, which is turned off together with the sound effects.
- **Background music**: on or off, with a volume control. The lobby track plays in the lobby and the battle track plays during a match. Boss Raid plays only its own boss-battle track instead, and the other modes keep the normal battle track.
- **Screen Shake**: On or Off
- **Graphics Effects (skin effects, etc.)**: Auto, High, Medium, Low. Auto adjusts based on game speed. If the game stutters, try lowering it.
- **Control Type (Mobile / Computer)**: Auto-detect, Mobile (touch), Computer (keyboard & mouse)
- **Frame Limit**: Unlimited, 60 FPS, 30 FPS
- The graphics effects and frame limit are linked to the shared optimization settings in the hub Settings (build 367). Auto exists only in this game, so while it is on, the hub's effect quality value is left unchanged.
- **Show FPS**: On or Off
- **Ability Activation**: The three options described above
- **Show Damage Numbers**: On or Off
- **Battery saver**: on or off, on by default. When on, menus are drawn at 30 FPS and matches are capped at 60 FPS to save battery.
- **Colorblind mode**: on or off. When on, team colors and health bar colors change, and teams are told apart by shape as well as color.
- Settings are saved in this browser.
- **Back to site**: Press this button on the settings screen to go to the games hub.

## iPad & phones (touch)
- Touch controls turn on automatically on touch devices. Devices with a mouse or trackpad connected are treated as computers. If your iPad has a keyboard/trackpad attached, try switching to Mobile manually in Settings.
- Move with the left joystick. Push it up to jump, push it down for a down input.
- Pressing the red joystick on the right attacks, and you aim in the direction you drag. If an enemy is near the aim direction, the aim snaps to it, and a short tap on the aim side attacks the nearest enemy.
- Buttons: skill, ultimate, jump and 💨 (dash and teleport). Tap 💨 to dash and hold it to teleport; the teleport goes in the aim direction. The emote button (😀) is at the top right.
- The Ultimate and Skill buttons auto-aim at the nearest enemy.
- The joystick appears where you put your thumb, and the buttons are small and transparent so they block less of the screen.
- On a phone held sideways (a touch device with a short screen), the menu, character selection and bottom bar get smaller. On the character selection and ban screens the joysticks and buttons are hidden (build 355). Tablets and computers keep their size.
- The ⛶ button in the top right toggles fullscreen.
- On the settings screen, **Touch Button Size** is chosen from Small, Normal, Large and Extra Large (build 368).
- **Touch Button Height** is chosen from Default, A little up and Far up, and it moves the button area upward (build 368).

## Gamepad
- You can play with a gamepad connected by Bluetooth or other means.
- The left stick moves, A jumps, B dashes, X uses the Skill, Y uses the Ultimate and LB teleports. Aim with the right stick and attack with RT.
- The D-pad also moves you, and RB also attacks.
- While you are not touching the gamepad, keyboard and touch controls keep working as usual. The same guide appears in the settings screen.
- If you hold the device upright, you'll be asked to rotate to landscape. Pressing the **Fullscreen + lock landscape** button in the notice switches to fullscreen and locks the screen to landscape (supported browsers only, build 368).

## Emotes & chat
- Press V to open the emote wheel. The 8 default emotes are 👍 😂 😡 😭 🔥 👋 ❓ 💀. You can add or remove emotes bought in the shop, and the wheel holds up to 8.
- Press Enter to open chat and Enter again to send. Esc closes it.
- After using an emote, you can use another one after 1.2 seconds.

## When you die
- While waiting to respawn, use the arrow keys or your Move Left/Right keys to cycle through living players' views.
- If you're eliminated in Battle Royale, Battle Royale Duo or Tournament, the defeat screen appears right away. Choose **Leave** to exit the room or **Spectate** to keep watching.

stickseum/modes.b:
:: Modes = 13
:: Daily modes = 10
:: Deathmatch = 3 min, most kills wins
:: Domination = Hold the point, first to 100
:: Ranked = 1v1 Duel (best of 3)

Stickseum has 13 modes, 10 daily modes that rotate each day, and Ranked. The online mode list shows Ranked, the daily mode, the 6 modes from Deathmatch to Domination, the 4 from Bomb Pass to Capture the Flag, and then the co-op modes (Boss Raid and Tournament). Since v360 Hide and Seek is no longer in this list and can only be picked in a private room. The Zombie Game was removed in build 372. The detailed rules of the special-rule modes and the daily modes are on the Special Modes & Daily Modes page.

## Quick overview
- Deathmatch: Most kills in 3 minutes wins.
- Battle Royale: No respawns, last one standing.
- Battle Royale Duo: Teams of 2, at least 8 players.
- Team Battle: Two teams; wipe out the other team to win.
- Duel: 1v1, best 2 out of 3.
- Domination: Hold the point and reach 100 first.

## Core battle modes
- **Deathmatch**: The basic mode, a free-for-all with respawns at the map's default player count (4 on 4-player maps, 6 on 6-player maps, 8 on 8-player maps). Matches last 3 minutes, and whoever has the most kills when time runs out wins. If kills are tied, it ends as a shared win (draw).
- **Battle Royale**: The map's default player count, no respawns. Fight until only 1 is left. When you're eliminated, you can leave or spectate from the defeat screen.
- **Battle Royale Duo**: Teams of 2 fight until one team is left. At least 8 players, and only on 8+ player maps. A team is out only when both members are down. In a party, only 2-person parties can join.
- **Team Battle**: The map's default player count plus 2, split into two teams (6 on 4-player maps, 8 on 6-player maps, 10 on 8-player maps). Wipe out the other team to win.
- **Duel**: A one-on-one, best 2 out of 3 rounds. You pick a new character every round. Characters you've already used can't be picked again, so you'll need to handle several characters to win. Before each round starts, each player bans one character for the opponent.
- **Domination**: Two teams fight over the point in the middle of the map (the floating platform closest to the map's center). Holding the point earns 1 point per second, and the first team to 100 points wins. You respawn 5 seconds after dying. Player count is 6–12 depending on the map (6 on 4-player maps, 8 on 6-player maps, 10 on 8-player maps, 12 on large maps). Minimum 6 players. Bots with an assigned personality (such as the sniper type) also head for the point and fight there.

## Battle Royale danger zone and supply crates
- These apply to Battle Royale, Battle Royale Duo and the daily mode Infinite Dash Battle Royale.
- **Danger zone**: 30 seconds after the start it closes in from both ends, and standing in the red area deals damage. It reaches its minimum width at about 140 seconds.
- **Supply crates**: They drop onto platforms, and opening one gives one of: health recovery, ultimate charge or skill charge. They drop more often on high platforms.
- **Bots**: Bots go to the supply crates and pick them up. When hurt, they look for a health crate first.
- A bot that ends up outside the danger zone steps onto platforms and returns inside.
- **Starting positions**: Widened to every platform on the map. Duo teams start scattered across high and low places.

## Minimum players and maps by mode
- Battle Royale Duo needs at least 8 players, so it only opens on 8+ player maps.
- Domination needs at least 6 players and opens on 4+ player maps.
- The Zombie Game was removed in build 372 and no longer opens.
- Survival, Boss Raid and Tournament only open on 8+ player maps.
- Hide and Seek is locked to a single 32-player map (Mega Arena). It is not in the online mode list and can only be picked in a private room (v360).
- Capture the Flag and Gold Grab are played on the same 4 dedicated large maps. The Parkour mode was removed in v352.
- Capture the Flag, Gold Grab and Mega Arena maps only show up in those modes or in private rooms. More on maps in the Map Guide page.

## Ranked
- A 1v1 Duel (best 2 out of 3) only between logged-in players. No bots.
- Details on points and tiers are on the Ranked & Seasons page.

## Character ban stage
- In duels (ranked included) and team battles, a ban stage comes before you pick your character. In it you choose one character that the other side cannot pick.
- It lasts 20 seconds. In a duel each player bans one character, and in a team battle every teammate picks one character to ban. In team battles, two players can't ban the same character.
- Even after the 20 seconds are up, character select only begins once both sides have chosen their bans. If either side hasn't chosen yet, it waits. After the ban stage you pick your character.
- A banned character cannot be picked by the other side. In team battles, every ban chosen by the teammates applies to the whole other team and lasts for that match. In a duel, each player bans one character for the opponent not only in the first round but before every round. The ban applies only to character selection in that round, and characters used in earlier rounds still can't be picked again.
- During the ban, the teammate slots show the character your team banned, and you can also see whether the other side has chosen its ban. The characters the other side is banning are also shown in real time. In team battles, every ban is also shown on the character select screen.
- In the ban phase, each bot bans a character on its own at a random moment within 1 to 7 seconds after the phase starts. Even after the humans have decided, the game waits until all the bots have decided.
- There is no ban stage in random weapon mode (private rooms).

## Match intro
- When a match starts, character cards appear. You and your allies get a blue background, and enemies get a red one. The card borders are deep blue for allies and deep red for enemies.
- In a duel, your character is on the left and your opponent on the right. Team battle, Conquest and Capture the Flag split into team versus team, with your team on the left and the other team on the right.
- In free-for-all modes like Battle Royale, your character is shown large on the left and the others small on the right.
- The confirmation window that used to appear after character selection is gone.

## Practice Mode
- Pick a map, a character and opponents (None, Dummy, Moving Dummy, Bot) and practice solo. You can have up to 8 opponents.
- Cooldowns are short (Ultimate 3 seconds, Skill 2 seconds, Teleport 2 seconds), and you respawn 2 seconds after dying.
- The damage you deal is displayed: DPS over the last 5 seconds, best DPS and total damage, with a reset button for the record.
- Capture the Flag and Gold Grab maps can't be chosen as practice maps.
- No XP, gold, achievements or mastery are earned.

## Private rooms
- The host chooses the mode, map and weapon rules. Every mode and the daily mode can be chosen, and so can One Shot, which is no longer a daily mode.
- Weapon rules are **Normal Mode** (pick from every character) and **Random Weapon Mode** (each player is offered 3 random characters to choose from).
- Turn on **Auto Team Balance** to even out team sizes. Turn on **Map Vote** to let players vote on the map before the match.
- Private rooms give no rewards like XP, gold, soul stones, missions or achievements.
- If the host leaves or disconnects mid-match, the match keeps going and someone else becomes host.

## After the match
- When a match ends, the victory screen comes first, then a large MVP vote window with a countdown appears for the people on the winning team. An MVP is chosen only in team modes, and free-for-all modes have none. Both the voters and the candidates are members of the winning team, and you can't vote for yourself. The candidates appear as tall cards lined up side by side in one row. The top of each card shows that person's character (color, skin, weapon) in a large picture, and below it are the nickname, the character, and the kills, assists, deaths and damage dealt in that match. Your own card is shown too, with your character and match stats, but it is grayed out and you can't vote for yourself. The losing team gets no vote window and its leave button is not blocked. If the winning team has only bots and no people, the vote is skipped. When voting ends, the winner gets a "You are the MVP!" notice and 50 XP, then everyone goes back to the main screen. In a match with only one person (such as playing with bots), the bots also vote, and in a boss raid the winning allies (people and bots) are the candidates. The MVP is decided by vote only.
- The MVP vote screen also shows your team's total kills and deaths (build 454).
- After a match, kill moments are automatically saved as highlights. You can rewatch them on the records screen.

stickseum/minigames.b:
:: Special-rule modes = 7
:: Daily modes = 10 (one per day)
:: Capture the Flag = First to 3 points, 8 min limit
:: Hide and Seek = 1 min 30 s
:: Boss Raid = 4 players · 3-min time limit
:: Tournament = 16 players (1v1)

These are the modes with special rules, different from the core battles. Here are the 7 special-rule modes, the 10 daily modes (one of which opens each day), and One Shot, which can only be picked in private rooms.

## Zombie Game (removed)
- The mode was dropped from the mode list in build 372, and it no longer counts for the Mode Collector achievement or the weekly mission pool. The zombie disaster in Survival is still there.

## Bomb Pass
- At least 4 players. Everyone starts right away as a bare-handed stickman with no weapon, Ultimate or Teleport — only Dash.
- One player starts holding the bomb, and it explodes after 20 seconds. Click a nearby player to pass the bomb (they have to be close to where you're aiming).
- When it explodes, whoever is holding it is out. If more than half of the starting players are still alive, the next round starts after 3 seconds.
- If the bomb explodes once survivors are down to half or fewer, the remaining survivors win.
- A ticking sound plays while the bomb is going around, and there is also a sound when the bomb is passed.
- The weapon label next to HP is hidden, and bots keep running away from whoever holds the bomb.

## Hide and Seek
- At least 5 players, always on the 32-player large map (Mega Arena). Everyone has 1 HP and no Dash, Ultimate, Teleport or weapon choice. It was taken out of the online mode list, so it can only be played in a private room (v360).
- One player is the seeker, and everyone else turns into a stationary platform to hide. The seeker's screen is covered for 10 seconds, and during that time hiders can move freely to find a spot.
- When the countdown ends, the seeker gets a pistol. A platform hit by the first shot turns back into a stickman (and can move again), and a second hit eliminates them.
- If the seeker finds everyone within 1 minute 30 seconds, the seeker wins; if even one hider is left, the survivors win.
- Bots can't play this mode, so it waits until enough real players join.
- The weapon label next to HP is not shown.

## Gold Grab
- Played on the same 4 dedicated large maps as Capture the Flag. Two teams (Blue and Red) compete for 3 minutes. At least 4 players, and bots can be added in private rooms.
- Take gold from the pile in the middle of the map and load it onto your team cart for 10 points per lump. Every 0.8 seconds you stand near the pile you get 1 lump, and the pile never runs out (build 383). Touching the cart loads it automatically.
- You can carry up to 3 lumps at a time and get a little slower with each. If a carrier is knocked out, the gold drops on the spot for anyone to pick up.
- The pile no longer shows how much is left (build 390). Each lump you load onto the cart gives 2 XP.
- The team with more points after 3 minutes wins. A tie is a draw. You respawn at your base 5 seconds after dying.

## Survival
- Only opens on 8+ player maps. At least 6 players, with no weapon choice, Teleport or characters (Dash is available).
- You have 1 HP, so getting hit by a disaster even once means you're out.
- After a 9-second wait, one random disaster hits for 12 seconds: lightning, tsunami, volcano, acid rain, flood, meteors, bombs or zombies. Survive it and it fades, then another 9-second wait begins.
- As rounds go on, disasters come more often, cover more area and move faster. Survive 5 disasters to win.
- When you die, an elimination screen appears where you can leave right away or choose to spectate.
- The weapon label next to HP is not shown.

## Capture the Flag
- Played on 4 dedicated large maps (Canyon Fortress, Volcano Basin, Sky Fortress, Desert Ruins). Maps hold up to 12 players.
- Two teams (Blue and Red) score 1 point by grabbing the flag from the enemy base and bringing it back to their own base. The point counts even when your own flag is held by the enemy or lying outside your base (build 383).
- The flag carrier is not slowed down any more (the slowdown was removed in build 382). They still can't Teleport.
- If the flag carrier dies, the flag drops where they fell. A dropped flag no longer returns by itself: it goes back to its base only when someone from its own team touches it (build 383). The other team can pick it up again.
- The first team to 3 points, or the team with more points after 8 minutes, wins. If it's tied when 8 minutes are up, the match ends in a draw.
- You respawn at your base 5 seconds after dying. At least 4 players, and bots can be added in private rooms.
- Bots: no bot just stands at its base. When opponents head toward our flag or our teammates, bots closest to the flag stand up to them, one bot per opponent. Opponents met on the way (within 420 pixels) are fought on the spot instead of being passed.
- Capturing a flag gives 25 player XP and 25 character XP.

## Boss Raid
- Only opens on 8+ player maps. Exactly 4 players team up in a co-op mode to take down one giant boss.
- The time limit is 3 minutes. Defeat the boss in time to succeed; if time runs out or everyone is wiped out, you fail.
- Boss Raid plays only its own boss-battle music. The other modes keep the normal battle music.
- The boss is randomly one of Flame Giant, Ice Golem or Thunder Demon King. Its HP is 1,700 plus 1,000 per player. Each boss has its own weapon: the Flame Giant uses a flamethrower, the Ice Golem a piercing ice spear, and the Thunder Demon King bouncing electric orbs.
- The boss slams the ground regularly. When a red circle flashes, jump! Each hit does 25 damage.
- When the boss's HP drops below 70%, 50% and 30%, it moves to the next phase. Phase 1 brings 2 minions, phase 2 brings 2 minions plus floor beams, and in phase 3 the boss goes into a rage and attacks faster alongside 3 minions.
- The minions appear as the Flame Swordsman, Ice Swordsman and Lightning Swordsman to match the boss, and they use the boss's color. They have 150 HP, and there can be up to 5 at a time.
- Team lives are shared: player count times 3, plus 3 (15 for 4 players). Anyone who goes down respawns after 6 seconds.
- A successful raid gives role bonuses: Damage Dealer (most damage dealt), Tank (most damage taken) and Cleanup (most minions killed) are worth 15 sC per role (build 375). If one player holds several roles, the bonuses add up.

## Tournament
- 16 players compete in 1v1 best-of-3 matches (first to 2 wins) through the Round of 16, quarterfinals, semifinals and final. Played on 8+ player maps.
- Matches in the same round run at the same time, and you only see your own. Each round lasts 75 seconds.
- You pick a new character every round. Unlike Duel, you can pick characters you've already used.
- Players who are done can spectate other matches. In the final, the arena gradually shrinks.
- Winning earns you titles: 1 win gets Tournament Champion, 5 wins gets Tournament Emperor, and 10 wins gets Tournament Legend.

## Daily modes (special modes)
- One of the 10 modes below opens as the daily mode each day. Today's mode is set by the date and doesn't change for the day.
- In private rooms, the host can pick any of the 10 freely from the mode list.
- **Protect the King**: Two teams, each with one King (crown overhead). The first team to take down the enemy King wins. Non-Kings respawn after 5 seconds. After 5 minutes, the team whose King has more HP left wins.
- A bot that is the King keeps as far from the enemies as it can and dashes away when they get close (build 372).
- **King of the Hill**: Free-for-all. Holding the point alone gives 1 point per second; if two or more are on it, scoring pauses. The point moves to a different platform every 20 seconds. First to 60 points, or the highest score after 6 minutes, wins. Respawn after 4 seconds.
- **Weapon Relay**: Everyone gets the same lineup of 10 characters in the same order. Each kill switches you to the next character, and getting a kill with the 10th character wins. After 6 minutes, whoever is furthest ahead wins. Respawn after 3 seconds.
- **Freeze Tag**: Two teams. When you die you freeze in place, and a teammate who touches you for 1.4 seconds frees you with 60% HP. Freeze the whole enemy team to win; after 4 minutes, the team with fewer frozen players wins.
- **Treasure Raid**: Gold coins keep appearing all over the map. When you die, you drop half your coins and anyone can pick them up. Whoever has the most coins after 4 minutes wins. Respawn after 4 seconds.
- **Weapon Roulette**: Every 12 seconds, everyone's character changes at random (cooldowns reset too). Most kills in 5 minutes wins. Respawn after 3 seconds.
- **Paint War**: Two teams. Stepping on a platform paints it your team's color. The more tiles you've painted, the faster your score goes up; first to 150 points, or the higher score after 4 minutes, wins. Respawn after 4 seconds.
- **Bounty Hunt**: Each kill is 1 point. The score leader (3+ points) gets a bounty (red marker). Taking down the bounty target is worth 4 points. First to 20 points, or the highest score after 5 minutes, wins. Respawn after 4 seconds.
- **Low-Gravity Brawl**: A brawl with weak gravity and strong knockback. You fly high and get launched far. Most kills in 4 minutes wins. Respawn after 3 seconds.
- **Infinite Dash Battle Royale**: Same rules as Battle Royale. The map's default player count joins, and you fight with no respawns until only 1 is left. The dash cooldown is 0 seconds, so you can chain dashes without stopping. Like in Battle Royale, the danger zone closes in and supply crates drop.
- Bots also keep dashing whenever they move, about once per second so they don't get too fast.

## One Shot (private rooms only)
- Since build 330 it is no longer a daily mode. You can only play it when the host picks it from the mode list in a private room.
- Everyone has 1 HP. One hit takes you down, and you respawn after 3 seconds. First to 100 kills wins, or the most kills after 4 minutes.

stickseum/maps.b:
:: Total maps = 22 (21 regular · 1 large)
:: Parkour maps = removed (along with the mode, in v352)
:: Capture the Flag and Gold Grab maps = 4 (12 players)
:: Large map = Mega Arena (32 players)
:: Map order = Shuffled in 10-minute blocks

There are 22 maps in total (21 regular and 1 large), plus 4 Capture the Flag and Gold Grab maps (the 4 Parkour-only maps are no longer used since the Parkour mode was removed in v352). The 4 tall 6-player maps were removed in build 353, Mirror Maze in build 372 and Collapsing Bridge in build 379. The player count next to each map name is the default for Deathmatch and Battle Royale. Team Battle adds 2 more players on top of that.

## How maps are chosen
- In online matchmaking, you don't pick the map. The map order is shuffled the same way in 10-minute blocks so people searching at the same time end up in the same room, and rooms are found in that order.
- In private rooms, the host picks the map. With Map Vote on, it's decided by vote before the match.
- In Practice Mode, you can pick any map except the Capture the Flag and Gold Grab maps.
- Which maps each mode can use is listed under minimum players on the Modes page.

## Map Editor
- You can make your own maps. Place platforms and spawn points to build a map, then save it.
- Saved maps can be shared with others using a map code.
- Maps you make can be used in Practice Mode and private rooms.

## 4-player maps (width 2200, height 900)
- Grassland, Volcano, Desert, Pyramid. They share the same layout — a flat floor with platforms stacked 5 levels high — and only differ in color and look.
- No gimmicks.

## 6-player maps
- Space, Palace, Cyber and Sky (width 1000, height 1400) were narrow, tall tower layouts, but they were removed in build 353 and no longer appear.
- Steampunk (width 2500, height 1000): Has 2 moving platforms that slide back and forth.
- Mirror Maze was removed in build 372 and no longer appears.

## 8-player maps
- Ocean, Programming, School, Playground (width 2600, height 1000): Wide maps with 3 levels of platforms.
- Sky Station (width 2600, height 1000): Has 1 platform in the middle that moves side to side.
- Colosseum (width 2400, height 900): The center rises in steps.
- Elevator Tower (width 1300, height 1500): A tall map with 1 moving platform.
- Ruined City (width 2400, height 1000): Broken pillars and walls stand around the map and can be used as cover.

## 8-player maps with gimmicks
- **Storm Pirate Ship** (2600 x 1000): The deck platforms stay fixed and do not move (build 452 stopped them swaying side to side). Every 16 seconds a wave sweeps across the floor, and if you're standing on the floor you get pushed up. A dark ripple shows up just before it hits, and the wave alternates direction.
- **Pipe Factory** (2400 x 1000): Conveyor platforms keep pushing anyone standing on them. 4 steam vents take turns blasting; a puff of white smoke appears briefly before each blast, and while it's blasting you get launched high into the air.
- **Underground Mine** (2600 x 1000): A minecart rolls back and forth on the floor rails. Getting hit deals 50 damage and big knockback. Every 22 seconds there's a blackout that darkens the screen, and you can only see inside the lamplight around you and your teammates.
- **Frozen Lake** (2400 x 1000): The floor is slippery, so you slide even when you try to stop. On a 16-second cycle, the middle of the floor cracks (at 9 seconds) and breaks (from 11 seconds), and freezing water shoots up. Touching the freezing water deals 25 damage and bounces you upward.
- **Dark Swamp** (2400 x 1000): There are stair-step platforms on both sides, 3 steps each, and 1 platform in the middle. A large swamp sits in the center; everyone inside it has their move speed reduced by 33% and their surrounding vision limited. Stepping-stone platforms are placed over the swamp.
- **Dungeon** (2400 x 1000): Two groups of iron-bar platforms take turns appearing and disappearing every 4 seconds. They flash red 1.2 seconds before vanishing as a warning.
- Collapsing Bridge was removed in build 379 and no longer appears.
- **Volcanic Land** (2400 x 1000): Two lava pools (300 wide each) sit in the floor. Every 12 seconds, a pool stays cool for the first 5 seconds, glows red for the next 2, and turns into lava for the last 5. Standing in a pool while it is lava deals 30 damage and bounces you upward.
- **Waterfall Cliffs** (2400 x 1000): There are cliff steps on both sides, and two waterfalls (120 wide each) pour down. If you are in the air inside a waterfall, the current lifts you upward. Shallow water in the middle of the floor (1000 wide) cuts your move speed by 20%. There are platforms behind the waterfalls where you can hide.

## Large map
- **Mega Arena** (3000 x 1200, 32 players): The Hide and Seek map. It can also be picked in private rooms. It doesn't appear in regular online matchmaking.

## Parkour-only maps (removed)
- Because the Parkour mode was removed in v352, the 4 maps Clear Morning, Above the Clouds, Lava Spire and Starlit Stairs no longer appear.
- They used to be maps built with every jump checked to be reachable, with the golden platform at the top as the goal.

## Capture the Flag and Gold Grab maps (12 players)
- Canyon Fortress (4400 x 1500), Volcano Basin (4800 x 1600), Sky Fortress (4000 x 1900), Desert Ruins (5200 x 1400).
- Long, horizontally symmetric maps with a base at each end.
- Gold Grab is also played on these 4 maps. There is a pile of gold lumps in the middle and a mine cart at each base.

## Map tips
- On Waterfall Cliffs, jumping inside a waterfall lets the current carry you up, so you can quickly reach the high platforms. The shallow water in the middle slows you down, so it's better to fight out of the water.
- On narrow, tall maps (Lift Tower), explosive weapons and high-knockback weapons have the edge. Falling off costs you a lot.
- On wide maps, long-range characters can keep their distance more easily.
- On gimmick maps, try turning the gimmicks against your enemies. Minecarts, freezing water and steam vents pair well with weapons that push opponents.
- On Volcanic Land, a pool glowing red is about to turn into lava. Weapons that push opponents are good for sending them into the lava.

stickseum/ranked.b:
:: Format = 1v1 Duel (best of 3)
:: Starting points = 1000
:: Rating system = Elo (max 32 per match)
:: Season = 1st of month (Korean time)
:: Top tier = Grandmaster (1550)
:: Leaderboard = Top 50

Ranked is a mode where logged-in players face off 1v1 for rating points. A new season starts every month.

## Rules
- It's a 1v1 Duel, best 2 out of 3. You pick a new character every round, and you can't pick a character you used in an earlier round.
- You only meet other logged-in players. Bots never join.
- Ranked runs in separate rooms, so you only meet people who are also looking for Ranked.
- The Ranked screen shows how many logged-in people are waiting for a ranked match right now (build 394), and the start-matching button also shows how many are waiting.
- If both players aren't logged in, the match is played as a practice match and points don't change.
- You can't play Ranked while in a party.
- A 20-second ban stage comes when the match starts and before every round. Character select only begins once both sides have chosen their bans. Each player bans one character the opponent cannot pick, and the ban applies only to character selection in that round.

## Points
- Everyone starts at 1000 points at the start of a season.
- Points change using the Elo system. You go up when you win and down when you lose, and the higher your opponent's points compared to yours, the more you gain for winning. The most you can gain in one match is 32 points, and a win always gives at least 1 point.
- The loser's points never drop below 0.
- Between the same two players, only 3 matches within 24 hours change points. Play more than that and the results show, but points stay the same.
- Points only change on the server. The player who opened the match (the host) reports the result.

## Point examples
- Beat someone with a similar score and you gain about 16 points.
- Beat someone 200 points above you and you gain about 24 points.
- Beat someone 200 points below you and you gain about 8 points.
- The loser drops by as much as the winner gains. So high-rated players lose a lot when they lose to lower-rated opponents.

## Tiers
- Bronze: from 0 points
- Silver: from 950 points
- Gold: from 1050 points
- Platinum: from 1150 points
- Diamond: from 1250 points
- Master: from 1400 points
- Grandmaster: from 1550 points

## Titles
- The first time you reach Gold, Diamond or Master, you get a permanent title. The titles are Ranked Gold, Ranked Diamond and Ranked Master. They don't go away when the season ends.
- Pick one from the Title button on your profile to equip it, and it shows above your character's head.

## Seasons and leaderboards
- Seasons last one month and run on Korean time. On the 1st of every month, everyone resets to 1000 points.
- On the Ranked screen, you can see the top 50 players of the current season. Your own points, tier, rank, wins and losses, and win rate are shown too.
- The Leaderboard page on the site also shows this month's Ranked season standings and the clan rankings.

## Don't mix these up
- Ranked tiers (Bronze to Grandmaster, based on points) and character ranks (Novice to Grandmaster, based on that character's mastery points) are different things. The names are similar, but they go up separately.
- The Season Pass season is one month based on your device's calendar. It runs separately from the Ranked season.
- Ranked isn't a private room, so XP, gold, mastery and mission progress all build up as usual.

## Ranked tips
- Since you pick a new character each round and can't reuse one, it pays to be comfortable with two or three characters.
- You can see what your opponent picked and choose a counter for the next round. You have 15 seconds to pick a character.
- In the ban stage, it helps to ban a character the opponent is good with. Bans are made fresh every round, so prepare two or three characters in case the one you wanted gets banned.
- Points don't change after 3 matches with the same opponent in 24 hours, so even if you're winning, it's not efficient to keep playing the same person.

stickseum/characters.b:
:: Characters = 28
:: HP = 300
:: Skill cooldown = 5 s
:: Ultimate cooldown = 20 s
:: Dash cooldown = 1.5 s (Assassin 0.5 s)
:: Teleport cooldown = 10 s

There are 28 characters. Each has a different weapon, Skill (F) and Ultimate (R). Every character shares the same cooldowns: 5 seconds for Skill and 20 seconds for Ultimate. Numbers come from the game's v238 code and the character codex. Detailed write-ups for every character are collected on the Characters page.

## What every character has in common
- 300 HP. That's in the standard modes.
- Each character has a basic attack (click), one Skill (F, 5-second cooldown) and one Ultimate (R, 20-second cooldown).
- Dash (Q) and Teleport (E) are the same for everyone. Dash can be used every 1.5 seconds by default, Teleport every 10 seconds. Only Assassin has a 0.5-second Dash.
- Teleport charges for 1.2 seconds after you use it, then moves you (up from 1 second in build 382). Flag and gold carriers can't Teleport.
- While stunned, you can't move, attack, Dash, Teleport, or use your Skill or Ultimate. Samurai can't be stunned during their Ultimate.

## New to the game? Try James (pistol)
- Appearance: Wears black sunglasses and a dark red necktie.
- Basic attack: A reliable pistol with 17 damage and 0.85-second fire rate.
- Skill **Rapid Fire**: Doubles fire rate for 1.8 seconds.
- Ultimate **Power Shot**: Your next shot becomes a big, fast bullet that deals 66 damage.
- Tip: Keep the Ultimate ready and fire when you know you'll land it. Hold R and click to fire that shot right away.

## Pick by type
- In the codex, you can filter characters by type, like **Gun, Melee, Throwing, Explosive, Shotgun, Card**. Slaughterer and Cleaner are special characters that don't belong to any type.
- On the character select screen in a match, there is a search box so you can find characters by name.
- Guns: James, Agent, Robin Hood, Ninja, Soldier, Gambler, Wizard, Dimension Traveler, Puppeteer (9)
- Melee: Pizarro, Jadai, Horemheb, Knight, Baseball Player, Boxer, Assassin, Dracula, Pirate, Samurai (10)
- Throwing: Hunter, Kurus (2)
- Explosive: Bomber, Heavy Gunner (2)
- Shotgun: Sheriff, Card: Magician, Special: Slaughterer, Cleaner

## Which character suits you?
- Easy to aim: Weapons that fly fast in a straight line, like the pistol (James), assault rifle (Soldier) and shuriken (Ninja).
- If you like fighting at range: Robin Hood (arcing shots), Gambler (long range), the vacuum (480 range), Wizard (piercing).
- If you like getting up close: Short-cooldown melee characters like Boxer, Assassin and Pirate are easy to pick up.
- If you love big single hits: Heavy Gunner (68), Bomber (52), Baseball Player (43).
- If you want to grow stronger as you fight: Each time Pizarro uses his Ultimate, his attack goes up and his cooldowns get shorter (stacks up to 3 times, reaching stage 4).
- If you like wearing opponents down with poison: Kan stacks poison darts to deal damage every second (up to 4 stacks).
- If you want to help the team: the Wizard's magic circle gives allies +30% attack and 12 healing per second for 10 seconds. It is especially reassuring in team modes.
- The busiest characters to play are Kurus, Dimension Traveler and Gambler. Give them a shot once you know the rules.

## Character ranks and exclusive skins
- Each character ranks up by its mastery points (build 410). With that character you earn 3 points per kill, 1 per assist, 4 for a win and 1 for finishing a match. Ranks start at: Novice 0, Bronze 88, Silver 263, Gold 525, Platinum 875, Diamond 1,750, Obsidian 3,063, Master 4,813, Grandmaster 7,000 points. From Bronze to Master there are II and III steps between ranks (build 411, exact points on the Progression page). Ranks already earned from kills are kept.
- Reaching Diamond (1,750 points) automatically unlocks that character's first tier-exclusive skin, and reaching Grandmaster (7,000 points) unlocks the second.
- Mastery level goes up separately. Details are on the Progression page.

## Codex and balance
- The character codex on the site lists each character's strong and weak matchups. These are measured from bot-vs-bot matches, so real games can differ.
- The Balance page on the site shows each character's win rate and the numbers changed in each patch. The current table was measured at build 407: every one of the 378 pairs of the 28 characters, 1 game per map on each of the 22 maps, 8,316 games in total. Characters changed in a patch, such as the Wizard, are measured again.

stickseum/shop-gold-achievements.b:
:: Kill reward = 5 sC + 1 soul stone
:: Assist reward = 3 sC
:: Tutorial reward = 100 sC (new accounts)
:: Random box = 10 soul stones
:: Daily mission = 15 sC
:: Weekly mission = 50 sC + 5 soul stones
:: Currency name = sC (formerly gold)

Collect sC and soul stones (💜) to buy cosmetics, and earn rewards from missions, the Season Pass and achievements. The currency was renamed from gold to sC in build 382. Practice Mode and private rooms don't give any rewards.

## How to earn sC
- 1 kill: 5 sC and 1 soul stone. Killing a teammate gives nothing. There is no limit on how many you can collect in one match (build 383).
- 1 assist: 3 sC (no soul stone). You get an assist if you damaged an opponent within 10 seconds before they died. This one has no per-match limit either.
- Finishing the tutorial: 100 sC (new accounts only).
- You get sC every time a character's mastery level goes up: 10 sC for Lv.1-5, 20 sC for Lv.6-10, 30 sC for Lv.11-15 and 45 sC from Lv.16 on (build 375).
- You also get sC from daily missions, weekly missions, the Season Pass, daily rewards, random boxes and achievements.
- A successful Boss Raid gives role bonuses (15 sC per role).
- Exchanging Hub Coin also gets you sC. See the Hub Coin Exchange page.
- Mastery XP is 6 per kill, 3 per assist, 3 for playing a match and 6 for a win (about 40% less since build 383). It doesn't build up in weaponless modes (Bomb Pass, Hide and Seek, Survival).

## How to earn soul stones
- You get 1 for every kill.
- They also come from finishing weekly missions (5 each), Season Pass tier rewards and random boxes.
- Soul stones are only used to buy random boxes.

## Cosmetics shop
- Tabs: Skins, Tier Exclusive, Name Colors, Character Colors, Kill Effects, Profile Backgrounds, Profile Borders, Emotes, Victory Poses, Boxes
- Prices and details for each type are on the Cosmetics Shop Guide page.
- You can also gift cosmetics to friends. Logged-in friends can send each other cosmetics that are buyable with sC, and if your friend already owns it, they get its price in sC instead. You can include a short message (up to 40 characters).

## Random boxes
- Cost 10 soul stones. Open them in the Boxes tab of the shop.
- Possible drops: 30, 40 or 50 sC, 40 random character XP, 80 player XP, 25, 50 or 100 Pick XP, 5, 10 or 15 soul stones, or 1 skin worth 400 sC or less
- The chance of a skin is about 8.9% (Pick XP together is about 10.7%). You won't get skins you already own, and if there are no skins left to get, it turns into 50 sC.
- Skins from boxes are basic skins priced at 400 sC or less. New skins and tier-exclusive skins don't drop.

## Daily rewards
- Once a day you get one gift: 50 sC (about 25%), 30 random character XP (about 21%), 60 player XP (about 21%), 1 random box (about 17%) or 25, 50 or 100 Pick XP (about 16% together).
- The date follows your device's date. If you set your device clock back, you can't claim it.

## Missions and Season Pass
- Details are on the Growth page. A daily mission gives 15 sC and a weekly mission gives 50 sC and 5 soul stones.

## Achievements
Completing an achievement gives you sC once. There are 54 achievements in total. The in-game achievement list only shows names and keeps the conditions secret. Here are the conditions and rewards. In practice mode and private rooms, achievements are never unlocked under any circumstances.
- First Blood (1 kill): 20 sC
- A Slaughterer Is Born (10 total kills): 30 sC
- Seasoned Warrior (50 total kills): 60 sC
- Sharpshooter (100 total kills): 100 sC
- First Victory: 30 sC
- Winning Streak (10 total wins): 80 sC
- Champion (30 total wins): 150 sC
- Destroyer (1,000 total damage): 40 sC
- Catastrophe (10,000 total damage): 120 sC
- Reliable Backup (20 total assists): 40 sC
- Regular Customer (100 total matches played): 100 sC
- All-Rounder (play all 6 modes from Deathmatch to Domination): 60 sC
- Mode Collector (play all 7 modes from Bomb Pass to Tournament): 60 sC
- True Pro Gamer (play 100 matches in each of those 13 modes, plus 100 daily-mode matches): 500 sC
- Master Duelist (100 Duel matches): 150 sC
- Teamwork Gone Wild (100 Team Battle matches): 150 sC
- Serial Killer (100 Deathmatch matches): 150 sC
- Every Man for Himself (100 Battle Royale matches): 150 sC
- Fun Together (100 Battle Royale Duo matches): 150 sC
- Expansionist (100 Domination matches): 150 sC
- Professional Flag Thief (100 Capture the Flag matches): 150 sC
- Blinded by Gold (100 Gold Grab matches): 150 sC
- True Champion (50 Tournament matches): 200 sC
- Growing Warrior (reach level 10): 50 sC
- Veteran (reach level 25): 150 sC
- Frenchfries777 Explorer (play all three games: Stickseum, Crown Envoy and Beaconfall): 300 sC

## Character achievements
Every character except Kan has one. Use that character's Skill or Ultimate a set number of times in a single match to get 150–250 sC. Skills have a 5-second cooldown and Ultimates 20 seconds, so Ultimate achievements need long matches.
- 250 sC: Assassin Master of Stealth (Ultimate 10 times), Jadai Lightning Strikes the Same Place 9 More Times (Ultimate 10 times), Magician Escape Artist (Ultimate 10 times), Dracula I Am the Bat (Ultimate 5 times)
- 250 sC: Puppeteer Puppet in My Hand (Ultimate 10 times)
- 200 sC: Knight Motion Sickness (Skill 20 times), Baseball Player Walk-Off Home Run (Ultimate 6 times), Hunter Boomerang Effect (Ultimate 6 times), Soldier Requesting Carpet Bombing (Ultimate 6 times), Bomber Blast Jump Addict (Skill 20 times), Heavy Gunner Missiles Are My Friends (Ultimate 6 times), Gambler Heads I Win (Skill 20 times), Wizard Magic Circle Collector (Ultimate 6 times), Cleaner Never Loses Suction (Skill 20 times), Pirate Gunner of the Seas (Ultimate 6 times), Kurus Shadow in the Swamp (Ultimate 6 times)
- 150 sC: Horemheb The King's Pitchfork Never Returns (Skill 15 times), Pizarro In the Name of God (Skill 15 times), Robin Hood Michael Jackson (Skill 10 times), James Hands Too Fast to See (Skill 15 times), Agent Agent in the Fog (Skill 15 times), Ninja A Ninja Leaves Afterimages (Skill 15 times), Sheriff The Sheriff's Knock (Skill 15 times), Boxer Sending You to the Sky (Skill 15 times), Slaughterer Playing with fire is dangerous (Skill 15 times), Dimension Traveler Ctrl + Z (Skill 12 times), Samurai Single Flash (Skill 15 times)
- 300 sC: Knight One Strike, Three Down (defeat 3 enemies with a single Ultimate)
- Each achievement is only rewarded once. There are 28 character achievements in total including One Strike, Three Down, and they are listed together in the in-game character achievement group (build 385). Kan does not have one yet.

stickseum/cosmetics.b:
:: Basic skins = 48 (300–1,200 sC)
:: New Skin = 1 per character, 2,000 sC (James 1,500 sC)
:: Tier Exclusive skins = 52 (not for sale)
:: Rainbow Nametag = 6,000 sC
:: Free character colors = 12
:: Boxes paid with = Soul stones

Cosmetics don't affect gameplay at all; they only change how you look. Everything in the shop costs sC (formerly called gold), except the Boxes tab, which uses soul stones. The shop tabs are Skins, Tier Exclusive, Name Colors, Character Colors, Kill Effects, Profile Backgrounds, Profile Borders, Emotes, Victory Poses and Boxes.
The shop's tab buttons are always laid out in 2 rows of 5 (they used to change between 4 and 5 per row depending on the tab, fixed in v341).

## Skins
- Skins are bought per character. All 26 characters other than Pizarro and Kan have basic skins, 48 in total. Kan has no skins yet, only his own profile background and frame. Pizarro has the Golden Morion Helmet for 400 sC, the Black Steel Morion Helmet for 300 sC and the New skin Gold Plunderer's Helmet for 2,000 sC, plus the tier-exclusive City of Gold Conqueror's Helmet (Diamond) and El Dorado Emperor's Crown Helmet (Grandmaster). Prices range from 300 sC to 1,200 sC.
- Every character has one top-priced 4,000 sC skin (build 373). They sit at the very bottom of the Skins tab, 28 in all, and Kan’s only skin is this one (Jade Serpent God Feather Crown). They never come out of random boxes.
- Concept skins (builds 405-407) change more than the color: the attacks and gear are drawn completely differently. Among the 4,000 sC skins there are Azure Dragon Wizard (bullets are azure dragons holding a pearl, two dragons over the Ultimate magic circle), Golden Knight (a golden sword and golden swings, a golden heavenly sword for the Ultimate), Dream Kurus (a dream-colored hood, potions and darkness) and Uno Magician (throws Uno cards). Among the New skins there are the Baseball Player's French Fry Player (2,000 sC, a server outfit that hits with fries instead of a bat), Robin Hood's Cupid (2,000 sC, hearts trail the arrows and the eyes are heart-shaped) and James's Banana James (1,500 sC, shoots while holding a banana and banana pulp flies out).
- The Slaughterer's 4,000 sC skin is Bad Breath Slaughterer (build 445). It has no weapon, smell particles drift around the body, the attack comes out of the mouth, and the shield and skill are smell-colored.
- You can search for skins in the shop's Skins tab (build 447).
- Most characters have 2 basic skins (a pricey one and a cheap one). Jadai, Horemheb, Slaughterer, Cleaner and Dimension Traveler have 1 basic skin each, priced at 300–400 sC. Kurus has 3 (300, 400 and 1000 sC).
- The Puppeteer has the Teal Jester Hat (400 sC) and the Purple Jester Hat (300 sC).
- Each character also has 1 **New Skin** for 2,000 sC. You'll find them at the very bottom of the Skins tab. Only James's New skin costs 1,500 sC (build 407).
- Basic skin price examples: James 800 sC and 300 sC, Knight 1,000 sC and 400 sC, Dracula 1,200 sC and 400 sC, Wizard 1,200 sC and 400 sC.

## Tier-exclusive skins
- These can't be bought. Each character has 2, for 52 in total.
- The first unlocks automatically when that character's mastery points reach 1,750 (Diamond rank), and the second at 7,000 (Grandmaster rank).
- You get an on-screen notification when you rank up. The in-game character codex shows how many points you need for the next rank.
- Grand Master skins were replaced in build 434 by new aurora-concept skins. An aurora curtain flows behind the body, and while one is worn the body color and the skill and Ultimate effects turn aurora-colored (builds 433-443). The Grand Master skin names written in the character pages may be the names from before the change.

## Name colors
- Sky Blue Nametag 500 sC, Pink Nametag 500 sC, Gold Nametag 1,000 sC, Rainbow Nametag 6,000 sC.
- The Rainbow Nametag used to cost 2,000 sC but went up to 6,000 sC in v228.

## Character colors
- The color your character wears in matches. Your bullets and effects use this color too.
- 12 free colors: Red, Mint, Yellow, Blue, Pink, Lime, Orange, Purple, Sky, Rose, Emerald, White.
- Shiny Silver 2,000 sC, Shiny Gold 2,500 sC, Rainbow 4,000 sC.
- With a rainbow or shiny color, the effect also shows on the color dot in the lobby player list, on your character on the character select screen (it keeps changing color and glows) and on the victory pose.

## Kill effects
- Effects that play when you get a kill.
- Confetti 400 sC, Heart Burst 400 sC, Skull Smoke 500 sC, Lightning Strike 600 sC, Fire Blast 600 sC, Gold Coin Rain 800 sC.
- **Body Split** 700 sC: the neck, torso, arms and legs of the opponent you defeated fly apart (v340).
- Starlight Burst and Ice Shards aren't sold in the shop; they're Season Pass rewards only.

## Profile backgrounds and borders
- 8 backgrounds: Starry Night 600 sC, Deep Forest 600 sC, Blue Sea 600 sC, Twilight Sunset 700 sC, Neon Grid 900 sC, Lava Fields 900 sC, Cherry Blossom Garden 1,200 sC, Milky Way 1,500 sC.
- 5 borders: Golden Border 800 sC, Cyan Border 800 sC, Pink Neon 1,000 sC, Flame Border 1,200 sC, Rainbow Border 1,800 sC.
- Character-exclusive backgrounds unlock automatically at that character's mastery Lv.10, and exclusive borders at Lv.20. All 27 characters have them.

## Emotes
- The 8 basic emotes are free: 👍 😂 😡 😭 🔥 👋 ❓ 💀.
- Shop emotes: 😎 Sunglasses, 🤡 Clown, 🥶 Frozen and 🫡 Salute are 300 sC each; 🤯 Mind Blown, 😈 Devil Grin, 🐔 Chicken, 💯 Hundred and 😜 Tongue Out are 500 sC each; 🎉 Confetti, 👑 Crown, 🏆 Trophy and 💸 Making It Rain are 800 sC each.
- The emote wheel (V key) holds up to 8 of the emotes you own.

## Victory poses
- The move the winner's character does on the results screen. Hooray is free, and anyone who hasn't picked one uses it.
- Flex 350 sC, Polite Bow 350 sC, Victory Dance 450 sC, Sky Punch 500 sC, Dab 550 sC, Chill Sit 650 sC, Backflip 800 sC, Cossack Dance 900 sC, Taunt 1,500 sC.
- Taunt is a sequence: tongue out, a butt-wiggle slap, then rolling on the floor laughing (added in v235).
- Cossack Dance is a deep squat with arms folded, kicking the legs out to the front in turns (build 399).

## Titles
- Titles aren't bought in the shop; you earn them. Equip one from the Title button on your profile and it shows above your head.
- Character titles: Adept at that character's mastery Lv.5, Expert at Lv.10, Legend at Lv.20. For example, James Adept.
- Season Pass: Season Veteran at tier 10, Season Master at tier 20, Season Hero at tier 30, Season Legend at tier 40, Season Mythic at tier 50, Season Eternal at tier 60.
- Tournament: Tournament Champion for 1 win, Tournament Emperor for 5, Tournament Legend for 10.
- Ranked: Ranked Gold at Gold, Ranked Diamond at Diamond, Ranked Master at Master.

## Gifts and boxes
- Anything buyable with gold among name colors, character colors, kill effects, emotes, victory poses, profile backgrounds and borders, and skins can be gifted to friends. Tier-exclusive, mastery-exclusive, season-exclusive and free cosmetics can't be gifted.
- Boxes only drop basic skins worth 400 sC or less.

stickseum/growth.t: Progression: Levels, Mastery, Missions & Season Pass
stickseum/growth.b:
:: Level cap = None
:: XP per kill = 20
:: Total XP for Lv.10 = 4,050
:: Daily missions = 3 (15 sC each)
:: Weekly missions = 3 (every Monday)
:: Season Pass = 60 tiers (300 XP each up to tier 30, 450 XP from tier 31)

Here's everything that grows as you play. None of it builds up in Practice Mode or private rooms. The currency was renamed from gold to sC in build 382, and wherever this page says gold it means sC.

## Player level
- There's no level cap. You earn 20 XP per kill, 5 per assist, 15 for finishing a match, and another 30 for winning.
- Up to level 10, the curve keeps getting steeper. Total XP needed: Lv.2 is 50, Lv.3 is 200, Lv.4 is 450, Lv.5 is 800, Lv.6 is 1,250, Lv.7 is 1,800, Lv.8 is 2,450, Lv.9 is 3,200, Lv.10 is 4,050.
- After Lv.10, every level takes 1,000 XP. Lv.11 is 5,050, Lv.12 is 6,050, and so on. When the cost changed from 950 to 1,000 (build 354), levels you had already reached were kept as they were.
- You also get XP from Capture the Flag captures (25 XP), each lump of gold put into the cart in Gold Grab (2 XP), finishing first in the MVP vote (50 XP), random boxes and daily rewards, and Season Pass rewards.
- There are achievements for reaching level 10 and level 25.

## Character mastery
- A separate level for each character. If you're holding that character when the match ends, it earns XP: 6 per kill, 3 per assist, 3 for playing the match, 6 for a win (about 40% less since build 383).
- It doesn't build up in modes without weapon picks (Bomb Pass, Hide and Seek, Survival).
- Total XP needed: Lv.2 40, Lv.3 100, Lv.4 200, Lv.5 350, Lv.6 550, Lv.7 800, Lv.8 1,100, Lv.9 1,450, Lv.10 1,850.
- After Lv.10, XP per level starts at 450 and goes up by 50 each level, then stays at 950 from Lv.20. Lv.11 is 2,300, Lv.15 is 4,600, Lv.20 is 8,600.
- Every level-up gives sC: 10 sC for Lv.1-5, 20 sC for Lv.6-10, 30 sC for Lv.11-15 and 45 sC from Lv.16 on (build 375). If you gain several levels at once, the amounts add up.
- At Lv.5, 10 and 20, that character's titles unlock (Adept, Expert, Legend).
- Lv.10 unlocks that character's profile background, and Lv.20 its profile border.
- Character XP from boxes and daily rewards goes to one random character. Pick XP, below, lets you choose the character yourself.

## Pick XP
- Pick XP is XP you can hand to a character of your choice as mastery XP.
- You don't get it for finishing a match. It comes from random boxes and the daily reward, in amounts of 25, 50 or 100.
- Press the Pick XP button in your profile to open the character picker. Choose a character and confirm once more, and all the Pick XP you have saved goes to that character as mastery XP.
- If its mastery level goes up, you get the usual sC.

## Character ranks (by mastery points)
- Ranks go up with mastery points, which each character earns separately (build 410). With that character you earn 3 points per kill, 1 per assist, 4 for a win and 1 for finishing a match. A match with 3 kills, 1 assist and a win gives 15 points.
- Each rank starts at: Novice 0, Bronze 88, Silver 263, Gold 525, Platinum 875, Diamond 1,750, Obsidian 3,063, Master 4,813, Grandmaster 7,000.
- From Bronze to Master there are II and III steps between ranks (build 411). Steps start at: Bronze 88 · II 146 · III 205; Silver 263 · II 350 · III 438; Gold 525 · II 642 · III 759; Platinum 875 · II 1,167 · III 1,459; Diamond 1,750 · II 2,188 · III 2,625; Obsidian 3,063 · II 3,646 · III 4,230; Master 4,813 · II 5,542 · III 6,271.
- Reaching Diamond (1,750 points) unlocks the first tier-exclusive skin, and Grandmaster (7,000 points) unlocks the second.
- Old kill counts carry over at 8.75 points per kill, and ranks already earned are kept.
- These go up separately from mastery level.

## Daily and weekly missions
- 3 new daily missions appear every day. Each one you finish gives 15 sC and 30 Season XP.
- 3 weekly missions change every Monday. Each one you finish gives 50 sC, 5 soul stones and 120 Season XP.
- When you finish a mission, you have to claim the reward yourself on the missions screen (📋).
- Daily mission pool: 3, 5 or 8 kills / 1 win / finish 2, 3 or 4 matches / 1,000 damage / 4 assists / 3 or 4 kills with gun characters / 3 or 4 kills with melee characters / a Domination, Team Battle or Deathmatch match. 3 of these are picked.
- Weekly mission pool: 25 or 40 kills / 4 or 6 wins / finish 12 or 18 matches / 4,000 or 6,000 damage / 10 or 15 assists / 3 Domination matches / 2 Capture the Flag matches / 15 kills with gun characters / 15 kills with melee characters. The Zombie Game mission left the pool when the mode was removed.
- Gun characters are the ones the codex classifies as guns (James, Agent, Robin Hood, Ninja, Soldier, Gambler, Wizard, Dimension Traveler), and melee characters are Jadai, Horemheb, Knight, Baseball Player, Boxer, Assassin, Dracula, Pirate and Samurai.

## Season Pass
- A season is one calendar month. It follows your device's date, and when the month changes, your Season XP and claimed rewards reset.
- There are 60 tiers. Each tier up to tier 30 takes 300 Season XP, and each tier from tier 31 takes 450 (22,500 to fill it all).
- You earn 20 Season XP for every match you finish, 20 more for winning, and 5 per kill (up to 15 kills per match). Mission rewards include Season XP too.
- When you reach a new tier, claim the reward yourself on the missions screen.
- Tier rewards:
- Tier 1: 50 gold, Tier 2: 3 soul stones, Tier 3: 1 random box, Tier 4: 80 gold, Tier 5: Starlight Burst kill effect
- Tier 6: 120 player XP, Tier 7: 5 soul stones, Tier 8: 100 gold, Tier 9: 1 random box, Tier 10: Season Veteran title
- Tier 11: 120 gold, Tier 12: 80 random character XP, Tier 13: 8 soul stones, Tier 14: 1 random box, Tier 15: Ice Shards kill effect
- Tier 16: 150 gold, Tier 17: 200 player XP, Tier 18: 10 soul stones, Tier 19: 2 random boxes, Tier 20: Season Master title
- Rewards got a little better from tier 21 and grow a lot from tier 31 (build 359). There is a title every 10 tiers.
- Tier 21: 170 gold, Tier 22: 260 player XP, Tier 23: 12 soul stones, Tier 24: 2 random boxes, Tier 25: 120 random character XP
- Tier 26: 170 gold, Tier 27: 260 player XP, Tier 28: 12 soul stones, Tier 29: 2 random boxes, Tier 30: Season Hero title
- Tier 31: 290 gold, Tier 32: 500 player XP, Tier 33: 23 soul stones, Tier 34: 3 random boxes, Tier 35: 1,050 gold
- Tier 36: 420 gold, Tier 37: 710 player XP, Tier 38: 32 soul stones, Tier 39: 3 random boxes, Tier 40: Season Legend title
- Tier 41: 550 gold, Tier 42: 920 player XP, Tier 43: 41 soul stones, Tier 44: 3 random boxes, Tier 45: 1,750 gold
- Tier 46: 680 gold, Tier 47: 1,130 player XP, Tier 48: 50 soul stones, Tier 49: 3 random boxes, Tier 50: Season Mythic title
- Tier 51: 810 gold, Tier 52: 1,340 player XP, Tier 53: 59 soul stones, Tier 54: 3 random boxes, Tier 55: 2,450 gold
- Tier 56: 940 gold, Tier 57: 1,550 player XP, Tier 58: 68 soul stones, Tier 59: 3 random boxes, Tier 60: Season Eternal title

stickseum/social.b:
:: Login ID = 3–16 letters or numbers
:: Nickname = up to 15 characters
:: Room code = 6 characters
:: Party = up to 4 people (including you)
:: Clan name = 2–12 characters
:: Invite expiry = 3 hours

This page gathers how to play with friends. Most of it requires logging in with a Frenchfries777 account.

## Account
- Log in or create an account from the friends box on the main screen. The ID is 3–16 letters or numbers, and the password is at least 6 characters.
- One Frenchfries777 account also lets you log in to the other Frenchfries777 games (Crown Envoy, Beaconfall).
- Logging in with the same account keeps your friends, profile card and progress. The profile card shows the games you've played and your Stickseum achievement progress, and the games section shows the total play time for each game.
- The Stickseum profile shows your longest win streak (build 438).
- Nicknames can be up to 15 characters (they were 12 characters before build 383).
- The nickname uses the same account information as the hub. A nickname changed on the hub is applied to your Stickseum profile, and the clan screen shows your current nickname.

## Friends
- Search for a friend by nickname and send a request. If they accept, you become friends.
- Friend requests, clan invites and game invites expire automatically if not answered within 3 hours. After they expire, you can send them again.
- Next to a friend in the friend list and in invites, a match-in-progress mark appears if that friend is in a match.
- The 💬 button in the friend list lets you chat with a friend. Each friend has a separate chat window that shows the last 50 lines, and you can send up to 200 characters at a time (build 394). Unread chats are shown as a count on the 💬 button. When a new chat arrives while you are not in a match, a notification with a reply button appears.
- After you connect and the intro finishes, pending friend requests, clan invites and room invites are gathered and shown together.
- In the friend list you can gift cosmetics to a friend. If the friend is online, the gift arrives right away; otherwise they receive it the next time they log in.
- People you've played with can be found again in the recent players list on the record screen.

## Private rooms
1. In Private Play, choose the mode and map (room settings), then press Create Room.
2. Tell your friends the 6-character code. Your friend enters the code under Join with Code and presses Join.
3. The host presses Start. If there aren't enough people, you can add bots (Easy, Normal or Hard).
- To start, the room needs at least 2 people (bots included). If you're alone, wait for a friend or add a bot.
- From the room, the Invite Friend button sends an invite to a logged-in friend. When the friend accepts, they join the room. Room codes are also linked to hub friend invites: the hub notifies the friend, and if they tap the notification within 30 minutes, they enter that room.
- All modes can be played. The host chooses the map, and map voting and automatic team balance can be turned on.
- Private rooms don't earn rewards. Even if the host leaves in the middle, another person takes over as host and the match continues.

## Spectating
- In a private room, you can watch without playing by using the Spectate button on the Join with Code screen. Enter the 6-character code and press Spectate.
- Spectating ends when the match is over or when the connection to the host is lost.
- You can still spectate after you are eliminated. If you're knocked out in Battle Royale, Battle Royale Duo or Tournament, choose Spectate on the defeat screen. While spectating, there is an Exit button at the top right.

## Parties
- You can group up to 4 online friends (including you) into a party. The person who creates the party is the party leader.
- While in a party, you can only play party modes: Team Battle, Domination, Capture the Flag, Battle Royale Duo and Boss Raid. Battle Royale Duo is only available to a 2-person party.
- Only the party leader chooses the mode. When the leader starts matchmaking, party members follow into the same room and the same team.
- If the party leader leaves, the party ends. Party invites can only be sent to friends, and the invite notification stays on screen for 20 seconds.
- Ranked and daily modes can't be played while in a party.

## Clans
- The clan screen opens only when logged in. It has three tabs: Find Clan, My Clan and Create Clan.
- When you create a clan, you choose: a name (2–12 characters), a tag (2–4 characters, letters, numbers or Korean letters, shown in front of nicknames as [TAG]), an emblem (16 free ones), a color (8 choices) and a description (up to 30 characters). A name or tag that already exists can't be used.
- The clan leader can still change the clan name and tag from the My Clan screen after creating the clan.
- A person can only be in one clan. You can join by searching for a name or tag under Find Clan, or by pressing an invite that a clan member sent to your friend. The list is sorted by clan score, and clans with developers appear first.
- The clan leader can write a clan notice (up to 40 characters). The notice appears when clan members log in.
- There is clan chat (up to 100 characters at a time).
- Clan members have clan tokens, and can donate 10 or 50 at a time to the clan vault. The leader uses the tokens collected in the vault to unlock special emblems: Diamond 100, Galaxy 150, Trident 200, Dragon 300, Comet 300, Castle 500. Five new emblems were added in build 604: Phoenix, Sun Crown, War Shield, World Tree and Storm Ring.
- When you win an online match with at least 2 people in it, the win is reported to your clan. Clan rankings can also be viewed on the ranking page of the site.
- **Clan Match**: Starting from the My Clan screen creates a team-battle room that only clan members can join. Bots don't join.
- If the clan leader leaves, the clan is disbanded and all members are removed. A member can leave at any time (press it, then press once more to confirm).

stickseum/hub-coin.b:
:: Exchange rate = 5 sC per coin
:: Daily login = 10 coins per day
:: Login streak = +20 bonus coins every 7 days
:: Gift limit = 100 per day
:: Undo exchange = Not possible
:: Added in = v238 (2026-10-16)

Hub Coin is the shared coin of the Frenchfries777 hub. You can turn coins you've collected on the hub into Stickseum gold. Added in v238 (2026-10-16).

## What's the rate?
- 1 coin is 5 Stickseum sC. Exchanging 10 coins gets you 50 sC. The currency was renamed from gold to sC in build 382, so everywhere this page says gold it means sC.
- For comparison, 1 kill is 5 sC, so the 10 coins (50 sC) from a daily check-in equal 10 kills.

## How to get coins
- Log in to the Frenchfries777 hub once a day to get 10 Hub Coin. Days run on Korean time.
- Every 7 days in a row you check in, you get a bonus 20 coins. You can see it on the hub's check-in calendar.
- You can gift coins to friends on the hub: 1–100 per gift, up to 100 per day.

## How to exchange
1. Log in on the hub. It has to be the same Frenchfries777 account you use in Stickseum.
2. In the hub's Hub Coin Exchange window, choose Stickseum, enter how many coins to exchange and hit Exchange. The hub deducts the coins and holds the gold for you.
3. Log in to Stickseum with the same account and the held gold is collected automatically. A "Hub Coin Exchange: gold + amount" notification appears.

## When the gold arrives
- It's checked right after you log in.
- It's also checked when the game window becomes visible again (when you come back from another tab or click the window again), but only if 15 seconds have passed since the last check.
- It isn't checked while a match is in progress. You'll get it after the match ends and you leave.
- Gold you've received is never paid out twice. Even with two windows open, it only arrives once.

## What can you buy?
- A New Skin (2,000 sC) is 400 coins. At 10 a day, that's 40 days.
- A 300 sC basic skin is 60 coins, and a 500 sC emote is 100 coins.
- Random boxes can only be bought with soul stones, not gold. Use gold for cosmetics in the shop instead.
- Exchanges can't be undone. Double-check the number of coins before you exchange.

## Good to know about Hub Coin
- Coins live in your hub wallet. In the game, they show up as sC, not coins.
- You have to exchange at least 1 coin at a time, and you can't exchange more than you have.
- Each game has its own rate, shown in the hub's exchange window. For Stickseum, it's 5 gold per coin.
- When you exchange on the hub, the hub records the gold and Stickseum picks it up, so it might not show up in Stickseum right after you exchange.

## If it doesn't arrive
- Make sure you're logged in to the hub and Stickseum with the same Frenchfries777 account.
- Check whether the hub's exchange window says there's gold still waiting. If so, go back to a non-match screen in Stickseum and try again.

stickseum/tips.b:
:: Natural regen = None (heal after 3 s still)
:: Skill cooldown = 5 s
:: Ultimate cooldown = 20 s
:: Teleport = Arrives after 1 s
:: Emote reuse = 1.2 s
:: Boss Raid = 3-min time limit

These tips are based on what we confirmed in the code and rules. They're not the only right answers, just a good direction to start in.

## General
- There's no natural regeneration. After a fight, hide and stay still for just 3 seconds to heal 5 every 0.5 seconds. Shooting is fine.
- Skills are 5 seconds and Ultimates 20 seconds, so using them beats saving them. That said, timing-sensitive ones like Barrier or Homing Missile should be used when they'll land.
- Teleport arrives 1 second after you use it. Even if your opponent moves in the meantime, you still go where you aimed, so it's better to use it ahead of time than in a panic.
- Hold Shift and press the Skill or Ultimate key to use it right away on the nearest opponent. Handy when things get hectic.
- Emotes can be used again after 1.2 seconds. Say hi casually.

## Deathmatch
- It's a 3-minute match, so kills are your score. You respawn after just 5 seconds, so feel free to play aggressively.
- In the last 30 seconds or so, go for nearby opponents. A tie means a shared win.

## Battle Royale & Duo
- No respawns, so managing HP is everything. Pick fewer fights and make time to stand still and heal.
- In Duo, your team is out only when both of you are down. Don't give up if one of you falls.

## Team Battle & Domination
- Teammates can't pick the same character. Try splitting up roles on your team (Wizard supports allies with Magic Circle).
- In Domination, holding the point gives 1 point per second. The goal is 100, so holding it nonstop ends the game in 100 seconds. Fight close to the point. You respawn 5 seconds after dying.
- The point is the floating platform closest to the center of the map.

## Duel & Ranked
- You pick a character again every round. You can't reuse characters, so have 3 different characters ready for 3 rounds.
- Look at what your opponent used in the first round and pick a counter for the next.
- You have 15 seconds to pick a character. Decide ahead of time.
- Duels and team battles have a 20-second ban stage before picking (it only moves on once both sides have chosen), and in duels it comes again before every round. In team battles, each teammate bans one character. Decide in advance which character the opponent is good with, and have a backup in case yours gets banned.

## Zombie Game (removed)
- The Zombie Game was removed in build 372. The zombie disaster still comes up in Survival, so keep moving to dodge the zombies.

## Bomb Pass
- Click a nearby player to pass. You have to pass within 20 seconds, so pick a direction as soon as you get the bomb.
- Close the gap with Dash to make sure the pass lands, and after passing, get away from whoever has the bomb.

## Hide and Seek
