- Hiders should disguise themselves as platforms in spots the seeker is unlikely to check. The first 10 seconds, while the seeker's screen is covered, are key.
- You have 1 HP; if the seeker's first shot hits you, your platform disguise breaks and you can move. A second hit eliminates you.
- The seeker has to find everyone within 1 minute 30 seconds.

## Gold Grab
- You can carry up to 3 lumps of gold, but each one slows you down, and you drop them when you go down. Carry them to the cart while teammates block the way. The pile never runs out, so you collect by standing beside it for 0.8 seconds per lump, but you are easy to hit while standing there, so get cover from teammates.

## Survival
- You have 1 HP, so one hit and you're done. Use the 9 seconds before each disaster to find a safe spot.
- Each disaster is one random pick from lightning, tsunami, volcano, acid rain, flood, meteors, bombs or zombies, lasting 12 seconds. They get stronger as rounds go on.
- Survive five of them to win.

## Capture the Flag
- The flag carrier can't Teleport (but is not slowed down). Have a teammate escort them.
- You can score with the enemy flag even when your own flag is out. A dropped flag of your team does not return by itself, so a teammate has to go and touch it to send it home.
- Scoring gives XP. You respawn at your base 5 seconds after dying.

## Boss Raid
- When a red circle flashes, jump. The ground slam does 22 damage.
- Minions spawn at 70%, 50% and 30% boss HP. Clearing minions can earn you the Cleanup bonus.
- Split the Damage Dealer, Tank, Cleanup and MVP roles so everyone gets a bonus. You only get them if the raid succeeds.
- The time limit is 3 minutes.

## Tournament
- You have to win 4 best-of-3 1v1 matches (first to 2) to win it all. You pick a character again every round. Unlike Duel, you can pick the same character again.
- In the final, the arena shrinks. Don't run; get in there.

## Daily modes
- In Protect the King, split roles between going for the enemy King and guarding your own. Non-Kings respawn after 5 seconds. A bot King runs away from enemies, so chase it down.
- In King of the Hill, your score only goes up when you're alone on the point. With two people it stops, so chase the other person off.
- In Weapon Relay, your character only changes when you get a kill. Don't give up when you're stuck on a weak character.
- In One Shot (private rooms only), everyone has 1 HP. Rapid-fire weapons hit most easily.
- In Paint War, covering lots of ground is how you score. Run around more than you fight.
- In Bounty Hunt, the leader (3+ points) gets a bounty. If you're the leader, hide; if not, go after the leader (worth 4 points).
- In Low-Gravity Brawl, knockback is strong and you fly far. High-knockback weapons like Home Run or the shotgun work great.
- In Infinite Dash Battle Royale, the dash cooldown is 0 seconds. Chain dashes to dodge attacks, and when the danger zone closes in, dash quickly toward the inside.

## Map tips
- Push opponents into the minecart (Underground Mine) or the freezing water (Frozen Lake) to damage them.
- The waves on Storm Pirate Ship alternate direction, so watch for the dark ripple before each wave arrives.
- On Dark Swamp, stay out of the big swamp in the center and cross on the stepping-stone platforms. Everyone inside the swamp slows down and sees less.

stickseum/faq.b:
:: Install = Not needed (internet required)
:: Browsers = Chrome, Edge, Safari, Firefox
:: Former names = ArenaClash, StickmanRumble
:: Invite expiry = 3 hours
:: Host change = Auto after 8 s no response
:: If the game is slow = Graphics Low / 30 FPS

Common questions and what to check when something goes wrong.

## Getting started & installing
- How do I open the downloaded file? Just double-click it and it opens in your browser (Chrome, Edge, Safari, Firefox). No installation or extra programs needed. You do need an internet connection.
- Why are old versions still around? They're kept in case you want to look at an older version. To play with friends, use the latest version.
- Does it work on phones? The site help recommends a computer since it's a keyboard-and-mouse game. Touch controls turn on automatically on touch devices, so you can give it a try. Turn your screen to landscape.
- The game name is different from before. It used to be called ArenaClash and StickmanRumble, and now it's Stickseum.

## Saving & accounts
- Where is my progress (gold, skins, level) saved? If you're not logged in, it's saved only in the browser you're using. If the site address changes or you open the game as a file, that's separate storage, so you start fresh.
- What happens when I log in? Log in with a Frenchfries777 account and your progress is also saved to your account, and logging in on another device loads or merges it. Your friends and profile carry over too.
- Will my records disappear if I switch accounts? Even when two different accounts log in on the same browser, their progress (gold, skins, level), highlights and recent players don't overlap. Each account's data is kept separately in this browser, and a new account doesn't inherit the previous account's progress. Existing progress belongs to the first account that logs in.

## Playing with friends
- My friend can't join the room. Check that the code is right (6 characters, uppercase letters and numbers) and that you're on the same version. If everyone joins through Play Now on the site, you're all on the same latest version.
- Chat or skins don't show up for one person. That's because your versions differ. Use the same latest version.
- The host left. If a match is in progress, someone else takes over as host and the match continues. If the host doesn't respond for more than 8 seconds, it switches automatically too.
- My friend request disappeared. Friend requests, clan invites and game invites expire after 3 hours. Send it again.

## Rewards & progress
- My gold or XP isn't going up. Practice Mode and private rooms don't give XP, gold, soul stones, missions, achievements or mastery.
- My mastery isn't going up. Bomb Pass, Hide and Seek and Survival don't involve picking a weapon, so mastery doesn't build up.
- I finished a mission but didn't get the reward. You have to claim it yourself on the missions screen (📋). Same goes for Season Pass tier rewards.
- I can't see achievement conditions. The in-game list only shows names and keeps the conditions secret. The conditions are on the Shop, Gold & Achievements page.
- How do I get tier-exclusive skins? They unlock automatically when that character's mastery points reach 1,750 (Diamond) and 7,000 (Grandmaster). They can't be bought in the shop.
- My Hub Coin exchange gold didn't arrive. See the "If it doesn't arrive" section on the Hub Coin Exchange page.

## Ranked
- My points aren't changing. Both players have to be logged in for it to count. Points also don't change after more than 3 matches with the same opponent within 24 hours.
- Will I face bots in Ranked? No. Ranked only matches logged-in players against each other.
- When does the season change? On the 1st of every month (Korean time), everyone restarts at 1000 points.

## Performance & display
- The game is slow. Try setting Graphics Effects to Low or Frame Limit to 30 FPS in Settings. Turn on Show FPS to see your current speed.
- The game looks frozen. When the game tab goes into the background, the browser slows it down. Keep the tab in front.
- There's no sound. Check that Sound Effects is turned on in Settings.
- I get touch controls on my iPad with a keyboard attached. Change Control Type to Computer in Settings.
- My controls are acting weird. Use Reset to Defaults under Key Bindings in Settings.

## Rules questions
- How long is Boss Raid? The time limit is 3 minutes.
- When does Deathmatch end? It ends after 3 minutes, and whoever has the most kills wins.
- When does the daily mode change? When your device's date changes.
- Which modes have character bans? Duels (ranked included) and team battles, when you pick a character yourself in the normal way. Random weapon mode has none.
- How do I get Pick XP? It comes from random boxes and the daily reward. Finishing a match does not give it. You spend it by choosing a character with the Pick XP button in your profile.
- I can't pick the same character as my teammate. Duplicates aren't allowed within the same team.
- The ban time is up but it won't move on. Is it a bug? No. The ban stage lasts 20 seconds, and even after that, character select only begins once both sides have chosen their bans. If one side hasn't chosen, it waits.
- Can I find characters by name? Yes, the character select screen has a search so you can find them by name.
- Can I play on a map I made? Maps made with the Map Editor can be used in Practice Mode and private rooms, and you can share them with others using a map code.

crownenvoy/getting-started.b:
:: Genre = Diplomacy and war strategy
:: Platform = Browser, nothing to install
:: Private room code = 5 characters
:: Starting sites = 5 (map mode)
:: Site pick time = 30 s first, then 10 s
:: Nation pick time = 90 s (historical templates)

Crown Envoy is a diplomacy and war strategy game where you send envoys to forge alliances and send armies to expand your territory. It runs right in your browser with nothing to install, and you can face off against friends in the same game.

## How to open the game
- Hit **Play Now** on the site and the latest version opens.
- The game screen shows the build number in the form 'v0.4 · build NN'.
- The latest version is 0.4 (released 2026-10-23, now at build 112). Every change up to 0.3 "The Age of Resources and Generals" (2026-10-17, build 60) carries over. 0.2 is kept separately, and future changes go into 0.4. Version 0.4 added the Papacy, Holy Roman Emperor elections, republic elections, missionaries, royal letters and the telegraph network, and referendums, law codes, neutrality declarations and press control. A country's color is now set automatically at the start and cannot be changed.
- The intro that plays when the game starts cannot be skipped by clicking or tapping, and it plays to the end. The automatic refresh when you leave a game and return to the lobby goes to the lobby without the intro.
- The music depends on the screen. The courtly track for harpsichord and strings loops in the lobby and on the title screen. During a game, three tracks alternate one after another: the original battle track, a war march, and a slow, solemn piece for strings, brass and timpani.
- When playing with friends, everyone should join through Play Now. Being on the same version avoids compatibility problems.
- Progress such as saved games is stored separately for each site address you use.
- Even if you switch accounts in the same browser, the scenario list, saved games, achievements and scenario stars are saved separately for each account. For details, see the **Account, Rankings & Achievements** document.

## Lobby menu
- **Online Play**: Automatically finds a room with people in it and joins. Empty slots are filled by AI.
- **Private Play**: Create a room, or join a friend's room with a 5-character code. The **Spectate** button lets you watch without taking a slot.
- **vs AI**: Play alone against AI kingdoms. In the lobby you can add up to 5 AIs with different personalities. The game autosaves at the start of each planning phase.
- **Scenario Editor**: Set nations, territories, hostilities and alliances yourself to make your own map.
- **Shared Scenarios**: Download and play scenarios made by other people. Some scenarios have a price (0–500 cC).
- Logging in with a Frenchfries777 account lets you join friends' rooms without a code, and invite them. Logging in is optional. You can play without logging in.
- Logging in also collects CrownCoin (cC). You earn it by playing and completing achievements, and you can check your balance with the 👑 button at the top. For details, see the **CrownCoin** document.

## First game (vs AI)
1. On the home screen, press **vs AI**.
2. Choose a map and an era template, then press **Start Game**.
3. In map mode, pick 5 starting sites (your starting territories). The first pick must be made within 30 seconds, and later picks within 10 seconds. In historical templates, choose your nation within 90 seconds.
4. Expand your territory with commands, diplomacy and technology.
5. When you've finished your plan, press **Confirm Plan**. When every living player has confirmed, the game moves on without waiting for the rest of the time.

The tutorial appears according to the situation. It guides you through choosing a nation and territory, declaring war on your weakest neighbor, attacking, moving troops and confirming plans, in that order. Press the **Tutorial** button during the game to see the detailed guide again.
In the lobby, you can type a nation name in the **My Nation Name** box (up to 16 characters; if left empty, one is assigned automatically). Each time you start a new vs AI game, the name you chose last time is cleared and the game starts with an automatic name (build 92).

## Keyboard shortcuts
- 1 ~ 5: Switch tabs (Map, Diplomacy, Trade, Technology, Goals)
- E: Confirm / cancel plan
- H: Move to your territory
- + / −: Zoom the map in / out
- Arrow keys or WASD: Move the map
- M: Turn the minimap on / off
- ?: Keyboard shortcut help

## Moving the map
- The stuttering that happened when dragging or zooming the map has been improved. While moving, the previously drawn map is reused, and when it stops, the map is redrawn sharply.
- If you turn on Optimization in the **Records & Settings** menu, the map is drawn at a lower resolution, the season and stamp effects are turned off, and battle effects show only a summary. This reduces the load on your device (build 96). This setting is linked to the hub's shared low-spec mode.

## iPad and touch screens
- Drag the map with one finger to move it, and pinch with two fingers to zoom in or out.
- Quickly tap twice with two fingers to return to the full map (build 97). On a computer, double-click the map.
- The zoom in (+) and zoom out (−) buttons, the Go to My Territory button and the full-view button are also available.
- Tap a territory to open its information and command panel.

## Further reading
- For the full flow of the rules, see **How to Play**. For new players, **Beginner Tips** and **FAQ** are recommended.

## Screen pictures
- The emoji of about 130 kinds on the game screen and the map are shown as Crown Envoy logo pictures (build 140). Chat keeps the emoji as they are.

crownenvoy/how-to-play.b:
:: One turn = 1 month
:: Planning time = Fixed at 50 seconds
:: Starting gold = 260
:: Minimum troops = Attack 200, move 100
:: Solo victory = 50% of land, 3 turns in a row
:: Coalition victory = 60% of land, 3 turns in a row

Crown Envoy is turn-based. Each turn is one month, and everyone plans at the same time before all plans are carried out together.

## How a turn flows
1. **Planning time**: The timer at the top of the screen is your planning time. It's **fixed at 50 seconds** and can't be changed in room settings. This is when you prepare attack and move orders, conscription and diplomacy.
2. Select one of your territories, then click a neighboring territory to create an attack or move order. Set your forces with the infantry, cavalry and artillery sliders and click **Add Attack**.
3. Once every living player clicks **Confirm Plan**, the turn runs right away even if time is left. AI kingdoms always count as ready.
4. When the turn runs, all orders are processed at once and battle animations play. The report time is 10 seconds by default, plus 22 seconds for each battle that actually happened.
5. The turn report shows changes in gold, territory, troops, battles and diplomacy on a single page.
- If someone still has an event choice to make, the timer pauses and waits for them, for up to 90 seconds.
- In solo play, you can undo previous turns during the planning phase, going back up to the last 4. Not available in multiplayer.
- Quiet months can be skipped automatically without orders (⏩ Skip). It stops when a battle, event or diplomatic proposal comes up.
- Territory selection rules: if you have selected another nation's territory (one where you have no troops) and click a different territory, the selection is cleared right away. If you have selected one of your territories and click another of your own that troops cannot reach, that territory becomes the new selection instead of an error message.

## Tabs
- **Map & Orders**: Territory info, orders, conscription, forts, buildings and more
- **Diplomacy**: Alliances, treaties, trade and declarations of war. You can search by nation name.
- **Politics**: Government type, religion, public opinion, council and will
- **Trade**: Check resource prices and buy or sell.
- **Tech**: Research to improve unit types and abilities.
- **Goals**: Each nation has its own assigned missions.
- You can change your flag from the menu even during play. The new flag takes effect in the game right away.

## Territory types (defaults)
- Capital: 60 income, 2 victory points
- Estate: 30 income, 1 victory point
- Trade Port: 55 income, 2 victory points
- Stronghold: 20 income, 2 victory points, defense bonus
- Granary: 38 income, 1 victory point
- Mine: 62 income, 2 victory points
- Defense depends on terrain (plains, coast, forest, hills, mountains). Mountains are the best, followed by hills, forest, coast and plains.

## Troop units
- In every mode (map and historical templates), troop numbers use the same scale (units of 10). Starting troops are about 4,800 in the capital and 2,000 in other territories, multiplied by each nation's modifier.
- Attacks need at least 200 troops, and moves at least 100.

## Managing money
- You start with 260 gold.
- Upkeep is paid every turn: 6 gold per general, 8 gold per diplomat, and soldier upkeep of 0.004 gold per soldier (about 4 gold per 1,000). Upkeep never exceeds 90% of that turn's income.
- If your gold goes negative, 5% of your troops desert. Morale also drops sharply.
- Income depends on territory type, stability, your government's taxes, trade and alliance bonuses, war weariness and more. See the **Economy & Trade** page for details.

## How to win
This is just a summary. See the **Victory & Scoring** page for details.
- **Missions**: Each nation gets 3 goals. Complete them all for a decisive victory.
- **Solo victory**: Hold 50% of all land by yourself for 3 turns in a row to win.
- **Coalition victory**: Nations linked by alliances win by holding 60% of all land for 3 turns in a row.
- When the set game length ends, the winner is decided by victory points.

crownenvoy/diplomacy.b:
:: Sending a diplomat = 20 gold
:: Diplomat upkeep = 8 gold per turn each
:: Upgrading to an embassy = 200 gold
:: At a time = Up to 2
:: Alliance proposal = At least 50 trust
:: Royal Marriage = 120 gold dowry, 48 turns
:: Mediation = 80 gold

Open a nation's card in the Diplomacy tab and you'll see the buttons split into three groups: **Improve Relations · Deals · Hostile**. The number on the right of the card is how that nation sees you (opinion), and clicking **Details** shows why your relations are the way they are.

## Contact and diplomats
- You can reach nations that share a border with you, nations you have a treaty or alliance with, and nations you're at war with, even without a diplomat.
- To reach faraway nations, you need to send a diplomat. Sending one costs 20 gold, and you can talk right away.
- You can have up to 2 out at a time, and each costs 8 gold per turn.
- **Embassy**: you can upgrade a diplomat who is already stationed abroad into an embassy for 200 gold. An embassy has no diplomat upkeep, and opinion builds up between the two nations every month (+8 in their view of you and +4 in your view of them each month, each up to 60). You cannot open one in a nation you are at war with.
- Without contact, you can't make treaties, exchanges or demands. You can still send troops, trade, go to war and spy.
- You can also expel the other side's diplomat or recall your own. Letters (chat) are visible only to the two nations involved.

## Improve Relations
- **Treaties**: Propose one of non-aggression (3 turns), trade (3 turns), military access (8 turns) or alliance (permanent). A trade treaty adds +20 gold per turn to your income, and an alliance adds +15 gold.
- Non-aggression, trade and military access need at least 30 trust to propose, and alliances need at least 50.
- Sweetening the deal with gold (up to 600 gold) makes it easier for them to accept. If the AI's score falls short, it may counter-propose asking for more gold. You can also send it as a secret treaty.
- Alliances are easier when you share a common enemy.
- **Union**: Can only be proposed to AI nations you're allied with, and they rarely accept.
- **Royal Marriage**: Form a marriage alliance for 48 turns with a 120 gold dowry. Opinion and trust (+4) go up. The other nation's view of you has to be at least +10, and you can have up to 2 at a time. Breaking a marriage costs −8 trust and a big drop in opinion.
- There's about a 1.5% chance each turn that the king of a marriage ally dies without an heir. When that happens, you can claim the throne and make them a vassal, or take gold instead.
- **Guarantee Independence**: Declare that you'll protect that nation for 24 turns. You can guarantee up to 3 at a time. Their opinion of you rises sharply, and AIs eyeing them back off. If they're attacked, you have to help; ignoring them costs −5 trust and some opinion. Attacking them yourself costs −25 trust.
- **Gifts**: Send gold (20 gold or more) to raise their opinion by that much, which slowly fades. You can also send troops, taking up to 60% from a single territory.
- **Royal letter**: pay 30 gold to have your monarch write personally to a country you have contact with (not one at war with you). You can send one to the same country once every 4 turns, and its opinion of you rises (+10). With a 12% chance the contents leak, which costs you 5 trust and cancels the gained opinion.
- **Missionary**: pay 90 gold to send a missionary to a country of a different faith (not one at war with you). You can have up to 2 out at once, and send one to the same country every 8 turns. It stays for 6 turns and raises opinion, but each turn there is a 10% chance it gets caught, which costs 6 trust and a large opinion drop (−25). If it completes the 6 turns, an AI country has a 45% chance to convert to your faith (+2 victory points), and if it doesn't convert, opinion rises by 10.

## What moves opinion
- Alliance +25, same religion +10, same ethnicity +12, same government type +8, at war −30.
- A common enemy adds up to +20.
- Check the score for each item under **Details**.

## Deals
- **Trade**: If a trade route is open between ports, your income goes up every turn. See **Economy & Trade** for details.
- Sending a merchant ship costs 50 gold, with up to 3 at a time (4 with a shipyard).
- Tariffs go from level 0 to 3. Each level raises your trade income with that nation by 25% and cuts theirs by 25%, but lowers their opinion of you.
- **Embargo**: Cut off trade for 6 turns for 40 gold. One nation's embargo cuts the target's income by about 20%; two nations' embargoes cut it by about 35%. Up to 2 at a time. Relations take a big hit. Can't be used on allies or trade partners.
- **Exchange**: Trade military access for 8 turns, gold, soldiers, territory (up to 3), or a declaration of war on the other side's enemy. You can also just give or just receive. Capitals can't be traded.

## Hostile
- **War**: You have to declare war before you can attack a nation. See the **War & Armies** page for details.
- **Demand (ultimatum)**: Demand gold (30 gold or more, up to 60% of their treasury) or up to 3 territories. If they refuse, war starts automatically.
- **Espionage**: See the **Espionage** page for details.
- **Cultural Influence**: Spread your culture into their territories. It's covered on the **Economy & Trade** page.

## Trust and betrayal
- Breaking a treaty to declare war counts as betrayal: −40 trust and −12 stability.
- Betraying an ally is far worse: −60 trust and −20 stability.
- With low trust, you can't even propose treaties. Keeping your word pays off.

## Mediation and peace talks
- You can mediate between two warring nations for 80 gold. If it works, they agree to a truce and you get +8 trust and +4 victory points. You have to wait 4 rounds before doing it again.
- You need diplomatic channels with both nations, and you can't mediate for a nation you're at war with.

crownenvoy/war-and-army.b:
:: Truce length = 12 turns
:: Unit types = Infantry, cavalry, artillery
:: Minimum troops = Attack 200, move 100
:: Conscripts join = Start of next planning phase
:: Mercenaries = 1.7x cost, 8 turns
:: Wounded return = 30% of casualties, in 2 turns

War starts with a declaration. You have to declare war before you can attack a nation, and to declare war on an ally, you have to break the alliance first.

## Declarations and war goals
- When declaring war, you can pick one goal: Conquest (capture 3 territories), Revenge (take their capital), Liberation (retake 2 of your lands) or Tribute (make them a vassal)
- The goal you pick before declaring war stays selected even when the screen refreshes, and it is applied to the declaration as chosen.
- Achieving the goal gives +12 morale for 8 turns; signing a truce without achieving it gives −10 morale. If the goal drags on for more than 30 turns, that's −8 morale too.
- In historical templates, the allies of the nation you attack join the war against you. You also can't attack your own allies in historical templates.
- **Joint War** (24 turns): Pledge to fight the same enemy together with an ally. Every time you capture one of that nation's territories, both of you get 15 gold in spoils, and if you destroy them, both get +5 victory points. Making a separate truce costs −20 trust and a big drop in opinion (−40).

## Truces and peace negotiations
- A truce is made only through a **truce council**. If you ask a country at war with you for a truce, a council opens at the start of the next turn. A truce lasts **12 turns**.
- When the council opens, both sides, AI included, present their demands live on the map. The turn stops during the council, it lasts up to 150 seconds, and either side can break it off.
- Peace negotiations use **tokens**. You get 2 tokens for each territory you captured during the war (captures × 2).
- Token cost of demands: Estate or Granary 2, Trade Port, Stronghold or Mine 3, Capital 5, vassalization 6. 1 token counts as 62.5 gold. You can make up any shortfall with gold.
- Captured territory goes back to its original owner at a truce unless you protect it with tokens. Protecting costs 1 less than the territory's value (ordinary territory 2→1, port, fortress and mine 3→2, capital 5→4).
- Captured land protected with tokens and land won by negotiation count as your own territory (except for rebellion and independence).
- Territory the other side demands can be blocked with tokens. Demands for reparations, prisoner exchange, vassalization and a declaration of war are used as before.
- A blocked (defended) demand can be **re-raised**. The cost of that demand goes up by 1 token, and the other side has to pay 1 more token to block it again. A single item can be raised up to 5 levels, and you can't raise it if you lack the tokens. The AI raises a demand at most 2 times (up to level 3).
- The AI shows its protecting of captured land, demands, defenses and its reasons for agreeing or refusing in the council record. When the AI refuses terms, the reason stays in the council record and a notice says the other side does not accept.
- The longer the negotiation goes on, the more easily the AI agrees.
- In peace negotiations, you can demand up to 8 territories, plus gold, prisoner exchanges, forced vassalization and forced declarations of war on a third nation.
- During a truce, neither side attacks. The AI won't declare war first during that time.

## Handling troops
- There are three unit types: infantry, cavalry and artillery. Cavalry costs 2x as much as infantry, and artillery 2.4x.
- You conscript in your territories during the planning phase. **Conscripted troops join at the start of the next turn's planning phase** (shown in green on screen). If you lose the territory in the meantime, those troops are lost too.
- Conscription costs 0.035 gold per base soldier, multiplied by the unit type modifier, weariness, and politics, religion and tech modifiers. The weaker side conscripts 20% cheaper.
- In a single territory, cavalry can't exceed 60% and artillery can't exceed 40%. Artillery can only be conscripted in cities, forts and trade ports, and cavalry can't be conscripted in mountains.
- Each region has a per-turn conscription limit: 60% of the regional troop cap, +50% for every city upgrade (×1.25 with the Railways tech).
- Mercenaries can be hired from 100 troops. They cost 1.7x, serve for 8 turns, and you can have up to 6,000 per territory.
- Attacks need at least 200 troops, and moves at least 100. Orders are split by unit type (infantry, cavalry, artillery).
- Cavalry can move two tiles within your own territory, but can only attack one tile away.
- Nations with alliances, military access or vassal ties can station troops in each other's territory.
- Wounded: 30% of battle casualties return after 2 turns. With the Field Medicine tech, it's 45%.

## Battle formations
- There are three formations: phalanx, wedge and line. The counters are phalanx > wedge > line > phalanx.
- You choose one in the planning phase in the **Battle formation** panel of the map/orders tab, and the opponent cannot see it.
- Beating the opponent's formation raises attack and defense (base +1.5%, +0.6 percentage points per leadership of the commanding general). Losing makes you weaker by half that amount, and the same formation has no effect.
- It applies only to land battles, not naval battles. The turn log after a battle shows the formation advantage.
- Bots also choose formations, and counter the formation of the opponent they fought recently with a 60% chance.

## Construction and facilities
- **City upgrade**: 120 gold → 240 gold → 400 gold, up to level 3 (politics and religion modifiers apply)
- **Fort**: 80 gold base, up to level 3. Level 3 (Great Fort) costs double and becomes a supply hub. Each level increases defense.
- **Trenches**: 70 gold, up to level 3. Can only be dug in the 1914, 1939 and Korean War eras.
- Forts and trenches raise the morale of troops stationed there by 10–30 depending on level.
- **Scorched Earth**: Burn your own territory to cut off its income for 6 rounds. Cooldown of 3, and stability drops by 4. Capitals can't be burned.
- **Move Capital**: Move your capital for 200 gold. Once every 24 rounds, −6 stability.
- **Scouting**: Scout another nation for 40 gold base (half with the Air Support tech).
- **Colonization**: Claim unowned land next to your territory or fleet for 50 gold + troops/30.
- For buildings, see the **Economy & Trade** page.

## Wonders
- A wonder can be built in a territory with a city of level 1 or higher. It costs 700 gold and 30 wood and takes 4 turns.
- Only one of each kind can be built in the world, and each nation can have at most 2.
- The effect applies to the whole nation, and completing one gives +5 victory points.
- Great Wall: +30% fortress defense in all territories.
- Great Library: +15% research speed.
- Golden Palace: +10% income.
- Grand Temple: +12% diplomatic persuasion.
- Hanging Gardens: −25% food consumption.
- Grand Arena: +25% general experience and −8% conscription cost.
- When a city is captured, a completed wonder passes to the conqueror, and one under construction is lost.
- Bots also build wonders when they have enough money.

## Expeditions and relics
- With a port, you can send one expedition team from the **Expeditions and relics** panel in the map/orders tab.
- Nearby ruins cost 100 gold and 3 wood, take 2 turns, and have a 60% chance of success.
- The distant desert and jungle cost 180 gold and 5 wood, take 4 turns, and have a 55% chance of success. Success gives +100 gold.
- The unknown continent costs 300 gold and 8 wood, takes 6 turns, and has a 40% chance of success. Success gives +300 gold and +4 victory points.
- If it fails, the expedition does not return.
- There are 8 relics, only one of each in the world, and each effect applies to the whole nation.
- Golden Mask: +6% income.
- Ancient Map: +8% diplomatic persuasion.
- War Drum: +5% attack.
- Shield of the Gods: +20% fortress defense.
- Scholar's Scroll: +8% research.
- Hero's Sword: +30% general experience.
- Horn of Plenty: −12% food consumption.
- Mercenary King's Seal: −10% conscription cost, −6% upkeep.
- After all relics have been found, a success only gives gold.
- If your capital is captured, your relics pass to the conqueror.
- Bots also send expeditions when they have a port and gold (420 or more).

## Bandit dens
- From turn 5, bandit dens appear on unowned land or land in unrest (not capitals). The number of dens grows as the game goes on, up to 5. The list of dens is under Policy in the Map tab.
- Every turn the bandits raid the den's territory and its neighbors, stealing gold and sometimes causing unrest. Their numbers grow by 25 each turn (up to 1,500).
- If you have at least 1.3 times the bandits' strength in the den or in your territory next to it, send your army in the planning phase to clear it out. You lose some troops but gain gold, and if a general is in that territory, the general gets +3 experience.
- Bots also clear bandit dens when they have enough troops.

## Occupation and supply
- Captured territories are restless for a while (resistance 2). A fort reduces this by 1, trenches by 2. Land held for a long time may declare independence. But land taken by someone other than its original owner starts at resistance 4 with low stability (see the Politics document for Assimilation, build 97).
- Capturing a capital gives the occupier +6 victory points. The defender loses 25 stability and their morale takes a heavy blow.
- Supply range differs by era (e.g., Korean War 13, 2026 16, Imjin War 6, Punic 5). The Supply System and Mechanization techs each add +1. Troops cut off from supply lose up to 10% per month (8% if fully isolated).
- Besieging an army trapped in a fort reduces it by 8% per month through starvation.
- **Encirclement**: a territory with 2 or more neighboring land territories, all owned by nations you are at war with, is cut off from supply. Its troops shrink by 8% every month (they never drop below 10), and that nation loses 1 morale every month. The map shows "Isolated N months", and the first time it happens it is written in the log.

## Government in exile
- Added in build 77. If you lose your last territory but have an ally, you go into exile instead of being destroyed. This happens once per game.
- You move to the capital of the ally with the most territories (or another of its territories if it has none), keeping 300 troops and half your gold. Your surviving generals go with you.
- If you retake one territory that was originally yours while in exile, your nation is restored. That territory becomes your new capital, and you get +6 victory points, +150 gold and +10 morale, with stability set to at least 60.
- If you lose all your troops while in exile, your nation is destroyed.

## Vassals
- You can create a vassal from one of your territories. You can't give away your capital, and you must keep at least one territory.
- Vassals pay 20% of their monthly income as tribute. You can release or annex a vassal, and vassals can declare independence too.
- If you're a vassal, you can't declare war on your overlord; you have to declare independence.

## Watch out
- Plague sometimes breaks out in ports and big cities, reducing troops. Medicine techs reduce the damage.
- Long wars lower public opinion, and with low stability and high war weariness, a coup can happen.
- For battle calculations and generals, see the **Generals & Battles** page; for techs, see the **Tech Tree** page.

crownenvoy/scenarios-and-maps.b:
:: Game length = Default/36/72/120/unlimited
:: Map default length = 60 turns
:: Starting sites = 5 each, snake draft
:: Historical templates = 19
:: General cap = Map 4, templates 8
:: Winter attack = −15% (December–February)

When creating a room, you choose whether to **Start from a Map** or use a **Historical Template**, and set the game length. Length options are the scenario default, 36 turns, 72 turns, 120 turns or unlimited.

## Start from a Map
In map mode, players take turns picking starting sites (5 each) in snake draft order, and the leftover land becomes AI kingdoms and neutral territory. Ports, mines and castles have higher income and victory points. The default length is 60 turns. In map mode, you can have up to 4 generals.
- **Europe**: A real administrative map stretching to North Africa, Egypt and the Levant (333 territories)
- **USA**: Each of the 50 states is one region.
- **World**: An administrative map of the whole world (908 territories)
- **Archipelago**: A fictional archipelago of 62 islands scattered across 52 sea zones. You have to cross between islands by ship.
- **East Asia**: The Korean Peninsula, Japan, eastern China, Mongolia and Taiwan. Naval battles and landings matter here.
- **Continent**: One large continent split three ways, surrounded by 31 sea zones.
- **Americas**: North, Central and South America plus the Caribbean
- **Africa**: The entire African continent and Madagascar
- **Oceania**: Australia, New Zealand, Papua New Guinea and the South Pacific island nations
- **Pangaea**: A supercontinent where all continents are joined as one

## 19 historical templates (default length)
- Second Punic War (218 BC, 72 turns)
- Three Kingdoms (229, 72 turns)
- The Fall of Rome (451)
- The Hundred Years' War (1428)
- The Rise of the Ottomans (1453)
- Age of Discovery (1492, 120 turns)
- Imjin War (1592, 72 turns)
- Thirty Years' War (1618, 72 turns)
- War of the Spanish Succession (1701, 72 turns)
- American Revolutionary War (1775, 96 turns)
- Napoleonic Wars (1803, 72 turns)
- Crimean War (1853, 36 turns)
- American Civil War (1861, 48 turns)
- Wars of German Unification (1864, 72 turns)
- World War I (1914, 52 turns)
- World War II (1939, 72 turns)
- Korean War (1950, 37 turns)
- Modern Europe (2026, 48 turns)
- Three Kingdoms Continent (fictional, 60 turns)

In templates, you start by picking a nation (within 90 seconds), and historical events happen at set times. Templates allow up to 8 generals. Each nation has an AI difficulty label (Easy, Normal, Hard), based on its size, its number of rivals and allies, and how many non-allied neighbors it has. "Neutral-leaning" nations have passive AI, but players can still pick them.
- For era-by-era guides, see the **Templates** page.

## Seasons and eras
- Map mode uses a calendar that starts in March, and templates use the real calendar.
- In winter (December–February), attack strength is −15% (−23% in mountains, −18% in hills and forest). Troops staying in someone else's hill or mountain land lose 3% per month, plus another 5% in the far north.
- Spring (March–April) is −8% (−11% on plains and coast), and summer (June–August) is +3% on plains, coast and hills.
- In the 1812 template, foreign troops on Russian soil lose 15% per month from September to March.
- In templates, techs can only be researched once their year has passed. Map mode has no year limits.

## Territory borders
- Territory borders are drawn as winding curves, and neighboring territories and coastlines fit together in the same shape.
- Small territory fragments that were stuck inland have been cleaned up.
- Small territories in South America, Southeast Asia and Africa that belong to the same nation have been merged into larger ones. The world map's territory count dropped from 1,273 to 907, and the Americas and Africa maps were merged the same way.
- A merged territory's income and per-turn conscription limit grow by the combined amount.
- The shapes of the territories around Provence (Toulon, Lyon, Dijon) on the Europe and World maps were fixed. Strips and fragments that were detached from their main territory were merged into neighboring territories; territory numbers and existing scenarios are unchanged.
- Existing templates and my scenarios are converted automatically. Earlier saved games can no longer be loaded.
- In build 44, the region around Istanbul was made into its own small port territory on the Bosporus strait. It is on the Europe map (333 territories) and the World map (908, previously 907). It starts at fort level 3, and the old tile became Edirne in Thrace.
- In build 49, Constantinople (Istanbul) was moved to the indentation of the Bosporus strait. This is the same on the Europe and World maps, and the links to neighboring territories stay as they were.
- This territory is shown as Constantinople in templates before 1453 (The Rise of the Ottomans, The Hundred Years' War, The Fall of Rome and others) and as Istanbul in templates from 1453 on. The capital of Byzantium (the Eastern Roman Empire) is also Constantinople, and this territory is Byzantine territory.
- In scenarios you make yourself, the city name is shown as Constantinople instead of Istanbul if the starting year is between 330 and 1453, and as Byzantium if it is before 330.
- In The Rise of the Ottomans and The Hundred Years' War templates, Byzantium starts with Constantinople and the Ottomans start with Edirne. In templates from 1453 on (1914, 1939 and 2026 included), the Ottomans/Turkey start with this territory.
- Scenarios saved earlier on the Europe and World maps open to fit the new territory.
- In build 112, the Korean (Hangul) names of some places, such as in Turkey, the Arab world, Central Asia and Southeast Asia, were corrected to be closer to the local pronunciation.

## Scenario list
- The historical template (scenario list) selection window is now wider. The seats and AI list moved to the left column, the scenario list shows close to 8 at a time, and scenario descriptions and the list of historical events are shown at greater length. Narrow screens keep the old layout.
- The list has a search box. Search by name, year or nation name.
- The category tabs are All / Default / Made by me / Downloaded.
- Sorting options are chronological, by name, most nations, highest stars and most played.
- Each scenario shows a map preview colored in the nations' colors and how many times you have played it. The play count is saved on this device for each account.

## Scenario challenges
- Finishing a historical scenario earns a rating of up to 3 stars, and your best record is saved to your account. Even if you switch accounts in the same browser, scenario stars are saved separately for each account.

## Scenario Editor and shared scenarios
- See the **Scenario Editor** page.

## Saving and continuing
- Saving only works in vs AI (solo). The game autosaves at the start of each planning phase, and you can also save manually from [Records & Settings] during a game.
- Pick a game to continue from **Saved Games** in the lobby.
- Even if you switch accounts in the same browser, saved games are kept separately for each account. Games saved on this device before logging in can be moved over with **Import to this account** on the Saved Games screen.
- The trial can only be played up to turn 12. When turn 12 ends, the result is decided and you can't continue.
- Games played with a trial scenario are not saved and don't appear in the saved games list.

crownenvoy/politics.b:
:: Government types = 6
:: Religions = 6
:: Government change = Once every 20 turns
:: Conversion = Once every 15 turns
:: Public opinion range = 0 to 100
:: Coup condition = Stability ≤22, weariness ≥35
:: Noble factions = Lords, Military, Merchants
:: Council = 5 members (3–7)
:: Will = Monarchy, Empire, Totalitarianism

The Politics tab handles government type, religion, public opinion, the council and the will. Nations with the same government or the same religion get an opinion bonus (government +8, religion +10). Your nation's name (Kingdom, Empire, Republic, etc.) also changes with your government.

## 6 government types
- **Monarchy** (Kingdom): Conscription cost −8%
- **Empire** (Empire): Conscription cost −16%, morale +5%
- **Republic** (Republic): Revolt chance −5%, morale +5%
- **Totalitarianism**: Morale +10%
- **Communism** (People's Republic): Taxes +3%, soldier upkeep −7%
- **Parliamentary System**: Revolt chance −10%, general XP +3%
- Switching to Totalitarianism or a Parliamentary System keeps your existing nation title (Kingdom, Republic, etc.).
- Not just anyone can become an **Empire**. You need at least 10 territories or 7% of the whole map, whichever is larger, and troops at least 1.5x the average of all surviving nations.
- You can change government only once every 20 turns. For 5 turns after switching, there's turmoil: half morale, double revolt chance, half income and so on. Be careful during wartime.

## 6 religions
- **Christianity**: Soldier attack +5%, morale +10%
- **Protestantism**: Tech +5%, revolt chance −5%, treaty acceptance +5%
- **Islam**: Conscription cost −10%, fort and city upgrade cost −5%
- **Atheism**: City and fort effects +10%, city structure effects +5%
- **Buddhism**: Revolt chance −10%, war weariness −15%
- **Confucianism**: Taxes +5%, general XP +5%
- You can convert once every 15 turns. For 3 turns right after converting, there's turmoil: revolt chance 1.7x and bigger morale swings.

## Public opinion
- Public opinion ranges from 0 to 100. It drops during war and slowly recovers toward 60 in peacetime.
- Below 15, income and morale drop to 0.85x. Below 30, revolt chance becomes 1.5x. At 75 or above, morale is 1.05x.
- **Propaganda**: Costs 35% of income (minimum 60 gold), 3-turn cooldown. Public opinion +10 (+15 during war), morale +4.
- **Festival**: Costs 80% of income (minimum 120 gold), 6-turn cooldown. Public opinion +20, stability +6.

## Morale and stability
- Target morale starts at 60, rises with high stability, and drops with war weariness, debt and resource shortages (−5 per missing resource). Actual morale moves 40% of the way toward the target each turn.
- Click the morale number to see a breakdown of what affected it and by how much.
- Low stability cuts income and raises the risk of revolts and coups. With stability at 22 or below and war weariness at 35 or above, a coup can happen.

## Noble factions
- Under Policy in the Map tab you can see the loyalty (0–100) of the three noble factions: Lords, Military and Merchants.
- **Lords**: high loyalty raises stability and the recruitment cap; low loyalty increases the risk of revolt.
- **Military**: high loyalty raises morale; low loyalty increases the risk of a coup.
- **Merchants**: high loyalty increases tax income; low loyalty reduces it.
- From turn 4, factions sometimes make demands (recognition of hereditary estates, a bigger military budget, a merchant charter). Pay gold (60% of income, 60–400 gold) to grant it for +18 loyalty, refuse for −12, and leave it unanswered for 4 turns for −10.
- During war, Military loyalty rises and Merchant loyalty falls; in peace it's the other way round. High stability raises Lord loyalty, and low stability lowers it.
- If loyalty drops below 15, the lords may turn against you and cause unrest, or the merchants may siphon off gold.

## Council
- Added in build 76. The council in the Politics tab starts with 5 members, one each from the Military, Merchant, Noble, People's and Clergy factions.
- Depending on your government, every 6–12 turns (Republic and Parliamentary System 6 turns, Monarchy 9, Empire and Communism 10, Totalitarianism 12) the faction with the most members makes a demand. Meeting it costs 20% of your gold (90–400 gold).
- Accepting costs the gold and gives +5 morale, plus a faction-specific effect: Military (bigger military budget) troop veterancy +4, Merchant (commercial subsidies) public opinion +6, Noble (estate grants) stability +4, People's (relief spending) public opinion +10, Clergy (cathedral funds) stability +3 and public opinion +4.
- Refusing makes the revolt chance 1.5x for 6 turns. Not choosing, or not having enough gold, also counts as a refusal.
- You can appoint a member of any faction for 80 gold; dismissing one costs −2 stability. You can change members only once per turn, and the council has 3–7 members.
- If one faction holds 60% or more of the seats, the council is lopsided and stability drops by 1 every turn.

## State tools
- Added in 0.4 to the **State tools** card on the Politics tab. AI countries also use law codes, referendums and press control.
- **Referendum**: pay 40 gold to ask for a vote of confidence. Once every 10 turns, and the higher public opinion is, the likelier you win (opinion ÷ 100 + 10%, from 10% to 95%). A win gives +12 stability and +10 opinion, a loss gives −12 stability and −12 opinion.
- **Law code**: pay 120 gold and it is finished 6 turns later, giving a permanent −10% rebellion chance and +5% income. It can be done once.
- **Neutrality declaration**: declare neutrality for 12 turns. It can't be declared while at war, and its cooldown is 20 turns. You can't declare war or propose alliances, but income rises 5% and public opinion climbs each peaceful turn. Attacking a neutral country lowers every country's opinion of you. You can also end it early.
- **Press control**: pay 60 gold to control the press for 6 turns. Public opinion falls half as fast during war, but each turn there is an 8% chance of being exposed, which costs 15 opinion and 3 stability and gets reported in the newspaper. The cooldown is 12 turns.
- **Telegraph network**: in scenarios from 1840 on, lay it for 250 gold. Espionage operations run immediately without an agent traveling, and the rebellion chance drops 8%. If an enemy sabotage cuts the line, it is out of use for 5 turns.

## Assimilating occupied lands
- Added in build 97. Land taken by someone other than its original owner starts with low stability. Land that had an owner starts at 10, unowned land starts at 40, and land retaken by its original owner is not affected.
- Occupied land gains 1.5 stability per turn on its own and becomes stable at 100. Below 40 stability, unrest continues, so the territory's income is halved and market and guild effects stop. Below 30, resistance (partisans) is more likely to rise and the land can declare independence after 6 turns instead of 10.
- **Assimilation**: The Assimilation card on the Politics tab lists up to 12 lands, starting with the lowest stability. For 40 gold, that land's stability rises by 6 each turn for 8 turns. Meanwhile residents leave and its troops shrink little by little. AI countries use this policy too.

## Will and succession
- Added in build 77. Monarchy, Empire and Totalitarianism nations have a ruler, and you see the ruler's name and age in the Will section of the Politics tab.
- The ruler ages one year every 12 turns. Past 52, they can die any turn, and the chance rises with age (up to 5% per turn). At 55, a reminder tells you to write a will.
- Name an heir in advance: Prince, General or Council nomination. After naming one, you must wait 6 turns before changing it.
- **Prince**: The bloodline continues and the nation stays steady, but with a young ruler, −6 morale lasts for 6 turns.
- **General**: The general with the highest stat total takes the throne. Morale +8, troop veterancy +4, stability −8. If you have no general, the prince succeeds instead.
- **Council nomination**: One of the council members becomes the new ruler. Public opinion +8, stability −3.
- If the ruler dies without a named heir, a war of succession breaks out. Stability −25, −12 morale for 10 turns, and if you have 3 or more territories, up to 2 break away.
- When the ruler changes, the will is cleared, so you need to name an heir again for the new ruler.
- Bots also write a will once their ruler turns 50.

## Tips for choosing
- If you plan to fight a lot, Empire, Monarchy or Islam help by lowering conscription costs.
- If revolts worry you, try a Parliamentary System or Buddhism to lower revolt chance.
- Pick the same government or religion as a neighbor you want to befriend to get an opinion bonus.
- Under Monarchy, Empire or Totalitarianism, write an heir in your will before your ruler gets old.

crownenvoy/economy-trade.b:
:: Resources = Wood, meat, flour, spices
:: Storehouse cap = 99 of each
:: Building slots = 1 + city level
:: Merchant ship = 50 gold, 3 at a time
:: Trade route = +12 gold per port pair
:: Loan = Repay 1.3x over 6 turns
:: War bonds = Repay 1.4x over 8 turns

Gold builds up from the income your territories produce. This page covers income, resources, buildings and trade.

## How income is calculated
- Each territory has a base income by type (Capital 60, Estate 30, Trade Port 55, Stronghold 20, Mine 62, Granary 38).
- Higher stability means more income (×0.6 at 0 stability, ×1.2 at 100). Restless territories earn half, burned territories earn 0, and blockaded ports earn ×0.7.
- Your government's tax modifier, your nation's income multiplier, embargoes (×0.8 for 1, ×0.65 for 2) and war weariness (−weariness/700) are multiplied in.
- On top of that, you add trade treaties +20, alliances +15, trade routes, market buildings and the imported resource bonus.
- Upkeep (generals 6, diplomats 8, soldiers 0.004) is only paid up to 90% of income.

## 4 resources
In the latest version, there are 4 resources: **wood, meat, flour and spices**. Base prices are wood 8, meat 10, flour 7 and spices 16, and prices swing between 0.55x and 1.8x of base. Your storehouse holds up to 99 of each.
- **Wood**: Comes from all land. Forests produce it every turn, other land every 2 turns. Constructing buildings uses wood.
- **Flour**: Granary buildings make +4 per turn.
- **Meat**: Butcher buildings make +3 per turn.
- **Spices**: Market buildings make +2 per turn.
- Consumption each turn scales with your number of territories (multiplied by 0.4 for flour, 0.25 for meat and 0.15 for spices, rounded up). It stops at 40 territories' worth, so the most that is eaten in one turn is 16 flour, 10 meat and 6 spices. You start with at least 20 wood and about 6 times the required amount of the others.
- If you run out of a resource, morale drops by −5 per missing resource, and each consecutive turn of shortage raises revolt chance by 1 percentage point (up to 30%). If you're short, buy some at the market.

## Buildings (territory slots are 1 + city level)
- **Walls** 150 gold, 6 wood: Defense +0.3
- **Barracks** 180 gold, 6 wood: +60 infantry per turn
- **Shipyard** 200 gold, 8 wood: Trade Ports only. Lets you send up to 4 merchant ships.
- **Granary** 140 gold, 4 wood: Flour +4
- **Butcher** 140 gold, 4 wood: Meat +3
- **Market** 160 gold, 5 wood: Spices +2, +6 gold per turn
- **Workshop** 220 gold, 6 wood: Turns 3 stored resources into 1 finished good that sells for 2.6x the price.
- **Theater** 260 gold, 8 wood: +2 victory points per turn, stronger cultural influence
- **Counterintelligence Office** 200 gold, 5 wood: Enemy espionage success rate −20 percentage points
- **Smithy** 240 gold, 8 wood: conscription cost −7% and unit upgrade cost −10%. Up to 2 can stack.
- **University** 300 gold, 8 wood: tech research speed +10%. Up to 3 can stack.
- **Military Academy** 300 gold, 8 wood: a general stationed here gains +1 in their lowest stat every 6 turns (up to 5). If any one of your territories has an Academy, general hiring costs 25% less. See the Generals & Battles page for details.

## Trade tab
- Buying from the market costs ×1.3 the price, and selling gets ×0.7. Turn on auto-sell and it sells whenever your storehouse goes over 30 (or 15).
- **Exclusive Contract**: Monopolize one resource for 12 turns for 220 gold. Up to 2 at a time.
- **Trading Post**: 150 gold, up to 3. +12 gold per turn for you, +5 gold for the side hosting it.
- **Loan**: Choose 100, 200 or 400 gold. Repay 1.3x over 6 turns.
- **Trade Fair**: Held every 8–14 turns. 40 gold entry fee, +3 victory points, and fair goods sell for 50% more.
- **Trade Agreement**: Exchange 3 units per turn for 8 turns. Up to 4 at a time. **Barter** happens instantly.
- **Imported resource bonus**: +8 gold for each type of resource you import.

## War bonds
- Under Policy in the Map tab you can issue war bonds, drawing on future income to get money right away. Choose 200, 400 or 800 gold, with up to two bonds at a time.
- You repay in installments over 8 turns, 140% in total. If you have enough gold, you can pay off the rest early in one go with a 10% discount.
- Your credit limit scales with income (at least 300 gold). Together with bonds already issued, you can't go over the limit.
- If you can't make a payment, stability drops by 6, trust by 8, and the remaining payments grow by 10%.
- This is separate from the Loan in the Trade tab.

## Trade routes and merchant ships
- +12 gold for each open port pair (up to 3 pairs). Adjusted ±25% by tariff level.
- **Merchant ship**: 50 gold, up to 3 at a time (4 with a shipyard). Travel takes ceil(route length/3) turns, and on arrival it earns 60 + 8×route length. It can be captured by enemy fleets (about 80% without an escort, about 35% with one) or lost to pirates.
- **Privateer**: Hunt enemy merchant ships for 80 gold.
- For **embargoes** and **tariffs**, see the **Diplomacy** page.

## Cultural influence
- For 60 gold, raise your culture value in another nation's territory by +14 (+4 more with a theater, and another +4 if the region is restless).
- The value fades by 1 each turn. At 40 or above, that region becomes restless, and at 100 it switches over to you. Can't be used on capitals or allied territory.

## Population and refugees
- Every territory has a population index (1.0 is normal). In peacetime it slowly grows up to 1.1–1.6 depending on the city level, with +0.1 if there is a granary.
- The population index affects territory income (0.8 + 0.2 × index) and the per-turn conscription limit (0.6 + 0.4 × index). The territory info shows the 'Population index'.
- Territories with battles, sieges, scorched land, plunder or unrest lose population, and the lost people become refugees who flow to safe neighboring territories (never to hostile nations).
- A neighboring nation that takes in refugees earns goodwill from the nation they came from.

## Economy that turns into victory points
- Theaters, trade fairs and historical bonuses (first 5 wins, first 5 techs, etc. give +100 gold and +4 victory points) all feed into victory points. See **Victory & Scoring**.

crownenvoy/technology.b:
:: Menu = Tech tab
:: Research cost = Research points (not gold)
:: Monthly points = At least 3
:: Year limit = Historical templates only
:: Upgrade cost = Minimum 30 gold

In the Tech tab, you pick one tech to research. The cost isn't gold but **research points**. Points build up every month, and once you have enough to cover the cost, the chosen tech is completed.

## Research points
- Monthly points = at least 3; normally (3 + income × 0.02) multiplied by tech bonuses (Protestantism +5%, etc.). Nations with higher income research faster.
- In historical templates, each tech has a set year when it becomes available. Map mode has no such limit.

## Tech list (cost / requirements / effect)
- **Military Drill** 90: Conscription cost −15%
- **Fortification** 110: Fort and trench cost −30%, defense +5%
- **Gunpowder Weapons** 150: Attack +6%. After 1300, requires Military Drill
- **Supply System** 140: Expedition supply range +1. Requires Military Drill
- **Ocean Navigation** 160: Troop losses at sea −40%. After 1400
- **Cuirassiers** 130: Unlocks cavalry upgrade. After 1450, requires Military Drill
- **Field Medicine** 170: Wounded soldiers returning goes from 30% → 45%. After 1800, requires Gunpowder Weapons
- **Railways** 200: Regional conscription limit +25%. After 1830, requires Supply System
- **Rifles** 200: Unlocks infantry upgrade. After 1830, requires Gunpowder Weapons
- **Rifled Artillery** 210: Easier fort sieges and attack +4%. After 1840, requires Gunpowder Weapons and Fortification
- **Steam Fleet** 230: An additional −40% sea attrition, naval combat +8%. After 1850, requires Ocean Navigation
- **Mechanization** 320: Attack +8%, supply range +1. After 1914, requires Railways and Rifled Artillery
- **Air Support** 360: Defense +6%, scouting cost −50%. After 1914, requires Mechanization
- **Tanks** 380: Upgrades cavalry to tanks. After 1930, requires Mechanization
- **Assault Rifles** 340: Unlocks infantry upgrade. After 1935, requires Rifles and Mechanization
- **Self-Propelled Artillery** 360: Unlocks artillery upgrade. After 1935, requires Rifled Artillery and Mechanization

## Unit tiers and upgrades
- Infantry: Infantry → Riflemen → Modern Infantry → Heavy Machine Gunners
- Cavalry: Shock Cavalry → Heavy Cavalry → Mounted Riflemen → Tanks
- Artillery: Catapults → Field Guns → Mortars → Anti-Aircraft Guns
- Moving up a tier requires the matching tech. Infantry goes Gunpowder Weapons → Rifles → Assault Rifles, cavalry goes Cuirassiers → Mechanization → Tanks, and artillery goes Gunpowder Weapons → Rifled Artillery → Self-Propelled Artillery.
- Upgrade cost is (0.02 / 0.035 / 0.055) × unit type modifier per soldier, minimum 30 gold.
- In map mode, every tier can be conscripted. In historical templates, they have to be unlocked with tech.
- Cavalry is strong on flat ground, and machine gunners are strong in trenches and rough terrain.

crownenvoy/generals.b:
:: Hiring a general = 150 gold
:: General cap = Map 4, templates 8
:: General upkeep = 6 gold per turn each
:: Stats = Attack, Defense, Command
:: Traits = 15
:: Rout threshold = Morale below 22
:: General's duel = 3 bouts (Strike, Guard, Opening)

## Generals
- Hiring a general costs 150 gold, with a maximum of 4 in map mode and 8 in historical templates. Each general costs 6 gold per turn.
- In the scenario editor you can set each nation's generals yourself. For details, see **Scenario Editor**.
- **Military Academy**: if any one of your territories has a Military Academy (300 gold, 8 wood), hiring costs 25% less, 113 gold, and a new general starts with +1 in one stat (up to 5). A general stationed in a territory with an Academy gains +1 in their lowest stat every 6 turns (up to 5), as long as the territory is not in unrest.
- Their stats are Attack, Defense and Command. Generals lead troops and make a difference in battle.
- In the attack and move window you pick the leading general with buttons, so the choice doesn't disappear when you scroll the window.
- Command raises army morale. Each stat point gives +6 morale.
- **Training**: Costs 30 × (current stat + 1) gold, and can raise a stat up to 5.
- Fighting battles builds XP. Every 5 points, their lowest stat goes up by +1 (up to 7).
- **Medals**: Earned for winning against the odds or for big victories (enemy losses of 4,000 or more). They go Bronze Star → Silver Star → Gold Star → Platinum Star → Grand Medal, and each medal gives +1 to the lowest stat (up to 8).
- Generals can be assassinated through espionage. An assassination also lowers morale.

## 15 general traits
- **God of the Navy**: +50% attack and +50% defense in naval battles (historical templates only)
- **Ambush**: +80% damage dealt in the first engagement
- **Iron Wall**: −20% damage taken when defending
- **Charisma**: +5 starting morale, lower rout threshold
- **Pursuit**: Extra damage to routing enemies
- **Artillery Warfare**: +35% damage dealt in the first two phases
- **Cavalry Charge**: +50% damage dealt in the decisive phase
- **Maneuver Warfare**: +12% attack modifier
- **Defensive Tactics**: +25% defense modifier (boosts fort and trench effects)
- **Indomitable**: Morale drops less when losing troops (−40%)
- **Army Surgeon**: −10% damage taken in battle
- **Rallying**: +8 morale at the start of battle
- **Blitzkrieg**: +20% damage dealt in every phase
- **Intelligence**: −8 enemy morale at the start of battle
- **Logistics**: −12% conscription cost for the whole nation (while alive)

## Battle calculation summary
- Battles run in 4 phases. The damage ratio for each phase is 0.14 / 0.26 / 0.22 / 0.12.
- A battle doesn't end until 33% of both sides' combined troops have died.
- If morale drops below 22, the army routs (12 with a Charisma general).
- The winner catches an extra 15% of the fleeing side's remaining troops (+15% with the Pursuit trait).
- A general's influence grows with their stats and the era multiplier. The effect coefficient for Attack and Defense stats is 0.14. Veteran troops get up to +30% stronger.
- Terrain, forts, trenches, season and supply all play a part. For seasons, see **Scenarios & Maps**.

## General's duel
- Added in build 75. In a land battle where both sides have a general, the attacking side challenges the other to a duel.
- A duel has 3 bouts. In each bout, each side plays Strike, Guard or Opening. Strike beats Opening, Opening beats Guard and Guard beats Strike, and winning the matchup adds +2 to that bout's score.
- A bout's score is the stat that matches the move (Attack for Strike, Defense for Guard, Command for Opening) plus 0–2. Every 10 XP adds +1 (up to +2), the Ambush trait gives +2 in the first bout, and the Iron Wall trait gives +1 when playing Guard.
- Whoever wins more of the 3 bouts wins. If it's even, the general with the higher stat total wins on points.
- The winner's army gets +8 morale (+11 with a Charisma general), and the loser's army gets −12 morale. The winning general gets +2 XP.
- The losing general has a 10% chance of dying and a 20% chance of being captured. If that happens, the battle is fought without that general.
- Refusing a duel costs the defending army 5 morale.
- In **Standing Orders** under Policy in the Map tab, you set in advance Request duels (Off/On), Accept duels (Refuse/Accept) and the 3-bout duel tactics (Strike, Guard or Opening for bouts 1–3). By default, requesting and accepting are on and the tactics are Strike, Guard, Opening in that order. Orders take effect from the next planning phase.
- Bots challenge to a duel 60% of the time, accept 70% of the time, and pick their moves at random.
- Duel results are shown in the turn log and in the quarterly news that comes every three months.

## A general's fate
- A defeated general has a 20% chance of dying and a 28% chance of being captured when defending. When losing an attack, it's 15% death and 20% capture.
- A captured general can be ransomed back or released. Capturing an enemy general also earns you an achievement.

crownenvoy/espionage.b:
:: Location = Diplomacy tab, Hostile group
:: Limit = Once per turn per nation
:: Success chance = 0.1 to 0.85
:: On failure = −8 trust, −15 opinion
:: Counterintelligence Office = 200 gold, success −20 pp
:: Agent arrival = 1 to 3 turns later

Espionage is in the **Hostile** group of the Diplomacy tab. It costs money, but you can use it even without contact.

## Rules
- You can only do it during the planning phase, once per turn per nation. Only one agent at a time can be heading to the same nation.
- You can't use it on nations you're allied with or that are your vassal or overlord.
- Success chance = operation base + veteran value/400 − target stability/400, kept between 0.1 and 0.85. If the target has planted a double agent on you, it's −25 percentage points, and if the target territory has a Counterintelligence Office, it's −20 percentage points.
- If it fails, your agent is caught. You still lose the gold, plus −8 trust and −15 opinion from the target.

## Agent movement
- When you choose an operation, you pay the gold and an agent sets out. The agent leaves from your territory closest to the destination and moves across the map as a 🕵 icon, and the destination is marked with 🎯.
- Depending on the distance, it arrives 1 to 3 turns later, and the operation is carried out on arrival. Whether it succeeds is also decided on arrival.
- If you have laid a telegraph network (from 1840 on, on the Politics tab), the agent doesn't travel and the operation runs immediately.
- The destination is the territory you chose or the territory where the chosen general is; operations with no chosen target head for the target nation's capital.
- The result of the operation is reported in the newspaper at the start of the turn after it arrives. The Diplomacy window shows agents on the way and the turns left until they arrive.
- If the target nation disappears or becomes your ally, vassal or overlord before the agent arrives, the agent comes back and you get the gold back.

## Choosing a target
- **Incite Revolt**, **Sabotage** and **Burn the Storehouse** let you pick the target territory yourself. You can't pick the capital.
- **Assassinate General** lets you pick the target general yourself.
- Choosing **Auto** lets the game decide. Incite Revolt and Sabotage go first for territories bordering yours, and among those the one with the most troops; Assassinate General goes for the best general.

## Operation types (cost / base success / effect)
- **Disguised Envoy** 90 gold / 60%: Steals 12% of the target's treasury (up to 90 gold).
- **Read the Ledgers** 80 gold / 65%: Peek into the target's situation.
- **Scout Units** 90 gold / 60%: Reveals the target's unit composition.
- **Incite Revolt** 100 gold / 55%: Makes a target territory restless, cuts its troops by 20% and lowers stability by 6.
- **Price Rumor** 110 gold / 55%: Crashes one resource's price by 35%.
- **Sabotage** 120 gold / 50%: Knocks forts and trenches down 1 level each and cuts troops by 15%.
- **Double Agent** 130 gold / 50%: Steals 5% (up to 15 gold) of the target's treasury every turn for 6 turns.
- **Burn the Storehouse** 130 gold / 45%: Halves their stored resources and burns down one building.
- **Steal Orders** 140 gold / 45%: Peek at the target's orders.
- **Assassinate General** 150 gold / 35%: Kills the chosen general (their best general on Auto) and lowers their morale by 6.

## How to defend
- Build a **Counterintelligence Office** (200 gold) to lower the success rate of operations targeting that territory by 20 percentage points.
- Keeping stability high lowers the success rate.

crownenvoy/events.b:
:: World events = Every 6–10 turns
:: Personal events = About 65% chance each turn
:: Choice wait = Up to 90 seconds
:: Coup condition = Stability ≤22, weariness ≥35
:: Wounded return = 30% of casualties, in 2 turns
:: Desertion = 5% of troops if gold negative

## World events (every 6–10 turns)
- Plague, famine, boom, invention and storms can happen.
- Reform, comets and earthquakes only happen in earlier eras.

## Personal events
- Each turn there's about a 65% chance that each nation gets one: famine (gold −40), bumper harvest (+50), plague (troops −6%), riot (stability −12), festival (stability +8, morale +6), trade boom (+25).
- Events with choices pause the timer for up to 90 seconds until a decision is made.

## Social phenomena
- **Plague**: Breaks out now and then in ports and big cities. The Field Medicine tech reduces the damage.
- **Resistance (partisans)**: Rise up in occupied land.
- **Coups**: Can happen when stability is 22 or below and war weariness is 35 or above.
- **War of succession**: Happens under Monarchy, Empire or Totalitarianism when the ruler dies without a named heir. It brings stability −25, a morale drop and territories breaking away (see Will and succession on the Politics & Religion page).
- **Council demands**: Depending on your government, the council makes a demand every 6–12 turns. Accepting gives +5 morale; refusing raises the revolt chance for 6 turns.
- **Independence**: Land occupied for a long time declares independence.
- **Refugees** and **wounded**: 30% of casualties return as wounded soldiers after 2 turns.
- **Revolts**: The chance changes with stability, politics, religion and resource shortages. Consecutive shortages raise the revolt chance.
- If your gold goes negative, 5% of your troops desert.

## Historical events
- In historical templates, events happen at set times. They're organized by era on the **Templates** page.
- For events with choices, only the player of that nation gets the decision window. The AI follows the default choice.

crownenvoy/naval-warfare.b:
:: Fleet = Troops in a sea zone
:: Losses at sea = 1–5% per turn (by era)
:: Landing losses = Extra 10–25%
:: Blockade = Port income −30%
:: Merchant capture = About 80%, 35% with escort
:: Shipyard = Trade Ports only, 4 ships

## Fleets and the sea
- Troops in a sea zone are your fleet. You don't build ships separately; you send troops into sea zones.
- Sea zones can be crossed without a treaty by nations that aren't at war with each other.
- On maps where the sea matters, like Archipelago (62 islands, 52 sea zones), Continent (31 sea zones) and East Asia, naval battles can decide the game.

## Troop losses at sea
- While at sea, you lose 1–5% of your troops each turn, depending on the era.
- The **Ocean Navigation** and **Steam Fleet** techs each cut this by −40%.
- Landings cost an extra 10–25% in losses.
- The **God of the Navy** trait boosts both attack and defense in naval battles.
- In the Age of Discovery template, the Aztecs, Maya and Inca can't go to sea.

## Ports and blockades
- A **Trade Port** is a territory with 55 income and 2 victory points. Each open trade route between ports gives +12 gold.
- A blockaded port loses 30% of its income.
- A **Shipyard** can only be built in Trade Ports and raises your merchant ship cap to 4.
- Merchant ships can be captured by pirates or enemy fleets. An escort drops the capture chance from about 80% to 35%. See **Economy & Trade** for details.
- **Colonization** can be done on unowned land next to your territory or fleet.

crownenvoy/victory-scoring.b:
:: Missions = 3 per nation
:: Decisive victory = Complete all missions
:: Solo victory = 50% of land, 3 turns in a row
:: Coalition victory = 60% of land, 3 turns in a row
:: Capturing a capital = +6 victory points
:: Map default length = 60 turns

## Missions and victory points
- Each nation gets 3 **Missions**. You can see them in the Goals tab.
- Every mission you complete gives a big boost to your victory points. Point values are adjusted to the game length.
- Territories give victory points every turn by type (Capital, Trade Port, Stronghold, Mine 2; Estate, Granary 1).
- Capturing a capital gives +6, a successful mediation +4, destroying an enemy in a joint war +5, joining a trade fair +3, and theaters give +2 per turn. Completing a wonder gives +5. A government in exile that retakes its old territory gets +6.
- Be the first to achieve a **historical first** (first 5 wins, first 5 techs, etc.) for +100 gold and +4 victory points.

## Victory conditions
- **Decisive victory**: Complete all your missions and the game ends right away.
- **Solo victory**: Hold 50% of all land for 3 turns in a row to win. Your victory points become ×1.5 plus 10.
- **Coalition victory**: Nations linked by alliances hold 60% of all land for 3 turns in a row.
- The game also ends on a **conquest victory** or when **everyone is allied**.
- **Time's up**: When the set number of turns ends, victory points decide it. Rankings compare performance relative to starting size (victory points ÷ (base victory points × rounds)), so small nations get a fair shot too.
- Scenarios made in the Scenario Editor can set up to 3 victory conditions from among holding N territories, collecting N gold, surviving N turns and capturing a specific nation's capital, and you win by achieving any one of them. Details are on the Scenario Editor page.
- When the game ends, a brass fanfare plays once if you won, and a slow piano piece if you lost.

## Game length
- Map mode defaults to 60 turns. When creating a room, you can also pick 36, 72 or 120 turns, or unlimited.
- Default template lengths are on the **Scenarios & Maps** page.

crownenvoy/multiplayer-rooms.b:
:: Room code = 5 characters
:: Seats = 3 (up to 6 with added AIs)
:: Spectators = Up to 12
:: Planning time = Fixed at 50 seconds
:: Start countdown = 5 s if full, otherwise 20 s
:: Undo & saving = Solo play only

## Creating and joining rooms
- Create a room in **Private Play** to get a 5-character code. Friends join with the code.
- Private room codes are linked to the hub's friend invites. When a friend who got the invite as a hub notification taps it, they join right away within 30 minutes.
- There are 3 seats by default. In private rooms and vs AI, the host can add up to 5 AIs, and the room grows to as many as 6 seats if needed. Online play stays at 3 seats. Empty seats are filled by AI.
- Up to 12 spectators can watch without taking a seat.
- Room settings are map or template, and game length. Planning time can't be set; it's fixed at 50 seconds.
- Once 2 or more people are in, the start countdown begins: 5 seconds if all seats are full, 20 seconds otherwise.
- **Online Play** finds a room automatically, and AI fills any empty seats.

## Turn flow
- Once every player clicks Confirm Plan, the turn moves on right away. AI always counts as ready.
- If there's an event that needs a choice, the timer pauses and waits for up to 90 seconds.
- In map mode, starting sites are picked in snake order, 5 each: 30 seconds for the first pick, 10 seconds after that.
- In templates, you have 90 seconds to pick a nation.
- The turn clock doesn't slow down even if the host's screen is in the background.

## Not available in multiplayer
- Undo and saving only work in solo play.

## AI personalities and names
- Tap a name in the lobby's AI row to add that AI right away. Each personality has a fixed name, and there is no button for changing personalities. AIs already added are greyed out and can't be picked again.
- **Alfred** (Expansionist): declares war first whenever he sees a chance and expands his territory.
- **Beatrice** (Trade-focused): grows her money with trade offers, merchant ships and new buildings.
- **Karl** (Politics-focused): strengthens his country from within by managing public opinion and the noble factions.
- **Delphine** (Defensive): builds forts, guards her capital and borders, and rarely strikes first.
- **Edgar** (Total war): raises troops with war bonds and full mobilization and fights several countries at once. He's slow to accept a truce.
- **Fiona** (Diplomatic): proposes alliances and non-aggression pacts, and fights only when she's clearly stronger.
- **Gabriel** (Balanced): reads the situation and picks whichever of the other personalities' behaviors fits best.

## AI on the diplomacy screen
- AI kingdoms that weren't added in the lobby (such as the countries in a template) get a personality that suits the country, like Conqueror, Defender, Diplomat, Seafarer, Avenger or Opportunist.
- In templates, each nation shows a difficulty (Easy, Normal, Hard).
- AI never targets the same empty land as another AI at the same time. When attacking, it takes into account technology, proficiency, morale and even allied troops stationed there, which cuts down on hopeless attacks.
- When targeting empty land, it sends enough troops, taking neighboring nations' armies into account. If there's no empty land left or it's far ahead in troops, it declares war more often.

crownenvoy/scenario-editor.b:
:: Location = Scenario Editor in the lobby
:: Strength multiplier = 0.4 / 0.7 / 1 / 1.5 / 2 / 3
:: Relations = War, alliance, non-aggression, vassal
:: Territory setup = City, Fort and Buildings tool
:: Saved in = Your browser
