- The only night-only monsters are slimes on the Starting Island and Forest Islands. They disappear during the day.
- Wolves on Forest Islands can appear during the day too (35% by day, 70% at night).
- Deserts have scorpions, volcanoes have Fire Spirits, jungles have spiders, mesas have snakes, Stone Islands have golems, mangroves have crocodiles, and ice has yetis.
- No monsters spawn on the Village Island.
- The number of monsters at once is close to 2 + player count, capped at 5–6.

## Raids

- Night Raids happen at a low chance per player, and when one hits, 8 monsters spawn nearby.
- During a raid, the elite chance goes up from 12% to 30%.

beaconfall/bosses.b:
:: Island bosses = 8
:: HP range = 70–150
:: Highest HP = Rock Giant (150)
:: Enrage = At 50% HP or below
:: Respawn = 2 days later
:: Recommended rune = Fire (+30% damage)
:: Final boss = Void Lord (700 HP)

Every boss follows the same rules. A warning (wind-up) appears before each pattern. When a boss enrages at 50% HP or below, new patterns unlock, its chase speed goes up x1.25 and the gaps between patterns get shorter. Patterns marked with an asterisk below only appear while enraged.

## Common rules

- Bosses appear when you get within about 55% of the island's radius from its center.
- After you defeat one, it comes back 2 days later.
- Rewards include 3–5 rolls on the treasure table on top of the boss's own drops.
- Each time you defeat an island boss, it drops its own relic (8 kinds, such as the Wolf King's Relic and the Scorpion's Relic). Relics are the materials for summoning the Void Lord; the dungeon level 5 boss gives no relic.

## Pattern glossary

- **Dash** (dash): 0.75-second warning, length 140. The long dash (dashL) is 0.9 seconds and 230, and the short dash (dashS) is 0.6 seconds and 110.
- **Slam** (slam): Radius 38, empowered version (slamB) 54
- **Leap** (leap): Radius 32, empowered version 48
- **Shockwave** (ring): An expanding ring
- **Falling attack** (rain): Attacks that drop from above. From smallest: rainS 3, rain 5, rainM 7, and boulders 9 projectiles.
- **Ice spikes** (lane): 7 spikes erupt one after another.
- **Summon** (summon): 3 wolves, 3 spiders or 2 crocodiles. Up to 6 summons at once, +1 when enraged.
- **Burrow** (burrow): Erupts in a radius of 30 after 1.9 seconds.
- **Cone** (cone): Radius 50
- **Beam** (beam): Length 210
- **Zones** (zones): Poison, fire or earth patches that last 7 seconds and deal 0.45x damage every 0.6 seconds.
- **Aura** (aura): 4 seconds, radius 64

## Wolf King (Forest Island)

- 70 HP, 3 damage. Drops: 3–5 bones, 3–5 resin
- Patterns: Dash, wolf summon, cone, long dash when enraged
- Strategy: The dash warning is short, so sidestep it. Take out the summoned wolves first.

## Giant Scorpion (Desert Island)

- 80 HP, 3 damage. Drops: 5–8 cactus fiber
- Patterns: Burrow, cone, small falling attack, zones when enraged
- Strategy: It poisons, so bring both an Antidote and Cactus Juice.

## Fire Giant (Volcanic Island)

- 140 HP, 3.5 damage. Drops: 4–6 volcanic rock, 4–6 ash
- Patterns: Shockwave, medium falling attack, empowered slam, zones when enraged
- Strategy: With burning and heat, a Fire Resistance Potion is practically a must.

## Venom Spider Queen (Jungle Island)

- 90 HP, 2.5 damage. Drops: 4–6 rubber
- Patterns: Beam, spider summon, leap, zones when enraged
- Strategy: Watch the beam's direction and move to the side. You'll need an Antidote.

## Sand Serpent (Mesa Island)

- 80 HP, 3 damage. Drops: 6–9 clay
- Patterns: Long dash, slam, beam, burrow when enraged
- Strategy: The long dash covers 230, so dodge far away right from the start.

## Rock Giant (Stone Island)

- 150 HP, 4 damage. Drops: 4–6 crystal, 6–10 stone
- Patterns: Empowered leap, falling boulders, shockwave, empowered slam when enraged
- Strategy: It has the most HP. An Ironskin Potion and good armor help.

## Swamp Croc King (Mangrove Island)

- 100 HP, 4 damage. Drops: 3–5 leather, 4–6 mangrove roots
- Patterns: Short dash, slam, zones, crocodile summon, leap when enraged
- Strategy: Short dashes and slams come often. Keep your distance.

## Great Yeti (Ice Island)

- 120 HP, 4 damage. Drops: 5–8 frost shards, 3–5 bones
- Patterns: Aura, ice spikes, leap, shockwave when enraged
- Strategy: The aura is wide, with a radius of 64. You'll need a full leather set because of the cold.

## Ghost Ship (night sea)

- 110 HP, 2.5 damage. Patterns: Shockwave, medium falling attack, falling attack, falling boulders when enraged
- Rewards are 2–3 crystal, 2–4 gold ingots, 1–3 pearls and the treasure table.

## Sky Guardian (sky fortress)
- 299 HP (1.15 times the base 260), 4.5 damage. It appears only in the throne room of the sky fortress, and looks like a winged armored knight.
- Patterns: Ice spikes, shockwave, empowered leap, medium falling attack, beam, zones and falling boulders when enraged
- Rewards: 5–7 crystal, 5–7 gold ingots and 2 pearls, plus its usual drop (2–3 crystal) and the treasure table.
- After you defeat it, it returns 3 days later. That differs from the 2 days of island bosses.
- Defeating it for the first time earns the Lord of the Sky achievement. See the Sky Fortress page for details.

## Dungeon level 5 boss

See the Dungeon page. It's one of the Rock Giant, Fire Giant, Great Yeti or Venom Spider Queen, decided by the seed.

## Void Lord (final boss)
- It appears when you use the Void Core made from the 8 relics at night and survive the ritual. It has 700 HP and 5.5 attack, and at 75, 50 and 25% HP it raises a barrier and calls 4 minions. See the Void Lord & True Ending page for the full guide.

## Tips

- Before a boss fight, bring Strength, Ironskin and a Full Course.
- Restore your durability at an Anvil before taking on a boss.
- Among runes, Fire raises damage by 30%, which is great for boss fights.

beaconfall/dungeon.b:
:: Levels = 5 (+ undersea level)
:: Level size = 40x40 tiles
:: Rooms = Up to 9 per level
:: Level 5 boss = 1 of 4, set by seed
:: Level reset = Every 3 days
:: Party revive = Within 45 seconds

The dungeon has 5 levels (plus a 6th undersea level if there's room). Each level is 40x40 tiles with up to 9 rooms, and has stairs going up and down.

## Entrance

- The dungeon cave entrance is on the island closest to the start (usually the Starting Island), away from the camp. We haven't confirmed whether it's always the Starting Island.

## Monsters by level

1. Level 1: Spiders, snakes
2. Level 2: Spiders, snakes, wolves
3. Level 3: Wolves, golems, scorpions
4. Level 4: Golems, Fire Spirits, yetis
5. Level 5: Golems, Fire Spirits, crocodiles, yetis

- Monster HP is 1 + 0.22 x (level - 1) times normal.
- The elite chance is 10% + 5% x level, with 2.5x HP.

## Chests

- 3 chests in the last room (5 on level 5)
- Other rooms have a 75% chance of 1
- Contents are ore, materials and coins (8 + 10 x level + 0–19).

## Level resets

If nobody is on a level, it's regenerated every 3 days.

## Level 5 boss

- One of the Rock Giant, Fire Giant, Great Yeti or Venom Spider Queen, decided by the seed.
- It has 1.15x HP.
- After you defeat it, it comes back 3 days later.
- Rewards: 3–4 crystal, 3–5 gold ingots, treasure table (once per player present, up to 3 times)

## Party revive

In the dungeon, a downed player can be revived by a teammate within 45 seconds. They come back with half HP. If no teammate is on the same level, it's a normal death.

## Reef diving

- Take a boat near a whirlpool and press F to dive. You need **Diving Gear**.
- Oxygen lasts 60 seconds, or 150 seconds with a Breathing Potion. If you run out of oxygen, you take 3 damage and surface.
- Reef chests contain coral, pearls, crystal, gold ingots, Breathing Potions, rubber and 30–69 coins.
- There's an undersea exploration achievement.

## Preparation

- Healing Potions, Full Course, Ironskin, Strength
- Iron-tier or better gear and armor
- A good bow and a few dozen arrows

## Level layout in detail

- Each level is 40x40 tiles with up to 9 rooms, plus stairs going up and stairs going down.
- The 6th undersea level only appears if there's room.
- Monsters on each level come from the list above. Golems show up from level 3, so bring Ironskin Potions.

## Clearing order

1. Levels 1 and 2 have spiders and snakes, so prepare for poison (Antidotes) before going in.
2. Level 3 mixes wolves, golems and scorpions. Keep your distance with a bow.
3. Levels 4 and 5 have Fire Spirits (burning) and yetis. Bring Fire Resistance Potions.
4. The last room on level 5 has 5 chests and the boss.

## Elite chance breakdown

- Level 1 15%, level 2 20%, level 3 25%, level 4 30%, level 5 35% (10% + 5% x level)
- Elites have 2.5x normal HP and drop gold ingots.
- Monster HP multiplier: level 1 x1, level 2 x1.22, level 3 x1.44, level 4 x1.66, level 5 x1.88

## Chest coins

- The deeper the level, the more coins in chests (base 8 + a value that scales with level + 0–19).

## Achievements

- Going Underground, Bottom of the Abyss (level 5) and Undersea Exploration are the dungeon achievements.

beaconfall/villages-trading.b:
:: Village NPCs = 6
:: Cottages = 3, 350 coins each
:: Prosperity ranks = 5
:: Max discount = 20% (Village Benefactor)
:: Haggling patience = 3
:: Trading Post buyers = NPCs

The Village Island is a safe island with no monsters. One of the Forest Islands becomes the village, with NPCs, shops and cottages.

You can also build Villager Houses on your own island and grow a settlement of your own. See the Settlement & Villagers page.

## Village NPCs

- **Bor the Blacksmith**: Gear and ingots
- **Mina the Farmer**: Seeds, food, carts, horses
- **Toby the Shopkeeper**: Basic materials and furniture
- **Haru the Sailor**: Boats, fishing rods, potions, runs the fishing tournament
- **Ria the Librarian**: Recipe books
- **Dowin the Village Chief**: Village prosperity and daily bonus

## Shop lists (prices in coins)

- Bor: Iron Longsword 110, Iron Pickaxe 110, Iron Axe 100, Iron Bow 100 / Gold Longsword 340, Gold Pickaxe 340, Gold Bow 320 / bundle of 8 arrows 16 / bundle of 6 feather arrows 54 / iron, copper and zinc ingots 30, gold ingot 90
- Mina: Seeds 8, sapling 10, bread 14, stew 36, milk 12, grilled fish 22, egg 8, string 6, cart 250 (Resident rank or higher), horse 500 (Neighbor rank or higher)
- Toby: Planks 5, bundle of 2 branches 2, bundle of 4 stone 5, log 4, leather 14, string 6, chest 30, bed 60
- Haru: Boat 240, Island Map 140, fishing rods 40, 130 and 400, Fire Resistance Potion 120, Antidote 40, Cactus Juice 30, bundle of 18 arrows 8

## Buying books (Ria the Librarian)

- Intro to Mechanical Engineering 150
- Signals & Circuits 220
- Gourmet Cookbook 90
- Compression Alchemy 180
- Books have to be bought separately for each save (world).

## Cottages

- There are 3, at 350 coins each. Buying one makes its bed your respawn point.

## Prosperity

As your prosperity score goes up, your rank goes up.

- Visitor 0, Resident 100, Neighbor 300, Honorary Resident 700, Village Benefactor 1500
- Purchase discounts: Visitor 0%; Resident, Neighbor and Honorary Resident 10%; Village Benefactor 20%
- Selling bonus: Honorary Resident +10%, Village Benefactor +15%
- Village chief's daily bonus coins: Neighbor 20, Honorary Resident 20, Village Benefactor 50
- Your score goes up from donating coins (1 point per coin), buying (money spent / 15), selling (money earned / 30) and donating items.

## Haggling

- You can haggle with merchants, and it resets daily. They have 3 patience.
- Asking for 10%, 20% or 30% off succeeds 70%, 45% or 25% of the time, varying slightly by merchant and prosperity rank.

## Selling prices

- Fish: 4, 10, 24 and 60 by tier
- Ingots: 12–36
- Crystal: 40

## Wandering merchants

- **Merchant Ship**: Arrives near the camp dock every 3 days after 7 AM. Bring it the items it wants and it gives rewards based on rarity.
- **Wandering Market (Kuro)**: Opens every 3 days on a random island other than the Village and Pirate Islands. It offers 7 random picks from 18 rare items, and buys fish at 1.5x.

## Player trading facilities

- **Trading Post**: Every 25 seconds, an NPC customer comes by and buys stocked goods at 1.15x x a distance multiplier (up to 1.8). Up to 6 item types, 300 stock and 3000 coins in stored cash. The farther away you build it, the more you earn. Unlike what the older pages said, it sells to NPCs, not other players.
- **Market Stall**: Sells to other players. Up to 6 item types, 99 of each; the default price is 1.5x the selling price, and you can change it yourself.
- **Mailbox**: Up to 10 letters, 60 characters each, up to 3 gift types. Delivery takes 15–240 seconds (depending on distance), and only the owner can read them.
- **Guestbook Stone**: Up to 12 entries, 40 characters, one per name

## Cargo Port

- Made from 1 boat, 1 Circuit Board and 2 Reinforced Brass Plates (requires Intro to Mechanical Engineering).
- A ship carries cargo fed in by conveyor to another Cargo Port on the same frequency.
- About halfway through the trip, pirates attack and take half the cargo. A Guard Post (needs 5 arrows loaded) or insurance prevents this.
- Guard Posts have 110 range and deal 4 damage.

## Coin-earning tips

- When you visit the Village Island, claim your Journal rewards and join the fishing tournament.
- Smelting ore into ingots adds a lot of value.
- Try haggling before making unnecessary purchases.

beaconfall/transportation.b:
:: Walking speed = 50
:: Horse = x1.9, 500 coins
:: Boat = Speed 80, 240 coins
:: Cart = 21 slots, 250 coins
:: Hot air balloon = 120-second flight
:: Ghost Ship = Night sea, 55% per day

Here's how to get between islands, plus the events that roam the world.

## Walking and speed

- Walking speed 50
- River water x0.6, mangrove x0.8
- Swiftness Potion +15%
- Horse x1.9, cart x0.92, boat 80, hot air balloon 72

## Boats

- Made from 5 planks and 2 iron ingots (also sold in the village for 240 coins).
- Hold it and press Shift at the water's edge to board. Press Shift or F to get off.

## Horses and carts

- Ride a horse with Shift. 500 coins from Mina the farmer (Neighbor rank or higher).
- Pull a cart with Shift. Carts have 21 slots. 250 coins (Resident rank or higher).

## Hot air balloons

- Flies for 120 seconds. Land with Shift.
- Up in the sky you'll see floating islands with waterfalls, sky whales, flocks of birds and thick clouds.
- There's one cloud treasure floating in the sky above each island. Take it and the same one reappears 2 days later.
- A sky fortress also floats up there. Reach its gate with the balloon and you go inside. See the Sky Fortress page.
- Rewards are the treasure table and 15–44 coins, with a 40% chance of a pearl too.

## Whirlpool reefs

Take a boat to a whirlpool and press F to dive in with Diving Gear. See the Dungeon page.

## Ghost Ship

- Appears at sea near players at night with a 55% chance each day.
- 110 HP. Defeat it for crystal, gold ingots, pearls and the treasure table.
- There's a "Ghost Ship Hunter" achievement.

## Merchant Ship and Wandering Market

- Every 3 days, a merchant ship comes to the camp dock to barter.
- A Wandering Market also opens somewhere every 3 days. Check its location on the map.

## Pirates

- They live on the Pirate Island. They're not monsters that roam the sea.
- If you ship cargo through a Cargo Port, pirates may attack it.

## Weather

- There's clear weather, rain and storms. Rain makes crops grow faster.

## The daily clock

- A day is 720 seconds, starting at 8 AM.
- It starts getting dark at 6 PM, and night runs from 8 PM to 5 AM.
- You can only sleep roughly between 7 PM and 6 AM.

## Travel tips

- Open the map to check the islands and explore them one at a time.

## Ride comparison

- Walking 50, horse x1.9 (about 95), cart x0.92, boat 80, hot air balloon 72.
- Horses and boats are best for long trips, and carts are best for hauling stuff.
- Swiftness Potions only give +15% to walking speed.

## Use cases

- For your first voyage, take a boat to a nearby island. It unlocks the First Voyage achievement.
- Gallop on a horse to earn the Rider achievement.
- With a hot air balloon, you have to find the cloud treasure and land within 120 seconds.

## Beware the night sea

- Ghost ships can appear at night, so gear up before sailing after dark.
- Defeating a ghost ship gets you crystal, gold ingots and pearls.

beaconfall/beacon-escape.b:
:: Ultimate goal = Escape via the Beacon
:: Required books = 2, 400 coins total
:: Iron ore = 294
:: Gold ore = 252
:: Calling time = 60 seconds
:: Spaceship stay = 180 seconds

The ultimate goal of the game is to build a **Beacon**, call a spaceship and escape the islands. It takes a huge amount of materials, so expect a long build-up.

Separately from the beacon escape, there's also a true ending: collect the eight bosses' relics and defeat the final boss, the Void Lord. See the Void Lord & True Ending page.

## Beacon recipe

- 2 Circuit Crystals + 2 Compressed Reinforced Gold Plates + 2 Ultra-Long-Range Signal Devices + 1 Sonic Wave Device

The sub-components are as follows.

- Circuit Crystal: 2 Circuit Fragments + 5 Circuit Boards (including slot layout)
- Ultra-Long-Range Signal Device: 4 Compressed Reinforced Iron Plates + 3 Remote Signalers
- Sonic Wave Device: 6 Compressed Reinforced Brass Plates + 1 Bell
- Bell: 3 copper ingots + 1 branch
- Remote Signaler: 2 Circuit Fragments
- Circuit Board: 2 Circuit Fragments + 3 Reinforced Gold Plates
- Circuit Fragment: 2 brass + 2 crystal
- Brass: 2 from 1 copper ingot + 1 zinc ingot

## Required books

- Signals & Circuits (220 coins) and Compression Alchemy (180 coins) are both essential. That's 400 coins total.

## Total raw materials (calculated)

- 294 iron ore, 252 gold ore, 72 crystal, 50 copper, 47 zinc, 1 branch
- Intermediate crafts: 42 Reinforced Iron, 6 Compressed Reinforced Iron, 8 Compressed Reinforced Iron Plates (2 crafts), 36 Reinforced Gold (15 for plates, 21 for compression), 2 Compressed Reinforced Gold Plates, 3 Compressed Reinforced Brass, 6 Compressed Reinforced Brass Plates, 93 brass (47 crafts), 36 Circuit Fragments, 10 Circuit Boards, 2 Circuit Crystals, 6 Remote Signalers, 2 Ultra-Long-Range Signal Devices, 1 Bell, 1 Sonic Wave Device
- Copper and zinc are needed in smaller amounts than the other ores. Make use of Stone Islands (rich in zinc) and Mesa Islands (copper).
- Smelting 294 iron ore at 3 seconds each takes almost 15 minutes. Set up several Smelters and run them in parallel.
- Automation (Auto Miners, conveyors, sorters) makes it much easier.

## Calling the ship

1. Place the Beacon and interact with it.
2. Calling: 60 seconds
3. Landing: 6 seconds
4. The spaceship stays for 180 seconds.
5. Takeoff: 6 seconds
- Removing the Beacon cancels the call.
- The spaceship lands at the Beacon's x coordinate + 66.
- Press F near the landed spaceship to escape. You can keep playing even after escaping.

## Achievements

- Build a Beacon
- Escape Successful

## Automation basics

- **Auto Logger and Auto Miner**: The material of the axe or pickaxe used to craft them sets their speed. They work on the adjacent 3x3 tiles.
- Work time: logging is 3 seconds per tree x material multiplier; mining is the required amount by rock type (3, 3, 4, 5, 4, 5) x material multiplier.
- **Overload**: Each material has a max number of operations (30, 40, 50, 70, 75, 80, 90, 84, 100). Place a **Controller** next to it and toggle it off and on to reset.
- **Conveyor Belt**: Speed 16. Rotate with F; for sorters, press Ctrl to switch the sort side and right-click to set the item. Lock the direction with Glue.
- **Signal devices**: Combine clocks, meters, remote signalers, bells and more to send signals. For details, see the Automation Guide and Signals & Circuits pages.

## Tips

- Don't try to build the Beacon all at once; stockpile parts step by step.
- If circuits or brass drop from chests, grab them first.
- In multiplayer, splitting up the mining makes it much faster.

beaconfall/achievements.b:
:: Achievement count = 60
:: View = J key
:: Categories = 7
:: Largest category = Exploration (14)
:: Sandbox = a world where sandbox was turned on at least once does not earn achievements
:: Final achievement = All Achievements
:: Achievement rewards = 5~50 bC

Achievements can be viewed separately from the journal by pressing the J key. There are 60 achievements in total, and the All Achievements achievement is earned by completing all the others, excluding itself.

## Exploration (14)

- First Landing: Discover a new island for the first time
- Around the World: Discover all islands
- Ruin Explorer: Visit the ruins on every island
- First Voyage: Go out to sea by boat
- Treasure Hunter: Open a treasure chest for the first time
- Treasure Collector: Open every treasure chest
- Ten Islands: Discover 10 islands
- Sky Journey: Ride a hot air balloon
- Rider: Ride and gallop a horse
- Underground: Enter the dungeon
- Bottom of the Abyss: Reach floor 5 of the dungeon
- Seabed Exploration: Enter the seabed ruins with diving gear
- Sky Fortress: Enter the Sky Fortress by hot air balloon
- Master of the Sky: Defeat the Sky Fortress guardian

## Combat (8)

- First Hunt, Monster Index (defeat every type), Boss Slayer (first boss), Legendary Hunter (all bosses), Veteran (100 kills), Ghost Ship Hunter, Grenadier (throw a potion), Rune Engraver

## Crafting (9)

- Gold Artisan: Make reinforced gold
- Reinforcement Master: Make reinforced wood, reinforced iron, reinforced copper, and reinforced gold
- Repairman: Repair with an anvil and hammer
- Master Smith: Forge ★★★ armor
- Armor Artisan: Forge helmet, chestplate, greaves, and boots
- Fully Armored: Equip armor in 4 slots
- Cold Weather Prep: Walk the Ice island in a full set of leather
- First Alchemy: Make a potion in the alchemy pot
- Grand Alchemist: Discover all alchemy pot combinations

## Automation (6)

- Circuit Technician (make a circuit device), Start of Automation (install a conveyor), Sorting Expert (install a sorter), Auto Crafting (auto-crafting device), Sending a Signal (ring a bell with a meter signal), Overload Solved (reset with a control device)

## Survival (10)

- Good Sleep: Spend a night in a bed
- First Trade
- Farmer: Plant wheat, potatoes, and corn
- Legendary Angler: Catch a legendary-rated fish
- Fishing Index: Every fish
- One Month Survival (30 days), Hundred Day Survival (100 days)
- Ranch Owner: Tame animals
- Hearty Meal: Eat a food that gives an effect
- Fishing Tournament Champion: Win first place

## Together (3)

- Rescue Team (revive a fallen companion), Letter Home (mailbox), Guestbook (leave a message on a gravestone)

## Special (10)

- Build a Signal Flare, Escape Successful
- Relic Collection Begins: Obtain a boss relic piece for the first time
- Eight Relics: Collect the relic pieces of all eight bosses
- Core of the Void: Make the Core of the Void
- Beyond the Void: Defeat the Void Lord and see the true ending
- First Resident: Welcome the first resident into a residence
- Small Village: Live with 4 residents
- Settlement Complete: Live with 8 residents
- All Achievements

## BeaCoin Rewards

When you earn an achievement, you receive 5~50 bC in BeaCoin depending on its difficulty. The amount is shown in the achievement window (J) and in the unlock notification. Easy achievements give 5 bC, and harder ones such as bosses, escape, and the true ending give more, while All Achievements gives 50 bC. Earning all 60 achievements totals 965 bC.
- 5 bC (10): First Landing, First Voyage, Treasure Hunter, First Hunt, Grenadier, Good Sleep, First Trade, Hearty Meal, Letter Home, Guestbook
- 10 bC (16): Sky Journey, Rider, Underground, Seabed Exploration, Rune Engraver, Gold Artisan, Repairman, Cold Weather Prep, First Alchemy, Circuit Technician, Start of Automation, Sorting Expert, Sending a Signal, Farmer, Ranch Owner, Rescue Team
- 15 bC (11): Sky Fortress, Boss Slayer, Ghost Ship Hunter, Reinforcement Master, Master Smith, Fully Armored, Auto Crafting, Overload Solved, Legendary Angler, Relic Collection Begins, First Resident
- 20 bC (11): Ruin Explorer, Treasure Collector, Ten Islands, Bottom of the Abyss, Veteran, Armor Artisan, Grand Alchemist, One Month Survival, Fishing Tournament Champion, Core of the Void, Small Village
- 25 bC (4): Around the World, Master of the Sky, Monster Index, Fishing Index
- 30 bC (6): Legendary Hunter, Hundred Day Survival, Build a Signal Flare, Escape Successful, Eight Relics, Settlement Complete
- 40 bC (1): Beyond the Void
- 50 bC (1): All Achievements
- BeaCoin is spent in the skin shop. See the skin shop document for details.

## Statistics

The statistics window shows play time, longest survival, distance walked and sailed, trees chopped, rocks mined, items crafted, blocks placed, monsters and bosses defeated, fish caught, and number of deaths.

## Sandbox

In a world where sandbox has been turned on at least once, achievements do not increase (build 100). This applies not only to the world that is currently on, but also to worlds where it was turned on and then off, so each world remembers separately whether sandbox was ever enabled. When you start playing in such a world, a notice appears once saying "Achievements do not increase in worlds where sandbox was ever enabled." Worlds you already made can be switched with the Sandbox On/Off button in the world list, but once you turn it on, the achievements for that world are blocked even if you turn it off. To earn achievements, play in a world where sandbox has never been turned on.

## Tips for Earning

- The Monster Index requires defeating all 9 monster types in the seed: Slime, Wolf, Scorpion, Fire Spirit, Spider, Serpent, Golem, Crocodile, and Yeti.
- Legendary Hunter requires defeating all 8 island bosses.
- The Together achievements need conditions such as multiplayer, or placing a mailbox or gravestone.
- For the relic and void achievements, see the Void Lord and True Ending document. For the resident achievements, see the Settlement and Residents documents.

beaconfall/multiplayer.b:
:: Method = P2P (PeerJS, WebRTC)
:: Server role = Host's browser
:: Room address = 3~24 characters
:: Player limit = No fixed limit
:: Chat = T key
:: Dungeon revive = within 45 seconds

You can play together with friends in the same world. Rooms use P2P (PeerJS, WebRTC), and the host's browser acts as the server.

## Opening a Room

1. Choose a world and press "Open room with my world."
2. Set the room address with "Create address." It uses lowercase letters, numbers, hyphens, and underscores, and is 3~24 characters. It must start with a letter or a number.
3. You cannot open two rooms with the same address at the same time.
4. Give the address to your friend.
5. You can also copy a link (game address ?join=room address) using the **Copy Invite Link** button in the host's multiplayer window and send it. When copying succeeds, the Copy Address and Copy Invite Link buttons change their label to "Copied ✓".

## Joining

- Enter the address to join.
- If you open an invite link, you join that room right after logging in.
- Enter the room address in the input field on the site's home screen and press **Join Room** to join immediately.
- From the friend list of the Frenchfries777 account, you can join without an address.
- Next to friends who are online there is a **Join Request** button. If a friend who has not opened a room **accepts**, the world the friend was playing opens as a room (random address isle-xxxx), and the requester joins right away. If the friend has an open room, you enter that room immediately.
- If the friend declines or is in another room, a notice "Join request was not accepted" appears. The request shows as "Requested" for 30 seconds.
- The **Invite** button is always visible next to online friends. If there is no room, one is opened and the invite is sent right away.
- When you open a room, the room code is linked to the hub friend invite. The **Invite** button in the multiplayer window's friend list also sends an invite through a hub notification, and when the friend taps the notification, they join that room directly within 30 minutes.

## Player Limit

There is no fixed player limit. However, the number of players that stays stable in practice has not been verified. It depends on the host's browser performance and network.

## Who Saves

- The world is saved **only in the host's browser**. Guests do not save the world.
- A guest's inventory is saved in their own browser, separately for each world seed.
- If the host closes the room, world progress remains in the host's saved data.
- If you are logged in to an account, cloud save uploads every 45 seconds (when there are changes) or when the tab is hidden.

## What You Can Do Together

- **Chat**: T key. Also shown as speech bubbles.
- **Working together**: Mining the same target together within 48 pixels speeds it up.
- **Sleep**: Morning comes only when all players except the dead are asleep.
- **Dungeon revive**: You can revive a fallen companion within 45 seconds.
- **Trade facilities**: Stalls, mailboxes, and guestbook gravestones are facilities shared with other players.
- **Monster spawns**: As the number of players grows, more monsters can be active at once.
- **Skins**: Skins bought in the skin shop are also visible to other participants in the same room.
- **Dungeon rewards**: The treasure list of the floor 5 boss grows with the number of people present (up to 3 times).

## Notes

- If the host leaves, the room closes.
- In a hardcore world, if the host falls, the world ends and the room closes too. Guests follow the item-keeping setting of the host's world.
- Trying to close the tab shows a confirmation window.
- World names can be up to 16 characters, and seeds can be up to 10 digits.

## Reconnecting and Guest Behavior

The detailed behavior when a guest reconnects has not been confirmed. One option is to store important items in a chest of the host's.

## Tips for Playing with Friends

- Divide the work: one person mines while the other handles cooking and farming, which speeds things up.
- Split the mining for signal flare materials.
- For boss fights, one person draws aggro while the other deals damage with a bow.

beaconfall/faq.b:
:: Island count = 30
:: Respawn location = Bed in residence or campfire
:: Achievement count = 60
:: Signal flare book cost = 400 coins
:: Furnace = 6 stone + 1 iron ore
:: Legendary fish = Sailfish, Golden Koi

These are collected questions and answers. Items I could not verify are marked as such.

## How Many Islands Are There

There are 30. That is the starting island plus 29 islands with themes. The village island and pirate island are not separate islands; they are added on top of existing islands.

## Where Do I Respawn When I Die

If you bought a residence (350 coins) in the village, you respawn next to that bed. Otherwise, you respawn next to the campfire at the starting camp. Your belongings stay at the place you died, with a gravestone. If you turned on the keep-items option in world settings, you wake up still carrying your belongings. In a hardcore world, one fall ends it.
If you fall outside a dungeon, all lost items are kept in the grave under the gravestone, and you recover everything by going close. Inside a dungeon, items drop to the floor as before. If you hold a will-o'-wisp or similar, it points toward the grave direction.

## Is There a Multiplayer Player Limit

There is no fixed player limit. The actual stable count has not been verified.

## Are Guests Saved

The world is saved only in the host's browser. A guest's inventory is saved in their own browser, separately for each world seed.

## What Hazards Are on Each Island

Desert and Mesa have daytime heat, Jungle and Mangrove have poison, Volcanic has lava and heat, Ice has cold, and Stone has falling rocks. See the island types and environmental hazards document for details.

## How Do I Put Out Fire

Make a bucket (4 planks + 1 stick), right-click next to water or a well to fill it, then right-click next to a fire to put out nearby fires. Fire spreads less and sometimes goes out in the rain. Fire is started by storm lightning, monsters hit by flame rune weapons, and volcanic lava. See the "Spreading Fire" section of the island types and environmental hazards document.

## Armor Defense

For a full set, leather ★2 gives 8.4 (25%), iron 10.5 (30%), copper 12.6 (34%), gold 22.1 (47%), crystal 30.4 (55%), and obsidian 34.6 (58%). See the armor and forging documents.

## Where Can I See Boss Patterns

Each boss has its own entry in the boss strategy document.

## Why Can't I Make a Compass or Island Map

A compass needs 2 iron ingots and 1 circuit piece. A circuit piece needs brass, and brass requires the Compressed Alchemy book. You buy that book from the village librarian, Ria, for 180 coins.

## The Furnace Won't Craft

It needs 6 stones and 1 iron ore. It takes ore, not iron ingots.

## I Mined Ore but Nothing Came Out

This happens because your pickaxe material is too weak. Iron ore needs a stone pickaxe, copper and gold need an iron pickaxe, and zinc needs a copper pickaxe or better.

## I Can't Cook at the Campfire

Cooking only works within 26 pixels of the campfire at the starting camp. Elsewhere, build an oven.

## I Can't Sleep

It must be dark enough. Roughly 7 PM to 6 AM, and there must be no monsters within 90 pixels. In multiplayer, everyone must sleep.

## Is Sailfish and Golden Koi Which Rarity

They are legendary.

## Who Does the Trading Post Sell To

To NPC customers. To sell to other players, use a stall.

## What Is the Floor 5 Boss of the Dungeon

Depending on the seed, one of the Rock Giant, Flame Giant, Great Snow Yeti, or Venom Spider Queen is determined. After you defeat it, it returns 3 days later.

## How Many Coins Does a Signal Flare Cost

Two books (Signals and Circuits 220, Compressed Alchemy 180) cost 400 coins in total. Ore is separate.

## Can I Roll a World Back to an Earlier State

Yes. A world is automatically backed up every 15 minutes when saved, and 3 backups are kept per world. You roll back from the backup list in the singleplayer list, and the state just before the rollback is kept as a backup too.

## Are There Endings Other Than the Signal Flare

Yes. If you make the Core of the Void with the relics of the eight island bosses and defeat the Void Lord, the true ending appears. See the Void Lord and True Ending document.

## Things I Could Not Confirm

- The effect of seasons on the game
- Mouse wheel zoom (it is in the patch notes, but I only confirmed +/- in key handling)
- The server readiness of account cloud save

## How Many Achievements Are There

There are 60. See the achievements document for details.

beaconfall/automation.b:
:: Unlocked by book = Intro to Mechanical Engineering (150 coins)
:: Craft time = 2 seconds (Auto Crafter)
:: Belt speed = 16
:: Work area = 3x3 tiles
:: Achievements = Dawn of Automation, Sorting Specialist, Auto Crafting

Automation means linking Auto Loggers, Auto Miners, conveyor belts, sorters, Auto Crafters and Cargo Ports to gather and process resources without using your hands. Reading Intro to Mechanical Engineering (150 coins) lets you build the Auto Logger, Auto Miner, Auto Crafter, Cargo Port, Conveyor Belt, Sorter and Guard Post.

## Auto Logger and Auto Miner

- Both are crafted at a Workbench. The material of the axe or pickaxe you put in decides the speed and what it can work on.
- They automatically work on trees or rocks within the adjacent 3x3 tiles.
- Logging takes 3 seconds per tree multiplied by the material multiplier.
- Mining takes the time required by each rock type (3, 3, 4, 5, 4, 5 seconds) multiplied by the material multiplier. Rocks the pickaxe can't mine are left alone.
- A mined rock reappears after 3 seconds.
- If there is a conveyor next to it, the output comes out onto the belt.
- Turn on **Replant saplings** in the Auto Logger's settings and it uses 1 branch and 1 leaf to plant a sapling. It is off by default.

## Overload

- A machine becomes overloaded after working a set number of times depending on its material: Log 30, Stone 40, Reinforced Wood 50, Iron 70, Copper 75, Reinforced Iron 80, Gold 90, Reinforced Copper 84 and Reinforced Gold 100. Any other material is 10.
- As the bar above a machine nears its limit, it turns red, smokes and flickers. When it hits the limit, the machine stops.
- Place a **Controller** next to it and toggle it off and on once to reset it. Resetting an overloaded machine earns the achievement "Overload Fixed".

## Conveyor Belts and Sorters

- A belt carries items at speed 16. Press F to rotate it.
- If there is a chest at the end of a belt, items go into it automatically.
- Hold Glue and right-click to lock a belt's direction.
- A **Sorter** pulls only the item you specify off to the side. Right-click to set the item and press Ctrl to switch the side (left or right) it pulls to. Everything else keeps going straight.
- Place a Controller next to a belt and turn it off to stop the belt. Turn it on and it moves again.

## Auto Crafter

- It receives materials by conveyor and automatically makes the item you set. One craft takes 2 seconds.
- Interact with it to choose the item to make. You can search by name. Recipes with an "any material" slot and recipes with more than one result can't be chosen.
- It stores up to 3 times the required amount of each material.
- Finished items fill a chest next to it first; if there is no chest, they go out onto a belt. You choose the output direction in the settings. The default is automatic.
- It stops if there is a switched-off Controller next to it.
- The first time it outputs a finished item, you get the achievement "Auto Crafting".

## Cargo Port

- Set a frequency (up to 8 characters) on a Cargo Port and a ship carries cargo to the other Cargo Ports with the same frequency.
- Connect the end of a belt to a Cargo Port and the items are loaded onto the ship. If several ports share a frequency, cargo is sent to them in turn.
- Upgrading raises the speed and capacity and lowers the pirate chance.
- The basic ship has speed x1, 6 bundles and a 12% pirate chance. The Clipper has x1.6, 12 bundles and 6%. The Large Clipper has x2.2, 24 bundles and 2%.
- Upgrading to the Clipper costs 10 planks and 3 Reinforced Brass Plates, or 220 coins. Upgrading to the Large Clipper costs 5 gold ingots, 2 Circuit Boards and 5 Reinforced Brass Plates, or 700 coins.
- Pirate insurance costs 80 coins.
- Cargo at sea is limited to 150 items in total.

## Guard Post

- Put arrows in and it shoots nearby monsters. It holds up to 200 arrows.
- If a nearby Cargo Port is raided by pirates, it drives them off using 5 arrows.
- Pay 100 coins to hire a guard and the fire rate doubles, the range grows by 30% and arrow damage rises by 1.

## Automation tips

- Build Auto Miners from high-tier materials, such as iron and copper pickaxes. They have a higher overload limit and work faster.
- If you attach a Controller next to your Auto Miners and Auto Loggers, you can reset overload all at once. The Meter and Remote Signaler on the Signals & Circuits page can do this reset automatically.
- Collecting ore with Auto Miners, belts and sorters and stockpiling it in chests makes preparing the Beacon, which needs 294 iron ore, much faster.
- Lining up sorters one after another lets a single belt split off several resources.
- Items pile up where a belt is blocked, so put a chest or a Cargo Port at the end.
- An Auto Crafter stops when its materials run out. Filter with sorters so the belt isn't blocked by other materials.
- If you're short on copper and zinc, have a Cargo Port receive cargo from a mining base on a Stone Island or Mesa Island.
- Automatic machines, conveyor belts and crops keep running even when the tab is hidden (build 115). While the browser stops drawing the screen, only the calculation continues.

beaconfall/circuits.b:
:: Unlocked by book = Signals & Circuits (220 coins)
:: Circuit Fragment = 2 brass + 2 crystal
:: Meter setting = 1-9999
:: Signal repeats = 1-9 times
:: Tag length = Up to 8 characters
:: Achievements = Circuit Technician, Sending Signals, Overload Fixed

Circuits are a system that starts from the **Circuit Fragment** and controls machines with the **Meter, Remote Signaler, Signal Relay, Bell and Controller**. Reading Signals & Circuits (220 coins) lets you build the Controller, Gear, Clock, Space-Time Teleporter, Signal Relay, Bell, Remote Signaler, Meter, Circuit Board and Beacon parts.

## Part recipes

- Circuit Fragment: brass + crystal + crystal + brass
- Circuit Board: Circuit Fragment + 3 Reinforced Gold Plates + Circuit Fragment
- Controller: Reinforced Copper Plate + Circuit Fragment + Reinforced Copper Plate
- Gear: Reinforced Wood + Circuit Fragment + Reinforced Wood
- Clock: 3 Gears
- Remote Signaler: 2 Circuit Fragments
- Meter: 4 Circuit Fragments + 1 Circuit Board
- Signal Relay: 4 Reinforced Brass Plates + 1 Circuit Board
- Bell: 3 copper ingots + 1 branch
- Sorter: conveyor + Circuit Fragment + conveyor
- Auto Crafter: Circuit Board + Reinforced Brass Plate + Reinforced Brass Plate + Controller + Circuit Board
- Space-Time Teleporter: 4 Compressed Reinforced Brass Plates + Clock

## Controller

- Place it next to an Auto Logger, Auto Miner, conveyor belt or Auto Crafter.
- Interact with it to turn it off and the machine next to it stops; turn it on and it works again.
- It resets machine overload.
- A Space-Time Teleporter works only while the Controller next to it is on.

## Meter

- Attach it to a chest, Auto Miner, Auto Logger, Auto Crafter, Clock, conveyor or sorter to count events. When it reaches the set count (1-9999, default 10), it sends a signal.
- Chest: sends once at the moment the number of items inside reaches the count or more.
- Auto Miner and Auto Logger: sends every time it harvests the set number.
- Conveyor and Sorter: sends every time the set number of items passes.
- Auto Crafter: sends every time it makes an item. The set count is ignored.
- Clock: sends every set number of seconds.
- The signal is passed straight to an adjacent Signal Relay and Remote Signaler.

## Remote Signaler

- It has three settings.
- **My tag**: it receives signals that arrive under this name.
- **Send tag**: it sends the signal received from a Meter to the Remote Signaler with this tag. If left empty, it sends to itself.
- **Send count**: sends 1-9 times, at 0.6-second intervals.
- When it receives a signal, the Bell next to it rings, the Signal Relay next to it receives the signal, and the Controller next to it flips between on and off.
- A tag can be up to 8 characters. Machines far apart can be linked with the same tag.

## Signal Relay

- Set a count (1-9999). Each time it receives that many signals, it sends out one.
- The signal goes to an adjacent Bell, Controller, Remote Signaler or other Signal Relay.
- Chaining relays multiplies the counts. Each one passes the signal on 0.15 seconds later.

## Bell

- When it receives a signal, it rings with a sound for 2 seconds.
- Ringing a Bell with a Meter signal earns the achievement "Sending Signals".

## Space-Time Teleporter

- It moves things to another powered-on device with the same frequency (up to 8 characters). If there are several devices, it sends them in turn.
- Standing on it moves players, non-boss monsters and items lying on the ground.
- You have to step off at the destination device once before it works again.
- Items go into an adjacent chest first; if there is none, onto an adjacent belt; if not even that, they are placed on the ground.
- Connect a belt to the end and you can send items over a long distance.

## Circuit examples

1. Automatic overload reset for an Auto Miner: attach a Meter to the Auto Miner and set the count lower than its limit. Place a Remote Signaler next to the Meter and set the send count to 2. Leave the send tag empty and attach the Auto Miner's Controller next to the Remote Signaler. Each time a signal arrives, the Controller switches off and on, resetting it.
2. Alert when a chest is full: attach a Meter to the chest and set the count near the chest's capacity. Put a Bell next to it and it rings the moment the chest fills.
3. Stopping auto crafting: collect the Auto Crafter's products in the chest next to it and attach a Meter to that chest with a set count. Attach the Auto Crafter's Controller next to the Remote Signaler beside the Meter, and the moment the chest fills to the set count, the Controller switches off and crafting stops.
4. Controlling a distant base: place a Remote Signaler next to the Clock and Meter at your main base and set the send tag to the base's tag. Put a Controller next to the Remote Signaler at the base, and you can turn machines far away on and off.

## Tips

- If the Meter's count is too low, signals go out too often and the relays get busy. Start with a large number and reduce it.
- If signals don't go out, check that the Meter and Remote Signaler are touching and that the tags are spelled the same.
- Circuit Fragments can be made only if you have brass. Brass can be made only if you have the Compression Alchemy book.
- Building the Beacon requires Circuit Boards, Remote Signalers and Bells. Stockpile the parts in advance.

beaconfall/void-lord.b:
:: Final boss = Void Lord
:: HP = 700
:: Attack = 5.5
:: Barrier = At 75, 50 and 25% HP
:: Summon = Use the Void Core at night
:: Rematch = 2 days later

The Void Lord is a final boss you challenge separately from the beacon escape. Collect the relics of the eight island bosses, craft the Void Core and survive a ritual at night, and it appears. Defeat it to see the true ending.

## Relics
- Each of the 8 island bosses drops its own relic every time you defeat it.
- They are the Wolf King's Relic, Scorpion's Relic, Flame Giant's Relic, Spider Queen's Relic, Sand Serpent's Relic, Rock Giant's Relic, Croc King's Relic and Great Yeti's Relic.
- Bosses come back after 2 days, so a lost relic can be earned again. The dungeon level 5 boss gives no relic.

## Crafting order
Everything is crafted in the Void Gate tab of the Workbench.
1. Void Essence: 3 reinforced gold + 3 crystal + 2 frost shards + 2 volcanic rock
2. Void Key · East: the Wolf King's, Scorpion's, Flame Giant's and Spider Queen's relics + 2 Void Essence + 3 gold ingots + 2 pearls
3. Void Key · West: the Sand Serpent's, Rock Giant's, Croc King's and Great Yeti's relics + 2 Void Essence + 3 gold ingots + 2 pearls
4. Void Core: both keys + 3 Void Essence + 6 reinforced gold + 3 crystal + 3 pearls
- You need 7 Void Essence in total. The essence alone takes 21 reinforced gold, 21 crystal, 14 frost shards and 14 volcanic rock.

## The Void Ritual
- The Void Core can only be used at night. Hold it and use it, and a purple circle forms on the spot as the ritual begins.
- For 50 seconds, elite monsters (2.5x HP) rush in over 4 waves. It starts with wolves and Fire Spirits, then scorpions, golems and crocodiles join in.
- Once the 50 seconds are up and every monster that came is defeated, the Void Lord appears.
- If everyone stays far outside the circle for 12 seconds, the ritual fails.
- It can't be used on the Village Island, in the dungeon, on a boat or in a hot air balloon.
- In a sandbox world, the **Open the Void Gate** button in the item list (B key) starts the ritual right away, regardless of night or the retry wait.

## The Void Lord
- It has 700 HP and 5.5 attack, far stronger than the island bosses (70–150 HP).
- Each time its HP drops to 75%, 50% and 25%, it raises a barrier and calls 4 minions. While minions are alive it takes only 1/4 damage, so defeat the minions first.
- It enrages at 50% HP and goes into a final rage at 25%, attacking even faster.
- If every player goes far away for 25 seconds, it disappears.
- When defeated it drops 8 crystal, 6 gold ingots, 3 pearls and treasure-table loot. The more people fought together, the more treasure rolls there are.

## True ending and rematch
- The first time you defeat it, the true ending "Beyond the Void" plays. It shows days survived, bosses defeated and achievements, and you can keep playing afterwards.
- The Void Core stays with you. After 2 days you can open the ritual again for a rematch.

## Related achievements
- Relic Collector, Eight Relics, Void Core, Beyond the Void

## Tips
- Before the ritual, bring Strength and Ironskin potions and a Full Course, and restore your gear's durability at the Anvil.
- Dodge patterns with the roll, and clear the minions first whenever a barrier goes up. After one roll you must eat before rolling again, so bring food.
- In multiplayer it goes faster if one person handles the minions while the others go for the Lord.

beaconfall/settlement.b:
:: Villager House = 6 planks + 2 roofs + 2 string
:: Move-in condition = Bed and torch within 8 tiles
:: Max villagers = 8
:: Jobs = 5
:: Production cycle = About 100 seconds
:: Max bonus = +100% production (tier 4)

Build Villager Houses on your island and villagers move in and gather resources for you. Unlike the NPCs on the Village Island, this is a settlement you grow yourself.

## Villager House
- Craft it in the Building tab of the Workbench from 6 planks, 2 roofs and 2 string.
- If there's a bed and a torch within 8 tiles of the house, a villager moves in after a short while. Press F at an empty house to see whether the bed and torch conditions are met.
- Torches are crafted by hand: 1 branch + 1 resin makes 2.
- You can have up to 8 villagers in total. A new villager takes whichever job currently has the fewest people.

## The 5 jobs
- **Farmer**: brings wheat, potatoes and corn.
- **Woodcutter**: brings logs and branches.
- **Miner**: brings stone, iron, copper and crystal.
- **Hunter**: brings meat, leather and feathers.
- **Guard**: instead of items, attacks monsters near the house.
- You can change a job at any time by pressing F at the house.

## Production and collecting
- Working villagers stack items in their house about every 100 seconds.
- Press F in front of the house and then Take all to collect them. A house holds at most 30 items, so collect often.

## Settlement tiers
- 1–2 villagers is tier 1, 3 villagers tier 2 (+30% production), 5 villagers tier 3 (+60%) and 7 villagers tier 4 (+100%).
- Higher tiers also make the guards hit harder.

## Related achievements
- First Villager, Small Village (4 villagers), Settlement Complete (8 villagers)

## Tips
- Put a bed and a torch in the middle and build the houses around them within 8 tiles to fill several houses at once.
- Start with farmers and woodcutters for basic materials, and place guards where monsters often show up.

beaconfall/building-blueprints.b:
:: Great Pillar = 6 stone bricks
:: Archway = 9 stone bricks
:: Spire = 12 stone bricks + 2 gold ingots
:: Saved blueprints = Up to 12
:: Blueprint size = Up to 20x20 tiles
:: Where to open = G key (Blueprint button at the bottom right on phones and tablets)

This page covers the large building parts for big structures, and blueprints, which save a whole building so you can put it up again somewhere else. Recipes for basic building materials such as walls, floors, doors and roofs are on the Crafting by Station page.

## Large building parts
They're crafted from stone bricks in the Building tab of the Workbench. Stone bricks are made 3 at a time from 3 Reinforced Stone.
- **Great Pillar**: 6 stone bricks. A big stone pillar that towers into the sky.
- **Archway**: 9 stone bricks. An arch you can walk through; place several in a row and they form a colonnade.
- **Spire**: 12 stone bricks + 2 gold ingots. A tall tower with a pointed roof whose windows light up at night.
- All three parts can be saved in blueprints.

## Saving a blueprint
1. Press the G key (the Blueprint button at the bottom right on phones and tablets) and choose New blueprint.
2. Tap one corner of the area to save, then the opposite corner. The area can be up to 20x20 tiles.
3. Name it and save. You can keep up to 12 blueprints; to save another, delete one first.
- Only regular structures such as walls, floors, doors, roofs, furniture and facilities are saved. Chests and crops are left out.

## Placing a blueprint
- Pick a blueprint from the list to see a placement preview. Tiles where it fits are green, and tiles where it doesn't are red.
- Press Place blueprint and as much as your materials allow is placed in one go. Placing requires the matching structure items (wooden walls, stone bricks, doors and so on) in your inventory.

## Building tips
- Line up archways into a colonnade and put Great Pillars at both ends for a temple-like entrance.
- Spires glow at night, so they make good markers for your base.
- Build a house you like once and save it as a blueprint, and you can put up the same house right away on a new island.

tools/getting-started.b:
:: Type = Browser toolkit
:: Address = frenchfries777.com/tools/
:: Tools = Fry Python, Fry Blocks (Block HTML), Fry Sheet, Fry Docs, Fry Slides, Fry Lab
:: Install = Not needed
:: Login = Not needed

Frenchfries777 Tools is a set of tools for studying and making things. Open a link and you can use it right away with nothing to install. It opens in PC, tablet and phone browsers alike.

## Tool list
- **Fry Python** : Runs Python code in the browser with nothing to install. You can draw turtle graphics and basic charts (site v35).
- **Fry Sheet** : A spreadsheet for making tables and calculating, like Excel. You can open and save Excel files.
- **Fry Docs** : A word-processor-style document editor that writes directly on A4 pages. You can export to Word files (site v34).
- **Fry Blocks** (formerly Block HTML) : A block-coding tool that snaps blocks together to build web pages, and exports them as HTML files.
- **Fry Slides** : A tool where you just write a topic and AI makes a presentation for you. You can receive it as a PPTX file.
- **Fry Lab** : A science and math lab for middle and high school students. You can adjust about 182 experiments yourself across 66 curriculum units.

## How to open
1. Type the address of the first page into the address bar.
2. Press the **Open** button on a tool card.
3. Press the potato fries icon at the top left of each tool to go back to the tool list.

## Common features
- What you make is saved automatically in this browser's localStorage. It isn't sent to a server.
- You can also download files. For details, see the saving and export document.
- You can choose the language at the top right of the first page. It supports 18 languages in total: 13 real languages and 5 fictional languages.
- The language choice uses the same value as the related sites Games and Educations.
- At the top of the first page, to the right of Games, Educations and Tools, there is a magnifier search button. Press it, or press Ctrl+K or the / key, to search tools, feature introductions and patch notes in one place. Choose with the arrow keys and Enter, and close with Esc.
- The patch notes for each tool are on the patch notes page (frenchfries777.com/tools/patchnotes/).
- Each tool has AI features. The default AI runs on your device, so you can use it without a key. See the common AI settings document. AI focuses on making formulas, charts and tables in Fry Sheet. The AI in other tools is experimental, so rough drafts may come out.
- The menu at the top of the first page has the same structure as Games and Educations (Wiki, Community, Lounge, Settings). Patch notes can be opened from the Lounge.
- Behind the first page, scenes from Fry Sheet, Fry Blocks, Fry Slides and Fry Lab play as the background. On a computer it's a moving video, and on phones or with the reduce-motion setting it's a still picture. The number line under the title shows 6 tools, 182 experiments, 235 block types and 18 languages.
- The six tool cards appear in the order Fry Python, Fry Blocks, Fry Sheet, Fry Docs, Fry Slides, Fry Lab, and each has its logo to the left of its name (card order in site v34–35). On the first page, cards are laid out three per row (two on a tablet, one on a phone; site v31).
- The first page has the same **online-count bar** as the hub and game sites (total, per game, and hub). When you use Tools while logged in, a connection signal is sent every minute. From 2026-10-26, this signal is sent as a hub connection signal. Signals sent from Educations and Tools are added together under the hub, and the online-count bar does not show separate Educations and Tools entries.
- When you log in, your profile photo and name appear on the connection bar. Friends who are online now are also shown with their profile photo, name and location (site v40).
- Tools you have opened once with **Install as app** also open without internet.
- The **AI Try** chat page (frenchfries777.com/tools/ai-chat/) lets you choose one of Tarius, Lectus and Premus (coming soon) and chat with it. Each model has an icon. You can choose the response style (Quick, Normal or Thorough; Normal at first). Conversations are saved automatically on this device so you can continue from past ones (up to 30), and you can press **Wrong** on any answer to report it. A **Wrong** press made while logged in is collected automatically and used for training.
- In AI Try, Quick mode makes 1 answer, Normal makes 3 and Thorough makes 7. They are voted on, and the most common answer is shown one character at a time. While answers are being made, only a thinking dot is shown. A note saying "the answer may be uncertain" appears only when the most common answer gets less than 40%. Jokes and self-introductions are answered from a prepared list.
- In Normal and Thorough modes, while answers are being made, a **Vote now** button and the count of answers made (for example 2/7) appear above the input box. If you press it after at least one answer has been made, it stops making the remaining answers and votes immediately to answer (AI v48).
- In AI Try, you can give a conversation a name (v44). You can name and rename conversations from the list of past conversations and the button above the conversation. Named conversations are not deleted even when old, and are marked with a ★ in the list. At the top of a conversation, the model and response style used are shown on one line.
- **AI Arena** (v45): The same question is answered by two models one after another, and you choose the better one. You can hide which one wrote which answer, and your win record on this device is shown. Open it with the AI Arena button on the first AI Try page.
- **My AI Notepad** (v45): Write down preferences such as speaking casually or the name you want to be called, and the AI refers to them. It is saved only on this device and is not sent to a server. When you say something like "from now on, do ~", it asks whether to put that in the notepad, and you can turn the notepad off, edit it or clear it. Because it is a small AI, it may sometimes fail to follow the notes.

## Recommended first steps
1. If you want to make a presentation, type a topic in Fry Slides and press **Make with AI**.
2. If you are new to coding, open one of the examples from the **Examples** menu in Block HTML.
3. For table calculations, type numbers into Fry Sheet and try the insert function button.
4. For experiments, choose a grade and subject on the Fry Lab start screen, then press a unit to open it.

## Screen pictures
- The emoji on the tools site are shown as 174 logo pictures we made. The text stays as it is, so you can copy and search it. Input boxes, the document editing area and chat emotes stay the same.

tools/ai-settings.b:
:: Applies to = Sheet, Block HTML, Slides, Lab
:: Default AI = Built-in AI (runs in the browser)
:: Requirement = A browser and device that support WebGPU
:: Optional = Claude, Gemini, OpenAI keys
:: Stored in = Browser localStorage (ffai.v1)

All four tools use the same settings window for their AI features. Change it with the **AI settings** button inside a tool, or in the window that opens the first time you use an AI feature.

## Settings window layout
- **AI provider** : Buttons for choosing among Built-in AI, Claude, Gemini and OpenAI.
- **API key** : An input field that appears when you choose a provider other than the built-in AI. The **Show** button reveals the text.
- **Model** : The list of models for the chosen provider.
- **Preload when a page opens** : A switch that appears when the built-in AI is chosen. It is off by default. If you turn it on and save, the built-in AI you have already downloaded is loaded in the background shortly after a page opens, so the first question is faster. It keeps using graphics card memory (VRAM), so turn it on only if you need it.
- **Test** : Checks whether the key is valid. With the built-in AI it becomes **Download now**.
- **Save** : Saves your choices and closes the window.
- **Remove key** : Deletes the saved key. With the built-in AI it becomes **Remove model** and deletes the model downloaded to your device.

## Built-in AI
- It runs a public model called Qwen3 inside the browser using WebLLM and WebGPU.
- The model is downloaded and stored once the first time, and after that it works without a key.
- The model list shows three models: FF777 1.6 tarius, FF777 1.6 lectus and FF777 1.6 premus. premus is shown as 'preparing' until its model is uploaded. The default model when you first use the built-in AI is lectus. Users who earlier picked a Qwen3 model are switched to tarius automatically. The FF777 models have their own document.
- It is less capable than large AI. If you need better answers, choose another provider.

## The That's wrong button
- On the AI Playground chat page, **That's wrong** reports made while logged in are collected automatically and used for training. Below is how the button works in each tool.
- There is a **That's wrong** button below AI answers (Fry Sheet, Fry Lab, Block HTML's block explanations). Pressing it opens a window where you write the correct answer, and what you write is saved on this device.

## Model list notes
- The own AI model list shows the download size (tarius about 1 GB, lectus about 2.5 GB, premus about 5 GB).
- When you pick any AI model, including Claude, Gemini and OpenAI, a one-line description appears at the very start of the guide text.

## Text-answer settings (own AI)
- Where the own AI answers in plain text (Sheet's Ask·Summary tab and =AI() function, Lab's AI helper, Block HTML's block explanations), it uses settings that pick words more naturally: temperature 0.7, top_p 0.8, presence_penalty 1.0.
- If one phrase (5 or more characters) comes up 3 times in a row, it stops right away from 150 characters on and shows only what came before the repetition.
- Text answers are limited to about 400 tokens. If cut off, the answer is finished at the end of the last sentence.
- If Chinese characters get mixed into an answer to a Korean question, only the text before them is kept, and the AI is asked once more to answer in Korean only. It does not apply when the question asks about Chinese characters, Chinese or Japanese.
- Answers for formulas, charts, tables, block XML, AI calculation and slide JSON keep the earlier calm settings.

## Using your own API key
- Supported providers and models are Claude (Opus 5.5, Sonnet 5.5, Haiku 5.5), Gemini (2.5 Flash, 2.5 Pro) and OpenAI (GPT-4.1 mini, GPT-4.1).
- The **Get a key** link in the settings window takes you to each provider's key page. Gemini is marked as having a free key available.
- The key is stored only in this browser and is sent directly to the AI provider you chose, not to this site.
- On a shared computer, it is best to press **Remove key** when you are done.
- The cost of using a key follows that provider's pricing. It is a separate charge unrelated to this site.

## Messages shown on errors
- A message saying the built-in AI can't be used on this device or browser means WebGPU is unavailable. Use an API key instead.
- A message saying this device is out of memory means you should choose a lighter model.
- A message saying the request is too long for the built-in AI means you should select fewer cells or use an API key.
- A message saying the key is invalid means you should check the key again.
- A message saying there are too many requests means you should try again in a moment.

tools/ff777-models.b:
:: Names = FF777 1.6 tarius, FF777 1.6 lectus, FF777 1.6 premus
:: Made by = Frenchfries777
:: Base models = Qwen3 1.7B, Qwen3 4B, Qwen3 8B (Apache 2.0)
:: Runs on = My browser (WebGPU)
:: Purpose = Own AI trained for Tools

The FF777 models are an own AI that the site's maker further trained for Tools. In the shared AI settings window, set **AI provider** to the built-in AI and choose from the **Model** list.

## Three models
- **FF777 1.6 tarius** : The light model. It is built on a newly trained Qwen3 1.7B. The name comes from the end of the Latin word elementarius (basic). Its earlier names were FF777 1.4 tarius and FF777 1.2 tarius. It became 1.6 in AI v46 (2026-10-23). It was trained further on 1,339 lines of dad jokes and word-chain games, and the number it got right on the dad joke test (115 questions, based on the test format) rose from 4 to 64. Tarius also talks in a simple tone with short jokes.
- **FF777 1.6 lectus** : The smarter model. It is built on a newly trained Qwen3 4B. The name comes from the end of the Latin word intellectus (understanding). Its earlier names were FF777 1.4 lectus and FF777 1.3 lectus. It became 1.6 in AI v51 (2026-10-26), and got 113 of 115 right in the dad joke check training. It talks in a simple tone with short jokes, and answers tables, formulas and code accurately. Repeating the same phrase, and answers mixing in Chinese characters, have decreased.
- **FF777 1.6 premus** : The smartest model. It is based on Qwen3 8B and is meant for computers with at least 8 GB of graphics memory. Its earlier name was FF777 1.4 premus. It became 1.6 in AI v50 (2026-10-26), and scored 115/115 on the dad joke check training and 114/115 on conversation. Until the model is uploaded, it is shown as "in preparation" in the list.
- The model file names are FF-Tools-1.7B, FF-Tools-4B and FF-Tools-8B.
- From 2026-10-26 (AI v51), all three models on the site are 1.6 (tarius at AI v46, premus at AI v50, lectus at AI v51). The model names (FF-Tools-1.7B, 4B and 8B) are unchanged, so a browser that downloaded an older model must **Remove model** and download it again to get 1.6. Premus uses a context length of 4096 to reduce the memory used per conversation and fit within 8 GB of graphics memory.
- Model files are downloaded from the Frenchfries777 account on Hugging Face.
- Only these three models appear in the model list. The default built-in AI model is lectus. Users who had chosen a Qwen3 model before are switched to tarius automatically.
- The download size is shown next to each model in the list: about 1 GB for tarius, about 2.5 GB for lectus and about 5 GB for premus.

## What is different
- It is trained to fit Block HTML and Fry Sheet. The AI requests of those two tools use a short, dedicated question format.
- Block HTML's AI sends lectus a short form that trains the page without a helper block. Other models get the full form.
- The features that use the dedicated format are code generation with Block HTML's AI and formula generation in Fry Sheet. How far the dedicated format is used in other features has not been confirmed.
- Tarius learned, through second-stage training, to answer questions and summaries, make presentations, know its own name, make charts, understand requests and write code. The second-stage training used 1,443 examples, and slide creation in Fry Slides was learned from 316 examples.
- For third-stage training, the training material grew. In addition to about 350 coding materials for new blocks, edits and understanding requests, there are coding and design materials, material that tells "making something new" apart from "editing", answers paired with each sample request sentence shown on the screen, material about courtesy and humility (admitting its own limits and always using polite speech) and the current version name, and AI material for Fry Slides. Training is done on a laptop, saved to Google Drive every 100 steps, and resumes from the last save if interrupted. Third-stage training is finished, and as a result the name of tarius became 1.2.
- The third-stage training material includes dad jokes. Training can also be done with the Kaggle notebook (train/kaggle.ipynb), and it resumes if interrupted.
- For free-form questions (summaries and questions in Fry Sheet, and the AI helper in Fry Lab), the model reads its own identity and the content the developer taught it, and answers using both.
- What the developer taught is a collection of short sentences, and only the developer's account can edit it. The teaching page is not shown to regular users.

## Preparing indicator
- If the model file is not yet uploaded, it can't be selected in the list and is marked as in preparation.
- If you press save in this state, a notice says the model is still in preparation.
- Whether the file is actually ready can't be confirmed from the code alone. To check, open the settings window and look for a preparing mark in the list.

## Things to know when using
- The first time you use a model, it has to be downloaded, so it takes time. Progress is shown at the bottom of the screen.
- While a model is loading, the notice shows the model name.
- Once downloaded, it is stored on the device, and you can delete it with **Remove model** in the settings window.
- If your browser already has the older lectus model, you must **Remove model** in the AI settings and download it again to get 1.6.
- Because these are small models, they may make mistakes or repeat the same phrase. If they repeat the same phrase, generation stops automatically and tells you to send the message again. Even if a block is repeated as a whole, it stops at the third repetition and is downloaded once more.
- The **AI Try** chat page lets you pick a model and chat. Each model has a cup-of-fries icon (the cup color and number of fries differ per model), and answers are made in several versions and chosen by vote. For details, see the Tools getting-started document. Scores for each model are on the developer teaching screen.
- As training material for FF777 1.7, 345 lines were added to the training repository (105 kinds of request phrasing). For loose requests such as "Tell me any dad joke", the model answers with one of the 115 prepared dad jokes instead of making one up (2026-10-26). The model name on the site is still 1.6.

- AI v60 (2026-11-01): The tarius name shown on the site became 1.9b, and a new model was uploaded.

tools/sheet-basics.b:
:: Type = Spreadsheet
:: Size = Starts at 100 rows by 26 columns, up to 5000 rows by 200 columns
:: Saving = Autosave (browser)
:: Files = Open and save Excel, CSV
:: Find a command = Ctrl+K (⌘K on Mac)
:: Address = tools/sheet/

Fry Sheet is a spreadsheet you use much like Excel. Click a cell to type text or numbers, and start with an equals sign (=) to calculate with a formula.

## Screen layout
- Top : The document name field, the **Saved** indicator, the File menu and the **Save as Excel** button.
- Ribbon : It has eight tabs, Home, Format, Insert, Rows & Columns, Data, Protect & Print, Chart and AI, plus a 🔍 Find a command box. See the Ribbon tabs and command search section below.
- Formula bar : Type a cell address (for example A1) in the left box and press Enter to jump to that cell.
- Bottom : Sheet tabs, the count, sum, average, minimum and maximum of the selected cells, and zoom buttons.

## Ribbon tabs and command search
- The toolbar is split into eight tabs: **Home**, **Format**, **Insert**, **Rows & Columns**, **Data**, **Protect & Print**, **Chart** and **AI**. Each tab has buttons with an icon and a short name, and the last tab you picked is remembered. Splitting what used to be crowded into the Home tab across Format, Rows & Columns and Protect & Print came with Fry Sheet v40.
- Home has undo, copy, cut and paste, bold, italic and underline, font size, text color, fill color, alignment, number format, increase and decrease decimals, and clear contents. Format has strikethrough, font, format painter, borders, table style, merge and clear formatting. Rows & Columns has inserting and deleting rows and columns, hiding and unhiding, column width fit, and freeze panes.
- Data has ascending and descending sort, filter, find and replace, pivot tables and pivot refresh, remove duplicates, split text, trim spaces, goal seek and formula tracing. Protect & Print has lock and unlock range, lock and unlock sheet, print and shortcuts. Insert has auto sum, function, checkbox, list, note, link, picture, other-sheet reference and named range. Chart has chart, visualization, color scale, data bars, conditional format and icons, and AI runs from making formulas to AI settings.
- What used to live in the old Rows & Columns and Data menus now shows as tab buttons. Hiding and freeze panes moved from the Data tab to the Rows & Columns tab, and locking moved to the Protect & Print tab (Fry Sheet v40).
- Find features with the **🔍 Find a command** box at the top or with Ctrl+K (⌘K on Mac). Search in Korean, English or similar words, and results show the tab name and shortcut. Items like open and save file or add sheet can be found here too.
- If a feature needs a selected range and you haven't picked one yet, its button in the tab blinks to show where it is.
- On iPad and phones the tabs can be swiped sideways and the buttons are bigger.

## Entering data and moving around
- Select a cell and start typing to begin entering. Double-click or press F2 to edit existing content.
- Enter confirms and moves down, Shift+Enter moves up, Tab moves right and Shift+Tab moves left.
- Esc cancels the entry. Delete or Backspace clears the selected cells.
- Arrow keys move, and Shift+arrow extends the range. Ctrl+arrow jumps to the end of the data.
- While writing a formula, clicking another cell inserts that cell's address into the formula.

## Shortcuts
- Ctrl+Z Undo, Ctrl+Y or Ctrl+Shift+Z Redo (up to 80 undo steps are kept)
- Ctrl+C, Ctrl+X, Ctrl+V Copy, cut, paste
- Ctrl+B Bold, Ctrl+I Italic, Ctrl+A Select all
- Ctrl+F or Ctrl+H Find and replace
- Ctrl+K opens the command search box (⌘K on Mac)
- Ctrl+S saves and Ctrl+D fills down. Home, PageUp and PageDown also move around. The full list is in the shortcuts help window.
- Ctrl+; enters today's date (with Shift it enters the date and time). Alt+= is AutoSum and fills the cells above or beside the selection with SUM. Ctrl+Shift+L turns the column filter on and off.
- On a Mac, the Command key does the same job as Ctrl.

## Formatting and conveniences
- Choose the number format from General, 1,234, 1,234.56, 12%, 12.3%, won (₩), dollar ($) or Text. The won and dollar formats are kept when saving to and opening from Excel.
- The **Insert** tab's **Row above**, **Row below**, **Column left**, **Column right**, **Delete row** and **Delete column** buttons insert or delete rows and columns. The **+ 50 rows** and **+ 10 columns** buttons at the bottom add more cells.
- Drag between column headers to change the column width.
- You can use multiple sheets. Add one with the **+** on the tabs, and click a tab to **Rename**, **Duplicate**, reorder or **Delete sheet**. In formulas, another sheet is referenced in the form SheetName!A1.
- Select a numeric range and press **Color scale** or **Bars** in the **Chart** tab, and colors or bars appear inside the cells according to their values. You can remove them with **Clear conditional formatting** in the same tab.
- Pressing **Checkbox** turns the selected cells into checkable cells. Cells that contain a formula can't be checked. In a checkbox cell, the Space key toggles the check.
- **Column filters** offer a value list, search and sorting.
- Sorting from a column header sorts the whole table that column belongs to.
- **Conditional formatting** rules can be added: greater than, less than, between, not equal, contains text, duplicates and blank cells.
- **Dropdown lists** and input restrictions can be set.
- **Notes** can be attached to cells.
- There are 4 **format templates**: report card, household ledger, attendance sheet and timetable.
- Under **Table style** on the **Home** tab, choose from 5 striped colors, header only, or clear.
- There are **Increase / Decrease decimals** buttons and a **Borders** button.
- The **fill handle** can continue days of the week and months.
- **Pivot table** : Groups by several columns and gives the sum, count, average, maximum or minimum. The result is saved as values in a new sheet, and you recalculate it with **Refresh** when the source changes.
- You can **merge cells** and give each cell a different border (position, color, thickness).
- When you save to and open from Excel (.xlsx), fonts, text and background colors, borders, number formats, merged cells, frozen panes, column widths, conditional formatting, dropdowns, notes and charts carry over. Row heights, sparklines and reversed icon sets are not supported, and unsupported conditional formats are dropped on import.
- **Named ranges** : Give a range a name and use it like =SUM(Sales). Manage them with the **Named ranges** button in the **Insert** tab, and jump to a range with the name box. Renaming a range also updates the formulas that use it.
- **Data cleanup** : Removes duplicates, splits text and clears extra spaces.
- **Lock** : With **Lock range** and **Lock sheet** in the **Data** tab you can lock the selected range or the whole sheet (no password). Locked cells cannot be edited, and **Unlock** releases them.
- **Find and replace** : Choose where to look (this sheet, the selection or all sheets) and whether case matters.
- In the **make reference to another sheet** window, pick a sheet and a range to put into a formula.


## Document management and conveniences
- In the **document manager** you create, open, rename, duplicate and delete documents.
- A document is deleted right away with no confirmation window. After deleting, an undo notice shows at the bottom of the screen for 7 seconds so you can restore it at once, and deleted documents can also be restored from recently deleted (Fry Sheet v38).
- A link that ends with #open=(document id) opens that document right away. Fry Lab's **Send to Fry Sheet** uses this link. A document with charts opens with the chart drawer expanded.
- **Freeze rows and columns** keeps headers fixed on screen.
- The **Data** tab has a **Freeze panes** button that freezes the area above and to the left of the selected cell in one go.
- Double-clicking (or double-tapping) a column border fits the column width to its content automatically.
- Function names are auto-completed while you type a formula.
- A cell with an error shows the cause and a hint for fixing it.
- You can print or save to PDF.
- From the File menu, you can load a CSV table from an https address, check a preview and put it into the selected cells. An overwrite warning appears, and you can undo once (Fry Sheet v32).
- **Cell diary**: when you edit a cell’s value, it remembers the previous value and the time of the change (up to 20 times per cell, formulas excluded). The formula explanation window lists the changes, for example 85 three days ago. The **Summarize as a story** button has the AI briefly explain when and from which value to which value it changed (Fry Sheet v35).
- **Version history**: the **Version** button at the top opens a list of earlier versions and restores one. You can save the current state with a name (up to 15), and an automatic version is kept when the content changes after 30 minutes (the latest 4 automatic ones).
