The state before a restore is also kept automatically, so you can come back to it (Fry Sheet v36).
- **Formula explanation**: the explain button at the right of the formula bar walks through the selected cell's formula step by step in Korean and shows the value at each step. It is solved by the formula interpreter, not by AI, and if the brackets are wrong it tells you how many opening and closing brackets there are and how to fix it (Fry Sheet v33).
- **AI cell marks and review**: cells from =AI() and formulas, tables and answers inserted from the AI window get a purple bar, and the mark disappears once you edit the cell. The ✨ AI cell review button on the bottom line lets you mark each cell as right or wrong. When the AI window inserts a formula, a one-line reason for how the AI wrote it goes into that cell's note too (cells that already have a note are left alone) (Fry Sheet v33-34).
- Excel-style features grew: underline (Ctrl+U), strikethrough (Ctrl+5), font sizes 9 to 28, 4 fonts (Gothic, Serif, Monospace, Handwriting), a format painter brush, cell links and the HYPERLINK function (Ctrl+click to open), hiding rows and columns, inserting pictures (drag to move, resize), goal seek, and formula tracing (showing the cells this cell uses and the cells that use this cell). Excel saving and opening now carry underline, strikethrough, font size and hidden rows and columns (Fry Sheet v39).

tools/sheet-formulas.b:
:: Supported functions = 190+
:: Start = type an equals sign (=) in the cell
:: Argument separator = comma (semicolons are also read as commas)
:: How to check = search in the Insert Function window on the ribbon
:: Recently added = Array functions (FILTER, SORT, etc.), about 70 trigonometric, statistical, and financial functions, CONVERT

Formulas start with an equals sign, for example =SUM(B2:B10). Function names are not case-sensitive. The names below are the ones you can actually use in Fry Sheet.

## Operators and References
- Use the arithmetic operators + - * /, exponent ^, text join &, and percent %.
- For comparisons, use equals, the greater-than and less-than signs, and the not-equal operator.
- Absolute references look like $A$1, ranges look like A1:B5, and whole columns look like A:A.
- Other sheets are written like SheetName!A1.
- You can write a list of values directly with braces, such as {1,2,3}.
- Calculations between ranges (=A2:A9*2), and IF and IFERROR when given a range, spill their results into the cells to the right and below.
- Error values are #DIV/0!, #VALUE!, #REF!, #NAME?, #N/A, #NUM!, #ERROR!, #CYCLE! (cells refer to each other in a loop), #AI! (AI function failed), and #SPILL! (the result spills and the space to fill is blocked).

## Math and Statistics
- Sums and counts: SUM, PRODUCT, COUNT, COUNTA, COUNTBLANK, SUMPRODUCT
- Averages and distribution: AVERAGE, MEDIAN, MODE, STDEV, STDEV.S, STDEVP, STDEV.P, VAR, VAR.S
- Max, min, and rank: MIN, MAX, LARGE, SMALL, RANK, RANK.EQ
- Rounding: ROUND, ROUNDUP, ROUNDDOWN, TRUNC, INT
- Number calculations: ABS, SQRT, POWER, MOD, SIGN, EXP, LN, LOG, LOG10
- Constants and random: PI, RAND, RANDBETWEEN
- Trigonometry and additional number calculations: SIN, COS, TAN, ASIN, ACOS, ATAN, ATAN2, SINH, COSH, TANH, FACT, COMBIN, PERMUT, GCD, LCM
- Additional statistics: MAXIFS, MINIFS, PERCENTILE, QUARTILE, CORREL, SLOPE, INTERCEPT, RSQ, FORECAST, GEOMEAN, HARMEAN, normal distribution (NORM.DIST, NORM.INV, NORM.S.DIST, NORM.S.INV), BINOM.DIST, POISSON.DIST, STANDARDIZE, COUNTUNIQUE, and more

## Conditional Aggregation
- COUNTIF, COUNTIFS, SUMIF, SUMIFS, AVERAGEIF, AVERAGEIFS
- Conditions can use comparison text such as ">=60" and wildcard characters such as * and ?.

## Logic
- IF, IFS, IFERROR, IFNA, SWITCH
- AND, OR, XOR, NOT, TRUE, FALSE
- ISBLANK, ISNUMBER, ISTEXT, ISERROR, ISNA, ISERR, N, T

## Text
- Length and cutting: LEN, LEFT, RIGHT, MID
- Changing case: UPPER, LOWER, PROPER, TRIM
- Joining: CONCAT, CONCATENATE, TEXTJOIN
- Find and replace: FIND, SEARCH, SUBSTITUTE, REPLACE
- Other: REPT, EXACT, VALUE, TEXT, CHAR
- Additional: TEXTBEFORE, TEXTAFTER, TEXTSPLIT, NUMBERVALUE, UNICHAR

## Lookup and Reference
- VLOOKUP, HLOOKUP, XLOOKUP, LOOKUP, INDEX, MATCH, CHOOSE
- ROW, COLUMN, ROWS, COLUMNS

## Dates
- TODAY, NOW (today's date, and current date and time)
- Date functions such as DATE and DATEDIF have been added. You can find their names in the Insert Function window.
- EOMONTH, WORKDAY, NETWORKDAYS, WEEKNUM, and DATEVALUE are also available.

## Finance
- PMT, FV, PV, NPER, NPV, IRR, SLN

## Array Functions and Spilling
- FILTER, SORT, SORTBY, UNIQUE, SEQUENCE, TRANSPOSE, VSTACK, HSTACK, TEXTSPLIT
- If the result spans several cells, it spills into the cells to the right and below. If the space to fill is blocked, a #SPILL! error occurs.
- Selecting a spilled cell shows a dashed border, and the formula input bar shows the original formula.
- Examples: =FILTER(A2:B20, B2:B20>=60), =SORT(A2:A20), =SEQUENCE(5)

## Unit Conversion
- Written as CONVERT(value, "from unit", "to unit"), using Excel unit names. Unit names are case-sensitive, and units with prefixes such as cm, km, mg, and ml also work.
- You can convert length, weight, temperature, volume, area, speed, time, data size, and more. For unit conversions written in words, the AI calculation tab in the Fry Sheet AI document calculates them directly.

## AI
- AI("task", cell, ...): The AI reads the cell contents and fills in an answer. Details are in the Fry Sheet AI document.

## Insert Function Window
- Press the **Function** button on the ribbon to open a list with a **Find Function** field. Search by name or by a Korean description (e.g., 합계 (sum)).
- This list includes about 60 frequently used functions with descriptions. Some functions in the list above do not appear in the window.

tools/sheet-ai.b:
:: Where to open = AI tab on the ribbon, the =AI function in a cell
:: Tabs = Make formula, AI calculate, Make chart, Make table, Ask & summarize
:: Shared setting = Common AI settings
:: Limit = The built-in AI reads up to 60 lines at a time
:: Caution = AI answers can be wrong

Fry Sheet's AI can be used in two ways: the window that opens from the **AI** tab on the ribbon, and the AI function written inside a cell.

## The five tabs of the AI window
- **Make formula** : Describe the calculation you want in words and it makes a formula. If the formula it makes has an error, it tells you. Translation requests are turned into an AI function formula such as =AI("translate to Spanish", A2). For requests that cannot become a formula, it explains why instead of forcing one.
- **AI calculate** : Turns a calculation written in words into one formula and shows the result. The result can be put into a cell. Multiplication, discounts, percentages, powers, roots and Korean number words (for example 삼백 더하기 이십 (three hundred plus twenty)) are calculated right away without AI, and so are unit conversions. Only words it cannot read are turned into a formula by the AI. That formula is checked by the engine, and if asking again still fails, it tells you.
- Unit conversion supports length, weight, temperature, volume, area, speed, time, data size and 평 (pyeong, about 3.3 m²), 근 (geun, about 600 g) and 돈 (don, about 3.75 g). Examples: "how many inches is 170cm" or "섭씨 30도는 화씨 (30 °C in °F)". To type it directly in a cell, use the CONVERT function.
- **Make chart** : When you open the tab, it recommends a chart that fits the table you selected (vertical bars, horizontal bars, lines, pie, scatter), with a reason. **Make this chart** puts it straight into the sheet, and **Another shape** lets you try a different one. It works without AI, and with AI turned on it polishes the explanation. You can also ask in words, and it places a suitable chart with **Insert chart**.
- **Make table** : For example, write "a table of the names, heights and favorite fruits of 6 students in my class" and it makes a table. The limit is 60 rows and 12 columns. Preview it, then put it into the sheet with the "Insert from cell" button.
- **Ask & summarize** : Looks at the table you selected and answers your question in text. Example buttons let you ask at once for a three-line summary, the maximum and minimum, or notable points. You can ask even without selecting a table.
- The Ask & summarize tab uses the text answer settings of the built-in AI. They block repeated phrases, mixed-in Chinese characters and answers that are too long (see the Common AI settings page).
- Use **Send** to submit a question and **Stop** to halt an answer partway through.
- When you open the AI window, the Make formula tab is shown first. The window gives guidance on what the AI does well (formulas, charts, table making) and what it can get wrong.
- The AI window only closes with the X button. Clicking outside it does not close it.
- Press the **Wrong** button under an AI answer to open a box where you type the correct answer. What you type is saved on this device.
- When a formula is inserted from the AI window, the AI adds a one-line note explaining why it wrote it, as the note on that cell (v34). Cells that already have a note are left as they are, and the note shows when you hover over the cell.

## AI functions
- Write it in a cell like =AI("task", A2). Write it in one cell and drag down to fill, and a whole column is processed at once.
- Example: write Korean sentences in column A, enter =AI("translate to English", A2) in B2, then drag down and column B fills with English. You only change the task, such as "translate to Japanese", "summarize in one line" or "positive/negative classification".
- The task can be a single word such as 주어 (subject), 동사 (verb), 날짜 (date), 이름 (name) or 숫자 (number). With =AI("주어", B1), only the subject is picked out of the text in B1. For several items, separate them with commas. Phrases such as '주어만' (subject only), '날짜 찾기' (find dates) and 'subject' mean the same thing.
- Examples of words you can use: 주어 (subject), 서술어 (predicate), 동사 (verb), 목적어 (object), 명사 (noun), 대명사 (pronoun), 형용사 (adjective), 날짜 (date), 시간 (time), 요일 (weekday), 이름 (name), 장소 (place), 숫자 (number), 금액 (amount), 전화번호 (phone number), 이메일 (email), 주소 (address), 나라 (country), 도시 (city), 색 (color), 키워드 (keyword)
- Using =AI("목적어", B1) or the other grammar terms 주어 (subject), 보어 (complement), 서술어 (predicate), 부사어 (adverbial) and 관형어 (attributive) sends the AI a method and examples for finding that part, so it is less confused. For example, the object of 동생이 사과를 먹었다 (my younger sibling ate an apple) is 사과를 (the apple, object form).
- =AI("명사", cell) picks out every noun in a sentence without missing any. Time words such as 오늘 (today) and 어제 (yesterday) are counted as nouns. =AI("대명사", cell) also picks out every pronoun such as 나 (I), 너 (you) and 우리 (we).
- While the AI is answering, the cell shows an hourglass. Up to 3 questions are asked at the same time.
- With the same question and the same cell contents, the saved answer is used, so recalculating does not call the AI again. The answers are saved inside the document.
- The **Ask the selected AI cells again** button discards the saved answers of the selected AI cells and asks again.
- When the cell range is large, up to 200 rows and 30 columns are read and sent. An answer is saved up to 2,000 characters.
- Translation, summary and spelling correction can be written in the task as =AI("translate", cell), =AI("summarize", cell) or =AI("proofread", cell).

## Limits and tips
- The built-in AI is small, so it shows only about 60 rows and 15 columns of a table at most. With an API key, it shows up to 300 rows and 30 columns.
- If the range is too long, you are told to reduce the cells or use an API key.
- If you have not set up AI, the setup window opens the first time you use it. When AI cannot be used, the cell shows an #AI! error.
- If the selected area has no AI function, you are told so.
- For numeric calculations, functions such as SUM are more accurate than leaving it to the AI. Check the AI's answer yourself.

tools/sheet-charts.b:
:: Chart location = Right drawer (Chart button)
:: Chart types = Columns, Bars, Line, Pie, Scatter
:: Visualization = Graph, Table, Diagram, Mind map
:: Saving = Save PNG
:: Range limit = Charts take up to 500 rows and 20 columns

Fry Sheet has two separate things: charts that stay attached to the sheet, and a visualization window that draws things large for viewing.

## Making a chart
1. Select a table with numbers (including the header).
2. Press the ribbon's **Chart** button. The chart drawer opens on the right.
3. Press **+ From selection** and a chart appears.
4. When you edit the table, the chart changes right away.
- Each chart can have a title and a type, and **Use current selection** changes its range. **Delete** removes the chart.
- The types are **Columns**, **Bars**, **Line**, **Pie** and Scatter. In a scatter chart, the first series is the horizontal axis values.
- There is also a **Two axes** type that draws two series of very different sizes against a left and a right axis. It is kept when you save to and open from Excel.
- If there is no numeric data, a message says there is no numeric data.
- The **To slides** button on a chart card sends the chart to Fry Slides. When the sheet values change, the linked slide changes too.

## Visualization window
- Open it with the ribbon's **Visualize** button. It shows the selected table in four forms.
- **Graph** : Draws bar, line, pie and scatter. **Pin as chart** lets you keep it as a chart.
- **Table** : Shows a clean table. Clicking a header cell sorts it, and only the first 500 rows are shown.
- **Diagram** : Choose among tree, flowchart and Venn diagram. A Venn diagram needs at least 2 yes/no columns such as O/X or checkboxes, and you choose up to 3.
- **Mind map** : Treats the leading text columns as levels and draws branches.
- You can write a title in the title field, and **Save PNG** downloads an image file. Mind maps, trees, flowcharts and tables are resized with the + and − buttons.

## Conditional formatting
- **Color scale** : Paints larger values in darker colors.
- **Bars** : Draws a bar in the cell as long as the value.
- Both features require selecting a range with numbers first. To remove them, use **Clear conditional formatting** in the **Chart** tab.
- In-cell **bars**, **mini charts** and **icons** (arrows and traffic lights) formats can also be used.

## Tips
- If you write headers (text) in the first row of the table, Visualize recognizes them.
- Even without a selection, clicking a single cell inside the table makes Visualize find and use the surrounding table.

tools/blocks-basics.b:
:: Kind = Make web pages with block coding
:: Base = Blockly 11.2.2
:: Output = HTML file
:: Saving = Auto-save (browser, My projects list), can also be saved as a JSON file
:: Address = tools/blocks/

Block HTML is a tool for building web pages by fitting blocks together, and for downloading the finished page as an HTML file. What appears on screen is built from blue screen blocks, and behavior is built from event blocks and action blocks.

## Screen layout
- Top: the project name box, the **Run**, **Pause** and **Stop** buttons, the **Blocks / Preview / Code** switch, and the **AI**, **Examples**, **File** and **Get HTML** buttons.
- Left: the block category list (toolbox).
- Middle: the work area where you place blocks.
- Right: the **Preview** and **HTML code** tabs. On a narrow screen, use the switch at the top to change between them.
- The **HTML code** tab is a plain text box without color highlighting, so you can edit it directly. Only after you edit does **Back to block code** appear, and changing a block returns you to block code.
- Pasting HTML code converts it to block code automatically. The **Convert to blocks** button also converts code you wrote yourself. Existing blocks become those blocks, and parts without a match go into **Write HTML directly** or **Write JS directly** blocks. The **Cancel conversion** button returns you to the original HTML code.
- The **Import HTML file** item in the File menu converts an .html file you made into blocks. Functions, loops, conditions, variables, timers and canvas drawing are turned into blocks as far as possible, and only the parts that cannot be converted stay as a **Write JS directly** block. The same conversion is used by **Convert to blocks**, paste and the AI window.
- Large code over 200 KB is loaded in pieces, with progress bars (reading code, splitting into blocks, placing on screen). Very large pages turn only the first 300 items into blocks and group the rest into large **Write HTML directly** and **Write JS directly** blocks.
- The HTML code box accepts up to 2,500 KB of pasted code. Very large code shows only the beginning, but preview, copy and download use the whole thing.
## Build order
- Block 1: Take a **Page** block from the **Screen** category. Set its title, background and center alignment.
- Block 2: Inside the **Screen** slot of the Page block, place screen blocks such as text, buttons and input boxes one after another. Each block has a name box.
- Block 3: Take an event block from the **Start** category (for example, when a name is clicked) and put action blocks inside it.
- Block 4: Check the behavior right away in the preview on the right. When you change a block, the program runs again automatically after a moment.

## Run buttons
- **Run** : Runs again from the beginning.
- **Pause** : Pauses briefly. The same button changes to **Resume**, so you can continue running.
- **Stop** : Stops completely. Pressing Run starts again from the beginning.
- The preview has a safety feature that stops with an error if a loop does not end.
- **Run one block at a time** : Runs by following the blocks one by one. You can choose **Next block**, **Run to the end** or **Quit**, and the variable values are displayed.

## Blocks and the screen
- Block sentences read naturally. Particles such as 을/를 (object particles) and 이/가 (subject particles) change automatically to match the letter before them.
- The block that is running now lights up, even when debug mode is off.
- **🔗 Show links** under the preview is on by default. Selecting a block puts a border on that element in the preview, and clicking an element in the preview moves you to its block. The same button turns it on and off.
- The **🍎 Add object** button under the preview also opens the object window. For details, see the Objects section of the block reference.
- Each category has one block color, which matches the category menu color. Blocks that used to span two categories were merged into one category.

## Editing tools and tips
- Select a block by clicking it, then use **Copy** and **Paste**. There are also **Undo**, **Redo** and **Delete all** buttons.
- Element names appear automatically in the dropdown inside blocks. If two names are the same, it gets confusing, so give each one a different name.
- If the element list in an event block is empty, create the screen block first.
- Screen blocks (text, pictures, buttons) that sit outside a **Page** block now also appear on the page.

## My projects
- In the **My projects** list you can create, open, rename and delete projects. A confirmation window appears before deleting.
- When you create variables, rename them or clear them, the browser's default pop-up does not appear. Instead you type the name and confirm in the site's own window. Confirmation and alert messages use the same window.

## Convenience features
- There is a block search. You can also open it with the slash (/) key.
- The **Tidy** and **Center** buttons arrange the blocks in the work area.
- Run records are kept in the log box under the preview, and when an error occurs, the block concerned is highlighted.
- Ctrl+Enter runs the project and Ctrl+S saves it.
- On iPad, the range in which blocks snap together is wider.

## New blocks and examples
- Blocks were added for saving, loading, writing to the log, distance, today, and move while held.
- The examples now include a calculator, a math quiz and a star-catching game.
- Movement blocks were added: a block that moves an element by the x or y amount you set, and a block that moves it horizontally and vertically at once.
- Follow-cursor blocks were added. You can choose to follow instantly, follow smoothly, or stop.
- Blocks for cursor position, element position, touching checks and a keep-inside-screen block were added.
- A cursor-following example was added.
- A game frame example that moves with the arrow keys was added.
- A reaction speed example was added to the examples menu.
- The examples grew to 14, and at one point there were 28, but in v40 they were reorganized and there are now 8. They run from Click Counter to Maze Escape. The list is in the Examples menu section of the block reference.
- The examples in the old list of 28 that were made by FF777, such as Clone Bullet Shooting and Tile Maze, were dropped in this reorganization. The clone and tilemap blocks are still there; only the Examples menu has been reduced to 8.
- The **Restart timer** block (time box) and the **When a key is pressed and released** event block (press or write box) were added.
- A group of game blocks was added: the **when X touches** event, change and set score, a scoreboard in the top right, and move to a random place on screen. Also 7 sound effects, playing notes (do-re-mi), setting the tempo, and the **Stop all sounds** block. Pressing Stop also stops the sounds.
- The **Show variables** button at the top shows the values of running variables right in a window.
- Key events can use A~Z, 0~9, Esc, Shift, Tab and Backspace. The **while a key is held down (smoothly)** block moves without hesitating or stuttering at first.
- The **My sound** block plays a sound file such as an mp3 once or on repeat. Sound files are saved with the project and must be 5 MB or less.
- Logic gates (AND, OR, XOR, NOR, NAND), a number-range check, and conditional loop blocks (**repeat while**, **do once then repeat**) were added.
- Cloning (create, delete, and move each clone separately, up to 500), square and circle touch checks, a tilemap, a high score record, a timer block that can be stopped by name, and a paint drawing block were added. For details, see the block reference.
- The **Share by link** item in the File menu shares a project with one link. A recipient opens the link to run it right away, and clicks **Edit** to bring it into their own projects. If the link is too long, pictures and sounds are removed and you are told so.
- Shared pictures were added. Use **🌍 Share to everyone** in the My pictures list or **🌍 Save and share** in the paint tool to upload a picture you drew, and get other people's pictures from the **🌍 Everyone's pictures** tab in the object window.
- Choose **Explain this block** from the menu of a block or block group (right-click) and it explains what it does in a sentence or two. Without AI, or if the answer is not right, it explains using the block name and help text.
- When running one block at a time, the number of clones is shown, and if there are more than 8 clones, it automatically runs to the end.
- The **JS expression and call** block group and the **Is a timer running?** block were added.
- The **(key) is held down?** condition block was added. When the key list is open, pressing a key on the keyboard selects that key.
- The **Keep repeating** block was added to the repeat list. It repeats the blocks inside every 0.03 seconds without freezing the screen.
- The picture and photo buttons now appear at the top of the **Screen** and **Paint** categories. The drawing window has new line, rectangle, circle, triangle, star and fill tools (hold Shift for a square or circle). While the drawing window is open, Ctrl+Z undoes the drawing.
- **Move vertically** was changed so that a positive value moves up and a negative value moves down. Older projects have their up and down reversed.
- The number of blocks for waiting, hiding and showing shapes, movement, rotating, flipping and shaking, gravity and jumping, sound volume, video, paths, scenes, the on-screen joystick, countdowns, and checking the user's language and device increased. For details, see the block reference.

tools/blocks-reference.b:
:: Categories = 12
:: Custom blocks = Page, Events, Actions, Canvas, Game, Clones, Tile map, Video, Paths, Scenes, Joystick, Countdown, Read aloud, Speech listening, Input elements, Internet, Tools
:: Standard blocks = Conditions, Loops, Math, Text, Lists, Variables, Functions
:: Direct writing = Write JS
:: Examples = 9 (the old list had 28)

This lists the categories and blocks in the left panel. The names are exactly as shown on screen.

## 12 categories
- The list on the left has 12 categories: Start, Screen, Look·Change, Move, Game, Canvas, Sound·Time, Save, Logic, Loops, Math, Variables·Functions.
- Inside a category, blocks are split into small labels (for example Speech bubble, Change content, Color and size, Get value).
- Clones and tilemaps are in the Game category, high score and log are in the Save category, and text and lists are in the Math category.
- Block colors are one per category and match the category menu color. Each block is in only one category.
- The section titles below describe features, so they can differ from the category names.

## Start
- There are event blocks **when the page opens**, **when (element) is pressed**, **when text is written in (input)**, **when (key) is pressed** (any key, space, enter, arrow keys, A–Z, 0–9, Esc, Shift, Tab, Backspace), **when (key) is released**, **while the key is held (smooth)** and **every (some) seconds**. The touch and clone events are in the Game and Clones groups.
- The press, type and key events are grouped in the **When pressed or typed** box, and the every-seconds event in the **Every few seconds** box. **Key released** runs when you let go of a keyboard key; choose any key or a specific one.

## Page
- **page** : Sets the title, background (white, night sky, black, light yellow, light blue, light pink, light green) and centering.
- Text : **Title** (large, medium, small), **text**, **list**, **link**
- Press and write : **button**, **input** (text or number)
- Group and space out : **box** (vertical or horizontal, background color), **blank space**, **raw HTML**

## Pictures
- **✏️ Draw a picture** : Draw by hand with a pen, fill and eraser, then put it on the page with **Save & add**. There is a transparent background option. The transparent background choice is remembered. You can draw straight lines, rectangles, circles, triangles and stars, and choose to fill them (hold Shift for a perfect square or circle). While the drawing window is open, Ctrl+Z undoes the drawing.
- The picture and photo buttons appear at the top of the **Page** and **Canvas** categories.
- **📷 Add a photo** : Adds a photo from your device. Large photos are shrunk.
- **🗂 My pictures** : The list of pictures you drew. Picture thumbnails now have a border.
- **🌍 Share with everyone** : A button on each picture in the My pictures list. **🌍 Save & share** in the drawing pad saves the picture and then opens the same window. Only pictures you drew yourself can be shared, not photos, objects, or pictures taken from 'Everyone's drawings'.
- To share, you must be logged in with a Frenchfries777 account. In the window you write a title (up to 30 characters), read the notice not to post personal information such as name, school, phone number, or faces, and press **Share**. The picture is shrunk to 256 px or less, and you can share up to 20 a day.
- The **My picture** block puts a picture you made on the page, and the **Web image URL** block puts a picture from a web address. A **My picture** block with no picture chosen shows a hint and a warning.

## Objects
- The **🍎 Objects** button sits on the **Pictures·Photos** row of the Screen category, and there is also a **🍎 Add object** button under the preview.
- The window holds 560 pictures in 14 tabs: Food & fruit, Animals, Vehicles, Space, School & things, Nature, Weather & sky, Game items, Fantasy, Characters & people, Faces, Buildings, Sports, Instruments & music.
- After the 14 tabs there is one more tab, **🌍 Everyone's drawings**. It shows drawings other people have shared, and you can search by title. Tapping one puts it into **My pictures**. The **⋯** menu on each picture shows who made it and lets you **Report** it, and you can **Delete** pictures you posted yourself. When reports pile up, the picture is hidden automatically.
- Search covers every category and works with names in 6 languages, including Korean and English. The window shows large pictures with no name text.
- Each category loads its pictures separately, so the window opens faster.
- A picture you pick goes into **My pictures**, where you can move it, clone it and use it in touch blocks right away.
- There are pictures made for games too (arrow and start buttons, a boom effect, speech bubbles, circles and squares).
- They are 86 pictures drawn by hand and 474 from Microsoft Fluent Emoji (MIT license). Check **Credits** in the window.

## Canvas
- On a **Canvas** element, draw **clear**, **rectangle**, **circle**, **line**, **text** and **image**. The **press position** block gives the x and y of where it was pressed.
- The **Canvas** also has blocks for fill all, line thickness, text size, empty rectangle and empty circle.

## Speech bubbles
- The **(element) says (text)** block shows a speech bubble next to an element. Choose **say** or **think** from the list.
- The **for N seconds** block shows the bubble only for that long.
- They are under the **Speech bubble** label in the Look·Change category.

## Change, looks and motion
- **change content of ... to ...**, **append**, **clear**, getting values (**content**, **number**, **width**, **height**), **ask and get answer**, **last key pressed**
- Change **text color and background color**, change **text size, width, height, opacity and rotation angle**, **show and hide**, color blocks, **random color**
- **Move to position x, y**, rotate
- **move vertically** moves up for + values and down for - values. In older projects, up and down are flipped.
- The Look·Change list has **hide (element)'s look** and **show (element)'s look** blocks. The old **show and hide** blocks still work as before.
- The Motion list has **(element) goes to (element)'s position in (number) seconds**, **(element) goes to position x y in (number) seconds** and **(element) faces (element)** blocks. The go blocks wait until the move is finished before moving on to the next block, and the face block sets the direction of travel toward that element.
- The Look·Change list has **turn/set (element)**, **flip left-right or up-down**, **match the look to the direction of travel**, **shake the whole screen or an element**, **flash** and **change (element)'s value slowly over (number) seconds** blocks.

## Game
- The **touch** event runs once the moment two elements touch. It runs again if they part and touch again.
- There are blocks to change or set the **score**, a **scoreboard** at the top right of the screen, and a score value block.
- There is a block that moves an element to a random spot on the screen.
- **Save best score** (stores it only when it is higher) and the best score value block are saved separately for each project.
- The Game list has **turn gravity on/off**, **jump with power (number)**, **standing on the ground?** and **make draggable with the mouse** blocks.

## Clones
- There are blocks to make a clone of an element, make one at a set position, delete a clone, delete all clones and read the clone count. Up to 500 clones can exist, and they all vanish when you stop.
- Inside the **when (element)'s clone starts** event, choose **me (this clone)** and only that clone moves on its own. There is also a block for values that each clone keeps for itself.
- The **touching** block lets you choose box or circle, and **any clone** works too. Inside the touch event you can delete the clone that was touched.

## Tile map
- Make a grid, fill or set cells with numbered tiles, and read a cell's tile number.
- Check walls with the **touching a wall of?** block. There are also blocks that move while being stopped by walls.

## Sound and alerts, time
- **play note** (do re mi fa sol la ti, C3–C6; give it beats and chain several to make a melody), **show alert**, **sound effect** (coin, jump, boom, laser, pop, success, fail), **tempo** (beats per minute), **stop all sounds**, **my sound** (plays a sound file such as an mp3, once or looped; saved with the project, 5 MB or smaller)
- The **my sound** block's list holds 5 default songs (Default song, Upbeat song, Calm song, Adventure song, Lullaby) that you can pick without a file. The default song is chosen at first, and you can pick your own file with add mp3 file at the bottom of the list. Only the songs you use go into the built page.
- The Sound list has **set sound volume to (number)%** and **stop my sound (name)** blocks. In the **my sound** list you can record your own voice for up to 10 seconds and use it.
- **seconds later**, **seconds, every time**, **stop all "every seconds"**, **restart** (resets the page to its first state and starts over), **now** (hour, minute, second, weekday, date)
- There are also time blocks with a name that can be stopped: **once after N seconds** and **keep going every N seconds**. There is also an **is the timer running** block.
- The **wait (number) seconds** block waits right there for the set time before moving on to the next block, and it waits inside loops too. The old 'after waiting seconds' block is gone from the block list, but it still works in projects made earlier.

## Video, paths, scenes, joystick, countdown
- **Video** : Blocks that show a video address or your own video file and set play, pause, back to start, volume and loop.
- **Move along a path** : Blocks that add points to a path and pass through the points in order, waiting until the whole path is done.
- **Scenes** : Blocks to show a scene, put an element into a scene, and check whether the current scene is ~. Elements not put into any scene are always visible.
- **On-screen joystick** : Blocks that place arrow buttons and a joystick for phones and run when a direction is pressed. The existing key blocks still work as before.
- **Countdown** : Blocks that start from a number of seconds, tell you the seconds left, and run when it ends.

## Read aloud, speech listening, input elements, internet, tools
- **Read aloud** : A block that reads text out in a voice. You choose the language and speed, and there is also a block that waits until reading is done before moving on to the next block. The **stop reading** block stops it mid-way.
- **Voice commands** : There is a **when someone says ~** event block plus **start listening**, **stop listening** and **what was just heard** blocks. The microphone turns on only when listening starts.
- **Input elements** : Slider, switch, select box, progress bar and table elements and their blocks. You can read and change their values, and there are event blocks that run when a value changes. In HTML import, sliders and select boxes turn into these blocks.
- **Internet** : The **get text from address** block only works with https addresses and stops after 8 seconds. There is also a block that pulls values out of JSON. When the **open web page** block runs, a confirmation window showing the address appears first, and the page opens in a new window only after you press Open. Only https and http addresses can be opened.
- **Screen and sharing** : Blocks to switch to full screen, share and copy, and make a QR code.
- **Lists and time** : Blocks to shuffle a list and pick one item, and a stopwatch block.

## Standard blocks
- **Conditions** : if block, if-else block, comparison, logic gates (AND, OR, XOR, NOR, NAND), number range check, negation, true/false, ternary choice, **is (key) key held down?** (while the key-picking list is open, pressing a key on the keyboard selects it), **is the user's language ~?**, **is the user's device mobile or computer?**
- **Loops** : a set number of times, while, count with a number, for each item in a list, **repeat while true**, **do once first**, then repeat while true, **repeat forever** (repeats the blocks inside every 0.03 seconds without freezing the screen)
- **Math**, **Text**, **Lists**, **Variables**, **Functions** : Ordinary Blockly blocks.
- With the **keep showing (variable)'s value on the side of the screen** block, you can keep a variable's value displayed on screen.
- **Write JS** : Write a line or an expression of JavaScript directly. It is for advanced users. There is also a **JS expressions and calls** block group.

## Examples menu
- There are 9: Click counter, Name greeting, Guess the number, To-do list, Reaction time game, Fruit catch game, Space shooter, Maze escape and Reaction speed test. They run from easy to harder.
- Each example has a title and a goal on the page, works with both touch and keys, and has short block comments to help you learn.
- The pictures come from the 🍎 Objects library (only the basket is drawn by hand), and they go into My pictures when you open the example.
- There used to be 14, and once 28, but they were reorganized into 8 in v40. Open one and learn by changing the blocks.

tools/blocks-ai.b:
:: Where to open = AI button at the top
:: Window name = Make Code with AI
:: What it does = Makes or changes blocks from a text description
:: Undo = Revert to before the AI
:: Recommended model = FF777 model or API key

Press the **AI** button at the top to open the **Make Code with AI** window. Describe what you want to make or change in text, and the AI decides on its own whether to edit the current blocks or write new ones. This AI button is gold.

## How to Use
1. Press the **AI** button.
2. Write what you want in the input field. For example, "a number guessing game from 1 to 100," and add that it should say higher or lower.
3. Press **Make Code**. The text the AI writes while working appears in the window, and when it finishes, blocks are created in the workspace.
4. If you don't like the result, press **Revert to Before AI**.
5. To stop partway through, press **Stop**.

## Example Buttons
- For new projects: Click Counter, To-Do List, Number Guessing, Reaction Speed. Only the 4 that the AI matches best are kept.
- Example buttons only fill the input field with text, and the AI writes the code itself. Previously they opened the same example from the examples menu and showed it as if it were the AI's answer.
- In an empty project, a short request (24 characters or fewer) that matches the name or a similar term of one of the 8 examples (for example "counter," "number guessing," or "maze," which are Korean keywords (카운터 (counter), 숫자 맞히기 (number guessing), 미로 (maze))) inserts that example right away. Requests that don't match or are long are written as HTML by the FF777 AI.
- When blocks already exist: three examples appear that modify them, such as dark mode, gradient background, and rewriting in the author's voice. Only the ones FF777 fixed correctly on both test pages were kept.

## Fixing Mistakes and History
- After an AI answer, press **Tell Me What's Wrong** and point out the wrong part, and the AI fixes only the wrong part. If the fix isn't right, it rewrites everything.
- An AI request history is kept for each project (up to 30). Select an entry to rewrite that request, or delete it.

## Block Descriptions
- Choose **Explain this block** from the block or block group menu (right-click), and the AI explains what it does in one or two sentences.
- If there is no AI or the answer is not right, the block name and help text are used as the explanation.
- Press the **Wrong** button under the explanation to open a window where you can write the correct explanation. What you write is saved on this device.
- This explanation uses the text answer settings of the built-in AI. It blocks repeated phrases and mixed-in Chinese characters, and limits answer length (see the Shared AI Settings document).

## Tips for Better Results
- Ask for one thing at a time. Make it first, then ask for changes.
- Describe concretely what is on screen and what should happen when something is pressed.
- Text you request is shown on screen in the language you requested.
- You can learn which blocks were used by opening the blocks the AI made.

## Limits
- The AI builds only with blocks available in this tool. If it can't read all of the code the AI wrote, the unreadable parts are loaded as a **Write JS Directly** block. If an AI answer can't be read as blocks, the site automatically requests it again, showing the previous answer and asking for a fix.
- The AI helper writes an HTML page first instead of blocks, and the site then converts it into blocks. Titles, text, buttons, input fields, drawing boards, lists, boxes, on press, and every N seconds become blocks, and parts that cannot be converted go into the "Write HTML Directly" and "Write JS Directly" blocks. Functions, loops, conditions, variables, timers, and canvas drawing are also converted to blocks where possible. This conversion is the same as **Import HTML File**, **Convert to Blocks**, and pasting from the File menu. If the conversion fails, the HTML code is inserted as is.
- If there is an error in the HTML or JS, you are told to ask the AI again, and you get one more try.
- If an AI answer contains invalid blocks, only those blocks are removed and the rest is opened.
- If the AI repeats the same phrase endlessly, it stops, and you get one more calm retry.
- The built-in AI is small, so it may not be able to make a complex game in one go. In that case, split the request into steps or use an API key.
- If the result differs from what you expected, fix the blocks yourself. Don't trust the AI result blindly; check it in the preview.
- For AI settings, see the Shared AI Settings document.

tools/slides.b:
:: Type = AI presentation maker
:: Number of slides = 3 to 15 (when made with AI)
:: Layouts = Title, Section, Bullets, Two columns, Big number, Quote, Closing, Table of contents, Timeline, Table, Chart, Quiz, Timer, Live screen
:: Export = PPTX, PDF (print), Markdown
:: Saving = Autosave (browser)
:: Find a command = Ctrl+K (⌘K on Mac)

Fry Slides is a tool where you write a presentation topic and the AI makes the slides. When it is done, click the text to edit it directly, then present as is or download it as a file. This AI button is gold-colored.

## Start screen
- Write the **Topic** (you can pick an example card), set the number of slides between 3 and 15, and if needed write the **Audience and purpose** (optional).
- Choose a **Theme** from twelve: Light, Dark, Chalkboard, Bold color, Minimal and Nature, plus Sunset, Ocean, Cherry blossom, Neon, Paper and Black and white.
- Press **Make it with AI** and the slides appear one by one. You can also make it with Ctrl+Enter in the topic field.
- **Start with a blank deck** starts with blank slides without AI.

## Tabbed toolbar and command search
- The buttons at the top of the editor are grouped by what you are doing into six tabs: **File**, **Home**, **Insert**, **Design**, **Present** and **AI**. Each tab shows only the buttons for that job, with an icon and a short name, and the last tab you opened is remembered.
- Master slide, auto-advance, find and replace, make table of contents, sheet link and quiz choices, which used to be inside menus, are now tab buttons too.
- Group and ungroup shapes, stacking order, align, fill, border and appear effects are in the tabs as well. They switch on when you pick a shape.
- In the **🔍 Find a command** box at the top, or with Ctrl+K (⌘K on Mac), you can search by name or similar words and run the command right away. Results show the tab name and shortcut.
- For a feature that needs a shape to be picked first, it opens that tab and blinks the button to show you.
- On iPad and phones the tabs and buttons can be swiped sideways, and larger buttons that are easy to press appear.

## Editing
- Pick a slide in the slide list and drag to reorder. On a narrow screen, the list lies horizontally at the bottom. There are also forward and back buttons.
- **Slide overview** : Select several slides to move, copy or delete them at once.
- Click the text on a slide to edit it directly. Leave the field with Esc or Enter.
- Drag text boxes and pictures to move them, and pull a corner to resize them, with a finger or a mouse. The new position is kept as it is in presenting, PDF, PPTX and link sharing.
- The **Shapes** menu inserts a rectangle, rounded rectangle, circle, triangle, star, diamond, hexagon, pentagon, parallelogram, chevron, plus, heart, speech bubble, donut, line, arrow or text box. You can choose the fill color, the outline color and thickness, and the transparency, and write text inside a shape. There is also a button to insert an emoji or icon (48 choices), and its size and position change like a shape's.
- **Effects menu** (Fry Slides v31): Rotate (15° and 90° to the left or right, or upright), Shadow (none, light, strong) and Add link. While presenting, clicking a shape that has a link opens it in a new tab. The new shapes, rotation, shadow and links are carried into the PPTX file.
- Select several shapes with Shift+click, by dragging on an empty area or with Ctrl+A, and group them with Ctrl+G (ungroup with Ctrl+Shift+G). A group is moved, resized, copied and deleted as one. In the PPTX file, the shapes go in separately.
- The stacking order is changed with To the front, Forward, Backward and To the back (Ctrl+], Ctrl+[). Selected text boxes, pictures and shapes can be aligned left, center, right, top or bottom. Copy shapes with Ctrl+C and Ctrl+V and paste them into another slide or another presentation too.
- When you move a box, guide lines appear that snap it to other boxes' edges, centers and equal spacing.
- There are **New slide**, duplicate and delete buttons. The last remaining slide can't be deleted.
- The **Layout** menu changes a slide's shape. For Big number, write a number and a description, and for Quote, write the quote and who said it. There are also Table of contents, Timeline, Table, Chart, Quiz and Timer layouts.
- Slide options set **Skip when presenting**, background color, bring to front or send to back, font and transition effect. You can also choose a font pairing that changes the title font and body font at once.
- The transition effect can be chosen differently for each slide. There are also effects that show one item at a time with each press while presenting. You can choose Fade in, Fly in, Zoom in, Zoom out, Spin, Bounce, Shake, Wipe, Blur to sharp, Flip, Unfold, Letter by letter, Flash highlight and Drop, and the effects look much bigger and last longer (about 0.9 seconds by default).
- For each effect you set the direction (left, right, up, down), duration, delay, and how it starts (on click, with the previous one, or automatically after the previous one). For text box effects, you can also pick **One click per line**. Effects in older presentations open as they were and look bigger.
- The **Theme** button changes the overall look. Write what you will say in the **Speaker notes** field below.
- Undo and redo work (Ctrl+Z, Ctrl+Y). Ctrl+D duplicates a slide, and there is a shortcut list in the help.
- **Connectors** : You can join two shapes with a line or an arrow, and the line follows when you move the shapes (Fry Slides v26).
- **Format painter**: pick a shape, text box or picture, press Home > Format Painter, then click another shape to apply its fill, transparency, border color and thickness, text alignment, font size and corner rounding. One press applies it once; two presses keep applying until you hit Esc. The shortcuts are Ctrl+Alt+C (copy) and Ctrl+Alt+V (paste) (Fry Slides v24).
- **Adding video and sound**: put your own file (mp4, webm, mp3, wav, up to 200 MB) or a YouTube, mp4 or mp3 address on a slide, and play it while presenting or have it play automatically (Fry Slides v30).
- **Gradients and SmartArt**: shapes can be filled with a gradient (9 colors or your own pick, 4 directions), and the slide background can be a gradient too. SmartArt comes in 6 kinds: steps, cycle, list boxes, pyramid, hierarchy and staircase (Fry Slides v30).
- **Presentation recording**: saves the screen and your voice as a video file while you present (Fry Slides v30).
- **Version history and deleting**: the **Version** button at the top opens earlier versions and restores one. You can save with a name (up to 15), an automatic version is kept when content changes after 30 minutes (the latest 4 automatic ones), and the state before a restore is kept automatically too (Fry Slides v27). Deleting a presentation or selected slides happens at once with no confirmation window, and an undo notice shows for 7 seconds below (Fry Slides v29).

## Pictures, templates and making slides from text
- Add pictures to a slide by dragging and dropping or pasting. They are also included in the PPTX file.
- Pictures can be cropped into a circle, rounded rectangle, heart, star, diamond, hexagon, triangle or arch, with a border color and thickness. This is reflected in the PPTX file too, and rounded shapes go in as cropped pictures.
- On the start screen you can begin from a self-introduction, report or class template.
- You can make slides from text you have written.
- **Paste a table** : Paste a table to make table and chart slides.
- On a table slide or chart slide, **Get from Fry Sheet (linked)** lets you pick a Fry Sheet document, a sheet and a range, preview it and link it. A linked slide reads the sheet's calculated values each time, and if you save the sheet in another tab it refreshes right away. This is the same in presenting, PDF, PPTX and shared links.
- A linked slide shows a sheet link mark, and you can use **Refresh now** and **Unlink**. Unlinking leaves the current values as they are. If the sheet disappears, the last values and a notice are shown.
- With the **Master slide**, a logo, a footer and slide numbers are put on all slides at once. Each can be switched on or off and its position chosen, and they are reflected in presenting, PDF and PPTX.
- **Find and replace** works on the text of all slides, text inside shapes and even notes. **Make a contents slide** collects the slide titles and puts a contents slide at the very front.

## Managing presentations
- In the **presentation manager** you create, open, rename, copy and delete presentations.
- The **New slide show**, **My slides** and **Delete** buttons create a presentation, open the list and delete.
- An older saved copy was moved automatically to be the first item in the list.

## Editing with AI
- From the **AI** button menu above the slide, choose **Rewrite**, **Shorter**, **More detail** or **Add a slide with AI**. If you don't like the result, use Undo.
- **Fix spelling** in the AI helper checks the title, content and speaker notes of the current slide. It shows the changes word by word, and you can accept or reject them one by one or all at once. Fields where the meaning was changed too much are left out, with a notice.
- In the AI window you can choose **Create new**, **Fix** or **Add after**. The AI window closes only with the × button.
- The built-in AI plans an outline first and writes the slides a few at a time. If you stop midway, the slides already made stay.
- AI settings are in the **AI settings** button. See the Common AI Settings page.

## Live screen
- The **Live screen** layout puts a Block HTML project, a Fry Lab experiment or pasted HTML inside a slide. You can click and try it directly while presenting.
- While presenting, the arrow keys turn slides when you are outside the screen. Click inside the screen to work with it, and press Esc to come back.
- It is saved as it looked when you added it. Later changes show up only after you pick it again.
- Thumbnails, PDF, PPTX and share links show only an info card. It is left out of share links.
- Up to 1.5 MB can go into one slide.
- With the **Size · position** handle at the top left of the live screen, drag to move it, and press it and pull a corner to resize. The size and position carry over to the presentation screen, and **Reset position** returns it to the original.
- Choose **Clear live screen** from the live screen slide's options menu to empty the screen.
- On a live screen slide, the Delete key clears the screen, and Ctrl+Z brings it back.
- All Fry Lab experiments and the templates for each unit (182) can be picked from a list grouped by grade and unit, with a search box. When Fry Lab gains experiments, the list follows automatically, and experiments in older presentations still open as before.

## Presenting
- Press **Present** and the presentation starts in full screen. F5 does the same (Shift+F5 starts from the current slide).
- Next : Right arrow, down arrow, PageDown, Space, Enter, N, tapping the right of the screen, swiping left
- Previous : Left arrow, up arrow, PageUp, Backspace, P, tapping the left 30% of the screen
- Home goes to the first slide and End to the last. End with Esc or ×.
- The presentation screen has a timer, speaker notes, a laser pointer, a screen-off option and a progress bar.
- **Auto-advance** : Set a total time for the presentation or a time for each slide and it moves on by itself. A remaining-time bar is shown, **K** pauses or resumes it, and it can also repeat. The setting is saved.
- Turn on **Effects appear automatically too** in the auto-advance window, and effects appear one after another without pressing, for the whole deck or per slide.
- During a presentation, use the **D**, **M** and **E** keys for the pen and the highlighter. What you drew is erased when you move to the next slide.
- The pen has three thicknesses, **X** is the eraser and **W** is the chalkboard background.
- **Presenter view** : Opens with the V key. It shows the next slide, the speaker notes and the timer. It works only within the same browser.
- Presenter helper: type a number and press Enter to jump to that slide. A shows the quiz answer and T starts the timer. There are new shortcuts too.

## Live audience quiz
- On a quiz slide while presenting, open the **Live quiz** with the 📲 button or the **Q** key. A join code, a QR code and a link appear, and the audience joins from the answer screen on their phones by typing only a name.
- The number of answers shows as a live bar chart together with the number of participants. **Reveal answer** shows the correct answer and the percentage correct. When you move on to the next quiz slide, phones show the next question too.
- **Audience emoji reactions** (Fry Slides v24): when the audience presses 👍 👏 😂 😮 ❤️ 🔥 on their phones, the emoji float up from the bottom of the presentation screen, and the number of presses per emoji is shown. You can turn reactions on and off in the live quiz window (they are on when a quiz starts). Each phone can send up to 4 per second, and up to 40 float on screen at once.
- People who join late see the current question, and a lost connection reconnects by itself. Up to 40 people can take part, only a name is typed, and nothing is stored on a server.
- The presenter and the phones connect directly browser to browser. The public PeerJS server is used only for them to find each other, so an internet connection is needed.
- The choices are written in slide options under **Edit live quiz choices**, one per line, up to 6. If left empty, lines such as "1) …" or "① …" in the question, or an O/X answer, are used as the choices.

Audience question box
- The audience can send questions of up to 80 characters from their phones, and the questions pile up in the presenter window. The presenter can pick a question and show it on screen as a large caption.
- Each phone can send only 1 question every 10 seconds, and up to 5 per quiz. Questions are not stored on a server.

## Exporting
- **Download PPTX** : Makes a PowerPoint file. Speaker notes are included. This feature loads the PPTX library the first time it is used.
- Tables and charts are also reflected in the PPTX file. Appear effects don't go into the PPTX, so everything is exported in its visible state.
- PPTX saving also carries video and sound, YouTube and gradients (Fry Slides v30).
- **Save as Markdown**: saves the slides as a text (Markdown) file.
- **Save as PDF · Print** in the **Decks** menu : Saves as PDF through the browser's print window.
- From the same menu, you can start a new deck, rename, see your decks list, and delete.

## Sharing with a link or QR
- Share a presentation as read-only with a link or a QR code.
- No server is used, and the presentation is packed into the link.
- Pictures are left out, and it is not a live follow-along view.
- A QR code can hold only about 2,900 characters.
- **Edit together** (Fry Slides v22): in the share window you can make an edit-together link, and the people who get it edit the same deck with you. You must be logged in to create one, but the people editing with you do not need to log in. Every 3 seconds each browser checks for newer changes and merges them, and anyone who knows the link can edit. Unlike the read-only link above, it uses a server (the ff_slides_share table in Supabase), so its SQL has to be run to turn it on, and before that it says "It turns on when the SQL is run". Ending it deletes it from the server so the link no longer opens, and the deck on this device stays.

tools/lab.b:
:: For = Middle and high school students
:: Units = 66 (math and science, grades 7 to 12)
:: Experiments = about 182 (middle-school math 41, high-school math 34, middle-school science 41, high-school science 45)
:: Common features = adjusting, measurements, records, auto record, graphs, CSV and Excel download, sending to Fry Sheet, reports, sharing, saving My versions
:: Saving = Browser (fflab.v1), records up to 500 rows per experiment
:: Address = tools/lab/

Fry Lab is a simulation you change by dragging. Pick a curriculum unit on the start screen and its experiment runs in the center, while you adjust the values on the right.

## Start screen: curriculum gallery
- The start screen shows 66 math and science units from grade 7 to grade 12 as cards.
- Filter by grade and subject at the top, and use the search box to find a unit by name.
- Every one of the 66 units has an experiment, and none is marked as coming soon. There are about 182 experiments in all.
- Example: the grade 7 unit "Various forces" has experiments on balance of forces, friction, buoyancy and springs.

## When a unit has several experiments
- If a unit has two or more experiments, a **N experiments** picker appears. Choose one there.
- The cards where you pick an experiment and the template list show a logo for each experiment. All 182 experiments have a logo (26 more were added in each of Lab v18 to v24).

## Editing values and My versions
- You can edit the values and formulas of a unit template.
- Save your changes as a **My version**, then load, rename or delete it later.

## Slider − / + buttons
- Every experiment has − and + buttons next to its sliders. A press changes the value by one step, holding repeats it, and it stops at the minimum and maximum. You can also type a number directly.
- In the balance-of-forces experiment, drag the tip of an arrow to change a force's size and direction, and drag the line of action to move it.

## How to use the screen
- **Experiment** tab : It has **Controls** (sliders and choices), **Measured**, **How it works** and **Try this**.
- There are **Start** (changes per experiment to Launch, Spin, Auto and so on), **Start over**, and a playback speed choice (0.25x to 4x). The speed choice and the Start button may be hidden depending on the experiment.
- Press **Record** and the current values are left in the table. Look at the table and graph in the **Data · Graph** tab.
- Turning on **Auto record** records the current values by itself at an interval you set between 0.5 and 10 seconds. If the values have not changed, that row is skipped.
- Adjusted values and records are saved automatically in the browser.

## The original experiments: math
- **Function graphs** : Write expressions in f(x), g(x) and h(x) and move a, b and c. Usable functions are sin, cos, tan, sqrt, abs, ln, log, exp and so on, plus the constants pi and e. It shows the y-intercept, x-intercept, the x where f and g meet, and the coordinates of point P. Drag to move, and zoom with the wheel or two fingers.
- **Probability** : Choose among a coin, one die, the sum of two dice and an estimate of pi (π). There are 1, 10, 100 and 1000 throws and auto throwing (5, 60 or 1000 per second). You watch the relative frequency approach the theoretical value.
- **Unit circle & trig** : Change and rotate the angle θ to see the sin, cos and tan values and graphs. The tan θ and cos θ graphs can be turned on and off.

## The original experiments: science
- **Projectile motion** : Change the initial speed, the throwing angle and height, gravity (Earth, Moon, Mars and Jupiter can be selected) and air resistance, then launch. Look at the range, maximum height and flight time.
- **Pendulum** : Change the string length, initial angle, gravity and air resistance. You can drag and release the weight and measure the period.
- **Springs & Hooke's law** : Change the mass of the weight, the spring constant, the initial stretch, gravity and air resistance. You can drag and release the weight.
- **Refraction of light** : Change the refractive indices of the upper and lower materials and the angle of incidence. Look at the refraction angle and total internal reflection.
- **Wave interference** : Change the wavelength, the distance between two sources, the phase difference and the frequency. There are a ripple view, a vibration-size view and a display of nodal lines.
- **Circuits & Ohm's law** : Change a single resistor, series and parallel connections, voltage and resistance. Look at the current and power.

## Reports and sharing
- The **Report** button at the top makes a one-page report with purpose, method, results and conclusion from the current experiment's conditions, records and graph. After editing the text, download it as .html or print it or save it as a PDF.
- Press **Draft with AI** in the report and the AI fills in the four parts using only the recorded numbers.
- The **Share** button at the top sends the experiment and its values (and the records too, if you want) as a single link and a QR code. Opening the link opens the same experiment with the same values.

## Records and graphs
- In the data tab, choose the horizontal and vertical axes and turn on **Best-fit line** to get the slope, y-intercept and R².
- Some experiments show a hint for reading values such as g, k or R from the slope.
- **Copy CSV** and **Download CSV** move the data to a spreadsheet. **Clear all** has to be pressed once more within 3 seconds to clear.
- **Send to Fry Sheet** makes a new sheet named after the experiment and the date, prepares the header, the records and even a scatter chart, and opens it in Fry Sheet. The columns for the graph's horizontal and vertical axes are put first, and columns without values are left out.
- **Download Excel** makes an Excel file with two sheets, the records and the graph, and **Graph CSV** downloads just the graph values.
- Under **Units & formulas** in the header, you can convert length, mass, time, speed, temperature, area, volume and energy, and look up 33 math and science formulas.

tools/lab-ai.b:
:: Where to open = The AI helper button at the top
:: What it does = Explains using the current experiment values
:: Asking = Ask button after the input field below
:: Also sent = Recorded table and best-fit line
:: Answer length = The built-in AI answers briefly

The **AI helper** reads the current experiment's control values and measurements and explains them in a way middle and high school students can follow. It opens as a panel on the right. This AI button is gold-colored.

## How to use
1. Pick an experiment and adjust the values.
2. Press **AI helper** at the top.
3. Write a question or press an example button. The examples are what is happening now, why the formula works this way, interpret my records and the next experiment to try.
4. Press **Ask**. While the answer is being written, you can interrupt with **Stop**.
- The AI helper also does **Change values** (say it in words and the slider values change within their range) and **Find an experiment** (describe it and it opens the matching experiment; even without AI settings, it searches by name and description).
- Press the **That's wrong** button below an answer to open a window where you write the correct answer; what you write is saved on this device.
5. You can change the model with the **AI settings** link.

## What is sent along
- The experiment name, control values and measurement results are sent as an English summary.
- If there are recorded rows, they are sent too. The built-in AI gets the latest 6 rows, and with a key up to the latest 40 rows.
- If there is a best-fit line, its slope, y-intercept and R² are sent as well.
- The panel shows how many rows are sent along.

## Shape of the answer
- If you ask in Korean, it answers in Korean. It answers to match the screen language.
- Formulas are written in text, like T = 2π√(L/g).
- The built-in AI answers briefly, at about 120 words, and with a key it answers at about 150 to 250 words.
- The own AI's text-answer settings apply, which prevent repetition, mixed-in Chinese characters and overly long answers. An answer ends at about 400 tokens, and if it is cut off it is finished at the end of the last sentence.
- It explains based on the numbers it is given, and it is asked not to make up measurements that were not provided.

## Limits
- A small built-in AI may be wrong or answer briefly on hard questions. For a detailed explanation, use an API key.
- It can't see the experiment's detailed screen (the picture), only a numeric summary.
- Check whether the answer is right against the explanation in the How it works panel or a textbook.
- If you choose an FF777 model, it also reads what the developer taught it when answering. See the FF777 Models page.

tools/saving-sharing.b:
:: Autosave = All tools, inside the browser
:: Account = Not required (only sharing pictures in Block HTML needs a Frenchfries777 account)
:: Files = xlsx, csv, json, html, pptx, pdf, png
:: Caution = Lost if browser data is cleared
:: Storage = A message appears when it is full

What you make in Tools is saved automatically in the storage (localStorage) of the browser you are using, not on a server. So you can pick up where you left off by opening it again on the same device and browser. It is not visible on other devices or other browsers.

## Autosave by tool
- **Fry Sheet** : Saved per document, and up to the 50 most recent documents stay in the **My documents** list. **Saved** appears on screen. When storage is full, a message says storage is full.
- **Block HTML**: each project is autosaved in the My projects list. If space runs out, a notice asks you to save the project as a file.
- **Fry Slides** : The list of decks is saved. When space is short, a message says it could not be saved.
- **Fry Lab** : The last experiment, control values and records per experiment (up to 500 rows) are saved.
- **Fry Docs** : Each document is auto-saved, with a My Documents list, a version history and restoring of deleted documents.
- **Fry Python** : There is a My Files list and a version history.
- **AI settings** : The chosen AI and model, and the API key you entered, are saved.

## Exporting as files
- **Fry Sheet** : Use **Save as Excel file (.xlsx)** and **Save this sheet as CSV** in the File menu. The **Save as Excel** button at the top does the same. Formulas go in as formulas, and values as values.
- **Opening in Fry Sheet** : **Open file (Excel, CSV)** opens xlsx, xls, xlsm, ods, csv, tsv and txt.
- **Block HTML** : **Get HTML** downloads a web page file. **Save project file** in the **File** menu saves the blocks as a json file, and **Open project file** opens it again.
- **Block HTML** : **Import HTML file** in the File menu turns an .html file you already made into blocks.
- **Block HTML** : **Share by link** in the File menu shares a project as a single link. A QR code also appears in the window. If the link would be too long, pictures and sounds are left out, with a notice.
- **Block HTML** : In **Get as app** in the menu, set a name and an icon and download the file. Add this file to the home screen on a phone or iPad and it opens like an app, without the address bar.
- **Block HTML** : A picture you drew yourself can be posted to 'Everyone's drawings' with **🌍 Share with everyone**. That picture is stored on a server, not in the browser, and is visible to everyone, and you must be logged in with a Frenchfries777 account. The person who posted a picture can delete it.
- **Fry Slides** : **Download PPTX**, **Save as PDF · Print**
- **Fry Docs** : exports to a Word file (docx), PDF, web page or text file, and opens Word documents, web pages and text files.
- **Fry Python** : opens and downloads .py files.
- **Fry Lab** : **Copy CSV**, **Download CSV**, **Download Excel** (two sheets: records and graph), **Graph CSV**, experiment **Report** (.html, print or PDF), and **Share**, which sends the experiment and its values as a link and QR code
- **Fry Lab** : **Send to Fry Sheet** sends the records to a new Fry Sheet document. The document opens through a link with the document id at the end of the address (#open=).
- **Save PNG** in Visualize makes an image file.

## How to keep things safe
- Download important things as files from time to time.
- Clearing the browser's site data, using a private window or running out of space can make saved content disappear or fail to save.
- On a shared computer, remove the AI key when you are done.
- Complete compatibility between file formats could not be confirmed. Some formatting may differ when opened in Excel.
- Fry Sheet keeps formatting, merged cells, frozen panes, conditional formatting, dropdowns, notes and charts when saving to and opening from Excel (.xlsx). Row heights, sparklines and reversed icon sets are not supported.

tools/tips.b:
:: For = All users
:: Topics = Quick tips per tool
:: Key idea = Start small and keep files
:: AI = Ask briefly and specifically
:: Mobile = Mostly supported

A collection of tips for using the tools more comfortably.

## Fry Sheet
- Select the cell below a column of numbers and press **AutoSum** to insert the sum.
- Drag a formula down to fill, and the same calculation applies to each row.
- Turn on **Color scale** or **Bars** for a score table to compare at a glance.
- Wrapping errors with IFERROR makes a tidier table.
- The status bar below the selected range shows the count, sum, average, minimum and maximum right away.
- For translating or classifying sentences, use the AI function to process a whole column at once.

## Block HTML
- Open an example from the **Examples** menu and learn by changing the blocks one at a time.
- Give elements short and distinct names. Example : score, startbutton.
- Build while pressing things right in the preview. You can read the actual HTML in the Code tab.
- When finished, make a file with **Get HTML** and send it to a friend. It opens as a single file.

## Fry Slides
- Write the audience and purpose along with the topic and the level of the writing is matched.
- Make about 5 slides first, and add more with **Add a slide with AI** if needed.
- Check slides where numbers matter yourself. The AI can make up exact numbers.
- Practice while reading the speaker notes.

## Fry Lab
- Change only one value at a time and record. That is how the rule shows up in the graph.
- Start by following the questions in the Try this list.
- Copy the records as CSV and paste them into Fry Sheet to calculate and draw charts yourself.

## AI in general
- Write one thing at a time, specifically.
- If the built-in AI is slow, choose a lighter model. If you need better answers, use an API key.

tools/faq.b:
:: Category = Troubleshooting and questions
:: Reference = site code
:: Not verified = listed separately below
:: GitHub = github.com/frenchfries777mc
:: Updates = may change when the tools are updated

## Pricing and Accounts
- Q: Does it cost money? A: The site needs no installation or login. The built-in AI needs no key. If you use Claude, Gemini, or OpenAI with your own key, that company's fees apply separately.
- Q: Where is what I make saved? A: Inside the browser you are using. It does not appear on other devices.

## When AI Doesn't Work
- Q: It says the built-in AI can't be used. A: The device or browser does not support WebGPU. Use a current browser or enter an API key.
- Q: It takes a long time at first. A: The model is being downloaded for the first time. The default model is about 1 GB. If it is slow, choose the light model (about 0.5 GB).
- Q: It says there is not enough memory. A: Choose a lighter model or close other tabs.
- Q: The AI answer is wrong. A: Small models can be wrong. Check it yourself, and if needed, enter a key to use a larger model.
- Q: A cell shows #AI!. A: The AI is unavailable or the request failed. Check the AI settings and ask the cell again.
- Q: Is my key safe? A: The key is stored only in this browser and sent only to the company you chose. On a shared computer, delete it.

## By Tool
- Q: The sheet is slow. A: It can be slow if there are many cells or many AI functions. The maximum is 5000 rows and 200 columns.
- Q: The formatting looks different in Excel. A: Full compatibility has not been verified. Row height, sparklines, and icon sets with reversed colors are not supported.
- Q: The block preview stopped. A: It may be in a paused state. Press Resume or Run.
- Q: Slides look different in PPTX. A: They use the same layout rules, but fonts differ between computers, so they may look slightly different.
- Q: My data disappeared. A: Browser data may have been cleared, or you may have been in a private window. Keep separate file backups.

## Things I Could Not Verify
- Whether the FF777 model files are actually uploaded right now
- The range of WebGPU support across mobile browsers
- Detailed formatting differences when opened in Excel and PowerPoint
- The exact storage limit (it differs by browser)

educations/classroom.b:
:: Room code = 5 uppercase letters and digits
:: Max players = 40
:: Games = SpeedCode, Timeline, Sentence Fixer, Balance Blueprint

## Creating a room
1. The teacher (host) enters a name and presses Create room. In Sentence Fixer it is Open a factory, and in Balance Blueprint it is Open a studio.
2. Tell the students the 5-character room code and the link shown on screen.
3. Students enter the code to join. They only write a name, and there is no login.
4. When participants have gathered in the lobby, the host presses Start.

## Host settings
- Choose the time limit. The choices differ by game.
- The host can only watch the leaderboard or take part directly.
- Even during play, the host can finish with End now.

## Rankings

- If scores are tied, whoever reached that score first ranks higher.

## Notes
