educations/planetsearch.b:
:: Subject = Grade 7 informatics, data
:: Modes = Solo (Start voyage), Start with a class code
:: Progress = 3 sectors, 5 planets per sector
:: Record = Best record (total population)

## Overview
A game where you become an alien probe, survey planets and settle each species on a suitable planet. You try binary decoding, storage capacity calculation and data organizing yourself.

## How to play
1. On the home screen, press Start voyage or Start with a class code. Write the class code in 12 characters or fewer.
2. **Decode Signals**: Add the place values of the lit bulbs and write the temperature, gravity, oxygen and radiation values in decimal. Units are ℃ for temperature, m/s² for gravity, % for oxygen and mSv for radiation. If your answer is wrong, a decoding failure is shown together with the correct binary number and the place-value working (e.g. 64 + 16 + 8 + 2 = 90).
3. **Find Water**, **Listen to Sound**, **Spot Hazards**: Scan photos, sounds and video within the storage capacity and record the results.
4. When all the planets in a sector are surveyed, assign species to planets in the migration request and begin settling.
5. After 3 years, view the settlement report and buy facilities and equipment with credits at the workshop.
6. When the voyage ends, press **Result sheet** on the result screen to write your name and print it.

## Score and rules
- The goal is to increase the settlement's total population.
- If the conditions are met the population grows, and if not it shrinks.
- There are 3 trust hearts (♥), and they decrease when the settlement collapses.
- In the survey log, view the data as a table, bar graph, scatter plot and Venn diagram.

## Result sheet
- When the voyage ends, open it with the Result sheet button on the result screen. You write your name yourself, up to 20 characters.
- At the top it shows the name, the class code (only if you started with a class code), the date and the result (Passed three sectors or Returned from sector N).
- Below that come the voyage result card, the migration request assignments (the number of assignments that met all conditions / the total number of settlements), the records by sector, the table design and the table of surveyed planets.
- The records-by-sector table shows the sector, the binary decoding (correct / total), the number of photo, sound and video scans, the bits used and the reply signal (success, failure, or — if none). Sectors you did not reach are not listed.
- The table design shows the columns you chose yourself, or Not chosen if you chose none.
- In the table of surveyed planets, a red value is a value that was decoded wrongly.
- Pressing Print prints it in a white print layout without buttons. Pressing Back returns to the result screen.

## Tips
- If a photo's resolution is low, you can miss small lakes.
- If you write the same class code, everyone starts with the same planets and requests, so you can compare results.
- Planet names are made by mixing syllables (for example, XX b), and the same name does not repeat within one voyage.

educations/speedcode.b:
:: Topic = Binary and decimal conversion
:: Modes = Solo practice, Room mode (up to 40 players)
:: Time = 1 min, 1 min 30 sec, 2 min, 3 min
:: Max digits = 6 bits, 8 bits, 10 bits

## Overview
A race game competing on speed at converting binary numbers to decimal. It starts at 3 bits, and as correct answers pile up, the number of digits grows.

## How to play
1. Enter a name and choose Solo practice, Create room or Join.
2. Choose the question direction. There are Binary → Decimal, Decimal → Binary and Mixed.
3. Look at the given binary number and enter it in decimal. In the opposite direction, press bits to build the binary number.
4. Press OK to grade it. You can also skip, but it counts as wrong and breaks your streak of correct answers.

## Host settings
- Set the time, max digits, question direction and place-value hint (show, hide).
- In room mode you choose the format: solve as many as possible within the time, or fill the question count. In fill the question count, whoever reaches the goal (10, 20 or 30 questions) first ranks higher, and the round ends early once everyone playing has reached the goal. The screen shows the number solved and the goal.
- You can limit the size of the numbers used in the questions by choosing a number range (fit to bits, up to 15, up to 31, up to 100, up to 255).
- The host chooses between Watch the board and Play too.

## Score
- You earn points for each correct answer. The base is 1 point, and as your streak of correct answers builds, it becomes 2 points from the 3rd, 3 points from the 6th and 4 points from the 9th, and keeps rising by 1 point every 3 answers after that.
- Now and then a ★ golden question appears. It can show up after you have solved 3 questions, never twice in a row, and a correct answer scores double.
- With a streak of 2 or more correct answers, the screen shows the combo and the points of the next correct answer.
- A wrong answer breaks the streak and locks input for 2 seconds. The seconds left are shown on the screen. There is no deduction, and the number of wrong answers is reflected in accuracy.
- The number of digits in the questions grows with the number of correct answers, not with the score.
- The ranking goes from the highest score down, and if scores are tied, whoever solved first ranks higher.
- The results table shows rank, name, score, decoded, accuracy and top digits.
- The results screen shows the place values you miss most often. It names the one you got wrong most and suggests checking that place once more.

## Tips
- If you turn on the place-value hint, you can check the values of the places from the largest to the smallest.
- A wrong answer locks input for 2 seconds, so it pays to check before you press rather than guess.

educations/timeline.b:
:: Subject = History, history of science
:: Cards = 121 (Korean history 47, world history 40, science and inventions 34)
:: Modes = Solo, Create room (up to 40 players)
:: Room time = 3 min, 5 min, 8 min

## Overview
A game where you fit event cards into the right place on a timeline. Each time you place a card, a one-line explanation of the event appears so you can learn.

## How to play
1. Enter a name and choose one of Solo, Create room or Join.
2. The card shown at the top of the screen is the question of when it happened.
3. Drag the card onto the timeline, or press the + on the timeline to choose the spot.
4. If it is right you earn points, and if it is wrong the correct spot is shown.

## Score
- Each correct answer is worth 100 points, and consecutive correct answers add 20 points each, up to 200.
- Solo ends when you lose all 3 lives or place all the cards. The best record is saved.
- Room mode ranks by score during the time limit.
- The results screen shows accuracy, best streak, the timeline you built and the most-missed events.

## Tips
- Press a card to see its explanation.
- The event map marks where each event took place with a pin. The 121 place names are shown only on the Korean screen, and other languages show just the pins.
- Use the most-missed events on the results screen for review.

educations/munjang.b:
:: Subject = Korean (spelling, word spacing, sentence agreement, honorifics)
:: Modes = Solo shift, Open a factory (up to 40 players)
:: Work time = 2 min, 3 min, 5 min
:: Sentence language = Korean

## Overview
A game where you fix the wrong words in sentences coming in on a conveyor belt, and let the correct sentences pass. Each time you fix one, it tells you the reason in one line.

## How to play
1. Enter a name and choose one of Solo shift, Open a factory or Join.
2. When a sentence comes in, press the wrong word and repair parts (choices) appear.
3. Choose the right choice to fix it.
4. If the sentence is correct, press ✓ Pass as OK.
5. When it ends, check the sentences to review again in the Work log.

## Score
- A correct answer is 100 base points plus a remaining-time bonus and a combo bonus (up to 10 combo).
- Solo shift has 3 lives, which decrease when you are wrong, and the belt gets faster over time.
- Room mode has no lives and competes on score during the time limit.
- The results show sentences handled, accuracy, best combo and the correct rate by area.

## Tips
- Sentences with no wrong word also appear, so don't rush to fix them.

educations/balance.b:
:: Subject = Grade 7 science, balance of forces
:: Stages = 5
:: Modes = Solo design (10 blueprints), Open a studio (up to 40 players)
:: Review = 3 times per blueprint

## Overview
A game where you draw force arrows on a blueprint yourself and get it reviewed for whether the balance conditions are met. For two forces to be balanced, they must be equal in magnitude, opposite in direction and on the same line of action.

## Stages
1. Basic balance
2. Tug of war and friction
3. Weight and buoyancy
4. Elastic force lab
5. Comprehensive design

## How to play
1. Read the work order with Open the drawing.
2. Draw arrows with the direction buttons, and choose the point of application if there are several.
3. Press Submit and you get approved or rejected.
4. If rejected, you can draw again, and if you are wrong all 3 times, the answer and what you learned are shown.

## Score
- Each blueprint is worth 100 points. If it is approved on the second review it is 70 points, and on the third 50.
- In room mode, the host sets the stage, the number of blueprints (5, 10, 15) and the time limit.
- The results show the record per blueprint and the balance conditions you missed.
- After a review, slow replay lets you watch how the forces act again, slowly. The resultant force and the turning force also appear on screen.

## Tips
- Weight is mass multiplied by 9.8 N/kg, and elastic force is the spring constant multiplied by the stretched length.

## Game news updates
- After logging in, above the news you can choose which games (Stickseum, Crown Envoy, Beaconfall) you want news from.
- When a new patch note is posted for a game you follow, a new-news mark appears on the news.

## Language and display

stickseum/all-characters.b:
:: Characters = 28
:: HP = 300
:: Based on = v238

All 28 characters are on this one page. Each has a picture, appearance, basic attack, skill, ultimate, passive and skins. Shop and New skins are bought with sC; Tier skins unlock when that character's mastery points reach Diamond (1,750) and Grandmaster (7,000). Pictures show the default skin. Win rates come from bot testing (as of build 254), so real matches may differ. Damage numbers have a different color for each type: fire damage is red (Robin Hood, Slaughterer, Heavy Gunner, Bomber, lava), electric damage is yellow (Agent, Jadai), and poison damage is dark green.

## James (pistol)
!img/pistol.webp
- Appearance: Wears black sunglasses and a dark red necktie.
- Basic attack: 17 damage, 0.85-second fire rate. A standard pistol with solid power and reliable accuracy.
- Skill **Rapid Fire**: Doubles fire rate for 1.8 seconds.
- Ultimate **Power Shot**: Your next shot becomes 1 big, fast bullet dealing 66 damage (pierces players, stops at platforms). Hold R and click to fire that shot right away.
- Passive: None.
- Skins: Shop Midnight Blue Tie (800 sC), Gray Suit Tie (300 sC) / New Banana James (1500 sC) / Tier Crystal Tie (Diamond), Emperor's Red Tie (Grandmaster)
- Hits needed to burn through 300 HP: 18
- Tip: Unload with Rapid Fire, and save Power Shot for when you're sure to land it. One hit is 22% of a full health bar.
- Win rate: 55.9%. Average of bot-vs-bot matches on all maps, as of build 254. It may differ from real matches.
- In codex testing (v237, bot vs bot 1v1), relatively strong matchups were Sheriff and Bomber, and weaker ones were Jadai and Dracula. These are bot measurements, so real matches differ.

## Agent (machine gun)
!img/smg.webp
- Appearance: Wears tactical goggles with light blue lenses and a headset.
- Basic attack: Fires a 10-round burst per click. 6 damage per bullet, 2.2-second cooldown, with slight spread. 60 if every bullet hits.
- Skill **Smoke Bomb**: Throws a smoke bomb at your aim. Thick smoke stays where it lands for 2.5 seconds, and anyone inside moves at half speed and has their view blocked.
- Ultimate **Barrier**: Puts up a wall for 3.5 seconds that blocks players and bullets. Your own bullets pass through.
- Passive: None.
- Skins: Shop Amber Goggles (800 sC), Khaki Goggles (300 sC) / New Hologram Goggles (2000 sC) / Tier Neon Cyber Goggles (Diamond), Plasma Headset (Grandmaster)
- Hits needed to burn through 300 HP: 5 (when all 10 bullets hit)
- Tip: The closer you are, the tighter the spread and the easier it hits. Shooting from behind your Barrier lets your bullets through while blocking enemy fire.
- Win rate: 59.0%. Average of bot-vs-bot matches on all maps, as of build 254. It may differ from real matches.
- In codex testing (v237, bot vs bot 1v1), relatively strong matchups were Kurus and Sheriff, and weaker ones were Jadai and Cleaner. These are bot measurements, so real matches differ.

## Robin Hood (bow)
!img/bow.webp
- Appearance: Wears a green hood.
- Basic attack: 30 damage, 1.5-second reload. Arrows are affected by gravity and fly in an arc.
- Skill **Backstep**: Leap backward and instantly finish reloading your bow.
- Ultimate **Fire Arrows**: Fires 3 fire arrows at once that deal damage over time on hit.
- Passive: None.
- Skins: Shop Twilight Hood (800 sC), Forest Green Hood (300 sC) / New Cupid (2000 sC) / Tier Frost Forest Hood (Diamond), World Tree Hood (Grandmaster)
- Hits needed to burn through 300 HP: 10
- Tip: Shoot from afar, and when someone closes in, Backstep away and fire again right away. Lead moving targets a little.
- Win rate: 51.7%. Average of bot-vs-bot matches on all maps, as of build 254. It may differ from real matches.
- In codex testing (v237, bot vs bot 1v1), relatively strong matchups were Sheriff and Bomber, and weaker ones were Slaughterer and Jadai. These are bot measurements, so real matches differ.

## Ninja (shuriken)
!img/shuriken.webp
- Appearance: Wears a black hood with a white band across the eyes.
- Basic attack: 13 damage, 0.48-second cooldown. Light, fast throws in quick succession.
- Skill **Shadow Step**: Teleport a short distance in your aim direction and go invisible for 1 second.
- Ultimate **Critical Strike**: If your next shuriken hits, it deals double damage (26) and you teleport a short way back. Hold R and click to throw that shot right away.
- Passive: None.
- Skins: Shop Crimson Hood (900 sC), Chestnut Hood (400 sC) / New Cherry Blossom Ninja Hood (2000 sC) / Tier Moonlight Hood (Diamond), Shadow Lord's Hood (Grandmaster)
- Hits needed to burn through 300 HP: 24
- Tip: Use Shadow Step to escape a dangerous range or to dive in. Critical Strike is for hit-and-run.
- Win rate: 54.3%. Average of bot-vs-bot matches on all maps, as of build 254. It may differ from real matches.
- In codex testing (v237, bot vs bot 1v1), relatively strong matchups were Dimension Traveler and Sheriff, and weaker ones were Jadai and Cleaner. These are bot measurements, so real matches differ.

## Soldier (assault rifle)
!img/rifle.webp
- Appearance: Wears an olive-green combat helmet.
- Basic attack: Fires a quick 3-round burst per click. 9 damage per bullet, 1.2-second cooldown. 27 if all hit.
- Skill **Mine Placement**: Places a mine (replaced Focused Fire in build 439).
- Ultimate **Missile Strike**: Missiles drop on 3 random spots. They pass through platforms, and they don't hurt you.
- Passive: None.
- Skins: Shop Desert Camo Cap (900 sC), Jungle Camo Cap (400 sC) / New Urban Night Camo Cap (2000 sC) / Tier Arctic Camo Cap (Diamond), Battlefield Commander's Helmet (Grandmaster)
- Hits needed to burn through 300 HP: 12 (when all 3 bullets hit)
- Tip: You can't tell where the missiles will land, so use them when enemies are bunched up.
- Win rate: 52.3%. Average of bot-vs-bot matches on all maps, as of build 254. It may differ from real matches.
- In codex testing (v237, bot vs bot 1v1), relatively strong matchups were Sheriff and Bomber, and weaker ones were Jadai and Dracula. These are bot measurements, so real matches differ.

## Gambler
!img/gambler.webp
- Appearance: Wears a green dealer's eyeshade.
- Basic attack: 20 damage, 1-second cooldown. Throws a chip straight and far. Each hit stacks 1 chip (up to 6). The more chips you have, the stronger your Skill and Ultimate.
- Skill **Coin Flip**: The chance of heads is 50% plus 7% per chip. Heads heals 25 HP plus 3 more per chip; tails deals 18 damage plus 4 more per chip to the nearest enemy. Chips aren't used up.
- Ultimate **Triple Gamble**: Draws 3 cards from a playing-card deck (52 cards plus 2 jokers). The sum of the numbers (A=1, J=11, Q=12, K=13) becomes the damage of your next basic attack, +1 per chip you hold, and all chips are spent. Same suit adds +5, same number +10, three consecutive numbers +15, and matching both suit and number +20. An A heals 30 HP, a K gives +50% movement speed for 5 seconds, a J resets Skill and Dash cooldowns, a Q makes the Dash cooldown 0 seconds for 1 second, and a Joker copies the card next to it. The cards spin and are revealed one by one from the left.
- Passive: None.
- Skins: Shop High Roller Visor (900 sC), Green Casino Visor (300 sC) / New Casino Royale Visor (2000 sC) / Tier Emerald Visor (Diamond), Jackpot Visor (Grandmaster)
- Hits needed to burn through 300 HP: 15
- Tip: Use your Ultimate with 6 chips and your next basic attack deals 6 more damage. Chips only stack when basic attacks hit, so landing hits first is key.
- Win rate: 52.1%. Average of bot-vs-bot matches on all maps, as of build 254. It may differ from real matches.
- In codex testing (v237, bot vs bot 1v1), relatively strong matchups were Dimension Traveler and Kurus, and weaker ones were Cleaner and Slaughterer. These are bot measurements, so real matches differ.

## Wizard
!img/wizard.webp
- Appearance: Wears a red wizard hat with a gold band at the bottom and a twisty pointed tip.
- Basic attack: A fire spell with 15 damage and a 0.7-second cooldown. It passes through platforms, pierces one player and stops at the second one it hits.
- Skill **Shockwave**: Knocks nearby opponents back really hard (10 damage).
- Ultimate **Magic Circle**: Summons a huge magic circle at your position for 10 seconds. You and your allies get +30% attack and 12 healing per second, and enemies inside take 9 damage per second.
- Passive: None.
- Skins: Shop Emerald Robe (1200 sC), Sky Blue Apprentice Robe (400 sC) / New Milky Way Wizard Hat (2000 sC) / Tier Starlight Wizard Hat (Diamond), Archmage's Hat (Grandmaster)
- Hits needed to burn through 300 HP: 20
- Tip: Your spells pass through platforms and reach opponents hiding behind them. In team modes, fighting together inside the Magic Circle is especially strong.
- Win rate: 56.4%. Average of bot-vs-bot matches on all maps, as of build 254. It may differ from real matches.
- In codex testing (v237, bot vs bot 1v1), relatively strong matchups were Dimension Traveler and Sheriff, and weaker ones were Slaughterer and Cleaner. These are bot measurements, so real matches differ.

## Dimension Traveler (portal gun)
!img/portalgun.webp
- Appearance: Wears goggles with purple lenses.
- Basic attack: 15 damage, 0.55-second cooldown. Bullets bounce up to 3 times off floors and platforms. A bullet that hits the underside of a platform bounces down instead of passing up through it.

beaconfall/sky-fortress.b:
:: Location = In the sky (reached by hot air balloon)
:: Entry = Reach the front gate by balloon
:: Treasure chests = 13
:: Boss = Sky Guardian (299 HP)
:: Respawn = 3 days later
:: Achievements = Sky Fortress, Lord of the Sky

The sky fortress is a fortress floating above the clouds. If you reach its gate by hot air balloon you can go inside, and the Sky Guardian waits in the throne room at the very back.

## How to find it
- Take a hot air balloon up into the sky. The fortress floats at a spot in the sky far from the start, and its position differs from world to world.
- When you get close, a notice appears saying you can see the fortress.
- Reach the front gate with the balloon and you go inside automatically and earn the Sky Fortress achievement.
- When you leave, you return to the spot in the sky where you entered. For 5 seconds after leaving you won't enter again.
- The balloon only flies for 120 seconds, so head straight for the gate once you see the fortress.
- Worlds with no room to place the inner space next to the dungeon get no sky fortress.

## Inside
- It runs from a landing dock through a long corridor, a great hall and two towers to the throne room.
- There are **13 treasure chests**: 3 in each tower, 2 in the great hall and 5 in the throne room. The chests hold ore, valuable items and coins.
- Monsters guard the great hall, the two towers and the approach to the throne room.
- It is decorated with a blue carpet, golden crest banners, stained-glass windows, beams of light through the windows and crystals floating above the pillars.

## Sky Guardian
- The boss that waits in the throne room. It has 299 HP and deals 4.5 damage.
- Patterns: Ice spikes, shockwave, empowered leap, medium falling attack and beam. When enraged, zones and falling boulders are added.
- Defeating it drops 5–7 crystal, 5–7 gold ingots, 2 pearls, its usual drop and the treasure table, and earns the Lord of the Sky achievement.
- It reappears 3 days after you defeat it.
- The same strategies as other bosses work. See the tips on the Boss Guide page.

## Tips
- Bring Strength, Ironskin and a Full Course before going in, and refill durability at the anvil.
- Dodge the beam and falling attacks after their warning appears.
- Grab the chests in the two towers and the great hall before heading to the throne room to stock up on gear and materials.

beaconfall/skin-shop.b:
:: Location = Skin Shop in the main menu
:: Currency = BeaCoin (bC)
:: Skins = 11
:: Prices = 300 bC to 2500 bC
:: Hair and face = 7 hairstyles and 7 faces (80–300 bC), 9 hair colors free
:: Exchange = 1 Hub Coin = 5 bC
:: Achievement rewards = 5 bC to 50 bC

The Skin Shop is where you buy and wear skins for your player character with BeaCoin. A skin only changes colors, headwear and decoration; your abilities stay the same.

## How to use it

- Open the **Skin Shop** from the main menu. Each skin has a preview and a price, and your BeaCoin balance is shown at the top.
- Press the price button to pay in BeaCoin and buy the skin; it is equipped right away. You can't buy it if you don't have enough BeaCoin.
- Switch to a skin you own with the **Equip** button. The skin you're wearing is marked Equipped.
- When logged in, you can exchange Hub Coin for BeaCoin inside the shop.
- Use the **Customize Hair & Face** button at the bottom to style your hairstyle and face separately from your skin (see Customize Hair & Face below).

## The 11 skins and their prices

- Sea Sailor: 300 bC
- Forest Hunter: 400 bC
- Desert Merchant: 600 bC
- Snow Explorer: 800 bC
- Night Shadow: 1000 bC
- Flame Smith: 1300 bC
- Silver Knight: 1600 bC
- Starlight Sage: 1900 bC
- Sky Guardian: 2100 bC
- King of Ruins: 2200 bC
- Void Disciple: 2500 bC
- Buying all 11 costs 14700 bC.

## Customize Hair & Face

- Added in build 87. Open it with the **Customize Hair & Face** button at the bottom of the Skin Shop. You choose it separately from your skin and it layers on top of any skin.
- The 7 hairstyles are bought with BeaCoin: Bald 100 bC; Spiky, Long Hair and Bun 150 bC; Ponytail 200 bC; Mohawk 250 bC; Curly 300 bC.
- The 7 faces are also bought with BeaCoin: Smile and Blush 80 bC; Sleepy, Grumpy and Surprised 100 bC; Wink 150 bC; Sunglasses 200 bC.
- The 9 hair colors (Default, Black, Blond, Red, White, Blue, Pink, Green, Purple) are free and you can change them as often as you like.
- Press the price button once more to buy. Things you already own aren't bought again and can be swapped freely.

## How to earn BeaCoin

- **Achievements**: each one pays 5 to 50 bC depending on difficulty. Earning all 60 adds up to 965 bC. See the Achievement List page for details.
- **Hub Coin**: 1 Hub Coin gives 5 bC. You can exchange in the Skin Shop or in the hub's coin exchange, and you need to be logged in. The exchanged BeaCoin arrives automatically when you return to the game.

## Good to know

- In multiplayer, you also see the skins, hairstyles and faces of the other players in the same room.
- A skin is cosmetic only. Armor is still drawn over the skin.
- Even if you log in with a different account in the same browser, skins and BeaCoin don't get mixed up. When you switch accounts, the previous account's save is kept separately, and it comes back as it was when you log in to that account again.
- Your BeaCoin balance and the skins you bought are saved in the game settings, and also uploaded to the cloud save when you're logged in. The cloud part may depend on the server's readiness.

crownenvoy/crowncoin.b:
:: Currency = CrownCoin (cC)
:: Balance = 👑 button at the top
:: Play reward = 10 cC every 15 turns
:: Daily limit = 100 cC
:: Achievement reward = 5–50 cC on first unlock
:: Hub Coin = 1 = 20 cC
:: Scenario price = 0–500 cC

CrownCoin (cC) is Crown Envoy's currency. You collect it by playing and unlocking achievements, and spend it on shared scenarios that have a price. You need to be logged in with a Frenchfries777 account to earn and spend it.

## How to earn it

- **Playing**: you get 10 cC for every 15 turns you play. The daily limit is 100 cC, and a day follows Korean time. It only accrues while you are alive and the game isn't over, and resuming a saved game doesn't pay for turns that already passed.
- **Achievements**: the first time you unlock an achievement you get 5 to 50 cC, once. It doesn't count toward the daily limit.
- **Selling scenarios**: when a scenario you uploaded is bought, you receive the full amount paid. There is no fee.
- **Hub Coin**: 1 Hub Coin can be exchanged for 20 cC. Exchange it in the hub's coin exchange window and it arrives in the in-game wallet.
- Your balance is shown on the 👑 button at the top, and pressing it shows how much you earned and how to spend it.

## Achievement rewards (30, 580 cC in total)

- 5 cC (6): First Campaign, First Conquest, Non-Aggression, Silk Road, The Guns Fall Silent, Bitter Lesson
- 10 cC (4): Seasoned Monarch, First Victory, Steadfast Alliance, War Together
- 15 cC (6): David and Goliath, Ruler of the Seas, Overflowing Treasury, Master of Vassals, Captured Enemy General, Rewriting History
- 20 cC (4): Ironclad Defense, Comeback General, Victory Together, Monarch Who Beat a Human
- 25 cC (2): Great Empire, Hundred Years' War
- 30 cC (4): Regular on the Throne, Crown of Victory, Ever Victorious, Phoenix
- 40 cC (3): Conqueror King, Unifier of the Realm, Hegemony
- 50 cC (1): Crown Envoy Conqueror

## How to spend it: shared scenarios with a price

- In Browse Shared Scenarios, a scenario with a price can be tried exactly once before you buy it. The trial copy appears at the bottom of the historical scenario list and disappears when you refresh the page. The trial can only be played up to turn 12; when turn 12 ends, the result is decided and you can't continue. Games played with a trial scenario are not saved and don't appear in the saved games list.
- Buying costs the price in cC and saves the scenario to your own scenarios. The full amount goes to the uploader. You can't buy it if you don't have enough cC.
- A scenario you bought cannot be shared again.
- Scenarios you uploaded yourself, ones you already bought, and free (0 cC) ones are simply downloaded.
- When you upload, you set the price between 0 and 500 cC. Scenarios uploaded before prices existed are all free.

## Good to know

- Your balance is kept in a server wallet, so it is the same in any browser with the same account.
- Without logging in no cC accrues. You can still play the game as usual.

isleport/getting-started.b:
:: Genre = Island tycoon sandbox
:: Win condition = None
:: Latest version = v0.2 build 63
:: Starting gold = 250
:: First seeds = 6 wheat seeds
:: Achievements = 113
:: Languages = 18 (13 real, 5 fictional)

Isleport is an island tycoon sandbox: you grow crops on your own island, process them, then steer ships across the sea to sell them at ports. There is no win condition, so you grow your island at your own pace while filling the codex and achievements. It starts right in the browser with nothing to install, and on phones and tablets you play with the on-screen joystick and buttons.

## Title screen
- When the game opens, a "Made by Frenchfries777" intro plays, then the title screen appears.
- The intro shows a dawn field where crops grow and a ship sails by far away, and it cannot be skipped (build 53). The intro has a song and the game music follows it. On browsers that block sound, tapping the screen starts the intro (build 55). It is drawn at a sharper resolution, and at a lower one with Optimization on (build 56).
- With no save there is a **Start** button; with a save there are **Continue** and **New game** buttons.
- There are **Log in**, **How to play** and **Patch notes** buttons and a language selector.
- The **Play** button on the site opens just one new tab (build 56).
- In Settings you can choose **Optimization** (On or Off), **Effects** (High, Medium, Low) and **Frame rate** (Auto, 30, 60). Turning Optimization on draws at 30 FPS and turns off rain and snow effects, which keeps the device cooler. Phones that look low-end start with Optimization already on (build 56). These values are linked to the hub's shared optimization settings.
- A new game starts on a spring day.

## Starting state
- You start with 250 gold, 6 wheat seeds, 6 fields, 4 ranch pens and one Sloop.
- At first the warehouse holds up to 30 of each good.
- The start is slow because you do the chores yourself. Research, workers, warehouse expansions, conveyors, greenhouses and sprinklers gradually make everything run by itself.

## Guide and quests
- In a new game, a one-line task appears at the bottom of the screen. It walks you through planting a field, harvesting, selling at the market and sending a ship from the harbor, and you can skip it.
- Fields to plant and fields to harvest get a blinking ▼ marker.
- When the guide ends, follow the ★ quests at the top. There are 17 quests, and each one pays gold (from 50 gold for the first to 9,000 gold for the last).
- You never get stuck even if you run out of both money and goods. A neighbor pays you a small wage so you can start again.
- In the **Story** page at the town hall you can follow an eight-chapter story about your grandfather's old ledger. In the last chapter, choosing the ledger's fate plays an ending scene with dialogue, and the credits roll. Donating the ledger to the museum makes museum admission 1.5 times higher, and keeping it to grow your company raises all sale prices by 3%. You can skip the credits, the game goes on after them, and you can rewatch the ending from the Story page at the town hall.

## Layout of the island
- Fields, ranch, town and harbor form one large map you can walk across. Instead of menus, you walk up to the house, warehouse, research, bank, notice board and harbor buildings to use them.
- The town has the market, seed shop, your own shop, town hall, train station, newsstand, restaurant street, museum, post office, inn and more.
- Day and night, weather and the seasons (spring, summer, autumn, winter) change slowly.

## Aquarium and tavern
- Added in build 45. The aquarium is in the south of town. When you catch a fish while fishing, one of 14 species is caught along with it, and displaying it in a tank builds up admission fees.
- The aquarium can be expanded twice, and each species caught for the first time gives bonus gold.
- There is a tavern by the port. Buy a drink and a sailor tells you which port has good prices right now, which goods are in heavy demand and news of storms. Very rarely he hands over a piece of an old map.

## Ranks
- Your rank rises through 7 steps based on the total gold you have earned: Peddler, Hawker (2,000), Merchant (10,000), Big merchant (40,000), Tycoon (150,000), Grand trader (500,000), Lord of the sea (2,000,000).
- A higher rank also raises how much you can borrow from the bank.

## Saving and accounts
- Progress is saved in this browser. If you clear site data or switch to another browser, the save is not visible.
- When you log in with a Frenchfries777 account, each account has its own save and your achievements appear on your hub profile card. You can even log in with a different account in each tab.
- Saves made while logged in and while logged out are separate.
- Press **Exit** on the settings screen to save and close the game window.
- The game runs in only one window at a time (build 56). If it is already running in another window, a notice says so, the game in this window stops and it does not save, so saves never overwrite each other.
- The **Lobby** button at the top right of the game screen opens a confirm window, and confirming saves and returns to the lobby. If you are in a room, you leave that room (build 59).

## More pages
Research, buildings, crops, ports, ranks, achievements, facilities, story, mines, multiplayer and strategy are covered in: **Research List**, **Buildings and Recipes**, **Crops and Goods Prices**, **Ports and Trade**, **Ranks and Bank**, **Achievement List**, **Town Facilities**, **Story and Villagers**, **Mine Isle and Volcano Isle**, **Playing Together**, **Strategy**

isleport/controls.b:
:: Move = Arrow keys, WASD, tap the screen
:: Use = E, Space, Enter
:: Take a photo = P
:: Collect all = H (needs research)
:: Switch scene = 1-4
:: Close window = Esc

## Keyboard
- **Arrow keys / WASD** : Walk your character. While sailing yourself, they steer the ship.
- **E / Space / Enter** : Use the thing nearby. When you get close, that object gets an outline. While sailing yourself, press E near an island to land and press E at your own harbor to return.
- **P** : Take a photo of the current screen.
- **H** : Collect all ripe crops and animal goods at once. You need to finish the "Reap all" research first.
- **1 / 2 / 3 / 4** : Jump straight to the fields, ranch, town or harbor.
- **Esc** : Close the open window. With no window open, it leaves the island landing map, returns from the sea view to your island, or ends a visit to someone else's island.

## Mouse and touch
- Tap the screen and your character walks to that spot.
- Ripe crops and animal goods are collected automatically when you walk over them. After the "Big basket" research, just getting close collects them.
- On phones and tablets, move with the on-screen joystick and use things with the Act button.

## Home menu
Using the house brings up the following menu.
- Decorate (up to 80 items), Hire workers (after the "Hire workers" research), Take a photo, Photo album
- Stats, Goals, Codex, Account, Settings, How to play
- Connect to others, Title

## Photo mode
- Press P or choose **Take a photo** in the home menu to capture the current screen. The screen flashes white at the moment you take it.
- Photos collect in the **Photo album**, up to 12. If you take more, the oldest photo drops out. In the album you can view a photo large or delete it, and the **Take one now** button takes one right away.
- The first photo you take at the fountain plaza, clock tower, lake, station, lighthouse, museum or harbor earns a 50 gold bonus. It is once per landmark, and the album shows how many landmarks you have earned.

isleport/farming.b:
:: Fields = 6 at first, up to 48
:: Ranch pens = 4 at first, up to 12
:: Crops = 23
:: Ranch buildings = 7
:: Seeds = Bought at the seed shop

## Planting and harvesting
- You need seeds to plant. At first you only have 6 wheat seeds; buy seeds for each crop at the **Seed shop** by the town gate, 1, 5 or 10 at a time.
- Press E at an empty field to plant, and walk over it to harvest when it is grown.
- Each crop has its own growth time and yield. Growth speed changes with the season and is usually slowest in winter.
- Tree crops (♻) keep bearing once planted: apple, grapes, olive, strawberry, tea leaves, pomegranate, dragon fruit and cocoa. Except for strawberry, tree crops take twice as long to grow.
- You buy more fields one at a time with gold. The price starts at 50 gold and rises by 22 for each field. Empty fields can also be sold.
- At the back hill clearing in the town hall, pay to clear the forest and rocks and you can use 12 more fields.

## Home island crops
Base growth time, yield and seed price.
- Wheat : 20 s, 3, 5 gold
- Potato : 25 s, 3, 6 gold
- Corn : 28 s, 3, 8 gold
- Tomato : 35 s, 3, 10 gold
- Pumpkin : 50 s, 2, 14 gold
- Cotton : 60 s, 4, 18 gold

The other crops are unlocked with gold by sailing to other islands. The list per island is on the Sailing and islands page.

## Farming research
- **Sturdy plow**, **Fertilizer** : Crops grow 10% faster each. **Sprinklers** add another 12%.
- **Greenhouse** : Crops grow almost on time even in winter.
- **Bumper harvest** : +1 per harvest.
- **Auto-sowing** : Turn on "Replant in every field" in the field menu and every harvest replants using one seed.
- **Sow all** : "Plant in all empty fields" sows every empty field at once.
- **Reap all** : Collect all ripe crops and goods at once at the warehouse or with the H key.
- **Hire workers** : Opens after Big basket. Hire up to 12 workers with gold at your house, and they collect ripe crops and goods. After **Overseer** the workers replant, and **Tractor** makes them 50% faster.
- **Endless seeds** : Opens after Overseer. Seeds never run out, so you plant unlocked crops without buying seeds.

## Ranch
Build cost, feed, output and time.
- Coop : 120 gold, 1 wheat, 2 eggs, 24 s
- Sheepfold : 220 gold, 2 wheat, 2 wool, 50 s
- Cow barn : 300 gold, 2 corn, 2 milk, 40 s
- Pigsty : 260 gold, 2 corn, 2 pork, 55 s
- Goat pen : 240 gold, 2 wheat, 2 goat milk, 42 s
- Fishing hut : 180 gold, no feed, 3 fish, 36 s
- Apiary : 200 gold, no feed, 2 honey, 45 s

Upgrading makes them produce faster and more. The **Better feed** research makes them 15% faster, and **Larger pens** adds +1 output.

## Warehouse
- At first it holds up to 30 of each good.
- **Expand warehouse** at the warehouse adds 25 at a time, up to 10 times. The **Big barn** research adds 40 more.

isleport/crafting.b:
:: Town buildings = 20
:: Home island buildings = Mill, Bakery, Dairy, Warehouse, Lighthouse, Stall, Shipyard
:: Market price = 65% of base price
:: Stall price = 90% of base price
:: Currency = Gold

## Crafting
- Build a workshop on town land and load ingredients, and over time it turns out pricier goods.
- Building a workshop or upgrading it takes construction time. It goes up in the order foundation, pillars, roof, and you cannot use it while it is under construction.
- At first you do it by hand. Tap a building and choose what to make to load ingredients from the warehouse, then take out the finished goods and carry them to the warehouse.
- The **Auto feed** research has buildings take ingredients from the warehouse by themselves, and **Auto carry** moves finished goods to the warehouse. **Quick hands** and **Mastery** each make crafting 15% faster, and **Conveyor belts** make it 20% faster.
- The market tells you how much a good's value rises if you process it.

## Crafting examples
- Mill : 2 wheat into flour, 2 rice into rice cake
- Bakery : 2 flour into bread, 1 flour and 2 apples into apple pie, 1 flour and 2 eggs into cookies
- Dairy : 2 milk into cheese or butter, 2 goat milk into goat cheese
- Kitchen : Apple jam, tomato sauce, pizza, spiced stew, pasta, sushi, curry
- Confectionery : Chocolate, cake, candy, pudding
- There are also the Winery, Oil press, Loom, Tailor, Cannery, Sugar mill, Smokehouse, Brewery, Tea house, Dyeworks and Jeweler.

There are utility buildings too. The Warehouse adds storage, the Lighthouse makes all ships faster, and the Shipyard lets you build bigger ships and lowers ship prices.

## Where to sell
- **Market** : Sell goods straight from the warehouse at the town gate. The price is 65% of base price, so once you have a lot it pays more to ship them to a port.
- **Stall** : Sells a chosen good little by little at 90% of base price.
- **Your own shop** : Stock goods and set a price multiplier, and customers buy them.
- **Ports** : Load a ship and send it off. Each port has its own prices and wanted goods. Selling a lot of the same good lowers its price, which recovers over time.
- **Port contracts and orders** : Filling them earns rewards and reputation. Contracts and orders that ask for processed goods pay much more, and higher reputation pays more when you sell.
- **Restaurant street and confectionery** : Deliver dishes or ingredients. Repeated deliveries bring regulars and raise rewards by up to 20%.
- **Visiting traders** : Sometimes come to town and pay extra.
- **Stall haggling** : Choose Stall haggling at the market and a customer comes wanting 3 to 5 of one good from your warehouse. The asking price starts at about 1.6 times the base price. Use **Cut 10%** to lower it, then try **Sell at this price**. If you press sell while the price is above what the customer will accept, their patience (4 pips) drops, and when it runs out they leave. After one round, the next customer comes 30 seconds later.
- **Pre-orders** : Choose them at the notice board. You can take them from 3 offers that change every 5 minutes, and hold up to 3 at once. You first receive 30% of the goods' value as a deposit, and if you deliver within the 8 to 12 minute deadline you get 140% of the value (deposit included). If you miss the deadline, you pay back the deposit plus 10%. Higher ranks bring pricier goods.

## Selling research
- **Haggling**, **Big spender**, **Exclusive deals** : +5% when selling, each.
- **Market intel** : Shows in advance whether port prices will rise or fall.
- **Contract broker** : Contract rewards +25%.

## Bank
- Buy and sell stocks. There are six sectors, grain, orchard, wine, textiles, fisheries and trade, and port bumper crops, festivals, storms and pirate raids affect the related stock prices.
- Money you deposit earns interest, and you can withdraw it at any time.
- Borrow money in the loan tab. The limit depends on your rank, from 500 gold to 500,000 gold.
- With trade insurance, you get back 70% of the value of cargo stolen by pirates.
- Buy a newspaper for 3 gold at the town newsstand and a paper with price tables, forecasts and news opens up.

isleport/sailing.b:
:: Ports = 6
:: Ships = Sloop, Merchant ship, Galleon
:: Max ships = 8
:: Secret islands = Coral Cay, Amber Isle, Ruin Atoll, Mine Isle, Volcano Isle
:: Inland regions = 3 (by train)

## Ships
- At the harbor, load a ship and send it to another port. Choose "Sail it yourself" at the harbor to steer the ship yourself.
- **Sloop** : Cargo 20, 400 gold
- **Merchant ship** : Cargo 45, 1,400 gold, needs shipyard Lv 1.
- **Galleon** : Cargo 90, 4,200 gold, needs shipyard Lv 2.
- The **Sturdy hulls** research makes ships 20% faster, **Navigation** and **Logistics** add 15% each, and **Bigger holds** adds 20% cargo. Fitting steel reinforcement with iron bars from Mine Isle increases cargo and speed.

## Crew and pirates
- Hire crew at the harbor. A Navigator makes ships 5% faster, a Gunner fends off pirates 10% better, a Porter adds 7% cargo, and a Haggler earns 1.5% more when selling.
- Each personality (Steady, Greedy, Lucky) has its own wage and skill.
- Pirates appear at sea. Add escorts to your ships, and the **Escort drills** research makes you 15% better at fending them off.

## Hull and dock repair
- Sailing through a storm or losing to pirates damages the ship’s hull (build 49).
- Below 70% hull the ship slows down, and below 30% cargo leaks while sailing.
- While docked, use the repair button in the ship list to do a dock repair.
- A ship out at sea (not on its way back) can be sent a **supply boat** from the ship list. It costs 60 gold plus 2 gold per cargo slot (100 gold for a sloop). It repairs the hull by 20%, and **Load cargo** lets you put more goods from the warehouse onto the ship, up to its free cargo space. Once the ship reaches port, loading is no longer possible.
- Turn on the **Credit sales** button in the ship list and you sell on credit to regular ports where your reputation is level 1 or higher, at a price 15% higher. You collect the money on your next visit to that port, but now and then it goes unpaid.

## Port news
Events sometimes happen at ports and last 90 seconds.
- **Bumper demand** : Demand for one good at that port rises 60%.
- **Festival** : All goods sell 20% higher.
- **Storm** : Voyages toward it take 50% longer.

## The 6 ports and unlocks
When you land on an island, you can unlock seeds and workshops your home island lacks with gold.
- **Goldport** : A grain port full of wheat and potatoes. Unlocks carrot, rice, sugarcane, gold barley and the Sugar mill and Brewery.
- **Redport** : A port with many apple orchards. Unlocks apple, strawberry, chili, pomegranate and the Kitchen and Confectionery.
- **Lavender Port** : A port known for vineyards and wine. Unlocks grapes, olive, lavender, saffron and the Winery and Oil press.
- **Cotton Port** : A port with cotton fields and a cloth market. Unlocks tea leaves, cocoa, cloud cotton and the Loom, Tailor and Tea house.
- **Salt Bay** : A fishing village that pays well for grain. Unlocks seaweed and the Cannery and Smokehouse.
- **Spiceport** : A distant trade hub with rare imports. Unlocks dragon fruit and the Dyeworks and Jeweler.

## Landing on islands
- When you reach an island by sailing yourself, you land on that island's map. Every island has its own shape and scenery.
- Pick up sparkling local goods, trade and unlock at the market building, and return to your ship at the pier.
- Tap a landmark and a resident asks a favor; help three times and you receive a map.

## Secret islands
- Fish bottles floating at sea out of the water to get map pieces. Every three pieces reveal one secret island.
- **Coral Cay**, **Amber Isle** and **Ruin Atoll** yield coral, amber and old porcelain.
- **Mine Isle** : Strike rocks to mine stone, iron ore, copper ore and rough gems. Melt them into iron and copper bars at the smelter.
- **Volcano Isle** : Mine obsidian, sulfur and rubies. When a red circle flashes on the ground, lava is about to burst, and if you do not get out of the way you lose gold.

## Trains and inland regions
- Take the train from the town station to three inland regions: Blue Highlands (rank 1), Pine Forest Village (rank 2) and Red Ridge Depot (rank 3).
- Each region has a walkable map, a market and residents. At regional markets you sell goods at high prices and buy that region's specialties cheaply.

isleport/faq.b:
:: Category = Frequently asked questions
:: Ending = None (sandbox)
:: Solo play = Yes
:: Room code = 4 letters
:: Save = Inside the browser

## Does it end?
No. It is a sandbox with no win condition. You grow your island at your own pace while filling the codex and achievements.

## Can I play alone?
Yes. Connecting to other islands is optional, and you can keep playing on your own island without connecting.

## How do I play with other people?
At your house or the notice board, press **Connect to others** to create a room or join with a 4-letter room code. Once connected you can visit other people's islands and trade live with anyone you meet there while both of you see the goods and gold on offer. The swap happens as soon as both press Ready. There are also auctions, chat, shared projects, big village orders and pirate raids. When you open or join a room, your hub friends can see it, and when a friend taps the invite notification the game opens and drops them straight into that room.

## My save is gone
Saves live inside the browser. If you clear site data or switch to another browser, they are not visible. Saves made while logged in and logged out are also separate.

## My gold hit 0
You are not stuck. Just sell something at the market. If you run out of both money and goods, a neighbor pays you a small wage.

## I have no seeds, so I cannot plant
Buy them at the seed shop by the town gate. More kinds of seeds are unlocked by sailing to other islands. After the **Endless seeds** research, seeds never run out.

## Pressing H does not harvest anything
You need the **Reap all** research. Reap all opens after **Sow all**.

## Where do I hire workers?
After finishing the **Hire workers** research (after Big basket), tap your house and hire them with gold under **Hire workers**. The maximum is 12.

## Fruit trees grow too slowly
Tree crops keep bearing once planted, but in exchange, except for strawberry, they take twice as long to grow.

## Where do photos go?
They collect in the **Photo album** in the home menu, up to 12. Take them with the P key.

## Does it work on phones?
Yes. Move with the on-screen joystick and use things with the Act button.

isleport/patch-history.b:
:: Latest build = v0.2 build 63
:: Photo mode = build 38
:: Aquarium and tavern = build 45
:: v0.2 release = 2026-10-18
:: v0.1 release = 2026-10-18

This records the main changes to Isleport. The latest build is v0.2 build 63 (2026-10-26). You can also see it under the **Patch notes** button on the in-game start screen.

## 2026-10-26
- **build 63** Calmer screen: Fixed the screen trembling while it followed you as you walked. Removed the up-and-down flicker on crops, ships, shops, villagers and island items, and made the water sparkle, flags and selection outline flicker slower and softer.

## 2026-10-25
- **build 62** Lighter load for the room host: Market updates sent by the host are spaced further apart (even further with the low-spec option). Position updates are skipped while nothing moves, and a message meant for one player is passed on only to that player. Island generation is faster, and islands are smaller with the low-spec option.
- **build 61** Bigger, grander islands: Other islands are about 30% bigger. Manors, towers, fountains, houses, stalls, lanterns and flower beds were added to every island, and walking on islands is faster. The shady traders and the report button were removed.
- **build 60**: Filled in missing translations (game text, intro, patch notes, versions).

educations/proverb.b:
:: Subject = Korean language (proverbs, idioms)
:: Stages = 6 (Complete the Proverb, Meaning, Missing Word, Idiom Investigation, Mixed Investigation, Endless Investigation)
:: Modes = Solo investigation, Open an office (room, up to 40 players)
:: Room code = 5 characters
:: Login = Not needed

## Overview
It is an investigation game where you solve cases of proverbs and idioms by working out the clues. The proverbs and idioms appear in Korean, and their meanings are shown translated.

## The six screens
1. Home: choose Solo investigation, Open an office or Enter with a code. The office code is the 5-character code the teacher gives you.
2. Choose a case type: when playing solo, you pick one of the 6 stages. Complete the Proverb gives the first half of a proverb and you add the second half, Meaning finds what a proverb means, and Missing Word fills in the empty word. Idiom Investigation uses the meaning as a clue to fill the blank of an idiom and to find its meaning. Mixed Investigation mixes all five proverb and idiom case types (15 cases). Endless Investigation starts with 3 lives, each mistake costs one, and the cases keep coming until they are all gone.
3. Office lobby: the host picks the case type, the number of cases (10, 15 or 20) and the time limit (3, 5 or 10 minutes), decides whether the host joins the investigation or just watches, then presses Start. The number of detectives who joined and your own name are shown.
4. Solving a case: the case number, score and time left are at the top. Pick an answer and the correct one is shown in green. After solving you move on to the next case, and you can end the run with Close Investigation.
5. Investigation status: this is the screen the host sees when only watching. It shows the office code, the time left and how many detectives have finished, and the host can press Close Investigation.
6. Investigation result: your score and an error log are shown. You can go back to the start or investigate again.

## Scoring and sound
- A correct answer is worth 100 points. Solving within 4 seconds adds 20 points, and within 8 seconds adds 10.
- Correct and wrong answers have sound effects, and the 🔊 button at the top turns the sound off and on.
- Room mode ranks players by score within the time limit, needs no login and only asks for a name.
- 78 proverbs and idioms come with a scene made of an emoji picture, a one-line situation and a line of dialogue. Scenes appear only on the Korean screen and not in other languages.

- **Isleport** : Harbor Day, Harbor Evening, Harbor Night, Harbor Morning, Harbor Afternoon, Harbor Midday, Harbor Dawn. The seven tracks take turns in the game and are also in the music room. There are no separate tracks for each place.
- Beaconfall's lobby music plays one track picked at random from the spring, summer, autumn and winter tracks, and a new one is picked when you come back to the lobby.

account/languages.b:
:: Language count = 18 (13 real languages, 5 fictional languages)
:: Real languages = Korean, English, Español, Français, Deutsch, 日本語, 简体中文, Português (Brasil), Русский, Türkçe, Italiano, Polski, العربية
:: Fictional languages = Newspeak, Translator Korean, Aurebesh, Standard Galactic, Emojiar
:: Where to change = Language selector on each site and game

## Overview
This document lists the languages supported by the hub and the game sites. Languages are shared across the hub, Stickseum, Crown Envoy, Beaconfall, Isleport, Educations, and Tools, so the same selection is used everywhere. If you change the language in one place, other sites open in the same language.

## 13 Real Languages
- Korean, English, Español, Français, Deutsch, 日本語: The 6 languages supported from the start.
- 简体中文, Português (Brasil), Русский, Türkçe: Added on 2026-10-21.
- Italiano, Polski, العربية: Added on 2026-10-22. Arabic lines run from right to left.

## How Far Translation Goes
- Hub: All 13 real languages and 5 fictional languages can be selected. For the wiki and patch notes, see the items below.
- Stickseum, Crown Envoy, Beaconfall, Isleport: Both the games and the sites let you select all 13 real languages and 5 fictional languages.
- Educations, Tools: The sites and tools also support the same 18 languages (13 real, 5 fictional). Problems that are inherently in Korean, such as the Proverb Detective, Four-Character Idioms, spelling quizzes, and the dad jokes in AI chat, are not translated and stay in Korean.
- Dummy Party: Supports 6 languages: Korean, English, Español, Français, Deutsch, and 日本語.
- Wiki: Each document has translations into English, Spanish, French, German, and Japanese. 简体中文, Português, Русский, Türkçe, Italiano, Polski, العربية, and Newspeak appear with English body text. Emojiar shows that English body text converted to emojis, and Translator Korean shows the original Korean text.
- Newly added phrases may appear in English or Korean until translation processing is finished.

## Translation Quality
- Translations into 简体中文, Português (Brasil), Русский, Türkçe, Italiano, Polski, and العربية are machine translations that have not been reviewed by people, so some parts may be awkward or wrong.
- Places that are easy to get wrong are wordplay, words attached to numbers (Russian, Polish, Turkish), short labels where the same English word has a different meaning, and long words that get cut off on narrow buttons.
- For Arabic, only the text lines run right to left, and numbers, formulas, and units stay as they are, so the order may look mixed within a sentence.
- If you notice a translation that looks wrong, let us know through community feedback in the hub.

## Fictional Languages
These are the 5 languages in the fictional language group of the language selection list. They are not made by a translation program; they are playful languages created with our own rules and fonts. Here is what each language is like.

### Newspeak (nw)
- Inspiration: Newspeak from George Orwell's novel 1984.
- Instead of using separate antonyms, un- is added in front of a word. Examples: optional = unmust, end date = Unstart date, ago = unnow, wrong = ungood.
- Word roots are few, and words are shortened or joined together. Examples: login = Selfgive, settings = Rules, score = Goodcounts, game = Joyduty, popular = Plusgoodthinked.
- Emphasis is added with plus and doubleplus. Example: Really delete? = Doubleplusvaporize?
- Only in this language, the hub's front page background shows the Two Minutes Hate scene (telescreen static, Goldstein, marching soldiers, the crowd, Big Brother and party slogans).
- The site logo changes to a Big Brother poster, WAR IS PEACE · FREEDOM IS SLAVERY · IGNORANCE IS STRENGTH appears at the bottom and top, and 2 + 2 = 5 appears below the hub number row. The community page closes with a screen showing that the telescreen is watching.

### Translator Korean (gk)
- Inspiration: Clumsy machine translation. English is translated word by word into Korean, so the meaning comes out wrong.
- Example: "Log in" comes out as "통나무 안에" (inside a log), games as "사냥감들" (prey), and settings as "환경들" (environments). Some English words are left unchanged.
- On the wiki, the original Korean text is shown as is.

### Aurebesh (au)
- Inspiration: Star Wars. Aurebesh is the name of the writing system used in the Star Wars universe.
- This is a font-based game that shows English in Aurebesh-style letters. It is not a language with separate translations; only the font of the English screen changes.
- The shapes of the letters A~Z and the digits 0~9 were not drawn by the owner. The owner took photos of the letters and showed them to Claude AI, and the font was made from those shapes. Digits are also drawn in Aurebesh letters.

### Standard Galactic (sg)
- Inspiration: The Commander Keen series. The letters are modeled on the Standard Galactic Alphabet that appears in Commander Keen.
- Minecraft is also an inspiration. The letters that appear on Minecraft's enchanting table are the same Standard Galactic letters.
- This is a font-based game that shows English in Standard Galactic letters. Like Aurebesh, it changes only the font on the English screen.
- The letter shapes were not drawn by the owner. The owner took photos of the letters and showed them to Claude AI, and the font was made from those. Only the English letters A~Z change, and digits stay as they are.

### Shared Rules for the Two Font Languages
- When selected, English is saved on all sites and only the font display is turned on separately. Choosing another language turns it off. In the language selection list, the name is always shown in its own font.

### Emojiar (em)
- Inspiration: A playful language that speaks with emojis instead of letters. In the language selection list, its name appears as 😀💬.
- When selected, English is saved, and the English text on screen is converted to emojis using a word dictionary and a list of common phrases. Examples: Log in = 🔑, Settings = ⚙️, Fry Lab = 🍟🧪, Thank you = 🙏.
- Words not in the dictionary are dropped. A single unknown word (such as a nickname) is left as is. Text left in Korean that was not translated to English has only the Korean words in the dictionary replaced.
- Hovering over the text shows the original English sentence. Input fields, code, and the language list are not changed.
- The page is hidden until the emoji conversion file is loaded, and it waits at most 2.5 seconds. If the file fails to load, English is shown as is. Like Aurebesh and Standard Galactic, the emoji display is turned on separately.

account/community.b:
:: Address = frenchfries777.com/community/
:: Where to open = Community in the hub’s top menu
:: Tabs = Board, Chat, Friend News, Play Together, Gallery, Feedback & Bug Reports
:: To write = Log in (Frenchfries777 account)

The community is the hub page where people write posts, chat and look for others to play with. It has six tabs, and polls and Hub Coin open in separate windows. Writing posts, chatting, posting a party call and sending feedback require logging in.

## Board
- The filters at the top are All, Popular, Free, Stickseum, Crown Envoy, Beaconfall and Developer Log. Popular shows posts that received likes, most popular first, up to 20. Only designated developers can pick Developer Log as a tag.
- A post has a tag, a title (up to 80 characters) and a body (up to 4000 characters). You can attach up to 4 photos per post, each up to 3 MB. Photos can also be pasted in.
- A search box finds posts by title and body. Posts show 20 at a time, and More loads further ones.
- Posts can get likes (👍) and comments (up to 1000 characters). Posts, comments and chat messages can get six emoji reactions: 😂 😮 😢 🔥 ❤️ 👏.
- The author and the admin can delete posts and comments. Deleting a post needs a second press of the button. Other people’s posts and comments have a report (🚩) button.

## Chat
- There is one room shared by everyone. New messages appear right away, and the latest 60 are shown.
- A message can be up to 300 characters, and you can send one photo at a time (pasting works). You can delete your own messages, and the admin can delete any. Messages from people you blocked are hidden.

## Friend News
- It gathers the achievements your friends earned in the last two weeks, the games they started for the first time and the posts they wrote. You must be logged in to see it.

## Play Together
- This is where you gather people to play with right now. You choose the game (Stickseum, Crown Envoy, Beaconfall), write a one-line note (up to 100 characters) and, if you like, add a room link (starting with https://, up to 300 characters).
- A call disappears after 2 hours, and the list refreshes by itself. If there is a room link, the Join button takes you straight into that room, otherwise an Open game button appears. The person who posted it can take it down.

## Gallery
- It collects only the photos attached to posts tagged with a game. Pressing a photo opens that post.

## Feedback & Bug Reports
- The kind is Bug, Idea or Other, and the target is chosen from Hub, Stickseum, Crown Envoy and Beaconfall. The text can be up to 2000 characters.
- What you send can be seen only by you and the admin. The address of the page that was open and your device information are sent along. When the admin has seen it, it is marked as confirmed and you get a notification.
- Reports about posts, chat messages or people are sent with the 🚩 Report button. You pick a reason from spam/ads, abuse/harassment, inappropriate photo and other, and can block that person at the same time. You get a notification when it has been handled.

## Polls
- Polls are not a tab but a separate window (📊). The poll button appears to the left of the account button only while a poll is open.
- The admin posts polls, and each person has one vote. Pressing another option changes your vote, and the Cancel choice button withdraws it. Results are shown after you vote or after the poll has ended.
- The question can be up to 200 characters with 2 to 6 options, and the end time is chosen from keep open, in 1 day or in 1 week. Designated developers can post a “next update poll”.

## Hub Coin
- The 🪙 number at the top of the hub is your Hub Coin. You get 10 coins for attending each day, and a streak of 7 days adds a +20 bonus. The day changes at Korean time.
- The daily quests are to play one game, write a post or comment on the board, say something in chat and take part in a poll. Each finished quest gives 5 coins, and collecting all 3 gives 5 more.
- You can gift up to 100 coins a day to friends. Coins can be exchanged for in-game currency.

## Friends and notifications
- In Friends in the account menu you search for people by nickname and send a request. Friends made here are friends inside the games too. Friends can message each other, but you cannot message people who are not your friends.
- The bell holds notifications for comments, likes, mentions, friend requests, messages, Hub Coin gifts, room invitations and admin replies. Which ones you receive is set in Settings. Blocking someone hides their posts and chat messages, and a block can be lifted.

account/settings.b:
:: Address = frenchfries777.com/settings/
:: Where to open = Settings in the hub’s top menu
:: Sections = Display, Language, Account, Optimization, Notifications
:: Scope = Display and language apply to the hub, games, educations and tools sites together, and optimization is read as the same values by the hub and the games

Settings is the hub page where you change the display, language, account, optimization and notifications in one place. The Back button at the top left returns you to the site you were on before opening Settings.

## Display
- The theme is one of five: Dark, Yellow, Red, Blue and Light.
- The text size has four steps: Small, Normal, Large and Extra large.

## Language
- You pick from 18 languages: 13 real and 5 fictional. The page reloads when you change it. For details, see the Languages page.

## Account
- If you are not logged in, a Log in button appears, and once you are, the My account panel appears. You can create an account with a username and password or continue with the GitHub or Google buttons. On your first visit you choose a username.
- A nickname can be up to 12 characters. A username is 3 to 16 letters, digits or underscores, and one that already exists cannot be used. If you change your username, you log in to every game with the new one.
- A password is 6 to 72 characters and can be changed. The server never stores a readable password. If you turn on Remember my password on this device, it is kept only in this browser, and you can show and copy it. Accounts made with the GitHub or Google button log in with that button.

## Optimization
- Turning on the **Low-spec Mode** switch reduces effects, shadows and particles and limits the frame rate to 30. Effect quality changes to Low and the frame limit to 30, and turning it off returns them to High and Unlimited.
- **Effect quality** has three levels, High, Medium and Low, and sets the amount of particles, shadows and screen effects.
- The **frame limit** is chosen from Unlimited, 60 and 30, and lowering it reduces battery use and heat.
- These values apply to this browser only. The hub and all games read the same values, and a changed value takes effect when you reopen a game.
- Stickseum, Crown Envoy, Beaconfall, Isleport, Dummy Party and Vowkeep read these values, and each game's own optimization button or setting is linked to them.

## Notifications
- You can turn each kind of notification on or off. The kinds are comments, likes, mentions, friend requests, messages, Hub Coin gifts and admin replies.
- With the pop-up switch on, a short pop-up appears at the bottom of the screen for each new notification.
- Notification settings apply to this browser only. Kinds you turn off do not appear in the bell or as pop-ups.

account/profile.b:
:: Where to open = Profile card in the account menu, Profile in the friends list
:: Sharing = Save as image, copy link (frenchfries777.com/games/?card=username)
:: Customizing = Your own card only (6 backgrounds, 6 borders, 13 titles, 17 profile photos, 274 game character photos)

A profile card shows one person’s nickname, intro, played games and achievements as a single picture. You can open your own card and your friends’ cards, save it as an image or share it as a link.

## What the card shows
- It shows the nickname, title, one-line intro and favourite game.
- The played-games area shows, for each game, how many times it was played, the total play time and the number of achievements earned. Games not yet played are marked as such.
- The achievements button opens a list of achievements by game. The percentage on each achievement is the share of all players who earned it. You need to open a game once before its earned achievements show up.

## Editing your card
- The one-line intro can be up to 60 characters. The favourite game is chosen from None, Stickseum, Crown Envoy and Beaconfall.
- There are 13 titles: Rookie, Traveler, Explorer, Good Friend, Popular, Writer, Commenter, Chatterbox, Helper, All-Rounder, Collector, Master and Legend. Each needs one hub achievement to unlock, and hovering over a locked title shows which achievement it needs.

## Customizing
- The Customize button on your own card lets you pick the card background and border. The more hub achievements you have earned, the more are unlocked.
- Backgrounds are Fries (from the start), Night sky (2 achievements), Ocean (4), Forest (6), Sakura (9) and Galaxy (12).
- Borders are Gold (from the start), Silver (3 achievements), Ruby (5), Emerald (8), Rainbow (11) and Crown (15).
- There are 17 profile photos. Pick one under **Profile photo** in the Customize panel. The default, **Game character**, shows your Stickseum character picture on the card. A chosen photo replaces the character picture on the card and is also included in the saved image.
- The 6 free photos are My account, Fries, Stickseum, Crown Envoy, Beaconfall and Isleport.
- The 6 photos bought with Hub Coin are Dummy Party (30), Vowkeep (40), Ranking (50), Fry Lab (50), Wiki (60) and Hub Coin (100). Buying asks you inside the panel, and a bought photo is saved to your account.
- On 2026-10-27, 274 game character photos were added. They are character pictures from Stickseum skins, Crown Envoy, Beaconfall, Isleport, Dummy Party and Vowkeep, and all of them are free.
- The 5 photos unlocked by hub achievements are Proverb Detective (play 2 different games), Planet Search (play 3 games), Sentence Fixer (write your first board post), Achievement Medal (10 achievements) and Timeline (30 achievements). A locked photo shows the achievement it needs.

## Sharing the card
- The Save image button saves the card as a picture file. The Link button copies the address that opens this card, and on phones the share sheet opens.

account/prototypes.b:
:: Address = frenchfries777.com/games/prototypes/
:: Where to open = The Prototypes card in the hub lounge
:: Games = None right now

## What the prototypes page is

:: Difficulty = Easy, Normal, Hard

:: Russian Campaign = Foreign armies -15% each month from Sept to March
