Historical templates start by choosing a nation, and events happen at set times (year and month). The difficulty next to each nation's name (Easy, Normal, Hard) is set by its size and the surrounding situation. Event timings below are in year.month format. The starting hostile count includes not only nations directly fighting you but also the enemies of your allies (as of build 135), and difficulty was re-rated using this value.
Each nation line lists in parentheses its difficulty, size, and the number of hostile, allied, and adjacent non-aligned nations at the start (the same values as the in-game difficulty description), and strategy is written separately for each nation based on its starting setup, generals, and events. Turn numbers for events count one turn as one month, with turn 1 being the template's starting month. For Rome's Fall, the Hundred Years' War, and the Rise of the Ottomans, which have no fixed starting month, years are used instead of turns. The starting army multiplier is the value set by the scenario, which is multiplied by the troops initially placed in each territory. Saying a nation has many or few troops compares it to the other nations in the same template.

## Ancient to Early Modern (218 BC~1618 AD, 11 templates)

### Second Punic War (218 BC, 72 turns)
!img/ce-tpl-punic.webp
- Events: Cannae -216.8, Macedonia -215.6, Scipio's landing -204.6, Zama -202.10, Peace -201.3
- All 27 nations show a difficulty. Easy 3, Normal 14, Hard 10. Below are 4 of the included nations.
- **Roman Republic** (Normal, large, hostile 6, allied 1, adjacent non-aligned 4): From the start you face Carthage and the Gallic tribes at the same time. The Cannae event comes on turn 30, so it's better to clear the Gallic side first. Place Fabius (Defense 5, Fortification) on the Carthage front, and save Scipio, who gets an attack bonus, for counterattacks.
- **Carthage** (Normal, large, hostile 4, allied 2, adjacent non-aligned 4): You fight directly against the Roman Republic, the Celtiberian tribes, and the Lusitanian tribes, and with the enemies of your allies the hostile count reaches 4. The Celtiberian tribes have thin troops, so it's easy to push them down first and clear your rear. Hannibal is a surprise general with Attack 5, Command 5, and +80% damage on first clash, so using him in the first major battle gives great value. The Macedonia event is on turn 40.
- **Celtiberian tribes** (Hard, neutral alignment, hostile 3, allied 0, adjacent non-aligned 3): Their troops are noticeably few, yet Carthage comes straight at them. Since this nation has no general, avoid a head-on fight, and first make a buffer zone through diplomacy with one of the three adjacent non-aligned nations.
- **Ptolemaic Egypt** (Normal, medium size, hostile 4, allied 1, adjacent non-aligned 3): There are no direct wars, and its only ally is the Roman Republic, but adding the enemies of its ally makes hostile count 4. Its total army is small, but the starting army multiplier is 2.47, so each territory starts with thick garrisons, and since there's no general, you win with these troops and the naval bonus of 1.5.

### Three Kingdoms (229 AD, 72 turns)
!img/ce-tpl-sam.webp
- Events: 229.6 Wu-Shu alliance, 230.8 Wei invasion, 231.5 Zhuge Liang, 234.8 Zhuge Liang dies, 238.1 Gongsun Yuan rebels, 238.8 Gongsun Yuan defeated
- All 20 nations show a difficulty. Easy 7, Normal 10, Hard 3. Below are 3 of the included nations.
- **Wei (Cao Wei)** (Normal, large, hostile 3, allied 0, adjacent non-aligned 4): Its army is larger than Wu (Eastern Wu) and Shu Han combined, but it fights three enemies at the same time: Shu Han, Wu (Eastern Wu), and the Xianbei. Sima Yi is a general with Attack, Defense, and Command all at 5, so keep him fixed on the most dangerous front, and save on conscription costs with Cao Zhen's logistics.
- **Wu (Eastern Wu)** (Easy, large, hostile 1, allied 1, adjacent non-aligned 2): The naval bonus is 1.6, so attacks at sea are about 30% stronger, which makes naval battle the core. Lu Xun has Attack, Defense, and Command all at 5 and also has an ambush ability, so send him to face the largest Wei force, and use Gan Ning's blitzkrieg to strike at openings.
- **Shu Han** (Easy, medium size, hostile 1, allied 1, adjacent non-aligned 7): Its troops are well below Wei's and its income multiplier is a low 0.9. So the first task is to hold Wei's invasion on turn 17 with mountain defense. Zhuge Liang has Command 6, but he withdraws at the Wuzhang Plains event on turn 65, so before that you must split attacks between Zhao Yun and Jiang Wei.

### Fall of Rome (451 AD, 60 turns by default)
!img/ce-tpl-rome.webp
- European map, 20 nations. Eastern and Western Rome, the Huns, the Vandals, and the Goths appear.
- All 20 nations show a difficulty. Easy 10, Normal 4, Hard 6. Below are 4 of the included nations.
- **Western Roman Empire (Valentinian III)** (Easy, superpower, hostile 3, allied 4, adjacent non-aligned 7): It faces the Hunnic Empire and the Alamanni at once, but four allies, the Visigoth Kingdom, the Frankish Kingdom, the Burgundian Kingdom, and the Eastern Roman Empire, support its flanks. Flavius Aetius is a mobile warfare general with Attack 5 and Command 5, so put him in charge of the main force toward the Huns, and place Majorian on defense.
- **Eastern Roman Empire (Marcian)** (Easy, superpower, hostile 3, allied 1, adjacent non-aligned 5): It has the largest army in this template, and since it has a non-aggression pact with the Sassanid Persian Empire, the east is empty. The only direct enemy is the Hunnic Empire, and adding the enemies of its ally makes hostile count 3, so squeezing the Huns from both front and back, as with the Western Roman Empire, will make it easy.
- **Hunnic Empire (Attila)** (Hard, medium size, hostile 5, allied 0, adjacent non-aligned 5): It is at war with both the Eastern and Western Roman Empires, and adding the Western Roman ally makes hostile count 5, with no allies at all, so it starts encircled. However, its starting army multiplier is 2.0 and Attila is a cavalry charge general with +50% damage in the decisive stage, so picking one Roman side and striking hard and short is the right approach.
- **Visigoth Kingdom (Theodoric I)** (Easy, small nation, hostile 2, allied 1, adjacent non-aligned 2): There are no direct wars at the start, and its only ally is the Western Roman Empire, but adding the Huns, the enemy of the Western Roman Empire, makes hostile count 2. At the Catalaunian Plains event in 451, it joins the war against the Huns on the Western side. Theodoric I has 5/4/5 and gives +5 starting morale through Charisma, and Torismund's cavalry charge backs him up, so when war opens, station the two together on the Hun front.

### Viking Age (865 AD, 60 turns by default)
!img/ce-tpl-viking.webp
- Events: 865.9 Great Heathen Army lands, 867.9 Basil I takes the throne, 867.11 York falls, 871.1 Battle of Ashdown, 871.4 Alfred takes the throne, 872.6 Battle of Hafrsfjord, 874.6 Mercia divided, 878.5 Battle of Edington
- European map, 57 nations. The Great Heathen Army, Anglo-Saxon kingdoms such as Wessex, the three Frankish kingdoms, Byzantium, the Abbasids, and Córdoba appear.
- All 57 nations show a difficulty. Easy 10, Normal 33, Hard 14. Below are 5 of the included nations.
- **Great Heathen Army (Ivar and Ubba)** (Normal, 1 region, hostile 4, allied 1, adjacent non-aligned 3): It is a naval power with only one territory. With a naval bonus of 2.2 and a starting army multiplier of 1.4, its troops are not thin, and Ivar the Boneless is a charismatic general with Attack 5 and Command 5. Ubba's blitzkrieg and Halfdan Ragnarsson's naval battles back him up, so after the landing in East Anglia on 865.9, use the fleet to slip into the gaps between the split Anglo-Saxon kingdoms.
- **Kingdom of Wessex (Æthelred I)** (Normal, 2 regions, hostile 3, allied 1, adjacent non-aligned 2): A small nation with two regions, with a starting army multiplier of 0.8 and few troops. Alfred is a defensive general with Defense 4 and Command 5, and the events Ashdown on 871.1, Alfred taking the throne on 871.4, and Edington on 878.5 follow in sequence, so the key is holding out until then.
- **Byzantine Empire (Michael III)** (Normal, 26 regions, hostile 6, allied 2, adjacent non-aligned 5): It has the most regions of any nation in this template, but with six hostile nations it's open on all sides. Naval bonus is 1.8, income is 1.3, and Bardas is a logistics general with Defense 4 and Command 5. On 867.9, Basil I drives Michael III out, so reduce your fronts before then.
- **East Frankish Kingdom (Louis the German)** (Normal, 15 regions, hostile 4, allied 1, adjacent non-aligned 7): Its starting army multiplier is 0.22, so troops are thin for its territory, and its naval bonus is 0.3, so you must give up on the sea. Louis the German is a defensive general with Attack, Defense, and Command all at 4, so keep him fixed on the most dangerous front, and save Carloman's cavalry charge for counterattacks. With seven adjacent non-aligned nations, there's plenty of room to widen buffer zones through diplomacy.
- **Emirate of Córdoba (Muhammad I)** (Easy, 11 regions, hostile 3, allied 1, adjacent non-aligned 3): Hostile count is 3, yet it is rated Easy. Income of 1.3 keeps money flowing well, Muhammad I is a defensive general, and Hisham ibn Abd al-Aziz's cavalry charge handles counterattacks.

### Reconquista (1031 AD, 60 turns by default)
!img/ce-tpl-reconq.webp
- Events: 1031.12 Caliphate of Córdoba abolished, 1035.10 Sancho III dies, 1035.11 Cnut the Great dies, 1037.9 Battle of Tamarón, 1038.6 Maniakes' Sicily campaign, 1038.8 Stephen I dies
- European map, 66 nations. The Islamic kingdom, a union of León, Castile, Navarre, and Barcelona, faces off against Byzantium, the Fatimids, and the Zirids, who contest land in the Mediterranean.
- All 66 nations show a difficulty. Easy 22, Normal 28, Hard 16. Below are 4 of the included nations.
- **Kingdom of León (Bermudo III)** (Easy, 4 regions, hostile 1, allied 3, adjacent non-aligned 1): It fights the Islamic kingdom (the Andalusian coalition) directly. Its starting army multiplier is 0.44, so troops are thin for its territory, and its only general is Bermudo III, a cavalry charge general. With three allies it's easy to split the front. The Battle of Tamarón on 1037.9 brings the event where Ferdinand I of Castile takes the throne of León.
- **Islamic Kingdom (Andalusian coalition)** (Normal, 11 regions, hostile 4, allied 0, adjacent non-aligned 5): It fights four enemies directly, León, Castile, Navarre, and Barcelona, with no allies at all. Income 1.3 leaves it with plenty of money, so secure the northern front with Ibn Abbad's defensive skill, and use Hubus ibn Machsan's ambush at the openings. Your first move is to bring one of the five adjacent non-aligned nations in through diplomacy.
- **Byzantine Empire (Romanos III)** (Easy, 35 regions, hostile 4, allied 1, adjacent non-aligned 9): With 35 regions, it is the largest nation in this template, with a naval bonus of 1.7 and income of 1.5. It fights four enemies directly: the Mirdasid dynasty (Aleppo), the Kalbid emirate of Sicily, the Fatimid Caliphate, and the Lombard principalities (Capua and Salerno). Georgios Maniakes is a charismatic general with Attack 5 and Command 5, so put him on the largest front, and gather troops in time for the Sicily campaign event on 1038.6.
- **Fatimid Caliphate (al-Zahir)** (Normal, 12 regions, hostile 4, allied 1, adjacent non-aligned 2): It fights the Zirid dynasty (al-Mu'izz) and the Byzantine Empire directly, and adding the enemies of its ally makes hostile count 4. Income 1.4 keeps money flowing well, but its starting army multiplier is low at 0.42. Use Anushtakin al-Dozaki's logistics to save on conscription costs, and block the Byzantine front first.

### Crusades (1096 AD, 60 turns by default)
!img/ce-tpl-crusade.webp
- Events: 1096.12 Alexios I demands oaths of loyalty, 1097.5 Siege of Nicaea, 1097.7 Battle of Dorylaeum, 1097.10 Siege of Antioch, 1098.6 Antioch falls, 1098.8 Fatimids retake Jerusalem, 1099.7 Crusaders take Jerusalem, 1099.8 Battle of Ascalon, 1101.8 Defeat in Asia Minor
- European map, 72 nations. Byzantium, the Seljuks, and the Fatimids contest the Holy Land, while in Europe the emperor and the pope clash.
- The First Crusade starts with troops stationed on Byzantine land, with no territory of its own.
- All 72 nations show a difficulty. Easy 27, Normal 23, Hard 22. Below are 4 of the included nations.
- **First Crusade** (Easy, no territory, hostile 3, allied 5, adjacent non-aligned 0): Five named generals, including Godfrey of Bouillon (Attack 5, Defense 4, Command 5, Charisma), Bohemond of Taranto, Raymond IV of Toulouse, Tancred, and Robert Curthose. It fights the Sultanate of Rum and the Emirate of Danishmend directly. Events run from the siege of Nicaea on 1097.5 to the capture of Jerusalem on 1099.7, so secure supplies before winter sets in during the siege of Antioch on 1097.10.
- **Byzantine Empire (Alexios I)** (Easy, 18 regions, hostile 3, allied 1, adjacent non-aligned 8): It fights the Sultanate of Rum and the Principality of Serbia directly. Its starting army multiplier is low at 0.29, but its naval bonus is 1.6. The first event is on 1096.12, when Alexios I demands oaths of loyalty from the crusader leaders, so use the crusaders' strength to drive out the Sultanate of Rum first.
- **Sultanate of Rum (Kilij Arslan I)** (Hard, 7 regions, hostile 7, allied 0, adjacent non-aligned 3): It fights the Byzantine Empire, the First Crusade, and the Emirate of Danishmend directly, and adding the enemies of its ally makes hostile count 7, with no allies at all. Kilij Arslan I is an ambush general with Attack 5 and Command 4, so target the crusader cavalry in the Battle of Dorylaeum event on 1097.7.
- **Fatimid Caliphate** (Normal, 7 regions, hostile 5, allied 0, adjacent non-aligned 4): It fights the Damascus Seljuks, the Great Seljuk Empire, and the Zirid dynasty directly, and adding the enemies of its ally makes hostile count 5. Income 1.4 keeps money flowing well, and there is an event on 1098.8 where it retakes Jerusalem. Use Al-Afdal Shahanshah's logistics to save on conscription costs, and block the eastern front first.

### Hundred Years' War (1428 AD, 60 turns by default)
!img/ce-tpl-hyw.webp
- European map, 36 nations.
- Constantinople is the Byzantine capital, a small port territory that starts with fortresses at level 3. Adrianople starts under Ottoman control.
- Events: Siege of Orléans, Joan of Arc, Treaty of Arras
- All 63 nations show a difficulty. Easy 16, Normal 25, Hard 22. Below are 4 of the included nations.
- **Kingdom of England (Henry VI)** (Normal, medium size, hostile 3, allied 2, adjacent non-aligned 3): It fights the Kingdom of France and the Kingdom of Scotland directly, and adding the enemies of its ally makes hostile count 3, but the Duchy of Burgundy and the Kingdom of Portugal are its allies. Talbot is an indomitable general with Attack 5, so place him on the front line at Orléans, and use Earl of Salisbury's artillery for sieges. You must settle matters before Burgundy turns away, as stated in the Treaty of Arras of 1435.
- **Kingdom of France (Charles VII)** (Normal, medium size, hostile 4, allied 2, adjacent non-aligned 5): Its starting army multiplier is 2.0, and Joan of Arc is a morale-boosting general with Command 5, who raises starting morale by +8, so it doesn't fall behind from the first clash. The events include the liberation of Orléans and the coronation at Reims in 1429, so the goal is to hold the Loire line with Dunois's mobile warfare until then.
- **Duchy of Burgundy (Philip the Good)** (Easy, medium size, hostile 2, allied 2, adjacent non-aligned 8): It has no direct wars, but it is hostile to the Kingdom of France, and adding the enemies of its ally makes hostile count 2. Its income multiplier of 1.5 makes it the nation in this group with the best flowing money. Combine Philip the Good's Charisma with Jean de Luxembourg's cavalry charge, swallow the weakest of the eight adjacent non-aligned nations first, and weigh whether to side with England or France.
- **Kingdom of Bohemia (Hussites)** (Hard, small nation, hostile 3, allied 0, adjacent non-aligned 5): As a small nation it has few troops, yet the one opponent, the Kingdom of Hungary (Sigismund), has even more. It has only one general, Procopius the Great, but his defensive skill gives +25% defense, so the basic setup is to station him on a key border point and absorb Hungary's offensive.

### Rise of the Ottomans (1453 AD, 60 turns by default)
!img/ce-tpl-ott1453.webp
- European map, 42 nations. The siege of Constantinople is at the center.
- The area around Istanbul is a small port territory marked as Constantinople in this template, and it is the Byzantine capital. It starts with fortresses at level 3, and Adrianople starts under Ottoman control.
- All 51 nations show a difficulty. Easy 25, Normal 13, Hard 13. Below are 4 of the included nations.
- **Ottoman Empire (Mehmed II)** (Easy, superpower, hostile 4, allied 1, adjacent non-aligned 7): It is already at war with the Eastern Roman Empire, the Principality of Karaman, and the Albanian League, but it has non-aggression pacts with the Mamluk Sultanate, the Republic of Venice, and the Kingdom of Hungary, so its western and southern rear is safe. The first goal is the capital defended by Constantine, so use Zaganos Pasha's logistics to reduce conscription costs and place the Ottoman corps artillery commander's bombardment in front of the walls. The April 1453 siege and the May general assault events follow directly, and before the Hungarian defense of Belgrade by Hunyadi in 1456, clear the Balkans in order.
- **Eastern Roman Empire (Constantine XI)** (Hard, small nation, hostile 2, allied 0, adjacent non-aligned 1): As a small nation with few troops, it cannot face the Ottoman Empire head-on. Instead, Constantine XI's Iron Wall reduces damage taken while defending by 20%, and Giovanni Giustiniani's Indomitable reduces morale loss by 40%, so keep both generals stationed in the capital.
- **Republic of Venice** (Normal, small nation, hostile 0, allied 1, adjacent non-aligned 8): It is a small nation, yet its naval bonus is 2.2, among the highest in this template, and its income multiplier is 1.5. It already has a non-aggression pact with the Ottoman Empire, so do not break it. The key is to bring in the eight adjacent non-aligned nations one by one through diplomacy, apart from its ally, the Republic of Florence.
- **Kingdom of Hungary (John Hunyadi)** (Easy, medium size, hostile 1, allied 2, adjacent non-aligned 6): It has no direct wars, and adding the enemies of its ally makes hostile count 1. It is allied with the Kingdom of Serbia (despotate) and the Polish-Lithuanian union (Casimir IV), and it has a non-aggression pact with the Ottoman Empire (Mehmed II). John Hunyadi is a general with 5/4/5 and Charisma, and the event text for Belgrade in 1456 says he blocks the Ottoman northward advance, so gather troops on the southern border before then.

### Age of Exploration (1492 AD, 120 turns)
!img/ce-tpl-age.webp
- Optional events: Columbus's petition (1492.9, Spain), Treaty of Tordesillas (1494.6)
- The Aztecs, Maya, and Inca cannot go to sea.
- All 162 nations show a difficulty. Easy 53, Normal 66, Hard 43. Below are 5 of the included nations.
- **Kingdom of Castile** (Easy, superpower, hostile 0, allied 2, adjacent non-aligned 2): On turn 2, Columbus's petition is an optional event, so it's a good bet to wager on exploration with a naval bonus of 1.5 and income of 1.2. France heads for Naples on turn 26, and the Holy League forms on turn 32, so prepare Gonzalo de Córdoba's artillery to go to Italy around that time.
- **Kingdom of Portugal** (Easy, medium size, hostile 5, allied 2, adjacent non-aligned 1): Its naval bonus is very high at 1.9 and its starting army multiplier is 2.09, but as a medium-sized nation with few total troops, its land forces are weak. The only direct enemy is the Maghreb and northern Sahara, and adding the enemies of its ally makes hostile count 5. It has two allies, England and Scotland, so keep land defense to a minimum and invest in the fleet. There is an event on turn 70 where Vasco da Gama reaches Calicut, and on turn 93 where Cabral lands in Brazil, so save on expedition costs with the logistics of Vasco da Gama and Afonso de Albuquerque and wait for those moments.
- **Kingdom of France** (Easy, superpower, hostile 0, allied 0, adjacent non-aligned 8): On turn 26, the event where France heads for Naples is right on your turn, so gather Gaston de Foix's blitzkrieg and Trivulzio's mobile warfare in the Italian theater. On turn 32 the Holy League opposes France, so before then, it's better to tie down at least one of the eight adjacent non-aligned nations.
- **Kingdom of England** (Easy, 8 regions, hostile 5, allied 1, adjacent non-aligned 2): Its starting army multiplier is 0.69, so its troops are thin for its size. There are no direct wars, and its only ally is the Kingdom of Portugal, but adding the enemies of its ally makes hostile count 5. Its naval bonus is 1.3, so investing in the sea is better than on land, and Francis Drake's ambush is for when naval clashes open.
- **Ming Dynasty** (Easy, superpower, hostile 1, allied 1, adjacent non-aligned 7): With an income multiplier of 1.5 and the most troops in this template, it has the greatest national power, and its only war is with the Northern Yuan Mongols. Since Korea is its ally, you need not worry about the east. Clear the north first, then expand into one adjacent non-aligned nation.

### Imjin War (1592 AD, 72 turns)
!img/ce-tpl-imjin.webp
- Events: 1592.4 Busan landing, 1592.7 Hansando, 1592.12 Ming intervention, 1597.2 Chŏngyu War, 1597.9 Myeongnyang, 1598.11 Japanese withdrawal
- Many battles are fought across the sea. See the **Naval Battles and Ports** document for reference.
- All 15 nations show a difficulty. Easy 3, Normal 6, Hard 6. Below are 3 of the included nations.
- **Joseon** (Normal, superpower, hostile 1, allied 0, adjacent non-aligned 3): Its starting skill is 10, a quarter of Japan's 40, and its troops are far fewer than Japan's, so a head-on fight on land loses. However, with a naval bonus of 1.8 and Yi Sun-sin as the god of the navy with +50% attack and defense at sea, the first move is to concentrate the fleet under Yi Sun-sin before the Battle of Hansando event on turn 4 and cut off Japanese supply. On land, hold on with Gwon Yul's defensive skill and Kim Si-min's indomitable spirit, and buy time until the Ming reinforcements arrive on turn 9.
- **Japan (Toyotomi)** (Normal, great power, hostile 1, allied 0, adjacent non-aligned 0): With a starting skill of 40 and far more troops, it overwhelms Joseon, and since its only enemy is Joseon, it has no reason to lose on land. The problem is the sea, where Japan's naval bonus of 1.0 keeps losing to Joseon's 1.8 and Yi Sun-sin, so before the Hansando event on turn 4, avoid naval battles and drive forward by land.
- **Ming Dynasty** (Normal, great power, hostile 0, allied 0, adjacent non-aligned 8): Until the event on turn 9 where it sends reinforcements to Joseon, it's better to tie down one of the eight adjacent non-aligned nations through diplomacy first. For the vanguard of the reinforcements, the fastest way to break Japanese infantry is to pair Li Rusong (Attack 5, Command 5, cavalry charge) with Chen Lin's artillery.

### Thirty Years' War (1618 AD, 72 turns)
!img/ce-tpl-1618.webp
- Events: 1625 Denmark joins, 1630 Sweden joins, 1635 France joins, 1648.10 Peace of Westphalia
- All 29 nations show a difficulty. Easy 3, Normal 6, Hard 20. Below are 4 of the included nations.
- **Habsburg Austria** (Normal, superpower, hostile 5, allied 2, adjacent non-aligned 7): Its only direct enemy is the Protestant Union, and adding the enemies of its ally makes hostile count 5. The Spanish Empire and the Catholic League are its allies, and it has non-aggression pacts with the Ottoman Empire and Poland-Lithuania, so its rear is safe. Its troops are fewer than its ally the Spanish Empire's, but it has a starting skill of 25, so the easiest path is to quickly suppress the Protestant Union.
- **Spanish Empire** (Easy, great power, hostile 6, allied 2, adjacent non-aligned 11): It fights the Dutch Republic and the Kingdom of France directly, and adding the enemies of its ally makes hostile count 6, but Habsburg Austria and the Catholic League (Bavaria) are its allies. With a starting skill of 35, it is ahead on land against France, which has skill 10, so use its army on the French front. The Netherlands has income of 2.2 and a naval bonus of 1.7, so at sea it surpasses Spain's 1.4, and it's better to avoid naval contests.
- **Kingdom of France** (Normal, great power, hostile 3, allied 0, adjacent non-aligned 5): It has no allies, yet its direct enemy is the Spanish Empire with starting skill 35, and adding the enemies of its ally makes hostile count 3. France's skill is at the default of 10, so avoid a head-on fight, and first raise a shield through diplomacy with one of the five adjacent non-aligned nations.
- **Kingdom of Sweden** (Hard, medium size, hostile 4, allied 0, adjacent non-aligned 4): It fights Poland-Lithuania and Denmark-Norway directly, and adding the enemies of its ally makes hostile count 4, yet its starting army multiplier is 0.27, so its starting strength is weak. Still, it has a starting skill of 25 and a naval bonus of 1.1, so first crush Denmark-Norway, which borders the sea, to close one front, and hold off Poland by bringing in one of the four adjacent non-aligned nations.

## 18th to 19th Century (1701 AD~1864 AD, 6 templates)

### War of the Spanish Succession (1701 AD, 72 turns)
!img/ce-tpl-1701.webp
- Events: 1703 Savoy and Portugal switch sides, 1709 Poltava, 1713 Treaty of Utrecht
- All 30 nations show a difficulty. Easy 8, Normal 6, Hard 16. Below are 5 of the included nations.
- **Kingdom of France (Louis XIV)** (Easy, great power, hostile 10, allied 3, adjacent non-aligned 4): Habsburg Austria, the Kingdom of England, and the Dutch Republic are its enemies, but the Kingdom of Spain, Bavaria, and the Duchy of Savoy are its allies, and its starting skill of 30 is higher than England's 25. On turn 21 Savoy turns to the Grand Alliance, so clear the Italian forces before then.
- **Kingdom of Spain (Philip V)** (Normal, great power, hostile 9, allied 1, adjacent non-aligned 10): Its only direct enemy is Habsburg Austria, and adding the enemies of its ally makes hostile count 9. Its ally is the Kingdom of France under Louis XIV, which has many troops and a starting skill of 30. Spain itself has a starting army multiplier of 0.25, so its troops are thin, and its skill is at the default of 10, so it's not a nation to attack alone.
- **Habsburg Austria** (Normal, great power, hostile 4, allied 8, adjacent non-aligned 6): It fights France (Louis XIV) and Spain (Philip V), and its starting army multiplier is 0.38 with skill at the default of 10, so it has more troops but is pushed back head-on by France's skill of 30. However, four allies, the Kingdom of England, the Dutch Republic, Brandenburg-Prussia, and the German princes (Holy Roman Empire), support it, and it has a non-aggression pact with the Ottoman Empire, so its east is empty.
- **Kingdom of England** (Normal, medium size, hostile 4, allied 3, adjacent non-aligned 0): Its starting army multiplier is 0.36, so its army is weak, but its income of 1.8 and naval bonus of 1.9 rank among the best in this setup. The three allies, the Dutch Republic, Habsburg Austria, and the Kingdom of Portugal, take on France on the continent, so England supports them with money and fleets while avoiding direct clashes.
- **Kingdom of Portugal** (Hard, very small nation, hostile 1, allied 1, adjacent non-aligned 1): It is a very small nation with a starting army multiplier of 0.25, the weakest in this template, and its starting skill is at the default of 10. Keep diplomacy steady so it doesn't break with the one adjacent non-aligned nation, and gather a small force at key border points, which is enough.

### American Revolutionary War (1775 AD, 96 turns)
!img/ce-tpl-1775.webp
- Optional event: alliance with France (1778.2)
- All 142 nations show a difficulty. Easy 31, Normal 44, Hard 67. Below are 4 of the included nations.
- **Continental Congress (13 colonies)** (Hard, superpower, hostile 6, allied 0, adjacent non-aligned 4): Its starting skill is 12, far below the 35 of the Kingdom of Great Britain (George III), and its troops are far fewer, so avoid big battles, give up space, and hold on. With no allies, the first goal is to survive until the Battle of Saratoga on turn 31 and the alliance choice with France on turn 35. Benedict Arnold is used for the Quebec event on turn 9.
- **Kingdom of Great Britain (George III)** (Normal, great power, hostile 6, allied 5, adjacent non-aligned 21): Its income multiplier of 2.6 and naval bonus of 2.6 put it ahead in both money and sea in this template, and its starting skill is 35. Its enemies are only the Continental Congress (13 colonies) and the Maratha Confederacy, so winning the colonial struggle before France intervenes on turn 35 is the top priority.
- **Kingdom of France (Louis XVI)** (Easy, superpower, hostile 0, allied 2, adjacent non-aligned 6): There is no war for now, and it is allied with the Kingdom of Spain and the Habsburg Monarchy (Joseph II). Income is 1.8 and starting skill is 30, so it has room. After Saratoga on turn 31, an event on turn 35 lets you choose an alliance with America, so gather the fleet until then, and when Spain declares war on Britain on turn 51, move together.
- **Russian Empire (Catherine II)** (Easy, great power, hostile 0, allied 1, adjacent non-aligned 13): There is no war, it is allied with the Kingdom of Prussia (Frederick the Great), and it has a non-aggression pact with the Ottoman Empire (Abdul Hamid I), making it the great power with the least threat. With thirteen adjacent non-aligned nations, there is much room to grow through diplomacy and expansion. Suvorov is a mobile warfare general with Command 6, and Rumyantsev's logistics reduce conscription costs, so make him the vanguard of expansion.

### Napoleonic Wars (1803 AD, 72 turns)
!img/ce-tpl-1803.webp
- Events: 1805 Third Coalition, 1808 Peninsular War, 1812.6 Russian invasion (650,000 strong army)
- Foreign armies that enter Russian territory lose 15% each month from September to March. Watch your supply and winter.
- All 28 nations show a difficulty. Easy 3, Normal 6, Hard 19. Below are 4 of the included nations.
- **French Republic (Napoleon)** (Hard, great power, hostile 11, allied 4, adjacent non-aligned 5): It is already at war with four nations, Britain, the Austrian Empire, the Kingdom of Prussia, and the German princes, but its four allies, including the Kingdom of Spain, and its starting skill of 35 and starting army multiplier of 1.8 support it. Its non-aggression pact with the Russian Empire is its shield, so leave the east alone until the Third Coalition event on turn 28. Take the center with Napoleon (Command 6), and while Davout's defensive skill holds one front, defeat the enemies one by one with Lannes's ambush and Murat's cavalry charge.
- **Britain** (Hard, great power, hostile 5, allied 4, adjacent non-aligned 0): It fights the French Republic (Napoleon) and the Kingdom of Spain directly, and adding the enemies of its ally makes hostile count 5, but its income of 2.8 and naval bonus of 2.4 are the best in this template, and its allies are the Kingdom of Portugal, the Kingdom of the Two Sicilies, the Kingdom of Ireland, and the Electorate of Hanover. Its starting skill is 25, so it's better to use money and fleets to support the continental allies than to clash with France, whose skill is 35, on land. Events in your favor follow: Austria opposes France on turn 28 and Spain rises against France on turn 61, so prepare landing forces for that timing.
- **Russian Empire (Alexander I)** (Normal, great power, hostile 1, allied 0, adjacent non-aligned 5): At the start its only war is with the Ottoman Empire, and it has a non-aggression pact with the French Republic, so it is the most comfortable great power. Its starting skill is 20, but its starting army multiplier is 0.35, so its starting troops are thin. Rather than one big battle, it's better to slowly erode the Ottoman side. There are no named generals, so keep diplomacy open with one of the three western adjacent non-aligned nations, and after the Third Coalition event on turn 28, decide whether to keep the non-aggression pact with France.
- **Kingdom of Prussia** (Hard, great power, hostile 5, allied 0, adjacent non-aligned 7): It has no allies, yet it is at war alone with the French Republic, and adding France's allies makes hostile count 5. Its starting skill is 25. With seven adjacent non-aligned nations, bringing in even one through diplomacy comes first, and until then hold out at the border fortresses to wear down the French army.

### Crimean War (1853 AD, 36 turns)
!img/ce-tpl-crimea.webp
- Events: 1853.11 Sinop, 1854.3 Britain and France join, 1854.9 Landing, 1855.1 Sardinia joins, 1855.4 Sevastopol, 1855.6 Peace
- All 28 nations show a difficulty. Easy 2, Normal 9, Hard 17. Below are 4 of the included nations.
- **Russian Empire** (Normal, great power, hostile 2, allied 0, adjacent non-aligned 4): Its only starting enemy is the Ottoman Empire, and its starting skill is 20, higher than the Ottomans' 10. The Battle of Sinop event on turn 2 destroys the Ottoman fleet, so take the Black Sea first with Nakhimov's Indomitable fleet, and achieve a big result on the Danube front before Britain declares war on turn 6. After the allied landing on turn 12, station Totleben (Defense 5, Fortification) in a Crimean fortress and hold out until the fall of Sevastopol on turn 19.
- **Ottoman Empire** (Normal, great power, hostile 1, allied 0, adjacent non-aligned 4): The Battle of Sinop event on turn 2 sweeps away its fleet, so give up the sea and station Omer Pasha (Command 5, mobile warfare) on the Danube land route to buy time. The British declaration of war on turn 6 and the allied landing on turn 12 are its help, so the goal is to keep the alliance with the Egyptian Viceroyalty and not lose the capital until then.
- **Britain** (Hard, great power, hostile 0, allied 0, adjacent non-aligned 0): It has no war at the start, it has a non-aggression pact with the Second French Empire, and with income 2.6, naval bonus 2.2, and starting army multiplier 2.57, it has the richest start. Until the event on turn 6 where it declares war on Russia, build up conscription and the fleet, and for the Crimean landing on turn 12, send Campbell's Indomitable and Raglan's logistics together.
- **Second French Empire** (Hard, superpower, hostile 0, allied 0, adjacent non-aligned 10): It has no war, it has a non-aggression pact with Britain, and with income 1.8, naval bonus 1.6, and starting army multiplier 2.77, it has a thick start. In the event on turn 6, it declares war on Russia together with Britain, and it joins the Crimean landing on turn 12. It has five named generals, so put Saint-Arnaud's morale boost in the main force, and place Canrobert's blitzkrieg and Bosquet's mobile warfare around the landing site.

### American Civil War (1861 AD, 48 turns)
!img/ce-tpl-civil.webp
- Events: 1861.7 Bull Run, 1861.8 Missouri, 1861.9 Kentucky, 1863.7 Gettysburg, 1865.4 Appomattox
- All 7 nations show a difficulty. Easy 1, Normal 1, Hard 5. Below are 2 of the included nations.
- **United States (North)** (Easy, great power, hostile 1, allied 0, adjacent non-aligned 5): Its starting skill is 10, lower than the Confederacy's 25, so early battles go against it, and in the Battle of Bull Run event on turn 4, the Union army retreats. So the first principle is to not hurry, and to rely on more troops than the South and the supply of income 1.6. Strengthen the front with Meade's defensive skill while gaining skill, and after Grant's logistics and Sherman's mobile warfare clear Kentucky by turn 6, expand the occupation.
- **Confederate States (Normal, great power, hostile 1, allied 0, adjacent non-aligned 4)**: Its army is half that of the United States (North), and its income is 1.0 to 1.6, so a long war is unfavorable. However, its starting skill of 25 and starting army multiplier of 1.32 are its early weapons, and since the Bull Run event on turn 4 is a Confederate win, aim for a decisive blow with Lee (ambush) and Jackson (mobile warfare) until then. Events where Missouri and Kentucky side with the Union follow on turns 5 and 6, so don't trust the border states, and try to decide the outcome as early as possible, before the Gettysburg event on turn 28.

### German Unification Wars (1864 AD, 72 turns)
!img/ce-tpl-ger.webp
- Optional events: War with Austria (1866.6), Ems Dispatch (1870.7, Prussia)
- All 26 nations show a difficulty. Easy 12, Normal 5, Hard 9. Below are 3 of the included nations.
- **Kingdom of Prussia (Wilhelm I)** (Easy, great power, hostile 1, allied 1, adjacent non-aligned 8): At the start it has only one war, fighting alongside the Kingdom of Denmark and the Austrian Empire. Its starting army multiplier is 6.88, the highest in this template, so its starting troops are the thickest. When the Danish war ends with the Treaty of Vienna on turn 9, the Gastein Convention on turn 19 splits it from Austria, and on turn 29 the choice of war with Austria comes. Use Moltke (logistics) to reduce conscription costs, and gather Karl von Steinmetz's blitzkrieg and Prince Friedrich Karl's artillery before the Battle of Königgrätz on turn 32.
- **Austrian Empire (Franz Joseph)** (Easy, great power, hostile 1, allied 7, adjacent non-aligned 4): The war with the Kingdom of Denmark is fought alongside Prussia, and it has five allies, including the Kingdom of Bavaria, so its start is solid. However, the Gastein Convention on turn 19 breaks its ties with Prussia, and the war event arrives on turn 29, so before then, gather the forces of its German princely allies in one place.
- **Second French Empire (Napoleon III)** (Easy, great power, hostile 0, allied 0, adjacent non-aligned 12): There are no wars, it has a non-aggression pact with the Kingdom of Italy, and with a starting army multiplier of 4.56, its size is ample. Its starting skill is 10, and apart from Patrice de MacMahon's Indomitable, no generals stand out, so instead of fighting quickly, the first move is diplomacy, getting closer to one of the twelve adjacent non-aligned nations. The Ems Dispatch option and the Sedan event fall on turns 78 and 83, beyond the default 72 turns, so within 72 turns this nation is one that watches who wins the Prussia-Austria fight and times its entry.

## 20th Century Onward (1914 AD~2026 AD, 4 templates)

### World War I (1914 AD, 52 turns)
!img/ce-tpl-1914.webp
- Events: 1914.8 Canada and Japan join, 1914.11 Ottoman Empire joins, 1915.5 Italy, 1915.10 Bulgaria, 1916.3 Portugal, 1916.8 Romania, 1917.4 United States, 1917.6 Greece, 1917.11 Russian Revolution and Soviet split, 1918.11 Armistice
- You can dig trenches, and mechanized and air technologies open up.
- All 54 nations show a difficulty. Easy 10, Normal 9, Hard 35. Below are 5 of the included nations.
- **British Empire** (Easy, great power, hostile 3, allied 5, adjacent non-aligned 15): Its income of 3.0 and naval bonus of 2.4 are the best in this template, but its starting army multiplier is 0.25, so its army is thin. Its only enemy is the German Empire, and the French Republic, the Russian Empire, the Kingdom of Belgium, the Portuguese Republic, and Canada are allies, so its role is to support the allies with money and fleets. Its starting skill is 40, so use a small elite force with Plumer's Defense and Haig's Indomitable to hold the Western Front.
- **French Republic** (Easy, great power, hostile 3, allied 2, adjacent non-aligned 13): Its only enemy is the German Empire, and the British Empire and the Russian Empire are allies, but Germany has a starting skill of 45 and France has 25, so France loses in a straight field battle. With income of 2.0, hold the line with Pétain's Defense and trenches, and save Foch's morale boost (starting morale +8) and Joffre's mobile warfare for counterattacks.
- **German Empire** (Hard, great power, hostile 9, allied 2, adjacent non-aligned 9): It fights the French Republic, the Russian Empire, the British Empire, and the Kingdom of Belgium directly, and adding the enemies of its allies makes hostile count 9. Yet its starting skill of 45 is the highest in this template, and its income is 2.8. Its allies are Austria-Hungary and the Ottoman Empire (joins on turn 5), so ending the Western war quickly is the standard approach. Put Ludendorff's mobile warfare and Falkenhayn's artillery in the west, and Hindenburg's Indomitable in the east.
- **Russian Empire** (Easy, great power, hostile 4, allied 3, adjacent non-aligned 11): It fights the German Empire, Austria-Hungary, and the Ottoman Empire directly, and adding the enemies of its allies makes hostile count 4. Its troops are the largest in this template, and its allies are the British Empire, the French Republic, and the Kingdom of Serbia. However, its starting skill is 15, far below Germany's 45, so buy time against Germany, and use Brusilov's blitzkrieg on Austria-Hungary, whose skill is similar.
- **Kingdom of Serbia** (Hard, small nation, hostile 4, allied 3, adjacent non-aligned 4): It is a small nation that fights Austria-Hungary and the Kingdom of Bulgaria, and its allies are the Russian Empire, the Kingdom of Montenegro, and the Kingdom of Greece. The basic plan is to raise starting morale by +8 with Putnik's morale boost, hold the defense line with Mišić's Indomitable, and wait for Italy's entry on turn 11. The event on turn 16, when Bulgaria joins as an ally, is the most dangerous turning point.

### World War II (1939 AD, 72 turns)
!img/ce-tpl-1939.webp
- From 1939.9 to 1945.8, many events occur: the Winter War, Barbarossa (1941.6), Operation Torch (1942.11), Sicily (1943.7), Normandy (1944.6), German surrender (1945.5), Japanese surrender (1945.8), and others.
- If Germany occupies Paris, the Vichy government splits off.
- You can dig trenches.
- All 56 nations show a difficulty. Easy 13, Normal 11, Hard 32. Below are 5 of the included nations.
- **United Kingdom** (Normal, great power, hostile 4, allied 7, adjacent non-aligned 15): It fights the Third Reich directly, and adding the enemies of its allies makes hostile count 4, but it has seven allies: the Kingdom of Egypt, France, Portugal, the Turkish Republic, the Kingdom of Greece, the Kingdom of Romania, and Canada. In the Italian invasion of Egypt event on turn 13, prepare Auchinleck's Indomitable and Montgomery's artillery for North Africa so the allied Egypt does not collapse, and the United States joins on turn 28.
- **France** (Easy, great power, hostile 2, allied 2, adjacent non-aligned 11): It stands alone against the Third Reich, and the United Kingdom and the Turkish Republic are its allies. France, starting with skill 25, is at a disadvantage if it takes Germany's 40 head-on, so build a defensive line with Béthouart's defensive skill and keep de Gaulle (Command 5, blitzkrieg) in reserve for counterattacks. The German invasions of Scandinavia and the Low Countries come on turns 8 and 9, so solidify the front before then.
- **Third Reich** (Hard, great power, hostile 8, allied 1, adjacent non-aligned 9): It fights the United Kingdom, France, and the Kingdom of Egypt, and is at non-aggression with the Soviet Union. With a starting army multiplier of 3.75 and a starting skill of 40, which exceeds France's 25, it saves time by striking the west first. The events of the invasion of Denmark and Norway on turn 8 and the invasion of the Netherlands and Belgium on turn 9 follow, and the reinforcement of the Afrika Korps on turn 18 comes, so split forces to match that schedule.
- **Soviet Union** (Normal, great power, hostile 6, allied 0, adjacent non-aligned 13): Its starting enemies are Finland and the Kingdom of Romania, and it has a non-aggression pact with the Third Reich. Its starting skill is 15, so it's easy to struggle against Finland's 35 in the Winter War, so attach Zhukov (5/5/5, Indomitable) to the Finnish front first.
- **United States** (Hard, superpower, hostile 0, allied 0, adjacent non-aligned 2): It starts with no wars and no alliances, and joins the war on turn 28 with the Pearl Harbor event. Its income of 3.0 and naval bonus of 1.9 are its strengths, but its starting army multiplier is 0.25, so its starting troops are thin, and its skill is at the default of 10. Until then, the time is for building strength while tying one of its two adjacent non-aligned nations to it through diplomacy.

### Korean War (1950 AD, 37 turns)
!img/ce-tpl-korea.webp
- Optional events: US intervention (1950.7), Battle of Inchon landing (1950.9), breakthrough of the 38th parallel (1950.10), crossing the Yalu and Chinese intervention (1950.10)
- US and Soviet forces are AI nations that fight with troops stationed on allied land, without territory of their own.
- Supply range is 13. You can dig trenches.
- All 12 nations show a difficulty. Easy 6, Normal 4, Hard 2. Below are 2 of the included nations.
- **Republic of Korea** (Normal, great power, hostile 2, allied 1, adjacent non-aligned 1): Its starting army multiplier is 0.41, so its starting strength is very weak, and it fights two enemies, the Democratic People's Republic of Korea and the Soviet forces. Hold the southern defense line with Paik Sun-yup's Indomitable and Lee Jong-chan's defensive skill, and the Nakdong River event on turn 3 and the Inchon landing choice on turn 4 open the path to counterattack.
- **Japan (US occupation)** (Easy, medium size, hostile 0, allied 0, adjacent non-aligned 0): Japan with US occupation in its name has no wars and no alliances, and its starting army multiplier is 0.07, so it has practically no troops. Its role is to watch Korean War events such as the US intervention on turn 2 and the Inchon landing on turn 4, and within the default 37 turns, the realistic goal is to widen its territory little by little.

### Modern Europe (2026 AD, 48 turns)
!img/ce-tpl-2026.webp
- There are no fixed historical events. Its supply range is 16, the longest.
- All 54 nations show a difficulty. Easy 32, Normal 12, Hard 10. Below are 5 of the included nations.
- **Russia** (Normal, great power, hostile 33, allied 2, adjacent non-aligned 8): It is at direct war with eight nations at once, Ukraine, Moldova, Georgia, Estonia, Latvia, Lithuania, Poland, and Finland, and adding the enemies of its allies makes hostile count 33. Its allies are Belarus and Armenia. Ukraine, with the strongest starting army multiplier of 3.01, is the toughest, so first clear the three small Baltic nations, Moldova, and Georgia to widen your base, and leave Poland, which has 28 allied enemies, for later.
- **Ukraine** (Normal, great power, hostile 3, allied 0, adjacent non-aligned 7): It fights Russia and Belarus directly, and adding the enemies of its allies makes hostile count 3. It has no allies, and its troops are fewer than Russia's. However, its starting army multiplier of 3.01 is high, so each territory starts with thick troops, and its first task is to bring the seven adjacent non-aligned nations in through diplomacy.
- **Poland** (Easy, great power, hostile 4, allied 28, adjacent non-aligned 3): It fights Russia and Belarus directly, and adding the enemies of its allies makes hostile count 4. Yet 28 nations, including the United Kingdom, France, and Germany, are its allies, and its income multiplier of 1.6 gives it great staying power. Its troops are far fewer than Russia's, so it's better to save its own troops and draw on the troops and resources of its allies.
- **Germany** (Easy, great power, hostile 3, allied 28, adjacent non-aligned 2): It has no direct wars, and adding the enemies of its allies makes hostile count 3. It is allied with 28 nations, including the United Kingdom, France, and Italy, and its income multiplier of 3.2 is the highest in this template. With 48 turns and no events at all, the sensible approach is to grow in size behind the shield of its allies, managing diplomacy so no adjacent non-aligned nations appear.
- **United Kingdom** (Easy, great power, hostile 3, allied 28, adjacent non-aligned 1): Like Germany, it has no direct wars (hostile count 3 including the enemies of its allies), and it is allied with 28 nations. Its naval bonus of 1.6 is tied with France as the best in this template, and its income of 3.0 is second highest. Its land army is thin, so the best path is to grow influence at sea and lean on the land forces of its allies.

## Related Documents
- **Scenarios and Maps**: Template list and map mode

:: Address = frenchfries777.com/games/dummyparty/
:: Genre = Party minigames
:: Players = 2–8
:: Minigames = 36 (7 per match)
:: Latest version = v0.1 build 76
:: Achievements = 33
:: Install = Not needed
:: More pages = **Controls and Rules**, **Minigames: Races and Brawls**, **Minigames: Timing and Precision**, **Shop and Achievements**, **Online Rooms**

It is a silly party game in which white mannequins compete in chaotic minigames. A match has 7 rounds, and 7 of the 36 minigames are picked at random for it. Each minigame first shows its name, description, method and controls on screen. A commentator makes absurd remarks, the moments before the end are replayed in slow motion, and an award ceremony with category special prizes closes the match.

## Rooms and flow
- On the start screen you pick Create room, Solo or Shop. A public room is listed in the full-screen room list window that the **Room list** button opens, so anyone can join (build 72), and a private room can only be joined with a 5-character room code. In the lobby the host can choose the number of matches and which minigames can appear.
- The minigame selection window has a Turn all off button and a search box, so you can find and switch on only the minigames you want.
- Solo is played with bots, and you set the number of bots in the lobby. You can play solo without logging in, but you cannot buy in the shop. If the host leaves, whoever joined first takes over as host.
- The host of a private room can use the **Invite friends** button in the lobby to send an invite by hub notification to hub friends and to players who are online now, and pressing the invite notification takes them straight into that room (build 71). The details are in the Online room page.

## Minigames and lobby
- There are 36 minigames, with time limits from 13 s (Guess the 3-Minute Ramen) to 130 s (Musical Chairs). Rules and controls are split between the races-and-brawls page and the timing-and-precision page.
- The lobby is wide and the screen follows your mannequin. It has a ball and goals, trampolines, a dance floor, coin picking, bowling, a punch machine, a firework button and a fountain, the theme changes between day, sunset and night, and it sometimes snows. The photo button on the final results saves the award ceremony scene as a picture file.

## Controls and rewards
- Controls in brief: in the lobby you move with WASD or by tapping the screen, jump with Space, throw with K and send emotes with 1 to 5. The A and B buttons inside minigames and the mashing rule are on the controls and rules page.
- If you log in with your hub account (the Frenchfries777 account), you earn the in-game currency dC by rank when a match ends: 15 for 1st, 10 for 2nd, 5 for 3rd and 3 dC for the rest. 1 Hub Coin exchanges for 8 dC. In the shop you buy faces, hats, glasses and victory dances with dC to dress up.
- There are 33 achievements. You see them with the **Achievements** button in the lobby, and when you are logged in they also appear on your hub profile (build 65).

## Settings and site
- Turning on the **Optimization** button (in the lobby and the top bar) lowers the resolution to 1x and removes the audience and confetti (build 60). It is linked to the hub's shared optimization settings, so Medium effects remove only the confetti and the 30 or 60 frame limit is followed too (build 61).
- New background music plays on the first screen, in the lobby and on the results screen (build 70). When you enter the first screen, the intro music plays right away without a click (build 75). If the browser blocks sound, the intro does not stop, and the music starts the moment a key, click or touch first comes in, and it is skipped if the intro is almost over. It does not play while sound effects are turned off.
- Pressing **Leave** in the lobby cleans up the room and then closes this game window (build 76). If the browser does not let the window be closed, you stay on the first screen.
- The official game site (games/dummyparty/) has an introduction, the minigame list, versions and patch notes. The game opens at games/dummyparty/play/, and the old prototype address and invite links redirect to the new address (build 62). This page is based on v0.1 build 76.

## Further reading
- **Controls and Rules**: key list, match flow, scoring, room rules, last-place boost, special awards.
- **Minigames: Races and Brawls** and **Minigames: Timing and Precision**: all 36 with rules, controls and time limits, 18 each.
- **Shop and Achievements**: prices by item, hub ranking point formula and all 33 achievements.
- **Online Rooms**: room codes, public and private rooms, host takeover, connection method.
