It is a co-op expedition game in which the last knights of a fallen order go down into a dungeon together. The picture is drawn from 3D models turned into pixel art. In Solo Expedition you only pick your role and bot companions take the other three seats. In Expedition with Friends you create a room and gather with a 6-character room code or a hub friend invite. Up to 4 can play and bots fill empty seats.

## How to Start
- For a solo expedition you pick your role and bots take the other three seats. For an expedition with friends, create a room and gather with the 6-digit room code or a hub friend invite. In a friend’s room you follow the host’s story, and the chapter you play continues from the saved story.
- Progress is saved in this browser, and chapters you have cleared can be replayed by choice. Finishing chapter 8 opens the Endless Abyss, and reaching the week’s chapter opens the Weekly Expedition.

## At a Glance
- Eight chapters and bosses: The Fallen Grand Master, Bern, Hunter of the Thorn Crown, Odric, the Drowned Archbishop, The Ashen King, Harald of the Frost Oath, Grom, the Stone-Swallowing Giant, Seraphine, Prophet of Flame, The Undying Flame. HP, phases and mid-bosses are on **Chapters and Bosses**.
- The four roles each have Q, E and R skills, and there are five combo attacks. Numbers are on **Roles and Skills**.
- Each chapter has 2 riddle rooms, 2 secret rooms, a dark room, a broken path, a lift, a fork mid-boss and 1 hidden Order banner. Where and how are on **Puzzles and Secrets**.
- Honor you collect buys gear and cosmetics and levels up roles. The rules of the Endless Abyss and the Weekly Expedition are on **Growth and Challenge Modes**.
- Regular enemies have their HP lowered to 70% and attack to 75%, and elites to 85%. Per-enemy numbers are on **Enemies and Stats**.

## Settings and Site
- The optimization setting (Off or On) is linked to the hub's shared optimization settings. Turning it on turns off shadows and bloom, halves the effect pieces and draws at 30 FPS.
- The official game site (games/vowkeep/) has an intro, features, tips, a version list and patch notes. The current version is v0.2 build 54 (Forked Path) with 33 achievements. If the host’s computer slows down it switches itself to a lighter mode, cutting updates sent to friends from 20 to 12 times and halving bot decisions, while the rules stay the same (build 51). The old prototype address and invite links lead to the new address.

## More Pages
- **Roles and Skills**: Controls, the four roles’ numbers and skills, 5 combos, levels
- **Chapters and Bosses**: HP and per-phase attacks of the eight bosses, fork mid-bosses, area names
- **Enemies and Stats**: Base enemy numbers, multiplier formulas, per-chapter enemy names and stats
- **Puzzles and Secrets**: 16 riddles, secret rooms, banner locations, lifts and forks
- **Growth and Challenge Modes**: How to earn Honor, gear and cosmetic prices, 12 blessings, the Abyss, the Weekly Expedition
- **Achievements**, **Old Records**, **Strategy**: All 33 achievements, the 16 old records, situational tips

dummyparty/rules-and-controls.b:
:: Category = Controls and rules guide
:: Match length = 7 rounds by default (1 to 12)
:: Round points = 1st 5, 2nd 3, 3rd 2, 4th 1
:: Players = Up to 8
:: Input = Keyboard, mouse, touch
:: See also = **Getting Started**, **Minigames: Races and Brawls**, **Minigames: Timing and Precision**, **Shop and Achievements**, **Online Rooms**

This page gathers the control keys, match flow, scoring, room rules, last-place boost and special awards as confirmed in the code. Rules for each minigame are on the two list pages.

## Controls
- Move with WASD or the arrow keys. On a phone, drag the bottom-left of the screen to get a joystick.
- The A button is Space, J, Z, Enter, a mouse click or the on-screen A. The B button is K, X, Shift, E or the on-screen B.
- What A and B do differs per minigame. In Simon Says, A is jump and B is crouch, while in Rising Lava B is the shove. A controls guide appears on screen before each start.
- Mashing A does not count a new press while another A input is still held, nor one arriving within 45 ms of the last. Alternating keys to double your mashing is blocked, so a single finger is the reliable way.
- In the lobby, Space jumps, K throws and keys 1 to 5 send emotes. After sending an emote you must wait 1.2 s before the next.

## Match flow
- Each minigame runs through a 6 s intro, a 3 s countdown, the game itself (a time limit that depends on the minigame), a 4 s ending and a 6 s results screen.
- Each round gives 5 points for 1st, 3 for 2nd, 2 for 3rd and 1 for 4th, and 0 from 5th on. Anyone missing from the ranking is placed last. The number of round wins is counted separately from points.
- After the last round comes the final results screen with the award ceremony, the special awards and the winner interview. For your record, a match win counts for everyone tied on the top score (not if the top score is 0).
- The last-place boost applies from round 2 on, with 3 or more players, and only when the number of players tied on the lowest score is at most a third of the room (rounded up). Boosted players move faster in the next game and the commentator comments.

## Room rules
- In the lobby the host sets the number of rounds (1 to 12, default 7) and which minigames can appear. Rounds cannot exceed the number of enabled minigames, and the round list is built by shuffling the enabled ones and cutting from the front, so the same minigame never appears twice in one match.
- The picker has a turn-all-off button and a search box. With fewer than 3 minigames enabled, the choice is ignored and the full list is used. The setting is saved in this browser, and guests see the round and minigame counts.
- The code still contains a maze game, a chess brawl and an Uno-style card game, but they are retired from matches and are not among the 36.

## Solo and Practice
- Solo mode is played with bots. There are 3 by default, adjustable from 1 to 7 with the plus and minus buttons in the lobby. Bot names come from twelve choices such as Spaced-Out Dummy, Shop Window Alum and One-Arm Kid.
- Practice lets you pick one minigame on the home screen and play it 3 times with one bot. It does not count for scores, coins, achievements or ranking.
- Without logging in, a Play offline button appears under the login. Offline you can only play solo, and shop purchases are unavailable.

## Special awards and interview
- Special awards are decided automatically from in-game records, collected on the host side. Fart King needs 3 or more farts, Fall King 2 or more falls and Punching Bag 4 or more hits taken. Eternal Last Place (2+ last places) and So Close Award (2+ second places) appear only with 3 or more players.
- A match gives at most 4 special awards and one player can win at most 2. Ties on a record are broken at random, and each award carries one of three commentary lines.
- The winner interview picks one of five questions, and once the winner chooses one of three answers, the commentator reacts to that answer.

## Tips
- Winning all 7 rounds gives a maximum of 35 points. The gap between 1st and 2nd (2 points) is larger than between 2nd and 3rd (1 point), so going for 1st is the efficient choice when you have a real shot.
- Elimination minigames (Island Shove, Hot Potato Bomb, Crumbling Tiles, Musical Chairs and so on) rank players by the reverse order of elimination. Even without winning, outlasting one more player protects your placement.
- Some minigames have their own tiebreakers: Freeze Pose favors faster reactions, Balloon Darts fewer darts thrown, Find the Mannequin fewer wrong picks and Cup Shuffle more correct picks. Accuracy and fewer wasted actions pay off.
- The base hub ranking points are double those of a bots-only match when two or more humans play, and each round win adds 5 on top. The same match is worth more to the ranking when played with other people.

dummyparty/minigames-action.b:
:: Category = Minigame list
:: Entries = 18 of the 36
:: Time limits = 40 to 130 s
:: Mostly uses = Movement, jumping, shoving, mashing
:: See also = **Getting Started**, **Controls and Rules**, **Minigames: Timing and Precision**

This page collects the 18 minigames where you compete by moving: running, shoving and surviving. Time limits and rules follow the descriptions and time values stored in the game code. The other 18 are on the timing and precision page.

## List
- **Obstacle Run**(60 s limit): Race to the finish line. Jump hurdles, avoid mud, and slip if you step on a banana. You can also throw bananas in front of rivals. A thrown banana lands much further ahead of the target (since build 76, 240 instead of the old 70, never past just before the finish line), so you can see it coming while running and jump over it. On-screen buttons: A = Jump, B = Banana. Ranking: order of crossing the finish line, then farthest distance for those who did not finish.
- **Island Shove**(80 s limit): On an island surrounded by sea, push rivals into the water and be the last one standing. The island keeps shrinking, and the shove needs a short rest before reuse. On-screen buttons: A = Shove. Ranking: last one standing on top and earlier fallers below, and if time runs out, survivors rank by closeness to the island center.
- **Brawl**(75 s limit): Random weapons keep appearing on the floor. Grab them, swing them and be the last one standing. Walk over a weapon box to pick it up. Weapons wear out as you use them. On-screen buttons: A = Attack, B = Drop weapon. Ranking: survivors by remaining HP, with earlier knock-outs below.
- **Hot Potato Bomb**(100 s limit): Touching someone passes the bomb on, and whoever holds it when it explodes is out. The bomb carrier is slightly faster and can dash to flee or chase. On-screen buttons: A = Dash. Ranking: last survivor first, earlier explosions lower.
- **Shop Window Freeze**(55 s limit): Sneak past the guard down a long corridor to the exit. Freeze when the guard turns around, since moving under the flashlight sends you back to the start. Move again once the light goes out. Ranking: order of reaching the exit, and the round ends as soon as 4 players arrive.
- **Crumbling Tiles**(75 s limit): Tiles break soon after you step on them, so keep moving and stay on the floor to the end. Shove rivals onto missing tiles. A jump can clear one gap. On-screen buttons: A = Shove, B = Jump. Ranking: last one on the floor first, earlier fallers lower.
- **Conveyor Survival**(65 s limit): Survive on a factory belt that keeps speeding up, dodging crates without falling into the furnace. Jump over crates. A hit makes your limbs fly off. On-screen buttons: A = Jump. Ranking: survivors on top and earlier furnace victims below.
- **Musical Chairs**(130 s limit): Sit on a chair when the music stops. There is always one chair too few. Circle the chairs while music plays, run for an empty one when it stops, and shoving is allowed. On-screen buttons: A = Shove. Ranking: last survivor first, earlier eliminations lower.
- **Photo Shoot**(80 s limit): Stand in the lit area and hold a pose. Moving when the shutter fires gives a blurry photo. Step into the light, hold the pose button and stay still. You can also shove rivals out of the light. On-screen buttons: A = Pose, B = Shove. Ranking: total score over the six shots.
- **Box Escape**(55 s limit): Start inside a parcel box, break out and run for the exit before the forklift catches you. Mash the button to smash the box, go around stacked boxes and use the dash to catch up. On-screen buttons: A = Pound · Jump, B = Dash. Ranking: order of reaching the exit, then farthest distance for those who did not make it.
- **Tug of War**(80 s limit): Everyone pulls the rope in a different direction to bring the knot to their own spot. Mash the button to pull. The first knot to reach you wins first place, then the knot returns to the center for the next player. On-screen buttons: A = Pull. Ranking: order of pulling the knot to your spot, then closeness of the knot to your spot for the rest.
- **Mannequin Hide and Seek**(50 s limit): One player is the seeker, and the hiders stand still among the displayed mannequins pretending to be real ones. A hider who stops loses their name tag and scarf. The seeker presses catch next to a suspect, and a wrong catch freezes the seeker briefly. On-screen buttons: A = Catch. Ranking: hiders score full marks if never caught or the share of time survived if caught, and the seeker scores by share of hiders caught.
- **Ball Pit Showdown**(45 s limit): Collect the most balls in a pool full of them. Walk over a ball to pick it up, and a golden ball counts as 5. Shoving a nearby player sends them flying. Balls cannot be stolen. On-screen buttons: A = Shove. Ranking: number of balls collected.
- **Fart Rocket Race**(55 s limit): Fly to the finish on fart power. Hold the button to inflate the balloon and release in the green zone to go farthest. Holding too long makes it burst and sends you backward. On-screen buttons: A = Hold to charge. Ranking: order of reaching the finish, then farthest position for the rest.
- **Rising Lava**(40 s limit): Lava rises from below, so climb to the upper platforms and last the longest. Move sideways and jump up. You can jump onto platforms from underneath. You can shove a nearby player, and touching lava eliminates you. On-screen buttons: A = Jump, B = Shove. Ranking: survivors by how high they stand on screen, and those who touched lava rank higher the later they did.
- **Shopping Cart Race**(55 s limit): Ride a shopping cart for 4 laps. Hold the button in corners to drift and build power, then release for a burst of speed. Hitting a wall or another cart spills goods, and stepping on spilled goods makes you slip. On-screen buttons: A = Drift. Ranking: order of finishing 4 laps, then progress for the rest.
- **Tightrope Race**(50 s limit): Walk along a narrow rope to the finish. Lean against the tilt to keep your balance. The closer to center you are, the faster you walk, and the button speeds you up but makes you wobble much more. If you fall, you climb back a little behind. On-screen buttons: A = Walk faster. Ranking: order of reaching the finish, then farthest distance for the rest.
- **Wall Squeeze**(42 s limit): Move up and down to line up with the hole in each approaching wall, and a collision costs a life. If the hole is narrow, flatten yourself with the button to pass (it needs a short rest before reuse). You have 2 lives, and whoever survives or passes the most walls wins. On-screen buttons: A = Flatten. Ranking: survivors by walls passed, and eliminated players rank higher the later they were out.

dummyparty/minigames-skill.b:
:: Category = Minigame list
:: Entries = 18 of the 36
:: Time limits = 13 to 64 s
:: Mostly uses = A and B buttons, aiming, timing
:: See also = **Getting Started**, **Controls and Rules**, **Minigames: Races and Brawls**

This page collects the 18 minigames decided by the moment of a button press, aiming, balance or memory. Most are short rounds of a few seconds to under a minute. The 18 where players collide are on the races and brawls page.

## List
- **Hot Dog Eating Contest**(45 s limit): Eat the most hot dogs. Mash the button to eat, but stop while the screen shows that it is hot, since pressing then makes you choke and rest. On-screen buttons: A = Chomp (mash). Ranking: number of hot dogs eaten.
- **Chicken Herding**(60 s limit): Herd fleeing chickens into your own coop, and whoever gets the most in wins. Chickens run when you approach, so push them toward the coop from behind. Shouting makes nearby chickens bolt. A golden chicken counts as 3. On-screen buttons: A = Cluck!. Ranking: number of chickens put in your coop.
- **Terrible Dance Battle**(30 s limit): A rhythm game. Press the matching direction (WASD) the moment each falling arrow reaches the line at the bottom. Accuracy earns more points and wrong presses lose points. Ranking: highest score.
- **Guess the 3-Minute Ramen**(13 s limit): When the ramen starts boiling, count in your head. The timer is hidden after 3 seconds, so press the button when you think exactly 8 seconds have passed. The closest wins. On-screen buttons: A = Now! (stop). Ranking: closeness of your press to 8 seconds, with no press ranking last.
- **Balloon Inflating**(35 s limit): The bigger the balloon, the more points, but it can burst at any time. Inflate with A and bank the points with B when it feels safe. A burst balloon scores 0. On-screen buttons: A = Blow, B = Bank points. Ranking: total of banked points.
- **Simon Says**(40 s limit): Obey only the commands that start with “Simon says”. Press A for Simon says jump, B for Simon says crouch, and press nothing for a bare “Jump!” without the phrase. On-screen buttons: A = Jump, B = Crouch. Ranking: highest score.
- **Jump Rope Contest**(45 s limit): Keep jumping an ever-faster rope. Getting caught eliminates you and the last one left wins. Jump with A just as the rope passes your feet, since jumping early while it is still coming down gets you caught. On-screen buttons: A = Jump. Ranking: survivors by number of jumps, and those caught rank higher the later they were caught.
- **Whack-a-Mole**(35 s limit): Whack the moles popping out of holes. Move the mallet with the movement keys and swing with A. Hitting a bomb mole costs points and stuns you briefly. On-screen buttons: A = Smash. Ranking: highest score.
- **Rock Paper Scissors Tournament**(50 s limit): Players pair up for rock-paper-scissors, the winner advances and the loser is out. Pick one of the rock, paper or scissors buttons at the bottom. When time is up your pick is used, and a tie is replayed. Ranking: the tournament champion first, earlier eliminations lower.
- **Human Cannon**(38 s limit): Get fired from a cannon to land in the center of a pool target, and the closer the better. Press A to stop the rising and falling angle, then A again to stop the power, and you launch. Watch the wind. The highest score after 4 shots wins. On-screen buttons: A = Stop angle/power. Ranking: sum of the four shots.
- **Freeze Pose**(55 s limit): When the music stops, copy the shown pose quickly. Up is hands raised, down is crouch, left is arms spread and right is push, and speed earns more points. When “Reverse!” appears press the opposite direction, and press nothing for “Fake!”. Ranking: highest score, with faster reactions winning ties.
- **Barber Shop Chaos**(38 s limit): Move the scissors up and down to cut the hair along the dotted line. The scissors advance to the right on their own, staying close to the line earns more points, and the accuracy of three rounds is added up for the ranking. Ranking: sum of the accuracy over three rounds.
- **Balloon Darts**(36 s limit): Pop rising balloons with darts. Move the crosshair with the direction keys and throw with the button. A normal balloon is 1 point, a small fast golden balloon is 3, and popping a black bomb balloon costs 2. The highest score over 30 seconds wins. On-screen buttons: A = Throw dart. Ranking: highest score, with fewer darts thrown winning ties.
- **Waiter Tray Run**(48 s limit): Press the button in the left kitchen to stack plates on the tray, then carry them to the guests’ table on the right. The faster you run the more the tray sways, and losing balance spills everything. Holding the second button makes you walk slowly and steady the tray. The more plates, the bigger the score. On-screen buttons: A = Stack plates, B = Walk slowly. Ranking: highest score.
- **Find the Mannequin**(62 s limit): Among the mannequins packed in the stands, find the single one whose scarf color and hat both match the mannequin shown above. Move the crosshair with the direction keys and pick with the button. The first finder gets 3 points, then 2, then 1, and a wrong pick locks you out briefly. On-screen buttons: A = This one!. Ranking: highest score, with fewer wrong picks winning ties.
- **Parachute Landing**(52 s limit): Jump from the sky, open your parachute and land in the center of the target. Move left and right over the target, press the button once to open the parachute and descend slowly while wind pushes you. Touching the ground without opening it is a failure. You jump 3 times in total. On-screen buttons: A = Open chute. Ranking: sum of the three jumps.
- **Cup Shuffle**(64 s limit): A ball hides under one of three cups. After a fast shuffle, pick the cup with the ball. A correct pick scores, faster picks score more, and you may change your pick within the time. 5 rounds in total. Ranking: highest score, with more correct picks winning ties.
- **Paint Mixing**(64 s limit): Mix a color on the palette as close as possible to the one shown above. Move the palette dot with the direction keys: color shifts from left to right, bright at the top and dark at the bottom. Confirm with the button when it matches best. The closer, the higher the score, over 6 rounds. On-screen buttons: A = Confirm color. Ranking: sum of the six rounds.

dummyparty/shop-and-achievements.b:
:: Category = Shop, ranking and achievements
:: Items for sale = 3 faces, 7 hats, 3 glasses, 6 dances, 12 titles
:: Exchange = 1 hub coin = 8 dC
:: Ranking points = Up to 200 per match
:: Achievements = 33
:: See also = **Getting Started**, **Controls and Rules**, **Online Rooms**

The shop opens from the Shop button on the home screen. Tapping a locked slot lets you preview it, and you can buy with dC only while logged in. The prices are the client-side table in the game code. A code comment says they must match a server-side table, which could not be checked in this repository.

## How to buy
- Tap a priced slot once for the price and a confirmation prompt, then tap the same slot again within 3 seconds to buy. After 3 seconds you start over. If your balance is short, the missing dC is shown.
- Hats and glasses unlock on their own after a number of round wins, and can also be bought early for that number times 10 dC. The count is the round-win total in the record saved on this device, and Practice does not count.
- Faces, dances and titles open only with dC. Your picks are saved on this device, and a title shows small beside your name.

## Price list
- Faces: Angry Uncle 60dC, Shocked face 30dC, Sleepy face 30dC
- Hats (brackets show round wins): Yellow crown 10 dC (1), Black top hat 20 dC (2), Blue baseball cap 40 dC (4), Propeller hat 60 dC (6), Yellow hard hat 90 dC (9), Chick hat 130 dC (13), Purple wizard hat 180 dC (18). The pink party hat is available from the start.
- Glasses (brackets show round wins): Black sunglasses 30 dC (3), Heart glasses 70 dC (7), Gold monocle 120 dC (12). The round glasses are available from the start.
- Victory dances: Disco Party 80dC, Robot Dance 100dC, Ballet Show 130dC, Breakdance 180dC, Take the L 160dC, Butt Bye-Bye 220dC
- The "Take the L" dance keeps repeating one hand raised in front of the forehead, a kick of the left foot to the left and, the moment it returns, a kick of the right foot to the right (build 73). In build 74 the hand waves as if teasing, the kicks became bigger and snappier, and a flash line and a floating "ㅋㅋ" (Korean laughter, like "haha") appear on each kick. In build 75 the hand no longer floats: an arm joined at the shoulder bends at the elbow, rises in front of the forehead and waves.
- Titles: Some Guy 20dC, Toot Master 30dC, Poot-Poot 40dC, 12-Layer Spy 60dC, President 150dC, Ex-Mannequin 50dC, Spring Knees 70dC, One-Arm Kid 80dC, 3-Min Ramen Pro 100dC, Hidden Mannequin 120dC, Window Legend 90dC, Reserved for Winner 200dC

## Hub ranking
- When logged in, each finished match adds points to the Dummy Party row of the hub ranking and shows a +N notice. The base comes from your place: 100 for 1st, 60 for 2nd, 40 for 3rd and 20 otherwise, plus 5 points for each round you won.
- In a match with no other human (bots only) the base is halved, and a single match never sends more than 200 points. A match tied with the top score is sent as a win, and Practice sends nothing.

## 33 achievements
Achievements are saved on this device, and while logged in the count and list are also posted to your hub profile. View them with the Achievements button in the lobby.
- **Mannequin Debut**: Finish a full match.
- **Accidental Winner**: Win a minigame for the first time.
- **Escaped the Shop Window**: Win a match overall.
- **Clocked In**: Finish 10 matches.
- **Party Is Home**: Finish 50 matches.
- **Crown Collector**: Win 5 matches overall.
- **The White Legend**: Win 20 matches overall.
- **Winning Is a Hobby**: Win minigames 10 times in total.
- **Winning Is My Job**: Win minigames 50 times in total.
- **Winning Like Breathing**: Win minigames 100 times in total.
- **All for Me**: Win every minigame of a match. (matches with 3 or more)
- **Revenge of the Last**: Be last at some point, then win overall. (3+ players)
- **Last Is Still a Rank**: Finish last in a minigame with 3 or more players.
- **Unstoppable Mannequin**: Win 3 minigames in a row.
- **Smells Like Humans**: Finish a match in a room with two or more people.
- **Humans Aren't So Tough**: Win overall in a room with two or more people.
- **Packed Showroom**: Finish a match with 8 players.
- **Nightmare of Bots**: Win overall in Solo mode.
- **Versatile Mannequin**: Win 10 different minigames.
- **All-Purpose Plastic**: Win 20 different minigames.
- **Minigame Nirvana**: Win all 36 minigames.
- **Professional Taster**: Play 20 different minigames.
- **Dojo Run Complete**: Play all 36 minigames.
- **National Jump Rope Team**: Win the Jump Rope Contest.
- **Master of Counting in Your Head**: Win Ramen 3-Minute Guess.
- **Master of the Gentle Fart**: Win the Fart Rocket Race. Gently, just right, without bursting.
- **Plastic Stomach**: Win the Hot Dog Eating Contest.
- **Made the Hustler Cry**: Win Cup Shuffle.
- **Hidden Mannequin Expert**: Win Find the Mannequin in the Crowd.
- **The Wallet Opened**: Buy something from the shop for the first time.
- **Impulse-Buying Mannequin**: Buy 5 items from the shop.
- **Emotes Over Words**: Use emotes 30 times.
- **dC-Rich Mannequin**: Save up 1000 dC.

dummyparty/online-play.b:
:: Category = Online rooms guide
:: Players = Up to 8 per room
:: Room code = 5 characters (capital letters and digits)
:: Connection = PeerJS, the host computer runs the game
:: Creating rooms = Login required
:: See also = **Getting Started**, **Controls and Rules**, **Shop and Achievements**

To play online you create a room or join one by code. This page covers the connection method, the difference between public and private rooms and what happens when the host leaves, as confirmed in the code and in-game messages.

## How to get in
- Enter your name (up to 12 characters) and press Create room. A friend types the 5-character room code on the home screen and presses Join. Codes use capital letters and digits and leave out the easily confused I, O, 0 and 1. Creating or joining a room requires logging in.
- Copy invite link in the lobby copies a link with room=code added to the address. Opening it fills in the code box.
- The host of a private room sees an **Invite friends** button in the lobby (while logged in, build 71). It opens a list of accepted friends (blocked people excluded) and other players who are online now (up to 40), with online friends first and the game each one is in. Pressing **Invite** sends the invite as a hub notification, and when the person presses the notification they enter this room right away.
- A sent invite can be taken back with **Cancel**, and it disappears by itself after 30 minutes or when the room closes. The list shows the time left in minutes. A cancelled or expired invite cannot be used to join.
- If the room is already mid-game you are asked to join the next one, and a full room of 8 refuses you. A wrong code gives a no-such-room message and a slow connection gives a timeout message.

## Public and private rooms
- A public room is listed in the full-screen window that the **Room list** button on the first screen opens (build 72), so anyone can pick it, while a private room admits only people who know the code. In the lobby the host can switch between public and private.
- A public room can be given a title (up to 20 characters), and the list shows it as "title-nickname". Without a title only the nickname shows. The information listed is the room code, the host name, the title, the number of players, whether the room is in the lobby, and the number of minigame kinds and matches. On the right of each row it shows "N minigames · M matches" and the player count, with a **Join** button. While the window is open it reloads every 5 seconds, and there is also a **Refresh** button. The room list is visible only when logged in, and if listing fails the code still works. The connection itself always runs on the room code.

## Connection and host
- The host computer runs the game. Guests only send their input roughly every 30 ms and the host sends back the state. With 4 or more guests the interval between state updates grows, and it grows further at 6 or more.
- If the host computer keeps falling behind, only that computer switches to lighter graphics, and the saved setting is left untouched.
- When the host leaves, whoever joined earliest among the rest becomes the new host. The match in progress restarts from the beginning with scores kept. If connecting to the new host fails, you get a message that the takeover failed and return to the home screen.

vowkeep/roles.b:
:: Category = Role guide
:: Roles = Knight, Archer, Priest, Squire
:: Skills = Three per role: Q, E, R
:: Dodge = Space (1.2 seconds until it can be used again)
:: Combined skills = 5 types
:: See also = **Getting Started**, **Chapters and Bosses**, **Enemies and Stats**, **Growth and Challenge Modes**, **Strategy**

The stats, skills, controls, and combined skills of the four roles (Knight, Archer, Priest, and Squire) are summarized using the numbers shown in the game. Skill descriptions and names match the in-game display.

## Controls
- PC: Move with WASD (up, down, left, right relative to the screen), aim with the mouse, attack with left click, skills with Q E R, dodge with Space, hold F to interact (revive a fallen ally, open a chest, light a campfire), choose a blessing with 1 2 3.
- Phone: Move with the left thumb, and use the right buttons to attack (automatically aims at the nearest enemy), skills, dodge, and interact.
- The phone screen was refined in build 54. Dialogue boxes appear small at the top edge of the screen instead of the middle (both vertical and horizontal), and room name tags, the leave button, notices, and control buttons are smaller so they don't cover the character. Pixel tiles are drawn more finely to fit the screen size, and the visible area is slightly wider.
- A dodge lasts 0.35 seconds, and you must wait 1.2 seconds to use it again. Choosing the Dodge Master blessing cuts the wait by 40%.
- Dodging just before an attack lands puts you in a brief focused state and earns the achievement "Paper-Thin Margin."
- A fallen ally gets back up at 50% health if another ally holds F for 1.6 seconds within 20 seconds (with the Comradeship blessing, it is twice as fast). If 20 seconds pass, they enter a defeated state, and if a living ally is present, they return after 12 seconds at the last campfire with 50% health.
- Hold F next to a campfire for 1 second to light it. After that, when everyone has fallen, the run restarts from the campfire where the last fire was lit with 70% health. At this point, the awakened enemies return to their original positions and fall asleep again.
- Bot allies loosely follow the one in front. When there is no enemy to fight, they begin to follow if they are more than 9 m from the leader and stop when they are within 5 m.

## Role Stats
- **Knight**: Health 170, movement speed 6, basic attack damage 18, interval 0.45 seconds, range 2.5. Draws enemies in front and blocks.
- **Archer**: Health 105, movement speed 6.4, basic attack damage 13, interval 0.36 seconds, arrow speed 26. Shoots weak points from a distance. Holding the attack button fires two arrows at 0.8 seconds and three arrows at 2 seconds.
- **Priest**: Health 115, movement speed 6, basic attack damage 11, interval 0.5 seconds, light orb speed 16. Protects allies with healing and shields.
- **Squire**: Health 150, movement speed 7, basic attack damage 15, interval 0.38 seconds, range 2.3. Helps with potions and traps, and is not hurt when stepping on floor traps (it disarms them). Instead of dodging, it slides and trips enemies' legs to knock them down.
- Each level raises maximum health and all damage by 3% (based on level 1). The role level is set by the honor earned with that role. Reaching level N requires honor of 25 × (N-1) × (N-1), and the maximum is level 10 (honor 2025).

## Skills
- Knight Q **Guard** (cooldown 5 seconds): Raises a shield for 1.2 seconds and reduces incoming damage from the front by 70%. If a boss charge is blocked within the first 0.4 seconds, the boss is stunned.
- Knight E **Charge** (cooldown 6 seconds): Charges forward and deals 30 damage to enemies hit, knocking them back.
- Knight R **Rally** (cooldown 12 seconds): Nearby enemies focus only on you for 4 seconds, and damage you take during that time is reduced by 30%.
- Archer Q **Piercing Arrow** (cooldown 5 seconds): A strong arrow that pierces through enemies. 45 damage.
- Archer E **Rain of Arrows** (cooldown 9 seconds): Drops a rain of arrows on the aimed spot for 1.5 seconds.
- Archer R **Mark Weakness** (cooldown 12 seconds): Leaves a mark on the aimed enemy for 6 seconds, increasing damage taken from everyone by 50%.
- Priest Q **Heal** (cooldown 7 seconds): Restores 35 health to yourself and nearby allies.
- Priest E **Shield** (cooldown 14 seconds): Puts a shield on nearby allies for 5 seconds that blocks 25 damage.
- Priest R **Light of Rebirth** (cooldown 50 seconds): Revives a nearby fallen ally at 25% health. You gather light for 1 second, then they rise.
- Squire Q **Throw Potion** (cooldown 7 seconds): Throws a potion at the aimed spot, restoring 40 health to any ally there.
- Squire E **Set Trap** (cooldown 7 seconds): Places a trap under your feet. An enemy that steps on it is flung into the air, held for 2.5 seconds, and takes 40 damage. The trap explodes in flames that spread and burn enemies around it.
- Squire R **War Cry** (cooldown 15 seconds): Raises the attack and speed of nearby allies by 30% for 7 seconds. During that time, the Squire's torch attacks throw sparks that burn nearby enemies too.

## Basic Attack Combos
- The Archer holds the attack button to charge the shot. A quick shot fires one arrow, 0.8 seconds of charge fires two, and 2 seconds of charge fires three, with two arrows dealing 1.3x damage and three arrows dealing 1.7x.
- The Knight's third slash, Smash, leaps up in place and strikes the enemy the moment it comes down to the ground. The Knight does not move while in the air. The first two hits are a downward slash from the upper right and a low sideways slash.
- The Priest's third attack gathers light in place (about 0.45 seconds) and then fires a large beam of light that pierces enemies. Damage is 2.4x the basic attack.
- The Squire, instead of dodging, slides forward on its feet and knocks down enemies it touches. Enemies caught in a trap are flung high, and the flames that burst out burn nearby enemies too.
- The damage of the third attack is 3.4x the basic attack for the Knight's Smash (area damage), 2.4x for the Priest, and 1.5x for the Squire (its area is 1.3x).
- If the basic attacks of the Knight, Priest, and Squire are chained within 0.65 seconds, the third hit becomes the strong attack. The Archer has no such combo.

## Combined Skills
When two roles use matching skills within 1 second of each other and within 12 m of each other, a combined skill is triggered. When a human uses a matching skill, a bot ally within 10 m uses its matching skill within 0.7 seconds to match.
- **Light Charge**: Knight Charge + Priest Shield: Light bursts along the path taken, and the Knight gets a large shield
- **Sanctuary Cry**: Knight Rally + Priest Heal: Heals nearby allies more, and deals light damage to enemies
- **Shield Wall**: Knight Guard + Squire War Cry: A large shield for all nearby allies
- **Fire Rain**: Archer Rain of Arrows + Squire Potion: The arrow rain catches fire and hurts twice as much
- **Hunter's Net**: Archer Mark Weakness + Squire Trap: Binds everything around the marked enemy

vowkeep/chapters-and-bosses.b:
:: Category = Chapter and boss guide
:: Chapters = 8 chapters + Endless Abyss
:: Boss HP = 12000 to 26000 (solo)
:: Phases = Change at 60% and 30% HP (a 4th at 12% in chapters 6 to 8)
:: Mid-bosses = One of two at each chapter’s fork
:: See also = **Getting Started**, **Roles and Skills**, **Enemies and Stats**, **Puzzles and Secrets**, **Strategy**

This page collects the eight chapters’ names, boss numbers and per-phase attacks, the fork mid-bosses and the area names exactly as they appear in the game data. Boss HP and attack values are for solo play.

## Boss Basics
- On entering the boss room, a roughly 3-second entrance plays and then the fight starts. A boss only chases players who are inside its room.
- The boss attack values on this page already include the boss damage multiplier of 1.3 on top of the base attack. With 2, 3 or 4 human players, boss and enemy HP becomes 1.35x, 1.7x or 2.05x.
- Defeating a boss ends the chapter on the spot and everyone gets 90 Honor. There is no falling-rock escape stage any more.
- Defeating the boss within 3 minutes of entering its room earns the Swift Boss Hunt achievement.
- From phase 2 the boss calls minions (3 every 11 to 15 s depending on the boss, 4 in phase 4) and they vanish when the boss falls.

## Chapter 1 · Beneath the Fallen Castle
- Boss **The Fallen Grand Master**: HP 12000, speed 3.9, attack 72, difficulty multiplier 1.
- Phase 2 (Skeleton Summon): The Grand Master summons skeleton soldiers. If the Knight blocks his charge, he is stunned.
- Phase 3 (Cracked Armor): The Grand Master's armor has cracked. Dodge the black flames and strike the red crack on his back. Double damage.
- Fork mid-bosses: Grave Sentinel (charger), Bone Summoner (summoner). Fork room: Reliquary.
- Map: 98×122 cells, 14 areas: Collapsed Stairs, Skeleton Barracks, Chamber of Plates, Armory, Collapsed Bridgehead, Abandoned Chapel, Flooded Cloister, Lightless Prison, Reliquary, Well Pulley, Chamber of the Shield Oath, Guard's Tomb, The Grand Master's Path, Grand Master's Chamber.

## Chapter 2 · The Ashen Forest
- Boss **Bern, Hunter of the Thorn Crown**: HP 15000, speed 4.6, attack 65, difficulty multiplier 1.12.
- Phase 2 (Wolf Pack): Bern calls wolves with his horn. Take down the wolves first, and roll to dodge his leaps.
- Phase 3 (Ring of Thorns): Thorns overrun the hunting ground. Get inside the ring of thorns.
- Fork mid-bosses: Enraged Wolf King (charger), Forest Shaman (summoner). Fork room: Bramble Path.
- Map: 116×164 cells, 16 areas: Forest Edge, Wolf Den, Hunter's Statue Grounds, Hunters' Camp, Severed Ravine, Fallen Log Bridge, Forest Cabin, Lightless Thicket, Fallen Old Tree, Bramble Path, Hunter's Watchtower Pulley, Chamber of High Targets, Alpha's Hill, Ashen Trail, Ashen Spring, Heart of the Hunting Ground.

## Chapter 3 · The Sunken Abbey
- Boss **Odric, the Drowned Archbishop**: HP 14000, speed 3.2, attack 62, difficulty multiplier 1.25.
- Phase 2 (Monk Summon): The Archbishop wakes the drowned monks. Don't lose track of where he teleports.
- Phase 3 (Black Water): The black water begins to rise. Avoid the pools and hold out to the end.
- Fork mid-bosses: Belfry Executioner (charger), Water Priest (summoner). Fork room: Sodden Library.
- Map: 80×210 cells, 15 areas: Flooded Gate, Baptistery, Candlestick Chantry, Collapsed Cloister, Collapsed Cloister, Sodden Library, Monks' Quarters, Underwater Cellar, Beneath the Bell Tower, Belfry Pulley, Chamber of the Fonts, Ossuary, Monks' Cloister, Choir Stalls, Sunken Cathedral.

## Chapter 4 · The Tower of the Vow
- Boss **The Ashen King**: HP 14000, speed 4, attack 65, difficulty multiplier 1.22.
- Phase 2 (Ash Knight Summon): The King summons ash knights. The Knight can block his charge.
- Phase 3 (Ashen Flame): Ashen flames blaze from the crown. Dodge the flames and go for the final blow.
- Fork mid-bosses: Ironclad Gatekeeper (charger), Tower Alchemist (summoner). Fork room: Armory.
- Map: 46×338 cells, 14 areas: Gate Beneath the Tower, Ruined Barracks, Tower Lever Room, Chain Bridge, Severed Tower Hall, Armory, Chamber of Oaths, Shadow Stairs, Burning Gallery, Tower Lift, Thornvine Chamber, Guards' Antechamber, Stairs Before the Throne, Throne Room.

## Chapter 5 · The Frozen Border
- Boss **Harald of the Frost Oath**: HP 15000, speed 4, attack 65, difficulty multiplier 1.3.
- Phase 2 (Brother Summon): Harald wakes the frozen brothers. Step between the three lines of ice spears. If hit, you freeze and slow down.
- Phase 3 (Ice Flame): Icicles fall from the fortress ceiling. Watch the shadows at your feet and keep moving.
- Fork mid-bosses: Frost Lancer (charger), Blizzard Witch (summoner). Fork room: Collapsed Watchtower.
- Map: 172×167 cells, 17 areas: Snowbound Gate, Frozen Parade Ground, Frost Sigil Floor, Ice Ramparts, Ice Rift, Collapsed Watchtower, Ice Cave, Brotherhood Refectory, Snowbound Storeroom, Blizzard Valley, Frost Gallery, Rampart Pulley, Ice Crystal Chamber, Brotherhood Master's Chamber, Frozen Bridge, Frozen Chapel, Ice Throne.

## Chapter 6 · The Forgotten Mine
- Boss **Grom, the Stone-Swallowing Giant**: HP 21000, speed 4.4, attack 68, difficulty multiplier 1.36.
- Phase 2 (Beast of the Shafts): Grom curls up and rolls around. He bounces off walls up to three times. Get out of his path.
- Phase 3 (Falling Rocks): Falling rocks pour into the shaft. Get far from his stomp, and sidestep the boulders.
- Phase 4 (Earthquake): Grom smashes the ground with all his strength. Dodge outside the three rings of the tremor.
- Fork mid-bosses: Mine Overseer (charger), Shaft Shaman (summoner). Fork room: Collapsed Dig Site.
- Map: 124×98 cells, 15 areas: Mine Entrance, First Shaft, Light Crystal Shaft, Cart Tracks, Caved-in Shaft, Collapsed Dig Site, Miners' Rest, Unlit Shaft, Underground Pool, Mine Lift, Lantern Row Shaft, Overseer's Office, Abandoned Shaft, Blackstone Store, Deepest Shaft.

## Chapter 7 · The Temple of Flame
- Boss **Seraphine, Prophet of Flame**: HP 20000, speed 3.3, attack 65, difficulty multiplier 1.42.
- Phase 2 (Zealot Summon): Seraphine calls her flame zealots. Dodge the cross-shaped fire pillars by standing between the lines.
- Phase 3 (Rising Flames): Fire pillars circle around Seraphine. Circle along with the rotating fire pillars.
- Phase 4 (Judgment of the Sun): Seraphine calls down the Judgment of the Sun. Eight lines of fire pillars split apart twice. Step between the lines.
- Fork mid-bosses: Sanctum Guardian Knight (charger), Censer Priest (summoner). Fork room: Censer Chamber.
- Map: 90×242 cells, 16 areas: Sand Stairs, Pilgrims' Court, Hall of Mirrors, Flame Oratory, Collapsed Pilgrim Road, Censer Chamber, Priests' Quarters, Smoke-Filled Crypt Shrine, Incense Room, Blazing Gallery, Temple Pulley, Circle of Prayer, Warden Knight's Gate, Pilgrims' Way, Shaded Well, Sanctum of the Flame.

## Chapter 8 · The Abyss of Ash
- Boss **The Undying Flame**: HP 26000, speed 4.2, attack 68, difficulty multiplier 1.5.
- Phase 2 (Oathbroken Summon): The Flame summons oathbroken knights. The swirling flames spread three times in a row.
- Phase 3 (Flame of the Abyss): Fireballs rain from the abyss sky. Avoid the fireball shadows and go for the final blow.
- Phase 4 (Undying Fire): The flame burns with the last of its strength. Dodge the five-layer whirlwinds and the fireball rain together.
- Fork mid-bosses: Abyss Hound (charger), Shadow Summoner (summoner). Fork room: Ashen Pillars.
- Map: 119×176 cells, 18 areas: Endless Stairs, Tomb of Broken Vows, Ember Altars, The Last Passage, Floating Bridge, Severed Abyss Bridge, Forest of Ash, Ashen Pillars, Last Refuge, Light-Swallowing Pit, Ember Bridge, Burning River, Ember Lift, Altar of Black Flame, Altar of the Oathsworn, Drifting Rock Isle, Ember Gate, Floor of the Abyss.

:: Category = Enemy guide
:: Common enemies = 4 types, names change per chapter
:: Special = Elite (captain), Mimic, mid-boss at forks
:: Health multiplier = +35% per player beyond the first
:: See also = **Getting Started**, **Chapters and Bosses**, **Secrets and Puzzles**, **Strategy**

This lists the base stats of enemies and the multipliers applied per chapter. The same 4 enemy types appear with different names and appearances in each chapter, and sleeping enemies wake when you get close.

## Base Stats (based on Chapter 1 Skeletons)
- **Skeleton Soldier**: Health 130, movement speed 4.4, attack 32, range 1.8, attack wind-up 0.42 seconds, interval 0.9 seconds, honor 1.
- **Skeleton Archer**: Health 85, movement speed 3.9, attack 25, range 12, attack wind-up 0.55 seconds, interval 1.6 seconds, honor 1.
- **Shield Skeleton**: Health 230, movement speed 3.5, attack 36, range 1.9, attack wind-up 0.5 seconds, interval 1.3 seconds, honor 2.
- **Skeleton Guard Captain**: Health 900, movement speed 4.2, attack 52, range 2.5, attack wind-up 0.55 seconds, interval 1.3 seconds, honor 6.
- **Mimic**: Health 760, movement speed 5.4, attack 40, range 2.1, attack wind-up 0.4 seconds, interval 1 second, honor 8.
- The Skeleton Archer keeps a distance of 7.5 and shoots, and the Shield Skeleton takes 70% less damage when hit from the front (piercing attacks still hit fully). Elites rush in with a charging slash.
- Defeating a Mimic gives an extra 40 honor on top of the honor above. Defeating an Elite grants the "Captain Slayer" achievement.

## Actual Stat Calculation
- Common enemy health = base health × type multiplier × chapter difficulty multiplier × 0.7 (Elite: 0.85). Attack = base attack × chapter difficulty multiplier × 0.75 (Elite: 0.85). Movement speed is the base speed multiplied by the type multiplier.
- Mimic health is multiplied only by the chapter difficulty multiplier, and its attack is the difficulty multiplier × 0.85.
- If there are two or more human players, the health of all enemies and bosses is multiplied by 1 + 0.35 × (number of players - 1). Bots are not counted as players.
- The fork mid-boss is an Elite with its health raised 3.2x and its body enlarged 1.25x. Defeating it gives 30 honor.

## Enemies by Chapter
The values below are for solo play (1 human player). The numbers in parentheses are health, attack, and movement speed, in that order.
- **Chapter 1 · Basement of the Fallen Castle**: Skeleton Soldier (91, 24, 4.4), Skeleton Archer (59, 19, 3.9), Shield Skeleton (161, 27, 3.5), Skeleton Guard Captain (765, 44, 4.2).
- **Chapter 2 · Ashen Forest**: Ashen Wolf (82, 27, 5.7), Ash Hunter (67, 21, 3.9), Bark Giant (216, 30, 3.0), Wolf Chieftain (857, 50, 4.8).
- **Chapter 3 · Sunken Monastery**: Drowned Monk (131, 30, 4.0), Servant of the Water (74, 23, 3.9), Bell Ringer (201, 34, 3.5), Monastery Sentinel (956, 55, 4.2).
- **Chapter 4 · Tower of Oaths**: Knight of Ash (122, 29, 4.4), Ash Crossbowman (73, 23, 3.9), Tower Shieldbearer (196, 33, 3.5), King's Guard Knight (933, 54, 4.2).
- **Chapter 5 · Frozen Border**: Frozen Brother (130, 31, 4.4), Frost Archer (77, 24, 3.9), Ice Shieldbearer (209, 35, 3.5), Frost Brotherhood Captain (994, 57, 4.2).
- **Chapter 6 · Forgotten Mine**: Skeleton Miner (130, 33, 4.4), Pickaxe Thrower (81, 26, 3.9), Rock Giant (274, 37, 3.0), Mine Overseer (1040, 60, 4.2).
- **Chapter 7 · Temple of Flames**: Flame Acolyte (129, 34, 4.8), Ash Priest (84, 27, 3.9), Censer Keeper (229, 38, 3.5), Temple Guardian Knight (1086, 63, 4.2).
- **Chapter 8 · Abyss of Ash**: Knight of the Broken Oath (157, 36, 4.4), Abyss Crossbowman (89, 28, 3.9), Abyss Shieldbearer (241, 40, 3.5), Oathkeeper of the Abyss (1148, 66, 4.2).

vowkeep/puzzles-and-secrets.b:
:: Category = Puzzle and secret guide
:: Puzzles = 16 kinds (2 per chapter)
:: Secret rooms = 2 per chapter
:: Order banners = 1 per chapter (none in the Abyss)
:: See also = **Getting Started**, **Roles and Skills**, **Chapters and Bosses**, **Old Records**, **Strategy**

Every chapter has two riddle rooms that open a portcullis, two secret rooms behind cracked walls, and one each of a dark room, a broken path, a lift and a fork. This page lists the rules of those rooms and where they are in each chapter, taken from the map data in the code.

## Riddle Room Rules
- Solving a riddle raises the portcullis and gives everyone 30 Honor. The first solve also earns the First Riddle achievement.
- Role-only riddles can only be solved by that role, and the hint text names which role. If no human plays that role, a bot with the same role solves it.
- If humans make no progress, a bot starts helping after 12 s, one step at a time. In the plate riddle, bots stand on the plates humans are not on.

## Riddles by Chapter
- Ch. 1 **Chamber of Plates**: There are four pressure plates on the floor. When everyone stands on one, the portcullis opens.
- Ch. 1 **Chamber of the Shield Oath**: Only the Knight can solve this. Block (Q) on each of the three shield slabs to open the portcullis.
- Ch. 2 **Hunter's Statue Grounds**: Turn all four statues to face the emblem in the center.
- Ch. 2 **Chamber of High Targets**: Only the Archer can solve this. Hit all three targets high on the wall with arrows within 10 seconds.
- Ch. 3 **Candlestick Chantry**: Light the braziers in the order shown on the stele. Get it wrong and they all go out.
- Ch. 3 **Chamber of the Fonts**: Only the Priest can solve this. Fill all four fonts with light using light orbs or Heal.
- Ch. 4 **Tower Lever Room**: Pulling a lever toggles its lantern and the lanterns on either side. Light all four lanterns.
- Ch. 4 **Thornvine Chamber**: Only the Squire can solve this. Burn all three thornvines with torch attacks.
- Ch. 5 **Frost Sigil Floor**: Step on all nine frost sigil tiles in a connected path, each only once, to make them all glow. Step on a glowing tile again and you start over.
- Ch. 5 **Ice Crystal Chamber**: Only the Knight can solve this. Shatter the three ice crystals with heavy strikes (attack·attack·heavy).
- Ch. 6 **Light Crystal Shaft**: Attack the four crystals to light them. The light fades after 8 seconds, so make all four glow at once.
- Ch. 6 **Lantern Row Shaft**: Only the Archer can solve this. Light all three lanterns in a row with a single Piercing Arrow (Q).
- Ch. 7 **Hall of Mirrors**: Turn the three mirrors (F) so the sunlight reaches the portcullis.
- Ch. 7 **Circle of Prayer**: Only the Priest can solve this. Stand in each of the three circles of light for 2 seconds to pray.
- Ch. 8 **Ember Altars**: Pick up an ember from the pile in the middle (F) and place one on each of the three altars (F).
- Ch. 8 **Altar of Black Flame**: Only the Squire can solve this. Throw potions (Q) to put out the three black flames.

## Secret Rooms and Cracked Walls
- A cracked wall falls after 6 normal hits, or in one hit from the knight’s heavy strike, a third-attack big blow or the archer’s piercing arrow. Opening it gives everyone 20 Honor and the one who opened it earns the Beyond the Broken Wall achievement.
- A secret room holds a treasure chest (60 Honor) and an old-record stone. Hold F for 0.8 s to read the stone. There are 16 old records in all, collected on the Old Records page.

## Order Banners
- Each chapter hides one banner, in a different kind of place per chapter. There is none in the Endless Abyss. Hold F in front of it for 1.5 s to pick it up.
- The carrier moves at 70% speed and cannot roll, attack or use skills, and enemies target that player first. Press F to put it down, and it drops where the carrier falls.
- If the carrier is still standing when the boss falls and the chapter ends, that chapter’s banner hangs on the lobby wall. Two achievements relate to banners: finishing a chapter while carrying one and hanging all eight.
The banner in each chapter is found here.
- Ch. 1: inside the second secret room
- Ch. 2: a niche that appears after solving the riddle room Chamber of High Targets
- Ch. 3: a corner niche in the dark room Underwater Cellar
- Ch. 4: inside the second secret room
- Ch. 5: a niche that appears after solving the riddle room Ice Crystal Chamber
- Ch. 6: a corner niche in the dark room Unlit Shaft
- Ch. 7: inside the second secret room
- Ch. 8: a niche that appears after solving the riddle room Altar of Black Flame

## Rooms Along the Way
- Dark room: take a torch from the rack at the entrance with F and only the area around that ally is lit. Up to two can carry torches per rack, and a torch carrier cannot use skills. The first time earns the Torch in the Dark achievement. If someone is in the room and nobody carries one, a bot picks it up.
- Broken path: topple the cracked pillar where the path breaks to make a bridge. It takes 6 normal hits, or one hit from the heavy strike, a third-attack big blow or a piercing arrow. Building the bridge gives everyone 20 Honor and the Pillar Bridge achievement. If people stay in the room for over 20 s, bots start hitting the pillar.
- Lift: the platform moves while you hold F near a handle on the lower or upper floor (3.5 s to travel), and once everyone is upstairs each gets 20 Honor and the Pulley Crew achievement.
- Mimic: one hides as a chest in each chapter except chapter 2. Defeating it gives 40 Honor on top of its base amount and the A Chest with Teeth achievement.
- Hold F for 1.2 s to open a treasure chest. A normal chest gives everyone 25 Honor and a secret-room chest 60. Hold F for 1 s at an altar and everyone gets 10 Honor and each player picks one blessing out of three random ones.
- Fork: each chapter has a room with two stone markers. Pick one and hold F for 1.2 s to summon a mid-boss, and the other side closes. The first marker is a charger dealing 1.25x damage, and the second is a summoner that calls two minions every 9 s, starting after 5 s. Defeating it gives everyone 30 Honor.

vowkeep/growth-and-modes.b:
:: Category = Progress and mode guide
:: Honor = Used for gear, cosmetics and role levels
:: Role level = Max 10
:: Blessings = 12 kinds
:: Curses = 7 kinds
:: See also = **Getting Started**, **Roles and Skills**, **Chapters and Bosses**, **Achievements**, **Strategy**

This page covers how Honor is earned and spent, gear and cosmetic prices, the twelve altar blessings, and the rules of the Endless Abyss and the Weekly Expedition, from the code’s data.

## Earning Honor
Honor earned on an expedition is saved to spend on gear and cosmetics, and the same amount becomes experience for the role you played. The values below go to everyone.
- Defeating enemies: soldier 1, archer 1, shield 2, elite 6, mimic 8 (plus 40). Names change per chapter but the values stay the same.
- Clearing a chapter by defeating the boss 90, fork mid-boss 30, solving a riddle 30, opening a cracked wall 20, building a pillar bridge 20, lifting everyone up 20, altar 10, normal chest 25, secret-room chest 60.
- With the Path of Honor blessing, the Honor you earn on that expedition is 25% higher. The Weekly Expedition adds 60 Honor for the first clear each week.

## Gear
- Each role upgrades its weapon and armor separately, from Worn to Decent (120 Honor) and then to Master-forged (320 Honor).
- A weapon raises all damage by +10% and +22% at the upper tiers, and armor raises max HP by +15 and +35.

## Cosmetics
Buy an item once with Honor and keep it, swapping freely. Stats do not change and friends can see them too.
- **Cape color**: Crimson 60, Forest green 60, Violet 90, Dawn gold 160
- **Helm ornament**: Red plume 80, Bone horns 100, Laurel wreath 120, Small crown 220
- **Shield emblem**: Cross 70, Star 90, Flame 110, Moon 140

## The 12 Blessings
At an altar you choose one of three, and it stays until the expedition ends. A blessing you already have does not come up again.
- **Sharp Blade**: Attack damage +15%
- **Light Feet**: Move speed +12%
- **Sturdy Armor**: Max HP +25
- **Quick Hands**: Basic attack interval -15%
- **Skill Mastery**: Skill cooldown -15%
- **Blood Oath**: Heal 1 HP each time you hit an enemy
- **Roll Master**: Roll cooldown -40%
- **Flame Weapon**: Basic attacks burn enemies
- **Thorn Armor**: Deal 8 damage to enemies that hit you
- **Brotherhood**: Revive allies twice as fast
- **Last Stand**: Below 30% HP, damage taken -25%
- **Path of Honor**: Honor earned this expedition +25%

## Endless Abyss
- It opens after chapter 8. Each floor gets a random map with a boss in the last room. The run ends when everyone falls, and the number of floors passed is saved as your best. There are achievements for reaching floors 5 and 10.
- The floor difficulty starts at 1.2 and rises by 0.06 per floor, and the floor boss is one of the chapter bosses at 45% HP, +10% per floor. Each cleared floor adds one of the 7 curses below at random.
- **Thick Bones**: Enemy HP +20%
- **Honed Weapons**: Enemy attack +15%
- **Hurried Feet**: Enemy move speed +10%
- **Dry Spring**: Healing received -25%
- **Heavy Hands**: Skill cooldown +15%
- **The Captain Returns**: One more enemy captain on every floor
- **Stubborn Guardians**: Floor guardian HP +30%

## Weekly Expedition
- It changes every Monday (Korean time). That week everyone runs the same chapter with the same two of the five weekly curses (the first five above), racing on time, and your best time is kept.
- Only players who have progressed up to that week’s chapter can play it, and the first clear that week adds 60 Honor. Records for the latest 12 weeks are kept.

All 33 in-game achievements are listed with their names and conditions exactly as written in the game. Chapters 2 to 8 each have a boss achievement.

## Full List
- **First Expedition**: Start your first expedition.
- **First Victory**: Defeat an enemy for the first time.
- **By the Bonfire**: Light a bonfire for the first time.
- **Captain Down**: Defeat the enemy captain found in every chapter.
- **Vowkeeper**: Defeat the Fallen Grand Master.
- **Perfect Block**: As the Knight, block a boss charge and stun it.
- **By a Hair**: Roll out of the way just before an attack lands.
- **Back on Your Feet**: Revive a fallen ally.
- **Expedition Together**: Go on an expedition with a friend in the same room.
- **Through the Ashen Wood**: Defeat Bern, Hunter of the Thorn Crown, in Chapter 2.
- **The Flame Reclaimed**: Defeat Odric, the Drowned Archbishop, in Chapter 3.
- **Crown Shattered**: Defeat the Ashen King in Chapter 4.
- **Thaw**: Defeat Harald of the Frost Oath in Chapter 5.
- **Source of the Stone**: Defeat Grom, the Stone-Swallowing Giant, in Chapter 6.
- **False Prophecy**: Defeat Seraphine, Prophet of Flame, in Chapter 7.
- **Those Who Kept the Vow**: Extinguish the Undying Flame in Chapter 8.
- **Beyond the Broken Wall**: Break a cracked wall and find a secret room.
- **Keeper of Old Records**: Read all 16 old records in the secret rooms.
- **Banner Keeper**: Finish a chapter while carrying the Order's banner.
- **Wall of the Order**: Hang the Order's banners from all eight chapters on the lobby wall.
- **Teamwork**: Use a combo with an ally for the first time.
- **Five Combos**: Try all five combos.
- **Abyss Floor 5**: Reach floor 5 of the Endless Abyss.
- **Abyss Floor 10**: Reach floor 10 of the Endless Abyss.
- **A Chest with Teeth**: Defeat a Mimic posing as a chest.
- **First Riddle**: Open a riddle room's portcullis for the first time.
- **Riddle Master**: Solve 10 riddles.
- **Torch in the Dark**: Pick up a torch in a dark room.
- **Swift Boss Hunt**: Defeat the boss within 3 minutes of entering the boss room.
- **Pillar Bridge**: Topple a cracked pillar to bridge a broken path.
- **Pulley Crew**: Ride the lift up a floor with everyone together.
- **Never Fell**: Clear a chapter without falling once.
- **Four Vows**: Clear at least one chapter with each of the four roles.

vowkeep/lore.b:
:: Category = Old records collection
:: Records = 16 (2 per chapter)
:: How to read = Hold F at the stone in a secret room
:: See also = **Getting Started**, **Chapters and Bosses**, **Puzzles and Secrets**, **Achievements**

These are the texts of the old-record stones in the two secret rooms of each chapter, exactly as written in the game. The secret rooms lie behind cracked walls. Reading them all earns the Keeper of Old Records achievement.

## Chapter 1 · Beneath the Fallen Castle
- Secret room 1: The first Grand Master, who founded the Order, never carved the vows into stone. "A vow is carved into the heart of the one who keeps it."
- Secret room 2: The last page of the Grand Master's diary: "The King showed me the flame. I could not refuse." At the end of the diary, four erased names are written.

## Chapter 2 · The Ashen Forest
- Secret room 1: The hunters' rule: never shoot a beast carrying young. Bern wrote that he first broke that rule on the King's orders.
- Secret room 2: Words carved into a tree stump: "The forest remembers. Even as ash." Beside it is a small wolf's pawprint.

## Chapter 3 · The Sunken Abbey
- Secret room 1: The abbey's first prayer: "The flame is borrowed, not owned." The Archbishop's own hand has struck through that line.
- Secret room 2: The names in the soaked ledger all belong to knights who took their vows in this abbey. On the very last line are the names of the four of you.

## Chapter 4 · The Tower of the Vow
- Secret room 1: A portrait of the King as a child hangs turned to face the wall. On the back is written: "I will be a king who conquers fear."
- Secret room 2: A guard knight's letter: "Every night, the King speaks to the flame." "He says the flame answers. That it came from the north."

## Chapter 5 · The Frozen Border
- Secret room 1: The Brotherhood's oath tablet: "When the cold comes, we share the fire." Harald kept that fire all to himself.
- Secret room 2: A letter trapped in ice: "Brother, the flame isn't warm." The writer's name is frozen over and can't be read.

## Chapter 6 · The Forgotten Mine
- Secret room 1: The miners' song: "Don't dig the black stone; when it wakes, it hungers." Beneath it, in the overseer's hand: "Double the output."
- Secret room 2: Grom's work log: "Swallowing stone makes me strong. I'm never hungry." The last page is torn by teeth marks.

## Chapter 7 · The Temple of Flame
- Secret room 1: A temple mural: the King, Harald, and Seraphine, kneeling before the flame. The fourth place is empty. Who could it be waiting for?
- Secret room 2: Seraphine's childhood prayer: "Please keep everyone warm." At some point, the prayer became "Please burn everyone."

## Chapter 8 · The Abyss of Ash
- Secret room 1: Thousands of vows carved into the walls of the abyss, all half worn away. This is how unkept vows became food for the flame.
- Secret room 2: Only the oldest vow remains clear. "We protect one another to the end." It's in the hand of the Order's first Grand Master.

vowkeep/strategy.b:
:: Category = Strategy collection
:: Basis = In-game numbers
:: See also = **Roles and Skills**, **Chapters and Bosses**, **Enemies and Stats**, **Secrets and Puzzles**, **Growth and Challenge Modes**

This only collects tips based on numbers from other documents. It's best to confirm the actual effects by trying them yourself.

## Team Composition and Player Count
- Bots are not counted as players, so even if bots fill empty slots, enemy and boss health does not go up. Each additional human raises health by 35%, so you need a stronger team.
- Bots use their matching skill to match the skills a human uses, so even playing alone you can aim for the "Five Combined Skills" achievement by using all 5 combined skills.

## Combat
- You can counter a boss charge and stun it if you time Knight's Guard within the first 0.4 seconds of the charge. Guard has a 5-second cooldown, so use it when you see the boss's charge windup. Rally (R) gathers enemies toward the Knight for 4 seconds and reduces damage taken by 30%, so use it when many enemies crowd in.
- Archer's Mark Weakness (R) increases the damage that the marked enemy takes from everyone by 50% for 6 seconds. It's most effective when used on Elites or bosses, timed with big skills from other roles.
- Priest's Heal (Q) restores 35 with a 7-second cooldown, and Light of Rebirth (R) has a 50-second cooldown. A fallen ally must be revived within 20 seconds, so when Light of Rebirth can't be used, another ally holds F for 1.6 seconds.
- Squire's Trap (E) binds an enemy for 2.5 seconds and deals 40 damage, and the Squire is not hurt by floor traps. The Shield Skeleton takes 70% less damage from the front, but Piercing Arrow (Archer Q) still hits fully, so use Piercing Arrow or attacks from the side and rear against Shield Skeletons.

## Boss Fights
- Bosses change phases at 60% and 30% health, and from phase 2 they summon minions. Save big skills and combined skills right before phase 2 to clear minions more easily. The bosses of chapters 6~8 switch to phase 4 at 12% and summon 4 minions at a time.
- Bosses only chase people inside their room. If you keep a campfire lit, when everyone falls you restart from the last campfire you lit. If you finish the fight within 3 minutes after entering the boss room, you also earn an achievement.
- A person carrying the banner cannot dodge, attack, or use skills, and enemies target them first. Put the banner down before entering the boss room, or have the safest ally carry it while another ally protects them.

## Gathering Honor
- The fixed rewards you can collect in every chapter are: 2 puzzles (60), 2 secret room entrances (40), 2 secret room chests (120), 2 regular chests (50), altars (20~30), elevator (20), pillar bridge (20), fork mid-boss (30), and boss (90). Mimics give an extra 40 in every chapter except chapter 2.
- The Path of Honor blessing increases honor earned by 25%, so it's advantageous on expeditions where you want to buy gear or cosmetics from altars. Gear raises weapons and armor separately, so the level and gear of one role do not carry over to another role.

## Abyss and Weekly Expeditions
- In the Abyss, curses that accumulate stack on one another. The Dry Well multiplies healing received down by 25% per stack, and the Heavy Hand increases skill cooldowns by 15% per stack, so when the same curses repeat, teams focused on priests and skills struggle first.
- Weekly expeditions compete on time for the same chapter and curse, so choose blessings to match that week's curse. For example, when Dry Well is present, blessings that don't depend on healing, such as Sturdy Armor or Last Stand, are useful.

isleport/research.b:
:: Category = Research guide
:: Researches = 32
:: Cheapest = Sturdy boots (150 gold)
:: Most expensive = Exclusive deals (20,000 gold)
:: Total cost = 90,750 gold
:: See also = **Getting Started**, **Farming and Ranch**, **Crafting and Selling**, **Sailing and Islands**, **Ranks and Bank**, **Strategy**

Research is a list of upgrades bought one at a time with gold. A research with a prerequisite can only be taken after that one, and a finished research is permanent. The descriptions below are the same sentences shown in the in-game research window.

## Farming
- **Sturdy plow** (200 gold): Crops grow 10% faster
- **Fertilizer** (600 gold · requires Sturdy plow): Crops grow another 10% faster
- **Bumper harvest** (1,500 gold · requires Fertilizer): +1 per harvest
- **Greenhouse** (2,500 gold · requires Fertilizer): Crops grow almost normally in winter
- **Sprinklers** (4,000 gold · requires Greenhouse): Crops grow 12% faster
- **Auto-sowing** (300 gold): Unlocks replant after harvest. Open a growing field and switch on Replant (or Replant in every field): each harvest then re-sows by itself using one seed
- **Sow all** (250 gold · requires Sturdy plow): Unlocks "Plant in all empty fields" in the field menu
- **Reap all** (800 gold · requires Sow all): Unlocks "Collect all" at the barn and with the H key
- **Endless seeds** (15,000 gold · requires Overseer): Seeds never run out. Plant any unlocked crop without buying seeds

## Ranch
- **Better feed** (400 gold): Animals produce 15% faster
- **Larger pens** (1,200 gold · requires Better feed): +1 output per cycle

## Crafting
- **Quick hands** (500 gold): Crafting 15% faster
- **Mastery** (1,500 gold · requires Quick hands): Crafting another 15% faster
- **Conveyor belts** (5,000 gold · requires Mastery): Workshops 20% faster
- **Auto feed** (1,000 gold · requires Quick hands): Buildings pull ingredients from the warehouse by themselves, so wheat to flour to bread chains on its own
- **Auto carry** (1,800 gold · requires Auto feed): Finished goods go to the warehouse by themselves

## Sailing
- **Sturdy hulls** (800 gold): Ships 20% faster
- **Navigation** (2,500 gold · requires Sturdy hulls): Ships another 15% faster
- **Logistics** (9,000 gold · requires Navigation): Ships another 15% faster
- **Bigger holds** (1,800 gold · requires Sturdy hulls): Ships carry 20% more
- **Escort drills** (1,400 gold): 15% better against pirates

## Selling
- **Haggling** (700 gold): +5% when selling
- **Big spender** (3,000 gold · requires Haggling): +5% when selling
- **Exclusive deals** (20,000 gold · requires Big spender): +5% when selling
- **Contract broker** (2,000 gold · requires Haggling): Contract rewards +25%
- **Market intel** (900 gold): Shows price trends

## Movement, storage, workers
- **Sturdy boots** (150 gold): Walk 25% faster
- **Big basket** (450 gold · requires Sturdy boots): Collect crops and goods from nearby without stepping on them
- **Big barn** (800 gold): +40 storage per good
- **Hire workers** (1,200 gold · requires Big basket): Hire workers at home. They harvest by themselves
- **Overseer** (3,500 gold · requires Hire workers): Workers replant what they harvest
- **Tractor** (6,000 gold · requires Overseer): Workers work 50% faster

## How effects stack
- Crop growth: Sturdy plow x0.9, Fertilizer x0.9 and Sprinklers x0.88 multiply together, so all three bring growth time to about 0.71 of normal. Greenhouse cuts the winter slowdown to a quarter, so a winter factor of 1.6 becomes 1.15.
- Crafting time: Quick hands x0.85, Mastery x0.85 and Conveyor belts x0.8 also multiply, so all three give about 0.58 of the crafting time. The building level speed (level 2 x1.4, level 3 x2) is applied on top.
- Ship speed: Sturdy hulls +20%, Navigation +15% and Logistics +15% add up. Each lighthouse level +6%, the Harbor lantern project +12%, the Flavors of far seas museum set +3% and navigator crew go into the same sum.
- Sale bonuses: Haggling, Big spender and Exclusive deals add 5% each. They are summed with the other bonuses such as reputation, the guild and codex tier, and applied as one multiplier. The full list is in the Ranks and Bank page.

Buildings go on the town lots and turn ingredients into processed goods. This page collects, straight from the code tables, each building's cost, required rank, how it is unlocked and every recipe. Base prices of goods are on the Crops and Goods Prices page.

## Rules
- Construction takes (15 + build cost / 12) seconds. A level-up takes the base construction time x 0.6 x the new level, and the building cannot be used while under construction.
- Higher building levels raise crafting speed to x1.4 at level 2 and x2 at level 3. With the right research a building fetches its own ingredients, otherwise you pick the recipe by hand and take the finished goods out.
- Without auto carry, a building holds at most 12 finished goods and stops crafting when it is full.
- The lot must be open to build. A building whose rank is too high or that is not unlocked appears locked in the list. Lots are opened in order from the front.

## Grain, dairy and baking
- **Mill**: build cost 100 gold, no rank needed, available from the start. Wheat ×2 → Flour (10 s) / Rice ×2 → Rice cake (12 s)
- **Bakery**: build cost 150 gold, no rank needed, available from the start. Flour ×2 → Bread (15 s) / Flour ×1 + Apple ×2 → Apple pie (20 s) / Flour ×1 + Egg ×2 → Cookies (18 s)
- **Dairy**: build cost 200 gold, from rank Hawker, available from the start. Milk ×2 → Cheese (25 s) / Milk ×2 → Butter (18 s) / Goat milk ×2 → Goat cheese (22 s)
- **Sugar mill**: build cost 280 gold, from rank Hawker, unlocked at Goldport for 300 gold. Sugarcane ×2 → Sugar (14 s)
- **Confectionery**: build cost 520 gold, from rank Merchant, unlocked at Redport for 1,400 gold. Sugar ×1 + Cocoa ×1 → Chocolate (22 s) / Flour ×1 + Sugar ×1 + Egg ×1 → Cake (28 s) / Sugar ×1 + Strawberry ×1 → Candy ×2 (16 s) / Egg ×2 + Milk ×1 + Sugar ×1 → Pudding (24 s)
- **Kitchen**: build cost 380 gold, from rank Merchant, unlocked at Redport for 600 gold. Apple ×2 → Apple jam (15 s) / Tomato ×2 + Salt ×1 → Tomato sauce (15 s) / Flour ×1 + Tomato ×1 + Cheese ×1 → Pizza (25 s) / Potato ×2 + Spice ×1 → Spiced stew (25 s) / Flour ×2 + Egg ×1 → Pasta (18 s) / Rice ×1 + Fish ×1 → Sushi (20 s) / Potato ×1 + Chili ×1 + Rice ×1 → Curry (26 s)

## Wine, oil, drinks and tea
- **Winery**: build cost 260 gold, from rank Hawker, unlocked at Lavender Port for 700 gold. Grapes ×2 → Wine (25 s)
- **Oil press**: build cost 240 gold, from rank Hawker, unlocked at Lavender Port for 600 gold. Olive ×2 → Olive oil (18 s)
- **Brewery**: build cost 480 gold, from rank Merchant, unlocked at Goldport for 900 gold. Rice ×3 → Rice wine (26 s) / Sugar ×2 → Rum (24 s) / Honey ×2 → Mead (22 s)
- **Tea house**: build cost 360 gold, from rank Hawker, unlocked at Cotton Port for 700 gold. Tea leaves ×2 → Green tea (16 s) / Lavender ×3 → Perfume (28 s)

## Cloth and jewels
- **Loom**: build cost 320 gold, from rank Hawker, unlocked at Cotton Port for 500 gold. Cotton ×2 → Cloth (25 s) / Wool ×2 → Cloth (25 s)
- **Tailor**: build cost 450 gold, from rank Merchant, unlocked at Cotton Port for 1,100 gold. Cloth ×2 → Clothes (30 s) / Cloth ×1 + Silk ×1 → Silk dress (40 s)
- **Dyeworks**: build cost 650 gold, from rank Big merchant, unlocked at Spiceport for 1,800 gold. Dye ×1 + Cloth ×1 → Dyed cloth (22 s) / Dyed cloth ×1 + Silk ×1 → Silk hanbok (36 s)
- **Jeweler**: build cost 1,200 gold, from rank Tycoon, unlocked at Spiceport for 3,500 gold. Pearl ×1 + Cloth ×1 → Pearl necklace (40 s)

## Meat and fish
- **Cannery**: build cost 300 gold, from rank Merchant, unlocked at Salt Bay for 700 gold. Fish ×2 + Salt ×1 → Canned fish (20 s)
- **Smokehouse**: build cost 420 gold, from rank Merchant, unlocked at Salt Bay for 1,000 gold. Pork ×2 + Salt ×1 → Ham (24 s) / Fish ×2 + Salt ×1 → Smoked fish (18 s)

## Utility buildings
- **Warehouse**: build cost 300 gold, no rank needed, available from the start.
- **Lighthouse**: build cost 500 gold, from rank Hawker, available from the start.
- **Stall**: build cost 220 gold, no rank needed, available from the start.
- **Shipyard**: build cost 700 gold, from rank Hawker, available from the start.

## Utility building numbers
- Warehouse: the per-good storage is 30 by default, +50 per building level, +40 from the Big barn research and +25 per Expand warehouse purchase (up to 10). The building description says 60 but the calculation uses 50. Expanding costs 120 gold at first and is multiplied by 1.6 each time.
- Lighthouse: every level raises the speed of all ships by 6%.
- Stall: sells one unit of the chosen good every (6 s / level) at 90% of its base price. From level 2 each level adds another 10% to the price.
- Shipyard: every level cuts ship prices by 8%. The merchant ship needs level 1 and the galleon level 2. A sloop costs 50% more for each ship you already own beyond the first.

This page collects, as in the code tables, the growth time, yield, seed price, base price, season factors and unlock condition of the 23 crops, plus base prices of ranch products, imports and processed goods. The base price is the starting point for port and market price calculations.

## How to read
- Growth time is the base value before season factors and research. Season factors are listed spring/summer/autumn/winter and are time multipliers, so a value above 1 means slower growth in that season.
- Tree crops keep bearing after one planting, and every tree crop except strawberry takes twice the growth time. The yield goes up by 1 with the Bumper harvest research.
- The seed price is the cost of one seed at the seed shop. The base price is the value of one harvested crop, and the market pays 65% of it.
