isleport/ports.b:
:: Category = Trade guide
:: Ports = 6
:: Inland regions = 3 (by train)
:: Price drop on selling = ×0.975 per unit sold
:: Buying price = 1.2x market price, ×1.02 per unit
:: See also = **Sailing and Islands**, **Crops and Goods Price List**, **Ranks and Bank**, **Buildings and Processed Food**, **Strategy**

This gathers the trade conditions of the six ports and three inland regions, the calculation that sets prices, port news, contracts, and the stats for pirates and crew. Sailing methods and ship types are in the Sailing and Islands document.

## Goldport
A breadbasket port where wheat and potatoes are plentiful. No rank requirement, about 24 seconds one way by sailboat.
- Goods sold cheap here (low price when you sell here, cheap when you buy them here): Wheat, potatoes, corn, carrots, rice, sugarcane
- Goods it buys at a high price: Bread, wine, cloth, ham, dyed cloth, seaweed
- Goods the port sells (you can bring them back by ship): Wheat, corn, salt, rice, carrots, golden barley

## Redport
A port with many apple orchards. No rank requirement, about 44 seconds one way by sailboat.
- Goods sold cheap here (low price when you sell here, cheap when you buy them here): Apples, tomatoes, pumpkins, strawberries, peppers
- Goods it buys at a high price: Wheat, cheese, cloth, chocolate, honey mead, saffron
- Goods the port sells (you can bring them back by ship): Apples, tomatoes, strawberries, peppers, pomegranates

## Lavenderport
A port known for vineyards and wine. Available from the Peddler rank, about 34 seconds one way by sailboat.
- Goods sold cheap here (low price when you sell here, cheap when you buy them here): Grapes, olives, wine, lavender, cacao, rum
- Goods it buys at a high price: Potatoes, pizza, coffee beans, perfume, sushi, cloud cotton, coral, amber
- Goods the port sells (you can bring them back by ship): Grapes, olives, lavender, dye, saffron

## Cottonport
A port with cotton fields and a cloth market. Available from the Peddler rank, about 16 seconds one way by sailboat.
- Goods sold cheap here (low price when you sell here, cheap when you buy them here): Cotton, wool, cloth, tea leaves, honey
- Goods it buys at a high price: Bread, apple jam, olive oil, candy, goat cheese, cookies, dragon fruit
- Goods the port sells (you can bring them back by ship): Cotton, wool, tea leaves, honey, cloud cotton

## Salt Bay
A fishing village that pays high prices for grain. Available from the Merchant rank, about 23 seconds one way by sailboat.
- Goods sold cheap here (low price when you sell here, cheap when you buy them here): Fish, canned fish, salt, pork
- Goods it buys at a high price: Wheat, potatoes, apple pie, curry, sake, golden barley
- Goods the port sells (you can bring them back by ship): Fish, salt, pearls, pork, seaweed

## Spiceport
A trading harbor on distant seas, where rare imports come in. Available from the Great Merchant rank, about 59 seconds one way by sailboat.
- Goods sold cheap here (low price when you sell here, cheap when you buy them here): Spices, silk, coffee beans, salt, vanilla
- Goods it buys at a high price: Clothes, silk clothes, cheese, pizza, spice stew, pearl necklaces, silk hanbok, perfume, chocolate, pudding, pomegranates, old pottery, amber
- Goods the port sells (you can bring them back by ship): Spices, silk, coffee beans, salt, vanilla, pearls, dragon fruit

## How Prices Are Set
- The market price is the base price of the good × port multiplier × demand × seasonal multiplier. Port multipliers are 0.72~0.78 for goods sold cheap there, 1.3~1.4 for goods it buys at a high price, and 0.92~1.12 for the rest, and they are set per port and per good.
- Demand starts at 1. If you sell n units at a port, demand drops by ×0.975 to the power of n, down to a minimum of 0.35. If you buy n units there, it rises by ×1.02 to the power of n, up to a maximum of 1.8. Demand returns toward 1 by 1% of the difference every second (2% after the market expansion project).
- When selling, the first unit sells at the market price, and each later unit is worth ×0.975 of the previous one, all added together (×0.982 after the market expansion project), and the total is multiplied by the sale multiplier. The more you sell at once, the lower the average price, so spreading shipments across several ports and goods loses less value.
- The buying price starts at 1.2x the market price and rises by ×1.02 per unit. On the same route, a ship can select goods to buy at the port it sells at.

## Port News
- A new news item comes up every 70~150 seconds, and it lasts 90 seconds. It appears at one of the ports you can reach, and the types are Bountiful Harvest, Festival, and Storm at 28% each, and Plague Rumor at 16%.
- When demand concentrates, that good's market price becomes ×1.6. A festival raises every good's price to ×1.2, and a storm makes travel time to that port ×1.5 and the ship's hull loses 10~20 points when departing.
- Cargo bought at a port with a plague rumor cannot be stored in the warehouse right away when it arrives and is held in quarantine. Quarantine lasts 150 seconds, and building a port quarantine station for 1,500 gold reduces it to 50 seconds.
- Each news item also affects stocks. Demand concentration raises related stocks by 7%, a festival raises the Trade Company by 5%, and a storm lowers the Fishers' Cooperative by 6%.

## Flow of One Voyage
- A ship loads cargo at a port, departs, sells and buys on arrival, and then returns. Travel time is distance ÷ (ship speed × modifier), and the return trip takes 0.9x that time. Sailboat speed is 3.6, merchant ship 3.2, and galleon 3.0.
- In the ship list, cargo holds can be upgraded to level 3 (250, 600, and 1,300 gold, +25% per level). Escorts also go up to level 3 at 200, 500, and 1,000 gold. The galleon starts with the level 1 escort share.
- The chance of meeting pirates on a voyage is 14% × (1 - 0.2 × escort) (minimum 0.2x, and if you carry no cargo, back up to 0.4x), and they appear at 35~65% of the way along the route.
- The chance of repelling pirates increases by 25% per escort level, 15% for Escort Training research, and 10% for a Gunner crew member. A win costs 5 hull points, gives a bounty of 80~299 gold, and has a 35% chance of a map fragment. A loss costs 15~25 hull points, 25% of the cargo is taken, and Trade Company stock drops by 4%.
- If you have trade insurance, you get back 70% of the cargo value that was taken. The premium is 5% of the total value of the ships you own, and it is valid for 10 minutes.

## Contracts and Reputation
- Contracts appear one at a time every 70~120 seconds, and up to 4 + rank-level contracts can accumulate at once. One of the ports you can reach requests them, and only goods already recorded in your catalog appear (imports excluded).
- Reward equals market price × quantity × 1.45~1.85, and processed-goods contracts pay 1.9~2.4x (×1.25 with the Contract Expert research). The deadline is 4 + quantity ÷ 5 minutes for regular contracts, and 7 + quantity × 1.5 minutes for processed-goods contracts.
- When a ship arrives at that port, contracts with enough cargo are filled automatically, in order. Filling one raises reputation by 3, and there is a 20% chance of a map fragment.
- Reputation builds up separately for each port. It rises by 1 every time you arrive there to sell, and the reputation level is the square root of (reputation ÷ 3), rounded down (max 10). Each level adds +1.5% to sales.

## Crew
- **Navigator**: Ships are 5% faster. Wages per minute: Diligent 4, Greedy 8, Lucky 5
- **Gunner**: Blocks pirates 10% better. Wages per minute: Diligent 5, Greedy 10, Lucky 7
- **Porter**: Cargo space increases by 7%. Wages per minute: Diligent 4, Greedy 9, Lucky 6
- **Trader**: Earns 1.5% more when selling. Wages per minute: Diligent 3, Greedy 5, Lucky 4
- The wages and effects differ among the three personalities. Diligent has wages ×0.75 with effects ×1, Greedy has wages ×1.5 with effects ×1.6, and Lucky has wages ×1 with effects ×1.2. The wage numbers above include this multiplier, and the personality order is Diligent, Greedy, Lucky.
- The hiring cost is 120 × (current crew + 1) gold, and the maximum crew is 2 + 2 × the ship's level (max 10). Wages are paid all at once every minute, and if you lack the money, every crew member's effect stops until wages are paid.

## Three Inland Regions
- **Bluehills Plateau** (from the Peddler rank, train fare 30 gold): A high pasture full of sheep and grass. It buys bread, wine, cloth, salt, and apple pie at a high price, and its specialty goods sold cheap are milk, cheese, wool, goat cheese, and butter.
- **Pinewood Village** (from the Merchant rank, train fare 60 gold): A quiet lumberjack village in a pine forest. It buys salt, tea leaves, coffee beans, canned fish, and apple jam at a high price, and its specialty goods sold cheap are honey, honey mead, pork, and ham.
- **Redridge Post Station** (from the Great Merchant rank, train fare 100 gold): A post station village below red rocky mountains. It buys bread, wine, canned fish, cheese, and clothes at a high price, and its specialty goods sold cheap are salt, amber, curry, and spice stew.
- The buying price at regional markets is the base price × 1.35 (goods wanted), × 1.05 (other goods), or × 0.8 (the region's specialty), multiplied by the sale multiplier and demand. When selling at once, the price drops 1.5% per unit (up to 20 units' worth), and demand falls ×0.97 per unit sold and recovers slowly. The buying price for specialty goods is 0.8x the base price.

isleport/economy.b:
:: Category = Money and rank guide
:: Ranks = 7 levels (raised by total income earned)
:: Loan interest = 1% per minute
:: Deposit interest = 0.2% per minute
:: Stocks = 6 companies, prices move every 8 seconds
:: Guide tasks = 17 (see the reward total below)
:: See also = **Getting Started**, **Ports and Trade**, **Processing and Selling**, **Research List**, **Town Facilities**, **Strategy**

This gathers the figures for ranks, bank deposits and loans, insurance, stocks, the items that add to the sales multiplier, guide tasks, and the construction projects that are built together. Your rank is set by the total gold you have earned so far, and it does not go down even if you spend or lose gold.

## Seven Ranks
- **Stall Vendor** (from the start): Loan limit 500 gold, deposit interest applies up to 1,500 gold. Unlocked at this rank: Goldport, Redport, Mill, Bakery, Warehouse, Stall
- **Peddler** (from 2,000 total income): Loan limit 1,500 gold, deposit interest applies up to 4,500 gold. Unlocked at this rank: Lavenderport, Cottonport, Bluehills Plateau, Dairy Workshop, Wine Cellar, Oil Press, Clothmaker, Lighthouse, Sugar Mill, Tea Plantation, Shipyard
- **Merchant** (from 10,000 total income): Loan limit 5,000 gold, deposit interest applies up to 15,000 gold. Unlocked at this rank: Salt Bay, Pinewood Village, Tailor, Kitchen, Cannery, Confectionery, Smokehouse, Brewery
- **Great Merchant** (from 40,000 total income): Loan limit 15,000 gold, deposit interest applies up to 45,000 gold. Unlocked at this rank: Spiceport, Redridge Post Station, Dye Workshop
- **Tycoon** (from 150,000 total income): Loan limit 50,000 gold, deposit interest applies up to 150,000 gold. Unlocked at this rank: Jeweler's Workshop
- **Grand Magnate** (from 500,000 total income): Loan limit 150,000 gold, deposit interest applies up to 450,000 gold
- **Sea Magnate** (from 2,000,000 total income): Loan limit 500,000 gold, deposit interest applies up to 1,500,000 gold

## Bank
- Deposits can be withdrawn at any time. Deposit interest of 0.2% is added every minute on the amount within the limit. The limit is 3 times the loan limit of your rank.
- Loans accrue 1% interest every minute on the outstanding debt. Borrowed money keeps growing until it is repaid, so it's expensive to borrow up to the limit and leave it.
- Trade insurance costs 5% of the total value of the ships you own and is valid for 10 minutes. If pirates take your cargo, 70% of its value is refunded. If auto-renewal is on, it is bought again at expiry when you have more than 3 times the premium in gold.

## Six Stocks
- **Grain Cooperative**: Base price 60 gold, volatility 3.5%. Goods moved by port news: wheat, potatoes, corn, carrots, rice, sugarcane, flour, bread
- **Orchard Company**: Base price 80 gold, volatility 4%. Goods moved by port news: apples, tomatoes, pumpkins, strawberries, peppers, olives, apple pie, apple jam, tomato sauce, olive oil
- **Winery**: Base price 120 gold, volatility 5%. Goods moved by port news: grapes, wine, rum, honey mead, sake
- **Textile Workshop**: Base price 70 gold, volatility 4%. Goods moved by port news: cotton, wool, cloth, clothes, silk clothes, silk, dyed cloth, silk hanbok, cloud cotton
- **Fishers' Cooperative**: Base price 50 gold, volatility 4.5%. Goods moved by port news: fish, canned fish, sushi, pearls, seaweed, coral
- **Trade Company**: Base price 150 gold, volatility 6%. All other goods not in the five companies above belong to this company
- Prices move once every 8 seconds. They rise and fall at random, drift gradually toward the base price, and never leave the range of 0.35x to 3x the base price. A 1% fee is deducted from the value when you sell.
- The price newspaper sold at the village newsstand for 3 gold gets a new edition every 3 minutes. Each edition carries predictions for 3 companies, and prices lean toward the predicted direction for 3 minutes. The prediction turns out correct 75% of the time. Results of the previous edition's predictions are also printed.

## What Adds to the Sales Multiplier
The multiplier when selling at a port is 1 plus all of the following.
- Port reputation: +1.5% per level (up to level 10, +15%)
- Research: Haggling, Big Spender, and Exclusive Contract each +5%
- Catalog rank: +0.4% per 10 kinds of goods in the catalog
- Merchant guild: Apprentice +1%, Member +2%, Expert +3%, Honored +5%
- Trader crew: +1.5% per person, multiplied by the personality multiplier
- Built-together projects: Trade Fair +5%, Island Museum Specialty Set +2%, story ending that grows the company +3%
Once the Market Expansion project is finished, the amount deducted per unit when selling in bulk is smaller (from 0.975 to 0.982). Net worth is gold + half of the money spent on buildings, land, and ships - debt + deposits + stocks + the base value of goods in warehouses and on ships.

## 17 Guide Tasks
The ★ tasks at the top come up one at a time in order, and the reward is paid as soon as the condition is met.
- 1. Plant any crop once: 50 gold
- 2. Harvest 10 crops: 80 gold
- 3. Sell goods at the market: 60 gold
- 4. Buy seeds at the seed shop: 60 gold
- 5. Send a ship out once: 100 gold
- 6. Build a mill in the village: 150 gold
- 7. Make 5 loaves of bread: 200 gold
- 8. Expand your field to 12 tiles: 250 gold
- 9. Build a chicken coop at the ranch: 300 gold
- 10. Fill one port contract: 400 gold
- 11. Finish one research: 500 gold
- 12. Become a Merchant: 800 gold
- 13. Visit four ports: 1,000 gold
- 14. Accumulate 50,000 gold in net worth: 3,000 gold
- 15. Expand your field to 24 tiles: 4,000 gold
- 16. Hire one worker: 6,000 gold
- 17. Make 15 different kinds of processed goods: 9,000 gold
The total of all rewards is 25,950 gold.

## 4 Built-Together Projects
In a room connected with other islands, everyone donates gold or goods (converted at base price) to fill them.
- **Harbor Lantern**: Goal 3,000. Everyone's ships are 12% faster
- **Market Expansion**: Goal 8,000. Prices recover faster after selling and drop less
- **Trade Fair**: Goal 20,000. Everyone earns 5% more when selling
- **Grand Voyage Fleet**: Goal 50,000. All ship cargo holds grow by 15%

isleport/achievements.b:
:: Category = Achievement guide

The names and conditions of the 113 achievements are grouped by topic in the order they appear in the code. When a condition is met, the achievement is earned automatically within 1 second and a notification appears. The names and condition sentences match the in-game display.

## Farming and Fields
- **First Harvest**: Harvest a crop for the first time
- **Farmer**: Harvest 100 crops
- **Great Farmer**: Harvest 1,000 crops
- **Master of Abundance**: Harvest 5,000 crops
- **All Crops**: Harvest all of the first nine crops
- **16 Tiles**: Expand the field to 16 tiles
- **24 Tiles**: Expand the field to 24 tiles
- **Orchard**: Raise 6 fruit trees
- **Endless Field**: Open all field tiles up to 48
- **Crop Doctor**: Harvest all seventeen crops
- **Ranch Tycoon**: Fill all 12 pens

## Sales, Gold, and Rank
- **First Sale**: Sell at a port for the first time
- **Big Deal**: Sell more than 1,000 gold in one go
- **Jackpot**: Sell more than 5,000 gold in one go
- **Mega Jackpot**: Sell more than 20,000 gold in one go
- **Ten Thousand Gold**: Total income of 10,000
- **One Hundred Thousand Gold**: Total income of 100,000
- **One Million Gold**: Total income of 1,000,000
- **Full Vault**: Accumulate 10,000 gold
- **Two Vaults**: Accumulate 100,000 gold
- **Peddler**: Reach the Peddler rank
- **Merchant**: Reach the Merchant rank
- **Great Merchant**: Reach the Great Merchant rank
- **Tycoon**: Reach the Tycoon rank
- **Grand Magnate**: Reach the Grand Magnate rank
- **Sea Magnate**: Reach the highest rank
- **Multimillionaire**: Accumulate a net worth of 10,000,000
- **Millionaire**: Accumulate a net worth of 1,000,000

## Processing and Orders
- **First Bread**: Make bread
- **First Wine**: Make wine
- **First Cloth**: Make cloth
- **First Cheese**: Make cheese
- **Pizza Party**: Make pizza
- **Silk Clothes**: Make silk clothes
- **Spice Stew**: Make spice stew
- **Twenty Kinds**: Make 20 different processed goods
- **Workshop Owner**: Make 500 processed goods
- **Factory Chief**: Make 3,000 processed goods
- **Workshop Order**: Fill one processed goods order
- **Order Master**: Fill 10 processed goods orders

## Ranch
- **Chicken Coop**: Build a chicken coop
- **Small Ranch**: Open 4 pens
- **Big Ranch**: Fill 9 pens
- **Top-Grade Pen**: Upgrade a pen to level 3
- **Animal Friends**: Build pens for all four kinds

## Village, Workers, and Decoration
- **Small Village**: Build 6 buildings
- **Busy Village**: Build 12 buildings
- **Master Craftsman's Workshop**: Upgrade a building to level 3
- **Street Vendor**: Open a stall
- **Lighthouse Keeper**: Build a lighthouse
- **Large Village**: Build 16 buildings
- **First Worker**: Hire one worker
- **Six Workers**: Hire 6 workers
- **Great Farm**: Hire 12 workers
- **Island Decorator**: Place 10 decorative items
- **Picturesque Island**: Place 40 decorative items
- **Fountain Island**: Place a fountain
- **Open for Business**: Receive the first customer at your shop
- **Local Favorite**: Sell 200 goods at your shop
- **Shared Order**: Fill one large village order
- **Order Solver**: Fill 10 large village orders

## Ships, Sailing, and Crew
- **Fleet**: Own 2 ships
- **Large Fleet**: Own 4 ships
- **Armada**: Own 8 ships
- **Merchant Ship**: Buy a merchant ship
- **Galleon**: Buy a galleon
- **Big Hold**: Upgrade a ship's cargo hold
- **Escort Ship**: Add an escort
- **Navigator**: Visit all six ports
- **Distant Seas**: Visit Spiceport
- **Importer**: Buy imported goods and return
- **Big Customer**: Buy 200 goods at ports
- **First Contract**: Fill one contract
- **Trustworthy Merchant**: Fill 10 contracts
- **Contract King**: Fill 50 contracts
- **Regular**: Build 5 reputation levels with one port
- **Hands-On Trade**: Go to a port by ship and sell in person
- **First Crew**: Hire one crew member
- **Six Crew**: Hire 6 crew members
- **Map in a Bottle**: Pick up a map fragment for the first time
- **Secret Island**: Discover one secret island
- **Sea Explorer**: Discover all three secret islands

## Research, Bank, and Catalog
- **Research Begins**: Finish one research
- **Scholar**: Finish 8 researches
- **All Research**: Finish all research
- **First Loan**: Borrow money from the bank
- **Debt Free**: Repay all borrowed money
- **Forty Kinds of Goods**: Hold 40 different kinds of goods
- **Specialty of Each Island**: Harvest the specialty crops of all six islands
- **Catalog Grade 3**: Reach catalog grade 3
- **Catalog Grade 6**: Reach catalog grade 6

## Seasons, Events, and Guide
- **Welcoming Guests**: Sell to a visiting merchant
- **Pirate Encounter**: Meet a pirate
- **Pirate Repelled**: Repel a pirate with an escort
- **Surviving Winter**: Get through one winter
- **One Year**: Experience all four seasons
- **End of the Guide**: Finish all guide tasks

## Playing Together
- **Play Together**: Connect with another player
- **Dealmaker**: Trade with another company
- **Sharing Hearts**: Give a gift to another company
- **Sea Pirate King**: Successfully raid another ship

## Things to Know
- Six Workers and Six Crew share a single achievement record. Because only one record remains, if the condition for one is met first and recorded, the other is not earned separately.
- The achievement for finishing all research is based on all the research currently available, not the number of research items completed.

isleport/town.b:
:: Category = Town facility guide
:: Facilities = Restaurant, Museum, Aquarium, Tavern, Eatery Row and Bakery, Post Office, Merchant Guild, Lodging, Real Estate, Festivals, Hall Challenges, Back Hill
:: Challenges = 3 at the same time, 15-minute limit
:: Real estate = 8 plots of land, 3 building types
:: See also = **Story and Residents**, **Processing and Selling**, **Ranks and Bank**, **Mine Isle and Volcanic Isle**, **Strategy**

This gathers how the facilities in town and around the island create money and rewards, along with the money and time needed and the figures for each level. The basic explanations are in the Getting Started and Processing and Selling documents.

## Restaurant
At the restaurant, you make dishes from ingredients in the warehouse, and customers take the ordered dishes and pay you. Each dish takes 5 seconds, one at a time.
- **Baked Potato**: Potatoes ×2, base value 55 gold
- **Corn Soup**: Corn ×2 + milk ×1, base value 110 gold
- **Tomato Stew**: Tomatoes ×2 + salt ×1, base value 125 gold
- **Grilled Fish**: Fish ×2 + salt ×1, base value 105 gold
- **Pumpkin Pie**: Pumpkins ×2 + flour ×1 + eggs ×1, base value 220 gold
- **Wine Course**: Wine ×1 + bread ×1 + cheese ×1, base value 485 gold
- Each restaurant level unlocks 2 more dishes you can make (level 1: 2, level 2: 4, level 3: 6). The costs to upgrade are 800 gold and 3,000 gold.
- The dish price is 1.7x the total base price of the ingredients, rounded to units of 5, plus 1% for each point of reputation (up to 30%). If you have the Artisan's Skill set in the museum, another 10% is added. Customers may also add a tip of up to 20%.
- Customers arrive roughly every (60 - reputation) seconds (reputation taken into account up to 30), and up to 2 + level orders can pile up at once. An order that isn't delivered within 150 seconds disappears and costs 1 reputation. Delivering a dish gives +1 reputation, and reputation ranges from 0 to 30.
- After 5 servings, a food critic sometimes visits and orders one dish. If you deliver it within 2 minutes, you receive 2~6x the dish price depending on a 1~5 star rating, and reputation goes up or down. If you fail to deliver, reputation drops by 3.

## Museum
The museum displays goods from your warehouse. Each exhibit adds an admission fee of 0.5 gold per minute (1.5x if you donated the ledger in the story), and the accumulated money must be collected by you. Once an item is displayed, you cannot take it back. Completing a set grants a permanent bonus.
- **Treasures of the Sea** (4): Pearls, coral, seaweed, amber. Bonus: Treasure chests are caught twice as often while fishing
- **Island Specialties** (5): Golden barley, pomegranates, saffron, cloud cotton, dragon fruit. Bonus: All sale prices rise by 2%
- **Flavors of Distant Seas** (5): Spices, coffee beans, silk, vanilla, salt. Bonus: Ships are 3% faster
- **Artisan's Skill** (5): Bread, cheese, wine, cloth, apple pie. Bonus: Restaurant dish prices +10%, customers wait longer

## Aquarium and Fishing
At the ranch's fishing spot, choose to fish and the fishing game starts. You cast the line, and after 1.5~4 seconds a bite comes. Hit at the moment the moving marker reaches the center within 4.4 seconds. Pressing in the yellow center zone is a perfect catch, which doubles the harvest.
- Weights of what you catch: Fish 60, seaweed 12 (+8 in spring), coral 3 (+6 in summer), pearls 2 (+3 on rainy days), old boots 12, treasure chest 1.5. A perfect catch doubles the weights of pearls and treasure chests, and if you have the Treasures of the Sea set in the museum, the treasure chest weight doubles again.
- Old boots give 6 gold as scrap value (12 if perfect), and treasure chests give 120~320 gold right away (double if perfect). When you catch a fish, one of the 14 aquarium species below is caught with it.
- The aquarium starts with 5 tanks, becomes level 2 (9 tanks) for 600 gold, and level 3 (14 tanks) for 1,800 gold. The total value of the species on display × 0.5 × (1 + 0.3 × (level - 1)) accumulates as admission every minute, and the cap on accumulated money is level × 300 gold.
- **Crucian Carp**: Value 2, weight 30
- **Carp**: Value 3, weight 24
- **Trout**: Value 4, weight 16 (spring, autumn, winter)
- **Sea Bream**: Value 5, weight 14
- **Flounder**: Value 6, weight 12
- **Pufferfish**: Value 7, weight 10 (summer, autumn)
- **Clownfish**: Value 9, weight 7 (summer, spring)
- **Blue Tang**: Value 10, weight 6 (summer, autumn)
- **Seahorse**: Value 14, weight 4
- **Stingray**: Value 16, weight 3.5
- **Moonlight Jellyfish**: Value 20, weight 2.5 (night only)
- **Brocade Koi**: Value 24, weight 2
- **Sea Turtle**: Value 30, weight 1.2 (summer, autumn)
- **Golden Koi**: Value 40, weight 0.8
The first time you catch a species, you receive a bonus of 10 times its value in gold. The weight is the relative chance of being caught, and species with a season or night condition are caught only at those times.

## Tavern
A drink costs 12 gold, and you must rest 12 seconds before buying the next one. Rumors are chosen by chance: map fragment 5% (when you have fewer than 3 map fragments), current port news 30%, the price at the port that buys at the highest price right now 45%, and the rest are sailors' gossip.

## Eatery Row and Bakery
Both places create an order slip every 25 seconds (they stop when the slots are full), and orders are valid for 360 seconds. Orders are half dishes and half ingredients.
- **Eatery Row**: Dishes spicy stew, pizza, pasta, sushi, curry, bread, cheese, ham, smoked fish, canned fish, apple pie. Ingredients eggs, milk, potatoes, tomatoes, carrots, rice, pork, fish, spices, salt, tomato sauce, corn, peppers, wheat, flour.
- **Bakery**: Dishes bread, cake, cookies, apple pie, pudding, chocolate, candy, rice cake, apple jam. Ingredients flour, sugar, butter, eggs, milk, cacao, vanilla, honey, strawberries, apples.
- Dish orders ask for 1~3 items, and ingredient orders ask for 3~8 items. The reward is base price × quantity × 1.6 (dishes) or 1.25 (ingredients), plus 10 gold. Each delivery adds loyalty points, and the level goes up every 8 points (max level 5). Each level adds 4% to rewards, and one more order slot is added every 2 levels (starts with 3 slots).

## Post Office
- Delivery requests appear one at a time every 30 seconds (up to 3) and are valid for 480 seconds. The destination is one of the ports you can reach now or an inland region, and the request asks for 3~8 goods whose base price is between 10 and 300.
- The reward is base price × quantity × 1.5 + 20 gold, and the postage is 8% of the reward. After you send it, a reply comes back 90 seconds later. Every 10 deliveries reduces the wait by 10%, up to a maximum reduction of 50%. You must collect the reply yourself for the reward to be paid.

## Merchant Guild
- The membership fee is 500 gold. Once you join, a request appears every 40 seconds (up to 3) and is valid for 420 seconds. Requests ask for 4~11 goods with base prices from 6 to 300, and the reward is base price × quantity × 1.35. Contribution is the quantity ÷ 3, rounded, giving points (minimum 1).
- 0 contribution points is Apprentice, 30 points is Member, 90 points is Expert, and 200 points is Honored rank. Each rank raises the selling price at ports and regions by 1%, 2%, 3%, and 5%.

## Lodging
- Rooms come 2 per level (level 1: 2, level 2: 4, level 3: 6). The costs to upgrade are 800 gold and 2,400 gold.
- When a room is empty, a guest arrives every 28 seconds (every 20 seconds if you have ridden the train at least once). After staying 90~180 seconds, the lodging fee builds up. One night costs (14 + 7 × level) gold plus a bonus (up to 50%) based on the lodging reputation and the number of festival wins.
- If you deliver a dish you made at the restaurant to a guest, the guest eats and pays a tip of 1.5x the dish price. You must collect the lodging fees yourself for them to be added.

## Real Estate
Buy land and build on it, and rent accumulates. Rent is calculated by multiplying by a market index, which slowly moves up and down around 1, between about 0.87 and 1.13. When you sell land, you receive 70% of (land price + building cost), multiplied by the index.
- **1 Maple Street**: Land price 500 gold, no rank requirement
- **Empty Lot by Oak Square**: Land price 900 gold, no rank requirement
- **East Hill Plot**: Land price 1,500 gold, from the Peddler rank
- **Harbor Front Plot**: Land price 2,400 gold, from the Peddler rank
- **Market Back Alley Plot**: Land price 3,600 gold, from the Merchant rank
- **Lighthouse Side Plot**: Land price 5,200 gold, from the Great Merchant rank
- **Castle Road Plot**: Land price 7,500 gold, from the Tycoon rank
- **Central Avenue Large Plot**: Land price 10,000 gold, from the Grand Magnate rank
- **House**: Build cost 400 gold, rent 7 per minute
- **Shop**: Build cost 1,200 gold, rent 24 per minute
- **Mansion**: Build cost 4,000 gold, rent 85 per minute

## Seasonal Festivals
One festival is held each season, and you can enter once per season. You choose up to 3 goods that fit that festival, and your score is set by the total base price with a luck factor of 0.85~1.25x. You compete against 3 rivals, and places 1~3 win prizes.
- **Spring Flower Festival**: Lavender, honey, strawberries, apple jam, cake
- **Summer Seafood Cook-Off**: Canned fish, smoked fish, sushi, spice stew, curry
- **Autumn Harvest Festival**: Pumpkins, apples, corn, grapes, wine, apple pie
- **Winter Feast**: Spice stew, chocolate, honey mead, sake, cake, cloth
- Prizes are 400 + 150 × rank level for 1st place, 200 + 80 × rank level for 2nd, and 100 + 40 × rank level for 3rd. A rival's score is set by the sum of the three most expensive festival goods multiplied by (0.45 + 0.08 × rank level), so rivals grow stronger as your rank rises. The rivals are the baker Rosa, the farmer Hans, and the chef Michelle.

## Hall Challenges
Challenges run in 3 slots at the same time, and each slot draws one different type. A newly drawn challenge must be completed within 15 minutes, and when you complete it, collect the reward at the Hall. Target counts and rewards grow as your rank rises, except for Pirate Repelled, Fishing, and Clearing Land, whose targets are fixed.
- **Harvest 20 Crops**: Base target 20, base reward 60 gold
- **Sell 30 Goods**: Base target 30, base reward 80 gold
- **Earn 400 Gold**: Base target 400, base reward 100 gold
- **Send Ships 3 Times**: Base target 3, base reward 90 gold
- **Complete 2 Contracts**: Base target 2, base reward 120 gold
- **Plant 15 Crops**: Base target 15, base reward 50 gold
- **Repel a Pirate Once**: Base target 1, base reward 150 gold (fixed target)
- **Catch 5 Fish with a Line**: Base target 5, base reward 70 gold (fixed target)
- **See 100 Profit from Stocks**: Base target 100, base reward 110 gold
- **Clear 1 Plot on the Back Hill**: Base target 1, base reward 130 gold (fixed target)
For challenges that do not have a fixed target, the target is base target × (1 + 0.7 × rank level), and the reward is base reward × (1 + 0.9 × rank level). Your title rises with the number of rewards you've collected: 0 times New Merchant, 5 times Apprentice Challenger, 15 times Seasoned Challenger, 30 times Island Notable, 60 times Island Legend.

## Back Hill Clearing and Large Town Orders
- The Back Hill lets you open 12 more field tiles. The clearing cost is 300 × (1 + 0.7 × number already cleared) gold, and the time is 20 + 6 × number already cleared seconds, one site at a time. Once clearing is finished, it becomes a separate field outside the regular 48 tiles, and it counts for workers and for the "harvest all" task.
- Large town orders ask for a single processed good in bulk. The quantity is 12 + 6 × rank level + 8 × number of players, the reward is base price × quantity × 2.1~2.5, plus 10% for each additional player, and the deadline is 14 minutes. Rewards are split by each person's share of contributed quantity. When the order is complete or its deadline passes, a new order appears 45 seconds later.

isleport/story.b:
:: Category = Story guide
:: Story = 8 chapters, 2 endings
:: Story characters = Grandma Martha, Navigator Organ, Merchant Mira
:: Resident requests = 12 residents, 3 requests each
:: Map fragments = 1 secret island per 3 fragments (5 in total)
:: See also = **Getting Started**, **Sailing and Islands**, **Mines and Volcanic Islands**, **Town Facilities**, **Ranks and Bank**

The story from the Town Hall is eight chapters that follow a grandfather's old ledger. This document gathers what each chapter asks you to do and the rewards, the results of the choices, the requests of the twelve island residents, and how to get map fragments.

## Story: 8 Chapters
Above a story character's head, ! means a new story, … means in progress, and ? means the goal is complete. Once you talk to the character, hear the story, and receive the goal, the count begins from that point.
- Chapter 1 **The Old Ledger** (Grandma Martha): Goal: Harvest 20 crops. Reward 150 gold
- Chapter 2 **The Navigator's Request** (Navigator Organ): Goal: Send a ship out once. Reward 100 gold, 1 map fragment
- Chapter 3 **A Trustworthy Merchant** (Merchant Mira): Goal: Complete 2 contracts. Reward 200 gold
- Chapter 4 **The Lost Dawn Ship** (Navigator Organ): Goal: Reach rank 2 or higher. Reward 300 gold (starts from the Peddler rank or higher)
- Chapter 5 **A Tale Heard at Sea** (Merchant Mira): Goal: Land on three islands. Reward 400 gold
- Chapter 6 **Sail with Stars** (Grandma Martha): Goal: Discover one hidden island. Reward 500 gold
- Chapter 7 **Scattered Pieces** (Navigator Organ): Goal: Discover all three hidden islands. Reward 800 gold, 1 map fragment
- Chapter 8 **Master of the Company** (Merchant Mira): No goal (you choose an ending at the end). Reward 2,000 gold
- Choice in chapter 3: If you show the ledger, you receive 1 map fragment. If you keep it secret, you receive 150 gold more.
- The choice in chapter 8 is permanent. If you donate the ledger to the museum, museum admission goes up 1.5x. If you keep the ledger and grow the company, all sale prices rise by 3%. The game continues after the ending is chosen, and you can view the ending again at the Hall.

## Requests from the 12 Island Residents
Talk to a resident next to a landmark on the island to receive a request. You fulfill three requests in order for each resident, and the reward is 1.8x the total base price of the requested goods. When you fulfill the third request, they give you an old map (1 map fragment).
- **Miller Marco**: 1) Wheat ×15 (324 gold), 2) Bread ×4 (612 gold), 3) Potatoes ×20 (576 gold)
- **Orchardkeeper Ella**: 1) Apples ×12 (648 gold), 2) Apple jam ×3 (459 gold), 3) Apple pie ×2 (540 gold)
- **Winery Owner Vincent**: 1) Grapes ×15 (1,134 gold), 2) Wine ×2 (468 gold), 3) Olive oil ×3 (594 gold)
- **Shepherdess Nina**: 1) Wool ×8 (648 gold), 2) Cloth ×3 (675 gold), 3) Honey ×5, tea leaves ×5 (882 gold)
- **Fisherman Jose**: 1) Salt ×10 (324 gold), 2) Canned fish ×4 (684 gold), 3) Sushi ×2 (630 gold)
- **Spice Merchant Raji**: 1) Spices ×6 (756 gold), 2) Coffee beans ×5 (810 gold), 3) Silk ×2 (576 gold)
- **Diver Marina**: 1) Fish ×8 (317 gold), 2) Seaweed ×6 (518 gold), 3) Pearls ×1 (468 gold)
- **Gatherer Luca**: 1) Pumpkins ×10 (720 gold), 2) Amber ×2 (936 gold), 3) Eggs ×10 (324 gold)
- **Archaeologist Henry**: 1) Bread ×5 (765 gold), 2) Pearl necklace ×1 (1,368 gold), 3) Spices ×4 (504 gold)
- **Herder Sam**: 1) Wool ×10 (810 gold), 2) Milk ×8 (374 gold), 3) Cheese ×3 (378 gold)
- **Woodcutter Jack**: 1) Salt ×10 (324 gold), 2) Honey ×6 (562 gold), 3) Honey mead ×2 (450 gold)
- **Stationmaster William**: 1) Bread ×8 (1,224 gold), 2) Spice stew ×3 (918 gold), 3) Amber ×3 (1,404 gold)

## Map Fragments and Secret Islands
Each time 3 map fragments are collected, one secret island appears. The order of appearance is Coral Isle, Amber Isle, Ruin Atoll, Mine Isle, and Volcanic Isle. Once all five have appeared, no more fragments accumulate.
- Ways to get them: Pick up a bottle floating on the sea during a voyage (30~89 gold and 1 fragment), 35% when you repel a pirate, 20% when you fill a contract, 5% from tavern rumors, the third request of an island resident, and rewards from chapters 2, 3, and 7 of the story.
- The specialty goods of a discovered secret island (coral, amber, old pottery) can be bought there at 55% of their base price. Mine Isle and Volcanic Isle are islands where you mine, so they have their own documents on the Mine Isle and Volcanic Isle.

isleport/mines.b:
:: Category = Mining guide
:: Mine Isle = stone, iron ore, copper ore, gem ore
:: Volcano Isle = obsidian, sulfur, ruby
:: Discovery = 3 map pieces each, the 4th and 5th secret islands
:: See also = **Sailing and Islands**, **Story and Villagers**, **Buildings and Recipes**, **Strategy**

These two islands are for breaking rocks to mine minerals. The haul is sold or processed for pickaxe, glove and ship upgrades and for rushing construction. The numbers are straight from the code tables.

## Mine Isle
- Ore sell prices: Stone 5 gold, Iron ore 18 gold, Copper ore 26 gold, Gem ore 240 gold.
- A rock takes 3 hits to break, one fewer per pickaxe upgrade, down to 1. The yield is 2-4 stone, 1 gem ore, and 1-2 iron or copper ore, plus the pickaxe level.
- At the smelter, 2 iron ore and 15 gold make an iron ingot (sells for 60) and 2 copper ore and 25 gold make a copper ingot (sells for 85).
- Pickaxe upgrades: level 1 takes 4 iron ingots and 400 gold, level 2 takes 6 iron ingots, 6 copper ingots and 1,500 gold (maximum level 2).
- Steel reinforcement for a ship goes up to level 3: level 1 takes 3 iron ingots, 10 stone and 500 gold, level 2 takes 6 iron ingots, 2 copper ingots, 20 stone and 1,500 gold, and level 3 takes 10 iron ingots, 6 copper ingots, 30 stone and 4,000 gold. Each level adds 4% speed and 8% cargo to that ship.
- Iron ingots also rush construction: paying 1 ingot per 15 seconds of remaining build time (rounded up) finishes it at once.

## Volcano Isle
- Mineral sell prices: Obsidian 45 gold, Sulfur 70 gold, Ruby 480 gold.
- When a red circle flashes on the ground, lava is about to burst. Getting hit costs 3% of your gold (minimum 30, maximum 1,500), and each glove level cuts that damage by 25%.
- Breaking a rock takes 3 hits, one fewer per glove level, down to 1. The yield is 1 ruby, 1-2 sulfur and 1-3 obsidian, with the glove level added to sulfur and obsidian but not to ruby.
- Heat gloves go up to level 3: level 1 takes 6 obsidian, 4 sulfur and 600 gold; level 2 takes 14 obsidian, 10 sulfur, 1 ruby and 2,000 gold; level 3 takes 30 obsidian, 20 sulfur, 3 rubies and 5,000 gold.

isleport/multiplayer.b:
:: Category = Multiplayer guide
:: Room code = 4 letters
:: Island slots = 8 (8 colors)
:: Pirate raid = 100 gold to hire, 45 s cooldown
:: Auctions = 12 per room, 3 per seller
:: See also = **FAQ**, **Ranks and Bank**, **Ports and Trade**, **Town Facilities**, **Strategy**

Connect to other islands from the house or the notice board to create a room or join with a 4-letter room code. The room creator's game calculates prices and port events, and goods sold by others are sent to it so everyone's demand reflects them. You can keep playing alone without connecting.

## Things to do together
- Island visits: you can walk around other players' islands, and they can visit yours. The Neighbor visit and Host achievements come from this.
- Live trade: both sides see the offered goods and gold, and when both press ready the swap happens at once. Gifts, chat and auctions also exist.
- Auctions: the seller sets a starting price and a duration. The first bid must be at least the start price and later bids at least 105% of the current bid. A room holds 12 auctions, and one player can list up to 3.
- The four shared projects and the town big order are filled by everyone donating. Goals and effects are on the Ranks and Bank and Town Facilities pages. Each extra player adds 8 units and 10% reward to the big order.

## Pirate raids
- For 100 gold you can send pirates against another player's outbound ship that carries cargo. After each raid you wait 45 s, and the same ship can be raided only once per voyage.
- The success chance is 60% minus 18 points per escort level of the target ship and 15 points if the target finished Escort drills, with a minimum of 12%. A success takes 30% of each kind of cargo. The defender who repels it earns the Iron defense achievement.

isleport/strategy.b:
:: Category = Strategy
:: Basis = Values calculated from numbers in the code
:: See also = **Getting Started**, **Ports and Trade**, **Buildings and Processed Food**, **Research List**, **Ranks and Bank**, **FAQ**

The numbers in this document are calculated directly from the in-game formulas and tables. Actual values change with reputation, research, and demand, so treat them as rough estimates.

## Reducing Losses When Selling
If you sell n units at once, the average price is 95% of market for 5 units, 89% for 10, 79% for 20, 60% for 45, and 40% for 90. Because the same good shares demand within one port, mixing goods in a shipment or sending them to several ports gives a higher average.
After a sale, demand's gap from 1 shrinks by 1% per second, so it takes about 69 seconds for the gap to halve (about 34 seconds after the Market Expansion project).
Example from the start: Selling 20 wheat at the market gives 12 × 0.65 × 20 = 156 gold. Sending wheat by sailboat to Redport, which buys it at 1.3~1.4x, gives about 248~267 gold (calculated without reputation or research).

## Profit from Processing
Based on base prices, these are the processed goods with the highest profit per second, calculated as (finished product value - material value) divided by the time to make it. Imported materials must be bought at ports, so actual profit is smaller than this.
- Dyed cloth ×1 + silk ×1 → Silk hanbok (36 seconds): profit 475, 13.2 per second
- Pearls ×1 + cloth ×1 → Pearl necklace (40 seconds): profit 375, 9.4 per second
- Cloth ×1 + silk ×1 → Silk clothes (40 seconds): profit 275, 6.9 per second
- Rice ×1 + fish ×1 → Sushi (20 seconds): profit 131, 6.5 per second
- Lavender ×3 → Perfume (28 seconds): profit 170, 6.1 per second
- Flour ×1 + sugar ×1 + eggs ×1 → Cake (28 seconds): profit 160, 5.7 per second
- Flour ×1 + tomato ×1 + cheese ×1 → Pizza (25 seconds): profit 132, 5.3 per second
- Potatoes ×1 + peppers ×1 + rice ×1 → Curry (26 seconds): profit 118, 4.5 per second
- Fish ×2 + salt ×1 → Smoked fish (18 seconds): profit 78, 4.3 per second
- Eggs ×2 + milk ×1 + sugar ×1 → Pudding (24 seconds): profit 96, 4 per second
As the building level goes up, the amount made in the same time becomes 1.4x (level 2) and 2x (level 3), so the profit per second above rises by the same amount.

## Preparing for Pirates
By escort level, the chance of an encounter and the chance of repelling (when you have the Escort Training research) are as follows. The galleon starts with escort 1 attached.
- Escort 0: Encounter chance 14%, repel chance 15% (0% without research)
- Escort 1: Encounter chance 11.2%, repel chance 40% (25% without research)
- Escort 2: Encounter chance 8.4%, repel chance 65% (50% without research)
- Escort 3: Encounter chance 5.6%, repel chance 90% (75% without research)
- Escort 4: Encounter chance 2.8%, repel chance 100% (100% without research)

## Managing Money
- Loans cost 1% per minute and deposits earn 0.2% per minute, so after one hour, debt grows to about 1.82x and deposits to about 1.13x. Borrow only what you will use and repay soon, to keep interest low.
- If you run out of both money and goods, the neighbors give you 20 gold, which is 4x the cheapest seed price.
- The total reward of the 17 guide tasks is 25,950 gold. The cheapest research, in order, is Boots 150, Plow 200, and Plant All 250 gold.

tools/python.b:
:: Kind = Python in the browser
:: Engine = Pyodide 0.27.7
:: Install = Not needed
:: Login = Not needed
:: Address = tools/code/
:: Examples = 10
:: Dictionary = About 150 commands

Fry Python is a tool for running Python code in the browser with nothing to install. The code runs inside your own browser through Pyodide, and the output, turtle drawings and graphs show up right next to it. It is the first card on the site's home page (site v35).

## Writing code
- The code box is color-highlighted and numbered by line. Starting a new line fixes the indentation automatically, and typing a bracket adds its partner too.
- As you type, an auto-complete list appears and the Tab key inserts the choice. You can also open it yourself with Ctrl+Space (Fry Python v2).
- The commands that can follow t., math., random. and plt. also show up in the list.
- The **Dictionary** button shows about 150 commands sorted into Basic commands, Syntax, Strings, Lists, Dictionaries, Turtle, Graphs, Math and Random. You can search it, and clicking one puts it into your code.

## Running and results
- When you run the code, print() output appears in the output box. An endless loop can be stopped with the Stop button.
- For code that uses input(), write the values in the **input box**, one per line, and they are fed in order.
- You can draw with the turtle module: colors, fills, circles, text and speed.
- Basic matplotlib graphs are supported: line, scatter, bar, horizontal bar, histogram and pie charts.
- When an error happens, the line with the error is marked and the AI explains it (a test feature, so it can be wrong).

## Examples and files
- There are 10 examples: Hello, Multiplication Table, Turtle Star, Turtle Flower, Turtle Spiral, Drawing a Graph, Bar Chart, Rolling a Die 1000 Times, Guess the Number (input values) and Trying an Error.
- An example is loaded into the current file instead of creating a new one, and Undo brings your old code back (Fry Python v2).
- There is a My Files list and a version history, and you can open and download .py files.


- See also: **Getting Started**, **Saving and Exporting**, **Common AI Settings**, **Fry Docs**.

tools/docs.b:
:: Kind = Word-style document writing
:: Page = Write straight on an A4 page
:: Fonts = 14
:: Paper = A4, A5, B5, Letter, Legal
:: Export = Word (docx), PDF, web page, text file
:: Saving = Auto-save (browser)
:: Address = tools/docs/
:: Top tabs = Home, Insert, Layout, Review, AI, View
:: Latest version = v5 (2026-10-26)

Fry Docs is a document editor that lets you write straight on an A4 page. Like a word processor, it handles fonts, tables, pictures and page setup, and it can export to Word files. On the site's home page tool cards, it sits between Fry Sheet and Fry Slides (site v34).

## Top tabs
- The top tabs are **Home, Insert, Layout, Review, AI and View** (Fry Docs v4). Each tab shows only the buttons for its task, and the tab you last opened in this browser tab is remembered.
- The Insert tab has buttons that work right away for links, special characters, dates, table of contents, footnotes, text boxes, formulas and shapes. The Review tab has buttons for comments, change tracking, capitalization and title lines, and the Layout tab has page setup and style editing.

## Formatting text
- You can use Heading 1, 2 and 3, quotes, bulleted lists and numbered lists, and choose bold, italic, underline, strikethrough, text color and alignment.
- There are 14 fonts (Noto Sans KR (본고딕), Noto Serif KR (본명조), Nanum Gothic (나눔고딕), Nanum Myeongjo (나눔명조), Gowun Dodum (고운돋움), Nanum Pen (나눔손글씨 펜), Jua (주아), Black Gothic (검은고딕), Malgun Gothic (맑은 고딕), Batang (바탕), Arial, Times New Roman, Courier New, Georgia). Choose the font size, or change it with the bigger and smaller buttons (Fry Docs v2).
- There are highlighter, superscript and subscript, format painter, line spacing, and indent and outdent (Tab, Shift+Tab).
- **Text effects** (Fry Docs v5): on the Home tab, choose shadow, outlined text, wider letter spacing or narrower letter spacing, and remove the effect with Clear effects.
- **Paragraph decoration** (v5): apply a bordered box, yellow background or left bar to a paragraph, and remove it with Clear decoration.
- **List styles** (v5): bullets can be a circle, hollow circle or square. Numbers can be 1. 2. 3., 01. 02. 03., a. b. c., A. B. C., i. ii. iii., I. II. III., 가. 나. 다. (Korean ordinals) or ㄱ. ㄴ. ㄷ. (Korean ordinals)
- Format painter copies not only the character format but also the paragraph format (heading, alignment, decoration) (v5).
- **Style editing** (v5): on the Layout tab, change the size and text color of Heading 1, 2 and 3. A button returns them to their original look.
- Find and replace (Ctrl+F, Ctrl+H) and inserting links (Ctrl+K) are available.

## Inserting and tables
- The **Insert** menu has special characters, date and time, table of contents, footnotes, figure and table captions, text boxes, and page break (Ctrl+Enter). You can also insert dividing lines.
- Tables let you add and remove rows and columns. Tab moves to the next cell, and pressing Tab in the last cell adds a new row (Fry Docs v2). Pictures are inserted with a chosen size.
- **Bookmarks** (v5): on the Insert tab, insert a bookmark and link selected text to it. Clicking the link moves you to that bookmark.
- **Formulas** (v3): choose fractions, superscripts and subscripts, square roots, sums and Greek letters, preview them and insert. A **check mark** can be placed at the start of a line.
- **Shapes** (v3): choose from 8 kinds (rectangle, rounded rectangle, circle or ellipse, triangle, star, arrow, speech bubble, diamond) with fill, border and text, and insert them as pictures. There are also buttons to change text to all capitals, all lowercase, or capitalize the first letter of each word.
- **Table tools**: turn the first row into a header row on or off, and fill cells with color (yellow, blue, green, pink or gray) (v3). You can also merge and split cells, add a column total row, and choose a table style (striped, no borders, horizontal lines only) (v5).
- **Picture tools** (v5): click a picture to show buttons for size (small, medium, full width), border, rounded corners, shadow, text wrapping to the left or right (including off), cropping edges and removing. Each press of Crop edges trims 10% from all sides.

## Page setup
- There are five paper sizes (A4, A5, B5, Letter, Legal), and you can choose landscape or portrait and margins.
- You can add 2 or 3 column layouts, headers and footers, page numbers and a watermark (Fry Docs v2).

## Review and view
- **Comments** (Fry Docs v3): attach a comment to selected text, then view, edit and delete comments collected in one place.
- **Change tracking** (v3): when on, deleted or newly written text is shown in color. You can accept or reject changes one at a time or all at once.
- **Compare documents** (v5): choose one of your documents and compare it with the current one. Text that was added appears in green and text that was removed appears in red. It is on the Review tab.
- **View tab** (Fry Docs v4): page break display, zoom from 50% to 200% in 10% steps (the middle button resets to 100%), and word count. Word count shows the number of characters (without and with spaces), words, sentences, paragraphs, the number of pictures, tables and comments, and the approximate reading time.

## Saving and exporting
- There is a list of your documents, and they are saved automatically. There is a version history, and deleted documents can be restored.
- Export to a Word file (docx), PDF, web page or text file. Word export reflects fonts and formatting, page setup, headers and footers, and page numbers (Fry Docs v2), and also comments, change tracking marks and cell colors (Fry Docs v3).
- Text effects, paragraph decoration, list styles, bookmarks and cell merging added in v5 are not reflected in Word files. Word files contain only the text and basic formatting.
- You can open Word documents, web pages and text files. Pictures inside Word documents are dropped.

## AI assistant
- The AI assistant (test feature) is on the AI tab. It has spelling correction, make it easier, summarize and continue writing, and Fry Docs v4 added 12 more: make it formal, make it gentle, shorten, lengthen, turn into a bulleted list, suggest titles, create an outline (whole document), translate into English, Korean or Japanese, ask the document a question, and write a draft from a topic. Asking the document a question reads only the first 4,000 characters. It is a test feature, so it may be wrong.

- See also: **Getting started**, **Saving and exporting**, **Common AI settings**, **Fry Python**.

tumblecrown/getting-started.b:
:: Address = frenchfries777mc.github.io/games/tumblecrown/
:: Genre = 5v5 flag-capture team battle
:: Players = 5 per team (empty slots are filled by bots)
:: Classes = 18 (6 melee damage, 5 ranged damage, 3 utility, 4 support)
:: Maps = 13
:: Latest version = v0.2 build 304
:: Installation = Not required
:: Detailed docs = **Modes**, **Flags and Neutral Monsters**, **Controls and Settings**, **Classes**, **Maps and Rules**, **Cosmetics and tC**, **Achievements**

Tumblecrown is a team battle game in which two teams of five fight on a medieval battlefield to capture seven flags on a large map. Pick a class, form your team, and the team that captures every flag wins. On screen, your own team is shown as "your team" and the opponents as "the enemy team". The game site is games/tumblecrown/, and you open the game with the Play button on the site.

## Flow of a Match
- The two teams start at opposite corners of a very large map. There are seven flags: two on each team's starting side and three in the middle. At the start, each team owns only the one flag closest to its own base.
- A team with more players standing around a flag captures it after standing there for 7 seconds. The more players, the faster the capture (one player 1x, two 1.5x, three 2x, up to a maximum of 3x), and if both teams have the same number of players, nobody captures it. The team that captures every flag wins.
- While a flag is being captured, a light pillar in the team color rises, and once it is captured, your teammates who were around it get +20% movement speed and attack for 5 seconds.
- If the enemy is capturing your flag, the flag at the top of the screen and the flag on the minimap blink red, with an alert and a sound. The flag row at the top always shows your team on the left and the enemy team on the right, regardless of position.
- When a team holds 5 or more flags, it is Pushing, and the enemy's respawn time increases by 5 seconds. When you are defeated, you get back up at your base after 15 seconds. On maps where you choose your respawn point, you can only choose your team's flags and base.
- If you defeat opponents in a row within 8 seconds, your skill cooldowns are halved each time.
- **Neutral Monsters**: One appears at each of two corners of the map. The team that defeats one gets a permanent, stacking +2% attack and capture speed, and each team's defeat effect lvl.n is shown on screen. When the level rises, light shoots up from under the feet of everyone on that team. Only the team that defeated the monster gets the credit. A monster does not chase opponents that are too far away and returns to its spot; while returning, it does not turn around when hit and recovers health very slowly.
- **F Recall**: Press F (on a computer, you can also use the Recall button at the far left of the skill slots) to open the recall map, then click one of your team's flags to move to that flag after 3 seconds. You cannot move while recalling, and even if you cancel, a 25-second cooldown starts.
- While you hold **Tab**, a per-team table of kills and deaths is shown. When the match ends, the results screen shows the ranking table right away, and the three players with the most kills stand on the podium; the podium numbers show kills on the left and deaths on the right. Each class has its own way of falling.

## Controls
- PC: The default movement is WASD, aiming is with the mouse, attacking is left click, skills are Q, E and R, and Space is roll. In class selection, the number keys 1~9 and 0 are used.
- In Settings you can choose the movement method among WASD, arrow keys and right click, and you can change the skill keys and the roll key. You can adjust the music and sound effect volume separately and choose a language, and the View Profile button opens your profile card.
- Every basic attack and skill shows its range in mint color while held and goes off when released (the Hunter's charged shot is also held and then released).
- If you roll just before an attack lands, you gain Focus for 2.5 seconds, and your damage increases by 50%.
- Phone: When you move with your left thumb, your character automatically faces the direction of travel, and when standing still it faces the nearest opponent. The buttons on the right are used for attack (auto-aims at the nearest opponent), skills, roll and recall. Holding a skill or attack button shows a preview, you drag to set the direction, and it goes off when you release.
- If the screen stays slow, turn on Optimization in Settings. It turns off shadows and glow and sets the screen to 30 frames.
- If you turn on the FPS display in Settings (off by default), the frames per second are shown on screen. Shadows are now redrawn only once every three frames, which makes the game lighter (build 266).

## Rooms and Practice
- In an online match, if there is even one person, bots fill the empty slots after 15 seconds and the match starts. Bots wait 1~4 seconds, then pick a class and get ready, and the match starts right away only when everyone is ready. While you are looking for people to play with, you cannot press any button.
- Bots split up between flags and monsters. They pick classes so that they do not overlap within the same team, and for a monster that nobody has touched, the nearest bot goes to hunt it. When in danger, a bot flees with a 75% chance.
- In **Practice vs Bots**, you can choose the map yourself (random by default). You do not earn tC in this room.
- In the **Training Ground** on the first screen, you pick a class and go in to hit six training dummies. The dummies do not fight back, and even when knocked down they stand back up after 2 seconds.
- When there is nobody in an online server room and a new build is uploaded, the room closes by itself and reopens on the new build.

## Cosmetics and Intro
- In the lobby's **Cosmetics · Skins**, you buy skins, back decorations, helmet decorations and shield emblems. The currency is tC, which you receive when an online match ends. Clicking an item first shows how it looks when worn, and buying, wearing and removing are done with the buttons below.
- The intro that plays when you open the site is a video recording of a match actually fought by ten bots.

## Modes
- Online matches open a separate room for each mode. The mode list is in the order Ranked, Hyper, Classic, Blitz, Duel (build 240).
- **Ranked**: Played by 10 people (5v5), and no bots join. Winning raises your ranking points, and losing lowers them.
- **10vs10 Hyper**: Twenty players clash on the same seven flags. Capturing is 1.5x faster and four neutral monsters appear. Defeating a monster permanently raises attack and capture by 3% each. Because of the large number of players, the information exchanged is reduced to 12 times per second.
- **5vs5 Classic**: Ten players compete over seven flags. You capture your side's flanks first, and on maps with four flanks you must hold the two nearest flanks to open the center. Once you hold the center, you capture the enemy-side flanks, then the enemy base, in that order.
- **3vs3 Blitz**: Six players compete over five flags. You must capture the flanks and the center first to open the enemy base.
- **1vs1 Duel**: Two players compete over three flags (both bases and the center). You must hold the center to open the enemy base, and capturing is only possible once 1 minute 30 seconds have passed since the start.
- The server room host can also open Hyper and Duel.

## Further Reading
- **Modes**: Player counts, flags and capture order for Ranked, Hyper, Classic, Blitz and Duel.
- **Flags and Neutral Monsters**: Flag capture, respawn, recall, neutral monsters.
- **Controls and Settings**: Computer and phone controls, roll, settings, optimization.
- **Rooms and Bots**: Online rooms, bots, the Training Ground.
- **Classes**: Pictures, health, basic attacks, skill names, cooldowns and effects of the 18 classes.
- **Classes at a Glance**: A line-by-line comparison of the classes and tips for choosing.
- **Class Level and Mastery**: Experience, ranks and Mastery skins.
- **Maps and Rules**: The layout of the thirteen maps and flag-capture tips.
- **Cosmetics and tC**: Cosmetic prices, how to earn tC, daily missions.
- **Achievements**: The 27 achievements.
- **Team Strategy and Tips**, **Glossary**, **FAQ · Troubleshooting**, **Patch History**.

tumblecrown/classes.b:
:: Number of classes = 18
:: Melee damage = Knight, Viking, Mamluk, Skeleton, Assassin, Spearman
:: Ranged damage = Hunter, Witch, Crossbowman, Bomber, Streltsy
:: Utility = Warden, Court Mage, Wellington
:: Support = Priest, Bard, Necromancer, Telaris
:: Class level = Max 10
:: Mastery = From Novice to Grandmaster V
:: Based on = v0.2 build 304

Tumblecrown has 18 classes. On the class selection screen (the waiting room and the Training Ground), you choose by clicking the list or pressing the number keys 1~9 and 0, and you can first see the chosen class as it appears on its pedestal. Above other players' heads, their role (melee damage, ranged damage, utility, support) is shown. There are three skills, Q, E and R, and the number in parentheses is the cooldown. Every basic attack and skill shows its range in mint color while held and goes off when released. The numbers are copied as-is from the game data (build 304). The pictures are taken directly in the game from the pedestals on the class selection screen.

A line-by-line comparison of the classes and tips for choosing are on the **Classes at a Glance** page, and class levels and Mastery are on the **Class Level and Mastery** page.

## Melee Damage

### Knight
!img/tc-knight.webp
A sturdy fighter who holds out and pushes forward with attack, attack, heavy strike.
- Health 335, move speed 6.8.
- Basic attack: Sword Slash (chained hits end with a heavy overhead smash on the third). Damage 27, 0.45 s interval.
- Q **Block** (5 s): Raises the shield for 1.2 seconds, reducing damage from the front by 70%.
- E **Charge** (5 s): Charges forward, dealing 40 damage to opponents it hits and slowing them for 1.5 seconds.
- R **Shield Bash** (10 s): Dashes a short way shield-first, dealing 36 damage and stunning the opponent for 1.1 seconds.

### Viking
!img/tc-viking.webp
The sturdiest warrior: slow, but every axe blow lands heavy.
- Health 314, move speed 6.16.
- Basic attack: Axe Chop. Damage 22, 0.55 s interval.
- Q **Leaping Slam** (5 s): Leaps far forward and lands, dealing 36 damage to opponents around you and slowing them for 1.5 seconds.
- E **Bloodlust** (12 s): For 5 seconds, your attacks are 30% faster and you recover part of the damage you deal as health.
- R **Earthquake** (12 s): Splits the ground in a long line 11 tiles ahead, dealing 42 damage to everyone on that path and slowing them.

### Mamluk
!img/tc-mamluk.webp
A nimble warrior who slashes and dives in quickly with a curved sword.
- Health 316, move speed 7.92.
- Basic attack: Curved Sword Combo. Damage 18, 0.3 s interval.
- Q **Flurry Slash** (4 s): Dives forward and slashes five times alternately, dealing 9 damage each.
- E **Spin Slash** (8 s): Spins twice in place, slashing everyone around three times for 12 damage each.
- R **Flash Slash** (10 s): Teleports behind the nearest opponent and slashes, dealing 34 damage.

### Skeleton
!img/tc-skeleton.webp
A light, fast pile of bones. Its body is frail, so dive in and pull back out.
- Health 292, move speed 7.7.
- Basic attack: Bone Club. Damage 16, 0.32 s interval.
- Q **Bone Scatter** (6 s): Falls back as the body scatters, and eight bone shards fly out in every direction. 12 damage each.
- E **Five Bone Spears** (6 s): Throws five bone spears in a fan. 15 damage each.
- R **Bone Storm** (14 s): Spins for 1.4 seconds, continuously striking everything around for 13 damage each.

### Assassin
!img/tc-assassin.webp
Sneaks in and cuts down a weak target. Its body is frail, so being spotted is dangerous.
- Health 220, move speed 8.58.
- Basic attack: Short Blade Combo Stabs. Damage 20, 0.3 s interval.
- Q **Shadow Step** (10 s): For 3.5 seconds, you are invisible to distant opponents and 25% faster. The first hit you land while hidden deals 1.8x damage.
- E **Poison Dagger** (9 s): Your next four attacks set the opponent ablaze.
- R **Execution** (14 s): Teleports behind the opponent with the lowest health and slashes. If the opponent's health is below 35%, the damage is doubled.

### Spearman
!img/tc-spearman.webp
Thrusts from afar with a long spear and pushes back approaching opponents with a charge and a sweep.
- Health 378, move speed 6.6.
- Basic attack: Long Forward Thrust. Damage 47, 0.6 s interval.
- Q **Charging Thrust** (6 s): Charges far forward, piercing opponents along the way. Deals 40 damage and slows for 1.5 seconds.
- E **Spear Throw** (10 s): Throws the spear far. The opponent hit is slowed for 1.5 seconds and takes 42 damage.
- R **Sweep** (14 s): Swings the spear in a wide arc, dealing 36 damage to opponents around you, knocking them back and slowing them for 1.5 seconds.

## Ranged Damage

### Hunter
!img/tc-archer.webp
Shoots from afar. If you hold the attack, it fires two arrows at once after 0.8 seconds and three after 2 seconds.
- Health 205, move speed 6.4.
- Basic attack: Arrow (holding fires several). Damage 13, 0.36 s interval.
- Q **Piercing Arrow** (5 s): A powerful arrow that flies through opponents. 45 damage.
- E **Arrow Rain** (9 s): Rains arrows on the aimed spot for 1.5 seconds.
- R **Mark Weakness** (12 s): Leaves a mark on the aimed opponent for 6 seconds, increasing the damage that opponent takes by 50%.

### Witch
!img/tc-witch.webp
Harasses from afar with magic orbs and curses.
- Health 163, move speed 6.2.
- Basic attack: Magic Orb. Damage 11, 0.45 s interval.
- Q **Poison Potion** (7 s): Throws a potion at the aimed spot, dealing 30 damage to opponents around where it bursts and setting them ablaze.
- E **Curse** (10 s): Detonates a curse at the aimed spot, dealing 40 damage after a moment and slowing for 3 seconds.
- R **Frost Burst** (12 s): Bursts frost at the aimed spot, dealing 22 damage to opponents around it, freezing them for 0.6 seconds and slowing them for 3 seconds.

### Crossbowman
!img/tc-crossbow.webp
Moves slowly, shoots one accurate shot at a time from afar, and finishes with a snipe.
- Health 190, move speed 5.8.
- Basic attack: Single Crossbow Shot (one shot at a time even when held). Damage 23, 0.6 s interval.
- Q **Binding Bolt** (8 s): Fires a bolt that heavily slows the opponent hit for 2.5 seconds. 18 damage.
- E **Backstep** (8 s): Leaps far backward, and for 3 seconds your attack damage is 1.5x.
- R **Snipe** (14 s): Walks slowly for 1.2 seconds while gathering aim, then fires a shot that pierces walls and flies all the way. 110 damage.

### Bomber
!img/tc-bomber.webp
Bombs the area above flags from behind walls to disrupt captures. It rarely hits opponents who move before it goes off.
- Health 290, move speed 6.3.
- Basic attack: Lobs a bomb in an arc (it explodes 0.75 seconds after landing). Damage 42, 1.3 s interval.
- Q **Big Bomb** (8 s): Throws a big bomb at the aimed spot. After 1.1 seconds it explodes over a wide area, dealing 60 damage.
- E **Sticky Bomb** (11 s): Heavily slows opponents caught in the explosion for 3 seconds. 15 damage.
- R **Bombardment** (18 s): Drops five bombs in a line ahead. 38 damage per bomb.

### Streltsy
!img/tc-streltsy.webp
Fires one powerful shot at a time from very far away, and swings an axe to shove away anyone who gets close.
- Health 220, move speed 5.6.
- Basic attack: Single Gun Shot (flies the farthest, but is hard to land and takes a long time before the next shot). Damage 67, 1.75 s interval.
- Q **Rapid Fire** (9 s): Fires three bullets in a row in the same direction. 26 damage per bullet.
- E **Giant Bullet** (11 s): Fires one large, slow bullet. 88 damage.
- R **Axe Swing** (14 s): Swings the Russian axe in the other hand in a wide fan ahead. Deals 90 damage to opponents nearby and knocks them back hard.

## Utility

### Warden
!img/tc-warden.webp
Blocks chokepoints and protects allies. Slow with weak attacks, but lasts the longest.
- Health 430, move speed 5.6.
- Basic attack: Heavy Shield Slam. Damage 24, 0.5 s interval.
- Q **Raise Barrier** (9 s): Raises a stone barrier in front of you for 4 seconds. Arrows and orbs that hit the barrier vanish.
- E **Guardian Oath** (14 s): Places an oath on a nearby ally for 6 seconds, and you take 40% of the damage that ally receives. If there is no ally, you place it on yourself and take 25% less damage for 6 seconds.
- R **Iron Wall** (16 s): For 3 seconds, you take 60% less damage from any direction, put a shield on nearby allies, and slow opponents around you.

### Court Mage
!img/tc-court.webp
Marks opponents with rune orbs. Swaps places to save allies and pulls opponents toward your side.
- Health 165, move speed 6.
- Basic attack: Rune Orb. Damage 10, 0.55 s interval.
- Q **Summon Swap** (12 s): Swaps places with a nearby ally. Pull a threatened ally out, or reach a flag first.
- E **Rune Shackle** (14 s): Places a rune circle on the ground for 3 seconds. Opponents inside are slowed, and opponents with a rune mark are pulled to the center.
- R **Court Shift** (22 s): Swaps places with an opponent that has a rune mark and halts them for 1 second.

### Wellington
!img/tc-wellington.webp
A commander who defends and seizes flags. Speeds up allies and turns the tide of flag fights.
- Health 250, move speed 6.
- Basic attack: Sword Slash (swung in a fan). Damage 18, 0.5 s interval.
- Q **Rally** (12 s): Raises a hand to increase the movement speed of allies in range (including yourself) by 50% for 2 seconds.
- E **Steadfast Defense** (18 s): Plants a golden flag on the flag of your team closest to you. For 8 seconds, that flag does not change even if enemies come.
- R **Capture** (24 s): Plants a purple flag on the enemy flag closest to you. For 8 seconds, that flag's enemy-flag effect disappears, and as long as even one ally is present, the capture progresses no matter how many opponents there are.

## Support

### Priest
!img/tc-priest.webp
Follows up with light orbs, and the third attack fires a big piercing beam of light.
- Health 150, move speed 6.
- Basic attack: Light Orb (the third is a big piercing beam of light). Damage 10, 0.5 s interval.
- Q **Heal** (9 s): Restores 18 of your own health.
- E **Shield** (14 s): Applies a shield that blocks 24 damage for 5 seconds.
- R **Smite** (12 s): Raises a pillar of light at the aimed spot. After a moment, opponents inside take heavy damage.

### Bard
!img/tc-bard.webp
Speeds up and heals allies with song. A lullaby slows approaching opponents and buys time.
- Health 175, move speed 6.2.
- Basic attack: Note Orb. Damage 9, 0.5 s interval.
- Q **March** (12 s): Nearby allies (including you) become 30% faster for 6 seconds and recover 8 health.
- E **Lullaby** (11 s): Opponents around you are heavily slowed for 3 seconds and take 12 damage.
- R **Chorus** (16 s): Restores 30 health to nearby allies (including you) and applies a shield that blocks 18 damage for 4 seconds.

### Necromancer
!img/tc-necro.webp
Fights from a distance with wide sweeping attacks. Heals allies and summons skeletons to form a front line.
- Health 190, move speed 5.8.
- Basic attack: Wide Rectangular Swing. Damage 16, 0.7 s interval.
- Q **Life Drain** (12 s): Restores 22 health to allies around you (including you).
- E **Summon Skeletons** (16 s): Summons four weak skeletons around you. The skeletons fight on your side for 18 seconds.
- R **Realm of Death** (24 s): Stuns opponents inside a wide circle for 1 second and damages them, then slows their movement speed by 50% for 3 seconds.

### Telaris
A guardian who protects allies with a shield and pushes forward. Slow, but the most dependable.
- Health 460, move speed 5.4.
- Basic attack: Shield Shove (shoves wide and knocks back far). Damage 20, 0.75 s interval.
- Q **Guardian's Blessing** (8 s): Applies a shield that blocks 60 damage for 4 seconds to the nearest ally (or yourself if there is none).
- E **Shield Slam** (12 s): Slams the shield into the ground, dealing 25 damage to opponents around you and stunning them for 0.8 seconds.
- R **Iron Wall Rush** (16 s): Curls into a ball and rolls at great speed for 4.5 seconds (movement keys do not work and you can only turn with the mouse; skill cooldowns do not recover while rolling). When an opponent touches the fan-shaped area ahead, you stop on the spot and deal damage (40~160) and knockback. The farther you roll, the greater both become. Hitting a wall leaves you briefly dizzy.

tumblecrown/maps-rules.b:
:: Map count = 13
:: Based on = v0.2 build 304

Maps are chosen at random for each match. In bot and practice rooms, you can choose the map yourself. The two teams start at opposite corners, and there are seven flags in total (two near each team's start and three in the middle). At the start, each team holds only the one flag nearest its base.

## How to read the minimap
- The whole map is shown small at the top right of the match screen. Every picture in this page is a real minimap from the game.
- The blue circle is the blue team's base and the red circle is the red team's base.
- The gray rings are flags. There are seven in total.
- Bright lines are walls and dark areas cannot be entered. The purple floor is where you can walk.

## Capturing flags
- A flag becomes your team's when the team with more people around it stands there for 7 seconds. The more people, the faster it goes.
- If both teams have the same number of people, nobody captures it.
- While an enemy is capturing your flag, the flag on the minimap flashes red, with an alert and a sound. Check the minimap often.
- All seven flags are used in 5vs5 Classic and 10vs10 Hyper. 3vs3 Blitz uses five flags and 1vs1 Duel uses three (the two bases and the middle).

## Three Lanes
The top, middle, and bottom lanes are divided by long walls. You can change lanes only through the wall ends and the gap in the center.
!img/tcmap-1.webp
- **Tip** : Pick one of the three lanes and push down it. Whoever holds the gap in the middle can switch lanes more easily.

## Central Fortress
Three flags are inside the fortress in the middle. The fortress has four doors.
!img/tcmap-2.webp
- **Tip** : All three middle flags sit in one place, so the team that takes the fortress first gets a big lead. Split up the four doors.

## Cross Plaza
A wide cross-shaped road runs between four clusters of buildings. Holding the middle of the plaza wins.
!img/tcmap-3.webp
- **Tip** : The four building clusters block your view. Wait for your teammates before you step out into the plaza.

## Stone Wall Village
A village where houses are connected by stone-walled alleys. Go around through the alleys to attack from behind.
!img/tcmap-4.webp
- **Tip** : There are many paths, so while one player holds the front, another can circle around through the alleys.

## Ice Lake
A large frozen lake sits in the middle, and four ice bridges connect to the central island. You can go around the lake or cross it on the ice bridges.
!img/tcmap-5.webp
- **Tip** : The path narrows while you cross a bridge. Check on the minimap where the enemy is before you cross.

## Abyss Bridge
One narrow, long central bridge connects the left and right islands. Whoever holds the bridge entrance has the advantage.
!img/tcmap-6.webp
- **Tip** : The bridge is narrow, so it is hard to dodge while crossing. Gather your teammates and cross together.

## Pirate Harbor
The sea cuts into the top and bottom in half-moon shapes, and piers stretch far out into the middle of the sea. Watch for narrow gaps between ships and warehouses.
!img/tcmap-7.webp
- **Tip** : You cannot walk where the sea cuts in. The narrow gap between the pier and the ships is the choke point, so guard it.

## Clock Tower
The middle flag is surrounded by a round gear wall, with only four doors open. Enter by going around between the tooth-shaped stone pillars along the gear's edge.
!img/tcmap-8.webp
- **Tip** : You can only get in through the four doors. Split into one player guarding a door and others entering by another.

## Underground Canal
Two waterways flowing horizontally divide the underground into three lanes, crossable only over six narrow bridges. You can also go around the ends of the waterways.
!img/tcmap-9.webp
- **Tip** : There are only six bridges to cross. Staying in front of a bridge makes you a target, so check before you cross.

## Burning Walls
Both bases are surrounded by burning walls with only three gates. Whoever holds the area in front of the gates has the advantage.
!img/tcmap-10.webp
- **Tip** : There are only three gates, so fights happen in front of them. Pass through a gate together with your teammates.

## Ruined Cathedral
Sight is blocked among the pillars of the ruined cathedral, and the central altar has only two doors. Approach from behind the round pillars.
!img/tcmap-11.webp
- **Tip** : The pillars block your view. Watch your back even when sneaking up behind a pillar. The altar has only two doors.

## Desert Temple
A flag sits inside the central temple. The temple door is closed and opens periodically, and the flag can be captured only while the door is open. The closed door is a sealed stone door that glows red, and when it opens, it sinks into the ground and the floor glows green. Sandstorms occasionally blow in and block the view into the distance.
!img/tcmap-12.webp
- **Tip** : You can only take the flag while the temple door is open. Wait near the door and go in the moment it opens.

## King's Road
Between the two bases are an upper road, a diagonal central road, and a lower road. A flag sits in a clearing in the forest between the roads, so you can slip in through the side paths.
!img/tcmap-13.webp
- **Tip** : This map has many paths. Watch the minimap to see which road the enemy takes and block them on the same road.
