This page compares all eighteen classes in one place. The description of each skill is on the **Classes** page.

## Melee Damage
- **Knight**: Health 335 · Move 6.8 · Basic attack 27 (every 0.45 s, about 60 per second) · Skill cooldowns Q 5 s / E 5 s / R 10 s · Card bars Power 3, Speed 3, Range 2, Difficulty 1.
- **Viking**: Health 314 · Move 6.16 · Basic attack 22 (every 0.55 s, about 40 per second) · Skill cooldowns Q 5 s / E 12 s / R 12 s · Card bars Power 5, Speed 2, Range 2, Difficulty 2.

- **Assassin**: Health 220 · Move 8.58 · Basic attack 20 (every 0.3 s, about 67 per second) · Skill cooldowns Q 10 s / E 9 s / R 14 s · Card bars Power 4, Speed 5, Range 1, Difficulty 5.
- **Spearman**: Health 378 · Move 6.6 · Basic attack 47 (every 0.6 s, about 78 per second) · Skill cooldowns Q 6 s / E 10 s / R 14 s · Card bars Power 3, Speed 3, Range 3, Difficulty 3.

## Ranged Damage
- **Hunter**: Health 205 · Move 6.4 · Basic attack 13 (every 0.36 s, about 36 per second) · Skill cooldowns Q 5 s / E 9 s / R 12 s · Card bars Power 2, Speed 4, Range 5, Difficulty 3.
- **Witch**: Health 163 · Move 6.2 · Basic attack 11 (every 0.45 s, about 24 per second) · Skill cooldowns Q 7 s / E 10 s / R 12 s · Card bars Power 3, Speed 3, Range 4, Difficulty 4.
- **Crossbowman**: Health 190 · Move 5.8 · Basic attack 23 (every 0.6 s, about 38 per second) · Skill cooldowns Q 8 s / E 8 s / R 14 s · Card bars Power 4, Speed 2, Range 5, Difficulty 4.
- **Bomber**: Health 290 · Move 6.3 · Basic attack 42 (every 1.3 s, about 32 per second) · Skill cooldowns Q 8 s / E 11 s / R 18 s · Card bars Power 4, Speed 2, Range 3, Difficulty 4.
- **Streltsy**: Health 220 · Move 5.6 · Basic attack 67 (every 1.75 s, about 38 per second) · Skill cooldowns Q 9 s / E 11 s / R 14 s · Card bars Power 5, Speed 2, Range 5, Difficulty 3.

## Utility
- **Warden**: Health 430 · Move 5.6 · Basic attack 24 (every 0.5 s, about 48 per second) · Skill cooldowns Q 9 s / E 14 s / R 16 s · Card bars Power 3, Speed 1, Range 1, Difficulty 2.
- **Court Mage**: Health 165 · Move 6 · Basic attack 10 (every 0.55 s, about 18 per second) · Skill cooldowns Q 12 s / E 14 s / R 22 s · Card bars Power 1, Speed 2, Range 5, Difficulty 3.
- **Wellington**: Health 250 · Move 6 · Basic attack 18 (every 0.5 s, about 36 per second) · Skill cooldowns Q 12 s / E 18 s / R 24 s · Card bars Power 2, Speed 3, Range 2, Difficulty 4.

## Support
- **Priest**: Health 150 · Move 6 · Basic attack 10 (every 0.5 s, about 20 per second) · Skill cooldowns Q 9 s / E 14 s / R 12 s · Card bars Power 2, Speed 3, Range 4, Difficulty 2.
- **Bard**: Health 175 · Move 6.2 · Basic attack 9 (every 0.5 s, about 18 per second) · Skill cooldowns Q 12 s / E 11 s / R 16 s · Card bars Power 1, Speed 3, Range 5, Difficulty 3.
- **Necromancer**: Health 190 · Move 5.8 · Basic attack 16 (every 0.7 s, about 23 per second) · Skill cooldowns Q 12 s / E 16 s / R 24 s · Card bars Power 2, Speed 3, Range 3, Difficulty 3.
- **Telaris**: Health 460 · Move 5.4 · Basic attack 20 (every 0.75 s, about 27 per second) · Skill cooldowns Q 8 s / E 12 s / R 16 s · Card bars Power 4, Speed 1, Range 1, Difficulty 3.

## Rankings by the Numbers
- Classes with the highest health: Telaris 460, Warden 430, Spearman 378.
- Classes with the highest move speed: Assassin 8.58, Mamluk 7.92, Skeleton 7.7.
- Classes with the highest damage per hit: Streltsy 67, Spearman 47, Bomber 42.
- Classes with the shortest basic attack interval: Mamluk 0.3 s, Assassin 0.3 s, Skeleton 0.32 s.
- Within the same team, bots pick classes so that they do not overlap. Humans may overlap.

## Tips for Choosing
- **If you are new**: Start with the Knight, which has the lowest Difficulty bar on its class card (1 bar). The next easiest, the Priest, Viking and Warden (2 bars), are also good. Hitting the training dummies in the Training Ground will give you a feel for them.
- **If you want to capture flags quickly**: The fast Assassin, Mamluk and Skeleton move between flags the quickest. Wellington has skills for defending and taking over flags themselves.
- **If you want to block chokepoints**: The Warden and Telaris have the highest health, at 430 and 460. The Warden holds the path with barriers, and Telaris with shields and shoves.
- **If you want to help from a distance**: The Priest, Bard and Necromancer restore allies' health and apply shields. The Court Mage swaps places with allies to pull endangered allies out.
- **If you want one big hit**: The Crossbowman's Snipe (110 damage), the Streltsy's Giant Bullet (88 damage) and Axe Swing (90 damage) are the biggest.

tumblecrown/modes.b:
:: Number of modes = 5 (Ranked, Hyper, Classic, Blitz, Duel)
:: Mode list order = Ranked, Hyper, Classic, Blitz, Duel
:: Rooms = A separate room opens for each mode
:: Based on = v0.2 build 304
:: See also = **Flags and Neutral Monsters**, **Rooms and Bots**

In Tumblecrown's online matches, a separate room opens for each mode. The number of players, the number of flags and the capture order differ by mode. In Practice vs Bots rooms you can choose the mode yourself, and the online waiting screen has no mode selector.

## At a Glance
- **Ranked**: 5vs5, 10 humans, no bots. Winning raises your ranking points and losing lowers them.
- **10vs10 Hyper**: Twenty players, seven flags, 1.5x faster capture, four monsters.
- **5vs5 Classic**: Ten players, seven flags.
- **3vs3 Blitz**: Six players, five flags.
- **1vs1 Duel**: Two players, three flags.

## Ranked
- Played by ten humans (5v5), and no bots join.
- Winning raises your ranking points by 30 and losing lowers them by 20. They never drop below 0.
- Winning your first Ranked match earns the achievement **First Ranked Win**.

## 10vs10 Hyper
- Twenty players clash on the same seven flags.
- Capturing is 1.5x faster, and four neutral monsters appear. Defeating a monster permanently raises attack and capture by 3% each (2% in other modes).
- Because of the large number of players, the information exchanged is reduced to 12 times per second.
- Defeating ten opponents in one match earns the achievement **Thick of the Melee**.
- The server room host can also open Hyper.

## 5vs5 Classic
- Ten players gather and compete over seven flags.
- The capture order is fixed. You first capture the flanks on your side. On maps with four flanks, you must hold the two nearest flanks to open the center. Once you hold the center, you capture the enemy-side flanks, then the enemy base, in that order.
- Winning thirty times in Classic earns the achievement **Classic Conqueror**.

## 3vs3 Blitz
- Six players compete over five flags. You must capture the flanks and the center first to open the enemy base.
- Winning within 3 minutes in Blitz earns the achievement **Lightning Match**.

## 1vs1 Duel
- Two players compete over three flags (both bases and the center).
- You must hold the center to open the enemy base. Capturing is only possible once 1 minute 30 seconds have passed since the start, so use that time to take position and size each other up.
- The server room host can also open Duel.
- Winning ten times in Duel earns the achievement **Master of One-on-One**.

## What Every Mode Shares
- Mastery points and class experience accumulate in the same way regardless of mode. Details are on the **Class Level and Mastery** page.
- If you lose, you get back up at your base after 15 seconds, and when a team holds 5 or more flags, it is Pushing and the enemy's respawn time increases by 5 seconds.

tumblecrown/flags-monsters.b:
:: Flags = Seven (two on each base side, three in the middle)
:: Capture time = 7 seconds
:: Capture reward = +20% movement speed and attack for 5 seconds
:: Neutral monsters = One at each of two corners of the map (four in Hyper)
:: Monster reward = Permanent +2% attack and capture speed each (3% in Hyper)
:: Based on = v0.2 build 304

In this game, victory is decided at the flags. The team that captures every flag wins. This page explains how flags change hands, what you gain by defeating neutral monsters, and how recall and respawn work.

## Capturing Flags
- A team with more players standing around a flag captures it after standing there for 7 seconds.
- The more players, the faster the capture: one player 1x, two 1.5x, three 2x, up to a maximum of 3x.
- If both teams have the same number of players, nobody captures it.
- While a flag is being captured, a light pillar in the team color rises. Once it is captured, your teammates who were around it get +20% movement speed and attack for 5 seconds.
- At the start, each team owns only the one flag closest to its own base.
- Classic and Hyper have seven flags, Blitz has five, and Duel has three. The order is explained on the **Modes** page.

## Reading the Alerts
- If the enemy is capturing your flag, the flag at the top of the screen and the flag on the minimap blink red, with an alert and a sound.
- The flag row at the top always shows your team on the left and the enemy team on the right, regardless of position.
- On screen, your own team is shown as "your team" and the opponents as "the enemy team".

## Pushing and Respawn
- When a team holds 5 or more flags, it is Pushing, and the enemy's respawn time increases by 5 seconds.
- When you are defeated, you get back up at your base after 15 seconds. On maps where you choose your respawn point, you can only choose your team's flags and base.
- If you defeat opponents in a row within 8 seconds, your skill cooldowns are halved each time.

## F Recall
- Pressing F opens the recall map. On a computer, you can also open it with the Recall button at the far left of the skill slots.
- Click one of your team's flags to move to that flag after 3 seconds.
- You cannot move while recalling, and even if you cancel, a 25-second cooldown starts.

## Neutral Monsters
- One appears at each of two corners of the map. In 10vs10 Hyper there are four.
- The team that defeats one gets a permanent, stacking +2% attack and capture speed. In Hyper it is 3%. Each team's defeat effect lvl.n is shown on screen.
- When the level rises, light shoots up from under the feet of everyone on that team. Only the team that defeated the monster gets the credit.
- A monster does not chase opponents that are too far away and returns to its spot. While returning, it does not turn around when hit and recovers health very slowly.
- Defeating a monster for the first time earns the achievement **First Steps in Monster Hunting**, ten monsters earn **Monster Hunter**, and a hundred earn **Monster Hunting Master**.
- Monster kills also count toward Mastery points. Details are on the **Class Level and Mastery** page.

## How Bots Move
- Bots split up between flags and monsters. They pick classes so that they do not overlap within the same team.
- For a monster that nobody has touched, the nearest bot goes to hunt it.
- When in danger, a bot flees with a 75% chance.

tumblecrown/controls.b:
:: Computer movement = WASD (can be changed to arrow keys or right click in Settings)
:: Attack = Left mouse click
:: Skills = Q · E · R
:: Roll = Space
:: Recall = F
:: Scoreboard = Tab (while held)
:: Based on = v0.2 build 304

Tumblecrown can be played on both computers and phones. This page summarizes the controls and what you can change in Settings.

## Computer
- Movement is WASD by default, you aim with the mouse, and you attack with left click.
- Q, E and R are the three skills, and Space is roll.
- On the class selection screen, you choose a class with the number keys 1~9 and 0.
- While you hold Tab, a per-team table of kills and deaths is shown.
- Pressing F opens the recall map (see the **Flags and Neutral Monsters** page).
- Every basic attack and skill shows its range in mint color while held and goes off when released. The Hunter's charged shot is also held and then released.

## Roll and Focus
- If you roll just before an attack lands, you gain Focus for 2.5 seconds, and the damage you deal increases by 50%.
- Rolling is both a dodge and a counterattack setup. Try timing it for when an opponent's big skill is flying toward you.

## Phone
- When you move with your left thumb, your character automatically faces the direction of travel, and when standing still it faces the nearest opponent.
- The buttons on the right are used for attack (auto-aims at the nearest opponent), skills, roll and recall.
- Holding a skill or attack button shows a preview, you drag to set the direction, and it goes off when you release.

## What You Can Change in Settings
- You can choose the movement method among WASD, arrow keys and right click, and change the skill keys and the roll key.
- You can adjust the music and sound effect volume separately and choose a language.
- The **View Profile** button opens your profile card.
- If you turn on the FPS display (off by default), the frames per second are shown on screen.

## When the Screen Is Slow
- Turn on **Optimization** in Settings. It turns off shadows and glow and sets the screen to 30 frames.
- Shadows are now redrawn only once every three frames, which makes the game lighter (build 266).
- Optimization is linked to the shared optimization value in the Hub settings, so changing it on one side is reflected on the other.

tumblecrown/rooms-bots.b:
:: Online matches = If there is even one person, bots fill the empty slots after 15 seconds
:: Practice vs Bots = You can choose the map yourself, no tC
:: Training Ground = Six training dummies
:: Based on = v0.2 build 304

This page explains how to play alone and how online rooms work.

## Online Matches
- Online matches open a separate room for each mode. See the **Modes** page for the modes.
- If there is even one person, bots fill the empty slots after 15 seconds and the match starts.
- Bots wait 1~4 seconds, then pick a class and get ready, and the match starts right away only when everyone is ready.
- While you are looking for people to play with, you cannot press any button.
- Bots do not join Ranked matches.
- You cannot play together unless you are on the same version. Players on different versions cannot join the same room (since build 31).
- When there is nobody in an online server room and a new build is uploaded, the room closes by itself and reopens on the new build.

## Practice vs Bots
- In **Practice vs Bots**, you can choose the map yourself (random by default). You can also choose the mode.
- You do not earn tC in this room.

## Training Ground
- In the **Training Ground** on the first screen, you pick a class and go in to hit six training dummies.
- The dummies do not fight back, and even when knocked down they stand back up after 2 seconds.
- It is a good place to learn the skill range and timing of a new class.

## When the Match Ends
- The results screen shows the ranking table right away. The three players with the most kills stand on the podium, and the podium numbers show kills on the left and deaths on the right.
- Each class has its own way of falling.
- The tC you received, the experience you gained, your Mastery points and any level-ups are shown on the results screen.

## Intro Video
- The intro that plays when you open the site is a video recording of a match actually fought by ten bots.

tumblecrown/achievements.b:
:: Number of achievements = 27
:: Viewing names = Achievements in the lobby
:: Based on = v0.2 build 304

There are 27 achievements in all. You receive one as soon as you meet its condition. Anything done in the Training Ground (against dummies) does not count toward kills or victories.

## Firsts
- **First Match**: Start a match for the first time.
- **First Victory**: Win a match for the first time.
- **Ten Victories**: Win ten matches.
- **Playing Together**: Play a match in the same room as another person.

## Kills and Captures
- **Knockout Streak**: Defeat three or more opponents in one match.
- **Master of the Battlefield**: Defeat five or more opponents in one match.
- **Fifty Defeated**: Defeat fifty opponents in total.
- **Three Hundred Defeated**: Defeat three hundred opponents in total.
- **Flag Collector**: Capture flags ten times.
- **Lord of the Flags**: Capture flags a hundred times.
- **First Steps in Monster Hunting**: Defeat a neutral monster for the first time.
- **Monster Hunter**: Defeat ten neutral monsters.
- **Flawless Victory**: Win a match without being defeated even once.
- **Triple Kill**: Defeat three opponents in a row in a short time.
- **Monster Hunting Master**: Defeat a hundred neutral monsters.

## By Mode
- **Five-Minute Win**: Win a match within 5 minutes.
- **First Ranked Win**: Win a Ranked match for the first time.
- **Thick of the Melee**: Defeat ten opponents in one match of Hyper.
- **Classic Conqueror**: Win thirty times in Classic.
- **Lightning Match**: Win within 3 minutes in Blitz.
- **Master of One-on-One**: Win ten times in Duel.
- **Winning Streak**: Win 5 matches in a row.

## Progression
- **Crown of All Classes**: Win at least once with every class.
- **Battlefield Regular**: Finish fifty matches.
- **Class Master**: Raise one class to the max level.
- **Gold Rank**: Raise one class's Mastery to Gold.
- **Every Map Conquered**: Win at least once on every match map.

## Achievement Tips
- **Flawless Victory** requires never being defeated, so a class that helps with captures from behind the flag (Wellington, Warden) is worth trying.
- **Five-Minute Win** and **Lightning Match** require capturing flags quickly. Push together with your team using a fast class.
- **Crown of All Classes** and **Every Map Conquered** take a long time. For the thirteen maps, see the **Maps and Rules** page.

tumblecrown/mastery.b:
:: Class level = Max 10 (separate for each class)
:: Mastery = From Novice to Grandmaster V (separate for each class)
:: Experience = 20 per match, 5 per kill, 30 per win
:: Mastery points = 10 per kill, 5 per assist, 3 per monster, 20 per win, 5 for finishing, win-streak bonus
:: Based on = v0.2 build 304

Progression in Tumblecrown builds up separately for each class. Playing a lot of Knight will not raise your Priest's level. So every time you try a new class, you climb steadily from the start.

## Class Level
- Each class has its own level. The max level is 10.
- You receive 20 experience at the end of every match, 5 for each opponent you defeat, and 30 for a win.
- Reaching level 10 requires 2,025 experience in total. In a won match with 4 kills you earn 70, so it takes close to 30 matches.
- The class selection screen shows each class's level and experience bar, and the results screen shows the experience gained and any level-ups.
- Raising one class to the max level earns the achievement **Class Master**.

## Mastery Points
- Mastery points for each class accumulate when a match ends.
- Defeating an opponent gives 10 points, an assist 5, contributing to a neutral monster kill 3, a win 20, and finishing a match 5.
- A streak of wins adds a win-streak bonus: 5 points from a 3-win streak, 10 for 5 wins, 15 for 7 wins, and 20 for 10 wins.
- Each mode has a point multiplier, but all of them are currently 1x.
- Practice vs Bots rooms do not use the mode multiplier.
- The class selection screen shows your current rank and the points left to the next rank, and the results screen shows the points you earned.

## Mastery Ranks
- Starting from Novice (0 points), you rise through Bronze (90 points), Silver (260), Gold (530), Platinum (880), Diamond (1,750), Master (3,050) and Grandmaster (6,000), in that order.
- Bronze through Diamond have tiers I, II and III. The points between tiers are the points to the next rank divided into thirds.
- Master runs from I to V and rises by 600 points each. Grandmaster also runs from I to V and rises by 1,000 points each.
- Raising one class's Mastery to Gold earns the achievement **Gold Rank**.

## Mastery Skins
- Reaching Diamond (1,750 points), Master (3,050 points) and Grandmaster (6,000 points) unlocks a skin for that class. Details are on the **Cosmetics and tC** page.

- You receive 40 tC for each **daily mission** you complete. They refresh at midnight Korea time and can only be completed in online matches. The missions are: finish 2 online matches, defeat 12 opponents, win 1 match, and finish 1 match with the class set for that day.
- You can exchange Hub Coin for tC. One Hub Coin is 35 tC, and the exchanged tC is collected once each time you log in. See the Hub Coin page for how to exchange it on the Hub.

## Buying and Wearing

tumblecrown/tips.b:
:: Key point = Have more players on the flag
:: Related pages = **Flags and Neutral Monsters**, **Classes at a Glance**, **Maps and Rules**
:: Based on = v0.2 build 304

These are tips drawn directly from the rules and class data. There is no single right answer; they are organized to help first-time players get less lost.

## Flag Fights
- The side with more players wins the flag. Do not try to capture alone; with two or more standing together the speed is 1.5x, and with three it is 2x.
- If both teams have the same number of players, nobody captures it. Even one extra player changes the situation.
- For 5 seconds right after a capture, movement speed and attack are up 20%, so move straight into the fight as soon as the capture finishes.
- If your flag blinks red, someone is capturing it. Check the minimap often.
- If a team holding 5 or more flags pushes, the enemy's respawn time increases by 5 seconds. Pressing on while ahead helps lock in the lead.

## Neutral Monsters
- The more you defeat monsters, the stronger your whole team becomes permanently. Taking one early gives an advantage until the end of the match.
- Only the team that defeated the monster gets the credit. A monster does not chase opponents that are too far away and returns to its spot, so rather than dragging it around, gather and take it down all at once.

## Roll and Kill Chains
- If you roll just before an attack lands, your damage increases by 50% for 2.5 seconds. You can defend and counterattack in a single move.
- If you defeat opponents in a row within 8 seconds, your skill cooldowns are halved. Once you take one down, go straight for the next opponent.

## Recall and Respawn
- If a distant flag is in danger, recall with F and go to your flag after 3 seconds. You cannot move while recalling, so use it when no opponents are around.
- Even if you cancel, a 25-second cooldown starts. Pressing it and then changing your mind costs you.

## Class Compositions
- If a team gathers only melee damage classes, capturing flags is easy but you get hit from a distance. Mix in ranged damage classes and supports.
- With a Warden or Telaris blocking the chokepoint and a Priest and Bard helping from behind, you hold out for a long time.
- Wellington can defend your flag with Steadfast Defense or steal an enemy flag with Capture. These skills turn the tide of flag fights.
- Bots pick classes so that they do not overlap within the same team. If you pick a class that does not overlap with your human teammates, the composition improves.

## By Mode
- Blitz has only five flags, so matches are fast. Once you are pushed back, it is hard to recover.
- In Duel you cannot capture for the first 1 minute 30 seconds. Use that time to read the classes' skill ranges and cooldowns.
- Hyper has four monsters and many players, so many clash at once. Move as a team rather than as individuals.

tumblecrown/faq.b:
:: Based on = v0.2 build 304

A collection of frequently asked questions and things to check when a problem occurs.

## Game
- **Where do I play the game?** Press the Play button on the Tumblecrown page of the game site. There is nothing to install.
- **Can I play alone?** You can play alone in Practice vs Bots or the Training Ground. In online matches too, if there is even one person, bots fill the empty slots after 15 seconds. Only Ranked does not let bots in.
- **I want to play together but cannot join the room.** You cannot play together if the versions differ. Refresh the site and check that you are on the latest build.
- **A new build was uploaded and my room disappeared.** When there is nobody in an online server room and a new build is uploaded, the room closes by itself and reopens on the new build.

## tC and Cosmetics
- **My tC is not coming in.** You do not receive tC in Practice vs Bots or private rooms. You receive it if you play an online match to the end.
- **My daily mission is not progressing.** It can only be completed in online matches. It refreshes at midnight Korea time.
- **Where is the tC I exchanged from Hub Coin?** It is collected once each time you log in. When you receive it, a notification appears in the lobby.
- **Where do I buy the Diamond Skin?** You do not buy it. It unlocks when the Mastery points of the class you currently have selected reach 1,750.

## Controls
- **I am typing in Korean and the keys do not work.** Even with the Korean input mode on, keys are read by the key in the same position.
- **My attacks do not land on a phone.** The button on the right auto-aims at the nearest opponent. For skills, hold and drag to set the direction.
- **The screen is slow.** Try turning on Optimization in Settings. It turns off shadows and glow and sets the game to 30 frames.

## Rules
- **The flag will not change hands.** If both teams have the same number of players, nobody captures it. You need one more player.
- **I cannot capture the flag at the Desert Temple.** You can only capture that flag while the temple door is open.
- **I cancelled recall but cannot use it.** Even if you cancel, a 25-second cooldown starts.

tumblecrown/glossary.b:
:: Based on = v0.2 build 304

An explanation of the terms that appear in the Tumblecrown pages and on the game screen.

## Teams and Screen
- **Your team / Enemy team**: On screen, your own team is shown as "your team" and the opponents as "the enemy team". The blue team and red team colors refer to the base colors on the map.
- **Base**: The place where a team starts and respawns. On the map it appears as a blue circle and a red circle.
- **Minimap**: The small map at the upper right of the match screen. It shows flags, bases and walls.
- **Podium**: The place where the three players with the most kills stand when the match ends.

## Flag Fights
- **Capture**: More players standing around a flag until the 7 seconds are filled.
- **Flank / Center**: The positions where flags are placed. In Classic, you capture in the order of your side's flanks, the center, the enemy-side flanks, and the enemy base.
- **Pushing**: The state in which a team holds 5 or more flags. The enemy's respawn time increases by 5 seconds.
- **Recall**: Moving to one of your team's flags after 3 seconds with F.
- **Neutral monster**: An enemy to both teams. Defeating one permanently raises that team's attack and capture speed.
- **lvl.n**: The level of the effect a team has gained from monsters it has defeated.

## Combat
- **Focus**: The state in which rolling just before an attack lands increases your damage by 50% for 2.5 seconds.
- **Skills / Basic attack**: The basic attack is the left mouse button, and the skills are Q, E and R.
- **Cooldown (reuse wait time)**: The time it takes before a skill can be used again.
- **Stun / Slow / Burn**: Stun means you cannot move for a moment, slow means your movement speed is reduced, and burn means you take damage over time.

## Progression and Currency
- **tC**: Tumblecrown's currency. You earn it from online matches and daily missions and use it to buy cosmetics.
- **Class level**: The experience tier built up for each class. The max is 10.
- **Mastery**: The points and rank built up for each class. It runs from Novice to Grandmaster V.
- **Ranking points**: Points that rise and fall with wins and losses in Ranked.
- **Hub Coin**: The coin you collect on the Hub. One can be exchanged for 35 tC.

## Main Changes in This Version
- New character Kurus, private game rewards removed, balance page changed to measurements that use ultimates, skills and dashes together, 4 new maps, colorblind mode and gamepad added.

## Build Records
- **v227**: New character Kurus, private game rewards removed (experience, gold, soul stones, Season Pass, character experience, missions, achievements).
- **v228**: Wizard skill changed to a shockwave, 2 Kurus skins and the Tongue Out emote added, Rainbow nameplate raised from 2000 to 6000 G, New tab removed from the shop (new skins go to the bottom of the Skins tab).
- **v229**: New map Swamp of Darkness and Kurus darkness overhaul.
- **v231**: Game files of the old names (ArenaClash, StickmanRumble) deleted.
- **v232~v234**: Fixed Kurus darkness lingering until the next round in Duel; added and fixed Kurus W/S darkness movement.
- **v235**: Victory pose Taunt added (1500 G).
- **v236**: Slayer flame max duration from 9 seconds to 8 seconds.
- **v237**: Slayer flame max duration from 8 seconds to 7.5 seconds, flame shield durability from 75 to 60. Balance measurement changed from all 23 maps to 3 matches per pair per map (20,700 matches in total).
- **v238** (10-16): Added receiving gold exchanged from Hub Coin.
- **v240** (10-16): Kurus movement speed in darkness from 230 to 350, Sword of Darkness range from 85 to 120. Knight Heavenly Sword damage from 100 to 120, hit width from 190 to 280.
- **v241** (10-16): Multiplayer lag improved (the state data exchanged was reduced by about half).
- **v242** (10-16): Fixed tournament replays to show only one match, with ◀ ▶ to view other matches.
- **v243** (10-17): Fixed an issue where players and effects from other matches were visible in the tournament kill cam.
- **v244** (10-17): Swamp of Darkness map overhaul (stepped platforms on both sides, a large central swamp, stepping-stone platforms over the swamp). In the central swamp, everyone has 33% less movement speed and limited vision. On Kurus's darkness, Kurus has 30% more movement speed, and opponents on the darkness have 30% less and limited vision.
- **v245** (10-17): Swamp of Darkness platforms fixed (3 tiers on one side, 1 in the center).
- **v246** (10-17): Boss raid overhaul. Time limit unified to 3 minutes (previously 4 minutes), boss health, movement speed and floor attacks weakened, bosses use a flamethrower, ice spear and electric orbs instead of a shotgun.
- **v247** (10-17): Fixed an issue where MVP was not chosen when playing with bots.
- **v248** (10-17): Raid minions changed to Flame Swordsman, Ice Swordsman and Lightning Swordsman to match the boss, with their colors changed to the boss color.
- **v249** (10-17): In bot matches, bots also take part in the MVP vote (chosen by the vote result).
- **v250** (10-17): Mobile controls improved. Aim automatically snaps to enemies near the aim direction, and a short tap toward the aim attacks the nearest enemy. Dash and teleport merged into a single 💨 button (tap to dash, long-press to teleport), emotes moved to the upper right (6 buttons down to 4). The joystick appears where you place your thumb, and the buttons became smaller and more transparent and moved above the skill bar.
- **v251** (10-17): Fixed an issue where MVP voting did not work in boss raids with bots. Allies (humans and bots) became vote candidates, and bots also vote.
- **v252** (10-17): The intro can no longer be skipped by touch, click or key input and plays to the end.
- **v253** (10-17): MVP vote overhaul. A large vote window with a countdown appears after the victory screen, the winner gets a notification and +50 experience, and then you exit to the main menu. The MVP display in boss raid results was removed, and MVP is decided only by vote.
- **v254** (10-17): Added lobby and battle background music. Added a music on/off toggle and volume control in Settings.
- **build 256** (10-17): Build notation changed to the "build N" format (both in-game and on the site). Pressing in-game buttons now makes a short click sound, linked to the sound effects off setting in Settings.
- **build 257** (10-17): Online lag reduced. Fixed characters and bullets looking choppy on the joining side so positions are displayed smoothly, and for rooms of 8 or fewer the host's state updates were raised from 20 to 30 per second.
- **build 258** (10-17): Battle Royale overhaul (both Battle Royale and Duo). A danger zone that closes in from both ends 30 seconds after the start, supply crates falling on platforms (health recovery, ultimate charge, skill charge), and starting positions widened to all platforms.
- **build 259** (10-17): Button click sound changed to a shorter, softer "tok" sound.
- **build 260** (10-17): Instant bot filling. If there is only 1 person in an online room, bots fill in after about 1.5 seconds instead of waiting 15 seconds. When in a party or with 2 or more people, the 15-second wait applies as before.
- **build 261** (10-17): MVP voting limited to team modes. MVP is chosen only in modes with teams, and there is none in free-for-all modes. Both voters and candidates are teammates who won; the vote window does not appear for the losing team and the leave button is not blocked. If the winning team has no humans and only bots, the vote is skipped.
- **build 262** (10-17): Immediate bot filling. If there is only 1 person in an online room, bots fill in right away with no notice text, and bots also join quickly. When in a party or with 2 or more people, the 15-second wait applies as before.
- **build 263** (10-17): Bots now go to find and pick up supply crates in Battle Royale and Battle Royale Duo (when hurt they look for health crates first). Bots that went outside the danger zone step onto platforms and return inward. Bots pick and confirm a weapon within 5 seconds.
- **build 264** (10-17): Faster online room finding (6 rooms are checked at the same time, and checking all rooms is kept). Added a ticking sound to hot potato and a sound when the bomb is passed.
- **build 265** (10-17): Kurus's Darkness Escape damage and vanishing darkness now apply only to the darkness connected to the darkness you are in and the darkness above and below it (the rest of my darkness remains).
- **build 266** (10-17): Steal the Flag bot improvements. No bots just standing at the base; if there is an opponent near our flag or heading toward our side, the bots closest to the flag fight back, matching the number of opponents.
- **build 267** (10-17): Steal the Flag bots now stop and fight opponents they meet on the way (within 420 pixels) instead of passing by. The clan leader can change the clan name and tag even after creating the clan.
- **build 268** (10-17): Nickname unification. A nickname changed on the Hub is applied to the Stickseum profile, and the clan screen shows the current nickname. Practice mode shows the damage I deal (DPS over the last 5 seconds, peak DPS, total damage, reset records).
- **build 269** (10-17): Cleaned up the Classic/minigame distinction so only modes remain. Minigames are no longer shown separately in private room mode selection. Achievement names cleaned up to All-Rounder and Mode Collector. Added a real gameplay video of bots fighting each other to the background at the top of the site.
- **build 270** (10-17): Added boss raid-exclusive background music (heavy drums, choir, bells). Only this track plays in boss raids, while other modes play the usual battle music.
- **build 271** (10-17): Added 4 new maps (Collapsing Bridge, Volcanic Zone, Ruined City, Mirror Maze). Frame rate improved with a background image cache and battery saver mode (can be turned off in Settings). Sound effects and music are loaded separately to shorten first-screen loading. Added colorblind mode (team colors and health bar colors distinguished by shape). Added gamepad (Bluetooth controller) support.
- **build 272** (10-17): Fixed bots walking toward vanished platforms on Collapsing Bridge and Underground Prison. The balance page was remeasured across all maps, including the 4 new maps.
- **build 273** (10-17): Fixed severe lag on the Collapsing Bridge map (bot pathfinding was recalculated every time the planks changed). Private play can start from a minimum of 2 players. The balance page was remeasured based on build 273 (27 maps).

v0.8 In Search of Gold is the version released on 2026-10-18. From build 372, records are organized in the order of the patch notes in the game. ## Main Changes in This Version
- New characters Pizarro and Khan, new map Waterfall Cliff, Team Battle character ban overhaul, bot teleportation, MVP vote card overhaul.

## Build Records (build 274~371)
- **build 274** (10-18): Character bans and post-selection screen cleanup. In Duel, Team Battle and Ranked, a 10-second phase was added before picking characters in which each side bans a character the opponent cannot pick (in Team Battle the team leader decides). The confirmation window that appeared after character selection was removed. In the start sequence, Team Battle, Domination and Steal the Flag are split into team versus team, while Battle Royale shows my character on the left and enemy characters on the right.
- **build 275** (10-18): Added Pick XP. At first it was earned by finishing a match (10 for finishing, +10 more for winning), and using it from the profile opens the character selection window and grants it as mastery XP to the chosen character. The Pick XP earned is shown on the match end screen.

- **build 278** (10-18): Fixed an issue where the danger zone start notice stayed on screen when leaving to the menu mid-match.
- **build 279** (10-18): Start sequence character cards now show a blue background for allies and a red background for enemies.
- **build 280** (10-18): Bot character ban display. Even a side with only bots bans a character by itself after a moment in the ban phase (even after a human decides, it waits until the bot decides), and the ban phase shows whether the opposing side has decided its ban.
- **build 282** (10-18): Fixed bots with an assigned personality in Domination not going to the control points and just staring upward from the floor. - **build 285** (10-18): Jadai now blocks short-range attacks instead of returning their damage. After a successful block, he can swing once more with no cooldown. Balance remeasured.
- **build 286** (10-18): Jadai damage from 34 to 26. Balance remeasured.
- **build 287** (10-18): Damage that Blast Maniac and Heavy Gunner take from their own explosions from 50% to 25%, Knight basic attack damage from 30 to 32, Knight skill damage from 30 to 32. Balance remeasured.

- **build 291** (10-18): Fixed progress (gold, skins, level), highlights and recently played-with players so they no longer overlap when two different accounts log in on the same browser (kept separately per account in this browser). - **build 304** (10-18): Added the new map Waterfall Cliff.

## Balance Measurement
- The site's balance page shows win rates from bot-versus-bot matches. The current measurement is 4 matches per pair per map across all 28 maps, 36,400 matches in total (as of build 299. From build 273 to 293 it was 27 maps and 32,400 matches, and from v240 to build 271 it was 23 maps and 27,600 matches).
- Because it is a bot measurement, it may differ from real matches.
- The win rate graph on the balance page shows only the 8 most recent builds, and you can drag left and right to see the rest.
- When the **Patches Only** button on the graph (on by default) is on, only the first measurement and the builds in which that character was patched are drawn, and when off, every changed measurement is drawn (build 370).
